# Roadmap: arithmetic dynamics

**Summary.** This roadmap builds the arithmetic of iterated self-maps: deciding when an orbit is finite, measuring its growth by canonical heights, relating global small points to local invariant measures, and studying the Galois action on iterated preimages. Its endpoints include dynamical equidistribution on the projective line, explicit rational-cycle and preperiodic-point problems, selected arboreal image theorems, canonical-height specialization, uniform common torsion images in the Legendre family, and étale dynamical Mordell–Lang. The concrete maps z↦z^d, z↦z²+c, and the Lattès maps provide checks across these theories.

The plan comprises the parent and its three reviewed continuations, integrated below by mathematical layer. All **490 targets** are retained under their original identifiers, with their hypotheses, proof routes, source locators, definition APIs and checks. There are **726 API items and 412 named unit tests**. Every implementation status is **unchecked**. All seven layers are **planned**, and none is **closed**: a chain may terminate in an exact supplier request or an explicitly recorded proof gap. An accepted source theorem is not a library implementation, and an arithmetic certificate with unproduced numerical data is not a completed computation.

The [suggested Lean file](../suggested/ArithmeticDynamics.lean) is a compact selection of statements expressible over carriers at the recorded pins. Heavy geometric, analytic and computational constructions are full mathematical targets here. The separate part files preserve the reviewed inputs; this document is the assembled reader. The [assembly handoff](../handoff/ASM-ArithmeticDynamics.md) records the changes that need independent review and every outstanding supplier or restructuring request.

## Scope and ownership

ArithmeticDynamics owns the dynamical constructions and their comparisons. Iteration, periodic points, minimal periods, semiconjugacy, polynomials and resultants, projective points, Weil heights and Northcott, Galois theory and Krull topologies are imported from the libraries. Tau Ceti's elliptic canonical height is an input to the Lattès comparison. The underlying algebraic curves, Riemann surfaces, analytic lines and general height machines each keep their existing owner.

## Conventions

For a self-map f, f^[n] denotes n-fold composition, including the identity at n=0. A preperiodic point has a finite forward orbit; an exact period is positive. Equality of iterates means equality of maps. The projective line has coordinates [x₀:x₁], affine coordinate x₀/x₁ and infinity [1:0]. Binary forms have their specified formal degrees even when dehomogenization drops the actual degree. The resultant orientation gives Res(X₀^d,X₁^d)=1, Res(X₁^d,X₀^d)=(−1)^d and Res(aX₀+bX₁,cX₀+eX₁)=ae−bc. Conjugation is the left action γ∘f∘γ⁻¹; a source using f^γ=γ⁻¹∘f∘γ uses the inverse group element.

Maps of degree at least two are required wherever a canonical dynamical limit, Julia-support theorem or entropy log d is asserted. Nodes state stronger field or characteristic conditions individually. Pullbacks of measures and divisors count local algebraic degrees, including inseparable multiplicity. This degree is not the separable degree or the number of distinct points in a fibre. Good reduction and potential good reduction are separate conditions; arbitrary PGL₂ conjugation need not preserve good reduction in the chosen coordinates.

Arithmetic heights are absolute unless explicitly called **native relative**. Over a number field K of degree q, the absolute logarithmic height is the native logarithmic height divided by q. Thus an absolute bound B gives native multiplicative radius exp(qB), while a native logarithmic bound B gives exp(B). Both lists returned by ED.0/bounded-height-enumeration are retained, with infinity added. A finite exact carrier, computable equality and a compatible field realization are additional execution requirements, not consequences of Northcott finiteness.

The elliptic comparison is revision-sensitive. At Tau Ceti f790474, Point.canonicalHeight is half the native limiting x-coordinate height: the raw Tate limit for doubling is twice it. At current library revision a91d3aa the factor one-half has been removed from that native definition. Dividing the pinned elliptic height by q, or the current one by 2q, gives the usual absolute Néron–Tate normalization used in the reader's Lattès comparison. Any migration must recheck this factor. The suggested file is tested at the original pins, not the current library.

Over C, the Riemann sphere has the topology of OnePoint C and the compatible compact uniformity; its complex charts are a separate imported structure. Over a complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field K, the Berkovich line is TB.0's multiplicative-seminorm space with the **weak** topology. Type-I points have their classical chordal topology; the strong hyperbolic-tree topology is different. No one-point compactification of K is a replacement for this analytic line. The exceptional set means classical points with finite backward orbit. A finite-grand-orbit predicate on all analytic points is distinct. Pure Frobenius can have infinitely many classical exceptional points.

The nonarchimedean sign is μ_f=Δĝ_F+δ_G, with Δlog⁺|T|=δ_G−δ∞. It is opposite to Baker–Rumely's convention. The complex sign is μ_f=Δg_F+ω, with normalized unit-circle angular probability ω and Δlog⁺|z|=ω−δ∞; on C, Δ is 1/(2π) times the Euclidean Laplacian and Δlog|z|=δ₀. The sphere's measure-valued Laplacian is defined on differences of subharmonic potentials with Radon Riesz measures, including the actual escape potential. Arbitrary continuous functions do not have measure-valued Laplacians. Continuous dynamical potentials rule out type-I atoms; they permit the Gauss atom. Measure support and topological entropy use the native library notions; measure entropy requires its stated supplier.

Y₁(n) is the affine dynatomic scheme, X₁(n) its regular projective characteristic-zero model, and X₀(n) the quotient by cycle rotation. Formal period need not be exact period at a root-of-unity multiplier. The period-three parametrization and the assertion of at most one rational three-cycle are separate nodes: the latter uses Morton's elliptic reduction. Poonen type-(3,2) and its dependent exclusions and bounds retain rank J(C₁(3₂))(Q)≤1. Stoll's six-cycle exclusion retains its genus-four rank hypothesis. No conjecture becomes an unconditional theorem merely by being named as a proposition.

In the Lech presentation A=Z[T₁,…,Tₙ], F=Frac(A), and the primitive variable Y is separate from the parameters. Marked expressions U(y,t)/V(t) have V in A, nonzero. Marks can include zero and need not generate the field. The primitive equation is generically separable and can be nonmonic over A. The parameter map is extended to the entire field before marked evaluation identities are used.

Within each layer, targets are ordered by their local prerequisites. DY.2 first constructs the parent measures independently of the transfer argument; the latter identifies them and proves support and entropy. The sharp period route is weighted coefficients → jet growth → rational-cycle adapter → the parent exponent endpoint. DY.3 builds the affine ring before its projective model; analytic identification supplies the smoothness/irreducibility endpoint. Its period-three parametrization feeds the two-cycle reduction, which feeds the final Poonen bound. This avoids a dependency backedge. The relative candidate adapter follows the number-field enumeration endpoint, whose exact runtime adapter is independent of that endpoint. In DY.6 primitive presentation and root transport feed Lech integral assembly, after the independent Hensel specialization already planned by the parent.

There is one useful forward reading reference: the DY.2 power-map comparison consumes the elementary DY.6/power-map. Read it after that example. Its prerequisite chain returns only to DY.0, so it creates no cycle. The four-packet union is a directed acyclic graph, rather than four separately checked graphs.

**Checks across layers.** For z↦z^d the absolute canonical height is the Weil height. Over C the Julia set and canonical-measure support are the unit circle; at nonarchimedean good reduction the classical Julia set is empty and the Berkovich Julia set is the Gauss singleton with mass one. These distinguish the carriers and the Laplacian normalization. Under z²+c a formal period-two root at c=−3/4 can be fixed, so formal and exact period must differ. The x²+1 arboreal example tests every finite level, whereas the postcritically finite x²−2 does not satisfy the same surjectivity statement. A finite marked set {0,1/6} in Q tests both zero marks and parameter-only denominators in Lech's theorem. Every object's more specific checks appear beside its contract below.

## Sources and status of the evidence

The sources are organized by the mathematics they support. Silverman's public AWS notes and Call–Silverman supply orbit/height and specialization contracts; Baker–Rumely, Favre–Rivera-Letelier, Benedetto and Lyubich supply local potential theory and dynamics; Morton–Silverman, Gao–Ou, Doyle–Poonen, Morton, Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer, Poonen, Stoll and Hutz supply periodic equations, curves and arithmetic reductions. Jones, Aitken–Hajir–Maire, Stoll and Juul supply the arboreal routes. The family targets use Ingram, DeMarco–Krieger–Ye, DeMarco–Wang–Ye, Milnor, Favre, Cassels, Bell and Bell–Ghioca–Tucker, with Ghioca–Tucker–Zieve for polynomial orbit intersections.

Each target below names the precise theorem, section and page locator recorded in its source version. The final bibliography preserves the reviewed versions, hashes and reading records; it does not claim this assembly re-read every source. Zieve's public thesis was fetched from his university page, its hash matched the reviewed record, and Chapter 2, Lemma 46, Corollaries 48–49 and Theorem 50 (printed pp.35–38) were re-read. Poonen's author errata, p.1, was rechecked against the rank caveat. This run used no uncleared book copy. The unresolved proof-access gaps for Tate variation and the minimum-conjugate-height comparison remain listed. All source issues are stated in our own words and keep their independent verdicts.

## Layer 0: Iteration, maps and moduli

Construct the orbit predicates first, then the homogeneous-form map and its degree/resultant contracts. Scheme comparisons and geometric moduli require their listed suppliers; a set quotient over K does not identify all twists with geometric K-points.

Planets: Preperiodic point; Resultant of a rational map; Rational map of ℙ¹; Moduli space M_d; Milnor's M₂ ≅ 𝔸²; Good reduction.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-forward-orbit"></a>

### 0.1 The forward orbit of a point under a self-map

For a type α, a self-map f : α → α and x : α, the forward orbit of x is O_f(x) = {f^n(x) : n ∈ ℕ} (with f^0(x) = x), the range of the orbit map ℕ → α, n ↦ f^[n] x (Mathlib's iterate `Nat.iterate`).

α any type; no structure on α is used. n = 0 is included, so x ∈ O_f(x).

Define O_f(x) as Set.range (n ↦ f^[n] x). Membership: y ∈ O_f(x) iff y = f^[n] x for some n (definition of range). Forward invariance f(O_f(x)) ⊆ O_f(x) and O_f(x) = {x} ∪ O_f(f x) from f^[n+1] x = f (f^[n] x) (Function.iterate_succ_apply'); iteration also commutes with f. Functoriality: if g ∘ fa = fb ∘ g (Function.Semiconj g fa fb) then g ∘ fa^[n] = fb^[n] ∘ g (Function.Semiconj.iterate_right), so g(O_fa(x)) = O_fb(g x).

*Needs:* `mathlib:Nat.iterate`; `mathlib:Function.iterate_succ_apply'`; `mathlib:Function.Semiconj`; `mathlib:Function.Semiconj.iterate_right`.

([silverman-aws-2010](#source-parent-silverman-aws-2010), §1, p. 2 — Exactly the definition (with ϕ^0(x) = x, stated on the same page); [call-silverman-1993](#source-parent-call-silverman-1993), §1, p. 168 — The orbit whose finiteness defines preperiodicity.)

The reusable interface consists of the following statements.

- **`forwardOrbit`** (data): O_f(x) = {f^[n] x : n ∈ ℕ} ⊆ α.
- **`mem_forwardOrbit_iff`** (characterisation): y ∈ O_f(x) ↔ ∃ n, f^[n] x = y.
- **`self_mem_forwardOrbit`** (simp): x ∈ O_f(x).
- **`mapsTo_forwardOrbit`** (structure): f maps O_f(x) into itself.
- **`forwardOrbit_eq_insert`** (relation): O_f(x) = insert x (O_f(f x)).
- **`image_forwardOrbit`** (functoriality): If Function.Semiconj g fa fb then g '' O_fa(x) = O_fb(g x).
- **`forwardOrbit_subset_of_mem`** (other): If y ∈ O_f(x) then O_f(y) ⊆ O_f(x).

**Checks.**

- **`TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics.forwardOrbit_succ_zero`** (computation): The forward orbit of 0 under n ↦ n + 1 on ℕ is all of ℕ.
- **`TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics.forwardOrbit_id`** (degenerate): For the identity map, forwardOrbit id x = {x}.
- **`TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics.forwardOrbit_sq_sub_one`** (computation): Under z ↦ z² − 1 on ℤ, the forward orbit of 1 is {1, 0, −1}.
- **`TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics.one_not_mem_forwardOrbit_succ_two`** (non-example): Under n ↦ n + 1 on ℤ, 1 ∉ O(2): the forward orbit is not the orbit of the ℤ-action generated by f.

**Endpoint checks.** Under n ↦ n + 1 on ℕ the orbit of 0 is ℕ; under the identity every orbit is a singleton. Under z ↦ z² − 1 on ℤ the orbit of 1 is {1, 0, −1} (Silverman, AWS notes, Example 2).

Consumers: Silverman, AWS notes, §1 — preperiodic and wandering points are those with finite and infinite orbit; Call–Silverman, Corollary 1.1.1(a) — the orbit of a point of canonical height zero has bounded height, hence is finite; ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/preperiodic-iff-finite-forward-orbit — the finite-orbit characterisation of preperiodic points; ArithmeticDynamics:DY.1/preperiodic-of-tate-limit-eq-zero — Northcott applied to the forward orbit; ArithmeticDynamicsPartIIBifurcation (DeMarco–Mavraki–Ye §2.2) — a map is PCF when every critical point has a finite forward orbit.

Suggested library home: `TauCeti/Dynamics/PreperiodicPts`, namespace `TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics`.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-preperiodic-point"></a>

### 0.2 Preperiodic points of a self-map

For f : α → α, a point x is preperiodic (IsPreperiodicPt f x) if some iterate f^[m] x lies in Mathlib's periodicPts f, i.e. f^[m + n] x = f^[m] x for some m and some n ≥ 1. The preperiodic points form preperiodicPts f ⊇ periodicPts f.

α any type. Period n ≥ 1 (a periodic point of period 0 is excluded, as in Mathlib's periodicPts).

Define IsPreperiodicPt f x := ∃ m, f^[m] x ∈ Function.periodicPts f and preperiodicPts f := {x | IsPreperiodicPt f x}. Periodic points are preperiodic (m = 0); x preperiodic iff f x preperiodic (shift m by one, using Function.IsPeriodicPt.apply_iterate). On a finite type every point is preperiodic, by pigeonhole on the orbit map (Finite.exists_ne_map_eq_of_infinite). For g ↦ g^d on a group with d ≥ 2: g^{d^{m+n}} = g^{d^m} with n ≥ 1 gives g^{d^m(d^n − 1)} = 1, so g has finite order; conversely if g has order N the powers d^m mod N repeat.

*Needs:* `mathlib:Function.periodicPts`; `mathlib:Function.IsPeriodicPt`; `mathlib:Finite.exists_ne_map_eq_of_infinite`; `mathlib:IsOfFinOrder`.

([silverman-aws-2010](#source-parent-silverman-aws-2010), §1, p. 3 — The notion; the equivalence with the iterate form is DY.0/preperiodic-iff-finite-forward-orbit; [call-silverman-1993](#source-parent-call-silverman-1993), §1, p. 168 — The defining form chosen here; [silverman-aws-2010](#source-parent-silverman-aws-2010), §1, p. 4, Exercise A — The compatibility test with Mathlib's IsOfFinOrder.)

The reusable interface consists of the following statements.

- **`IsPreperiodicPt`** (data): IsPreperiodicPt f x :↔ ∃ m, f^[m] x ∈ periodicPts f.
- **`preperiodicPts`** (data): The set {x | IsPreperiodicPt f x}.
- **`isPreperiodicPt_iff_exists_iterate_eq`** (characterisation): IsPreperiodicPt f x ↔ ∃ m n, 0 < n ∧ f^[m + n] x = f^[m] x.
- **`isPreperiodicPt_of_isPeriodicPt`** (compatibility): A periodic point of positive period (Mathlib's IsPeriodicPt f n x, n > 0) is preperiodic.
- **`periodicPts_subset_preperiodicPts`** (relation): periodicPts f ⊆ preperiodicPts f.
- **`isPreperiodicPt_apply_iff`** (simp): IsPreperiodicPt f (f x) ↔ IsPreperiodicPt f x.
- **`IsPreperiodicPt.iterate`** (structure): Preperiodicity is preserved along the orbit: f^[m] x is preperiodic.
- **`isPreperiodicPt_of_finite`** (other): On a finite type every point is preperiodic.
- **`isPreperiodicPt_iterate_iff`** (relation): For k ≥ 1, x is preperiodic for f^[k] iff it is for f.

**Checks.**

- **`TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics.isPreperiodicPt_one_sq_sub_one`** (computation): 1 is preperiodic but not periodic for z ↦ z² − 1 on ℤ.
- **`TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics.not_isPreperiodicPt_two_sq_sub_one`** (non-example): 2 is not preperiodic for z ↦ z² − 1 on ℤ (its orbit tends to ∞).
- **`TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics.isPreperiodicPt_pow_iff_isOfFinOrder`** (compatibility): For g ↦ g^d with d ≥ 2 on a group, IsPreperiodicPt ↔ Mathlib's IsOfFinOrder g.
- **`TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics.isPreperiodicPt_id`** (degenerate): Every point is preperiodic for the identity.

**Endpoint checks.** 1 is preperiodic but not periodic for z ↦ z² − 1 on ℤ; 2 is wandering (Silverman, AWS notes, Example 2). For g ↦ g^d (d ≥ 2) on a group the preperiodic points are the torsion elements (AWS notes, Exercise A).

Consumers: Call–Silverman, Corollary 1.1.1 — preperiodic points are exactly the points of canonical height zero, and form a set of bounded height; Silverman, AWS notes, Theorem 15 (Northcott) — PrePer(ϕ, K) is finite for a number field K; ArithmeticDynamics:DY.1/zero-canonical-height-iff-preperiodic-on-the-projective-line — the target predicate of the zero-height criterion; ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3 — finiteness of preperiodic points of bounded degree for a fixed polarized morphism; ArithmeticDynamics:DY.6 and ArithmeticDynamicsPartIIBifurcation — PCF maps: all critical points preperiodic; ĥ_crit = 0.

Suggested library home: `TauCeti/Dynamics/PreperiodicPts`, namespace `TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics`.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-iterate-of-endomorphism-on-points"></a>

### 0.3 Iterates of an endomorphism act on points by its powers

Let C be a category, X, T objects and φ ∈ End X (Mathlib's monoid CategoryTheory.End X). For every T-point P : T ⟶ X and n ∈ ℕ, (Q ↦ Q ≫ φ)^[n] P = P ≫ φ^n. Consequently P is periodic of period n for Q ↦ Q ≫ φ iff P ≫ φ^n = P: the iterates of a morphism of schemes (C = schemes over S, T = Spec K) are the powers φ^n in End X, and equality of iterates is equality of morphisms.

Any category; φ^n is the power in CategoryTheory.End X, whose product is xs * ys = ys ≫ xs (CategoryTheory.End.mul_def).

Induct on n. The zero case is P ≫ 𝟙 = P. For n + 1 use Function.iterate_succ_apply', φ^(n+1) = φ * φ^n = φ^n ≫ φ (pow_succ' and CategoryTheory.End.mul_def), and associativity. The periodicity statement is the case of Function.IsPeriodicPt unfolded with the first identity.

*Needs:* `mathlib:CategoryTheory.End`; `mathlib:CategoryTheory.End.mul_def`; `mathlib:Function.iterate_succ_apply'`; `mathlib:Function.IsPeriodicPt`.

([silverman-aws-2010](#source-parent-silverman-aws-2010), §1, p. 2 — Iteration of a self-map; here the self-map is postcomposition with a morphism; [silverman-aws-2010](#source-parent-silverman-aws-2010), §6.1, p. 19, Supplementary Material — Dynamical systems given by morphisms of schemes, whose iterates are compositions of morphisms.)

**Endpoint checks.** For C = Type and T = a point, the statement is Mathlib's Function.End pow = iterate. For X = P¹_K the powers of the scheme morphism of a rational map f are the morphisms of f^n (DY.0/rational-map-to-scheme-endomorphism).

Suggested library home: `TauCeti/Dynamics/Endomorphism`, namespace `TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics`.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-resultant-of-a-rational-map"></a>

### 0.4 The resultant of a pair of binary forms

For a commutative ring R, binary forms F, G ∈ R[X₀, X₁] and formal degrees m, n ∈ ℕ, Res_{m,n}(F, G) := Polynomial.resultant F(X, 1) G(X, 1) m n, Mathlib's (m + n) × (m + n) Sylvester determinant of the dehomogenisations F(X, 1) = aeval ![X, 1] F. For a homogeneous lift (F₀, F₁) of a degree-d rational map the resultant is Res_d(F₀, F₁) := Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁); since Res_{d,d}(cF₀, cF₁) = c^{2d} Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁), the resultant of the map is defined up to (K^×)^{2d}, and its valuation on a normalised lift is well defined. Orientation (pinned): Res_{d,d}(X₀^d, X₁^d) = 1 and Res_{d,d}(X₁^d, X₀^d) = (−1)^d; for m = n = d this is the determinant of Silverman (AWS notes, Example 23), Rumely ((1)) and Milnor (Appendix A).

R commutative; F, G arbitrary (in applications homogeneous of degrees m, n, so that F(X, 1), G(X, 1) have degree ≤ m, n). Formal degrees are explicit: they matter when a leading coefficient vanishes (a root at ∞).

Define binaryResultant m n F G := Polynomial.resultant (aeval ![X, 1] F) (aeval ![X, 1] G) m n. Compatibility with Mathlib's homogenisation: aeval ![X, 1] (homogenize f m) = f when deg f ≤ m (Polynomial.aeval_homogenize_X_one), so Res_{m,n}(homogenize f m, homogenize g n) = resultant f g m n. Scaling: Res_{m,n}(cF, G) = c^n Res and Res_{m,n}(F, cG) = c^m Res (Polynomial.resultant_C_mul_left, Polynomial.resultant_C_mul_right); symmetry (Polynomial.resultant_comm); base change (Polynomial.resultant_map_map); Res_{m,n}(0, G) = 0 for n ≠ 0 (Polynomial.resultant_zero_left). Res_{d,d}(X₀^d, X₁^d) = resultant (X^d) 1 d d = 1 (Polynomial.resultant_X_pow_left); for a polynomial p of degree n, Res_{n,n} of Mathlib's toTupleMvPolynomial p is lead(p)^n (repeat Polynomial.resultant_succ_left_deg on the constant second form).

*Needs:* `mathlib:Polynomial.resultant`; `mathlib:Polynomial.sylvester`; `mathlib:MvPolynomial.aeval`; `mathlib:Polynomial.homogenize`; `mathlib:Polynomial.aeval_homogenize_X_one`; `mathlib:Polynomial.resultant_C_mul_left`; `mathlib:Polynomial.resultant_C_mul_right`; `mathlib:Polynomial.resultant_comm`; `mathlib:Polynomial.resultant_map_map`; `mathlib:Polynomial.resultant_zero_left`; `mathlib:Polynomial.resultant_X_pow_left`; `mathlib:Polynomial.resultant_succ_left_deg`; `mathlib:Polynomial.toTupleMvPolynomial`.

([milnor-1993](#source-parent-milnor-1993), Appendix A, p. 39 (arXiv v1) — Formal degrees are part of the definition; [rumely-2013](#source-parent-rumely-2013), §0, p. 1 (arXiv v2) — The resultant of a homogeneous representation as a 2d × 2d Sylvester determinant; its orientation agrees with Mathlib's (same value on every pair); [silverman-aws-2010](#source-parent-silverman-aws-2010), §6.1, p. 19, Example 23 — The test binaryResultant_quadratic_silverman reproduces the displayed formula exactly.)

The reusable interface consists of the following statements.

- **`binaryResultant`** (data): Res_{m,n}(F, G) ∈ R.
- **`binaryResultant_homogenize`** (compatibility): Res_{m,n}(homogenize f m, homogenize g n) = Mathlib's resultant f g m n when deg f ≤ m, deg g ≤ n.

- **`binaryResultant_smul_right`** (simp): Res_{m,n}(F, c • G) = c^m · Res_{m,n}(F, G).

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-binary-form-factorisation"></a>

### 0.5 Binary forms split into linear forms over an algebraically closed field

Let K be algebraically closed and G ∈ K[X₀, X₁] nonzero and homogeneous of degree n. There are c ∈ K^× and n nonzero linear forms ℓ_i = a_i X₀ + b_i X₁ such that G = c·∏_i ℓ_i. The points [−b_i : a_i] are its zeros with multiplicity; ∞ occurs n − deg G(X, 1) times. The scalar is retained when n = 0, so a nonzero constant is c times the empty product.

K algebraically closed; G ≠ 0 homogeneous of degree n.

g = G(X, 1) is nonzero of degree k ≤ n, and G = homogenize g n (Polynomial.homogenize_eq_of_isHomogeneous). g splits (IsAlgClosed.splits_domain): g = lead(g) ∏_{r ∈ roots g} (X − r) (Polynomial.C_leadingCoeff_mul_prod_multiset_X_sub_C). Homogenising the product with degree 1 for each root factor and degree n − k for the leading coefficient gives G = lead(g)·X₁^{n−k}·∏(X₀ − rX₁). Retain lead(g) as the nonzero scalar; this also covers n = 0.

*Needs:* `mathlib:IsAlgClosed.splits_domain`; `mathlib:Polynomial.C_leadingCoeff_mul_prod_multiset_X_sub_C`; `mathlib:Polynomial.homogenize_eq_of_isHomogeneous`; `mathlib:Polynomial.homogenize_finsetProd`; `mathlib:Polynomial.homogenize_C`.

**Endpoint checks.** X₀X₁² = X₀ · X₁ · X₁ (zeros [0 : 1] once and ∞ twice). X₀² + X₁² = (X₀ + iX₁)(X₀ − iX₁) over ℚ̄, with no factorisation over ℚ. For G = 2 and n = 0 over ℚ̄, choose c = 2 and the empty family of linear forms; an empty product without a scalar would incorrectly give 1.

### 0.6 Reduction of points of ℙ¹ modulo the maximal ideal

For a valuation ring R with fraction field K and residue field k, projReduction R : ℙ¹(K) → ℙ¹(k) sends [x] to [x̃], where x is scaled to have coordinates in R with at least one unit coordinate and x̃ is its coordinatewise residue. It is surjective and sends ∞ to ∞.

R a valuation ring, K = Frac R.

Every x ≠ 0 in K² can be scaled into R² with a unit coordinate (valuation ring: divide by a coordinate of minimal valuation); two such scalings differ by a unit of R, so [x̃] is well defined (Projectivization.lift). x̃ ≠ 0 because a unit coordinate has nonzero residue (IsLocalRing.residue_ne_zero_iff_isUnit). Surjectivity: lift a representative with a nonzero coordinate from k to R (IsLocalRing.residue is surjective).

### 0.7 Preperiodic iff the forward orbit is finite

For f : α → α and x : α: IsPreperiodicPt f x ↔ (forwardOrbit f x).Finite.

α any type.

(⇒) If f^[m + n] x = f^[m] x with n ≥ 1, every f^[k] x with k ≥ m equals f^[m + ((k − m) mod n)] x (Function.IsPeriodicPt.iterate_mod_apply applied at f^[m] x), so O_f(x) ⊆ {f^[k] x : k < m + n}, a finite set (Set.Finite.subset). (⇐) If O_f(x) is finite the orbit map ℕ → O_f(x) is not injective (Finite.exists_ne_map_eq_of_infinite): f^[i] x = f^[j] x with i < j, so f^[i] x is periodic of period j − i.

### 0.8 Semiconjugacies preserve preperiodic points

(a) If g : α → β satisfies g ∘ fa = fb ∘ g (Function.Semiconj g fa fb) and x is preperiodic for fa, then g x is preperiodic for fb. (b) If moreover g is bijective, x is preperiodic for fa iff g x is preperiodic for fb.

No hypothesis on α, β; (b) needs g bijective.

(a) From f^[m] x ∈ periodicPts fa and Function.IsPeriodicPt.map (with Function.Semiconj.iterate_right to move g past fa^[m]) get fb^[m] (g x) = g (fa^[m] x) ∈ periodicPts fb. (b) The inverse of a bijective semiconjugacy semiconjugates fb to fa; apply (a) to it.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-binary-resultant-mul"></a>

### 0.9 Bimultiplicativity of the binary resultant

For binary forms over a commutative ring with F₁, F₂, G homogeneous of degrees m₁, m₂, n: Res_{m₁+m₂,n}(F₁F₂, G) = Res_{m₁,n}(F₁, G) · Res_{m₂,n}(F₂, G); symmetrically Res_{m,n₁+n₂}(F, G₁G₂) = Res_{m,n₁}(F, G₁) · Res_{m,n₂}(F, G₂).

Homogeneity gives deg F_i(X, 1) ≤ m_i and deg G(X, 1) ≤ n (MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.totalDegree_le).

Dehomogenisation is a ring homomorphism, so (F₁F₂)(X, 1) = F₁(X, 1)F₂(X, 1). With k_i = m_i − deg F_i(X, 1), Polynomial.resultant_add_left_deg moves the formal degree m_i to the actual degree at the cost of the factor (−1)^{n k_i} g_n^{k_i}, where g_n is the coefficient of X^n in G(X, 1). Polynomial.resultant_mul_left already places the product at the sum of the two input natDegrees, without assuming the product has that natDegree. Apply resultant_add_left_deg to raise those formal degrees by k₁ and k₂; the sum k₁ + k₂ raises the product degree to m₁ + m₂. The signs and g_n powers then multiply. This remains valid over rings with zero divisors, where natDegree of a product can drop. The second formula follows from the first by Polynomial.resultant_comm (or directly from Polynomial.resultant_mul_right and Polynomial.resultant_add_right_deg).

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-resultant-of-a-rational-map); `mathlib:Polynomial.resultant_mul_left`; `mathlib:Polynomial.resultant_mul_right`; `mathlib:Polynomial.resultant_add_left_deg`; `mathlib:Polynomial.resultant_add_right_deg`; `mathlib:Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le`; `mathlib:MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.totalDegree_le`; `mathlib:Polynomial.resultant_comm`.

([milnor-1993](#source-parent-milnor-1993), Appendix A, p. 39 (arXiv v1) — Exactly the formula, with formal degrees.)

**Endpoint checks.** X₀X₁ against X₀ + X₁: Res_{2,1}(X₀X₁, X₀ + X₁) = Res_{1,1}(X₀, X₀ + X₁) · Res_{1,1}(X₁, X₀ + X₁) = 1 · (−1) = −1.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-resultant-postcomp-linear"></a>

### 0.10 The resultant under a linear change of the pair of forms

For a commutative ring R, a matrix A ∈ M₂(R) and binary forms F₀, F₁ homogeneous of degree d: Res_{d,d}(A₀₀F₀ + A₀₁F₁, A₁₀F₀ + A₁₁F₁) = det(A)^d · Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁).

R commutative; F_j homogeneous of degree d.

The Sylvester matrix is linear in the coefficient vectors of both polynomials (Polynomial.sylvester): its first d columns carry shifts of the second form, its last d columns shifts of the first. Hence Syl(A·F) = Syl(F) · M where M is, after reindexing Fin (d + d) ≃ Fin 2 × Fin d, the Kronecker product of the 2 × 2 matrix of A (with rows and columns ordered as in the Sylvester blocks) with the d × d identity. det M = det(A)^d (Matrix.det_kronecker, Matrix.det_reindex_self), and Matrix.det_mul gives the claim.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-resultant-of-a-rational-map); `mathlib:Polynomial.sylvester`; `mathlib:Matrix.det_mul`; `mathlib:Matrix.det_kronecker`; `mathlib:Matrix.det_reindex_self`.

([milnor-1993](#source-parent-milnor-1993), Appendix A, p. 39 (arXiv v1) — The diagonal and swap cases; the general linear case is their common extension; [rumely-2013](#source-parent-rumely-2013), §1, p. 5 (arXiv v2) — The scalar case A = cI.)

### 0.11 The zeros of a binary form in ℙ¹, with multiplicity

For a field K, n ∈ ℕ and a binary form G, binaryRoots n G ∈ Multiset ℙ¹(K) consists of [r : 1] for each root r of G(X, 1) (with multiplicity) and ∞ = [1 : 0] with multiplicity n − deg G(X, 1); for G = 0 it is empty. For G ≠ 0 homogeneous of degree n its underlying set is the zero set of G in ℙ¹(K), and it has n elements when K is algebraically closed.

K a field; n is the formal degree (the multiplicity of ∞ depends on it).

Define binaryRoots n G := ((G(X, 1)).roots.map (r ↦ [r : 1])) + (n − deg G(X, 1)) • {∞} (Polynomial.roots), and 0 for G = 0. Membership: for x = (x₀, x₁) with x₁ ≠ 0, G(x) = x₁^n G(x₀/x₁, 1) (Polynomial.eval_homogenize); at ∞, G(1, 0) is the coefficient of X₀^n, zero iff deg G(X, 1) < n. Cardinality n over an algebraically closed field: deg G(X, 1) roots (IsAlgClosed.card_roots_eq_natDegree) plus n − deg at ∞. Multiplicativity under products (roots of a product, Polynomial.roots_mul) and invariance under scaling.

### 0.12 The resultant vanishes exactly at a common zero

Let K be a field, d ≥ 1 and F₀, F₁ ∈ K[X₀, X₁] homogeneous of degree d. Then Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁) = 0 iff F₀ and F₁ have a common zero x ∈ K̄² ∖ {0} (K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K), i.e. a common zero in ℙ¹(K̄).

d ≥ 1 (in degree 0 the resultant is 1 for every pair). Homogeneity of degree exactly d with formal degrees d, d.

Base change to K̄ does not change whether the resultant vanishes (Polynomial.resultant_map_map, injectivity of K → K̄). If F₀ = 0 (or F₁ = 0) the resultant is 0 (Polynomial.resultant_zero_left) and the other form has a zero in ℙ¹(K̄) by DY.0/binary-form-factorisation (d ≥ 1). Otherwise factor F₀ = ∏ ℓ_i and F₁ = ∏ m_j into linear forms (DY.0/binary-form-factorisation) and expand by DY.0/binary-resultant-mul: Res = ∏_{i,j} Res_{1,1}(ℓ_i, m_j). Res_{1,1}(aX₀ + bX₁, cX₀ + eX₁) = ae − bc (2 × 2 Sylvester determinant, Matrix.det_fin_two) vanishes iff the two linear forms are proportional iff they have the same zero; so Res = 0 iff some ℓ_i and m_j share a zero.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-resultant-precomp-linear"></a>

### 0.13 The resultant under a linear substitution of the variables

For a commutative ring R, A ∈ M₂(R) and binary forms F₀, F₁ homogeneous of degree d, write F∘A for the substitution X_i ↦ Σ_j A_ij X_j (linearSubst A). Then Res_{d,d}(F₀∘A, F₁∘A) = det(A)^{d²} · Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁).

R commutative; F_j homogeneous of degree d.

For d = 0 both resultants equal the determinant of the empty Sylvester matrix, namely 1, including when either form is zero; det(A)^0 = 1. In the remaining steps d > 0. Universal identity: both sides are integer polynomials in the entries of A and the coefficients of F; by Polynomial.resultant_map_map it suffices to prove it for the universal forms over ℤ[a, b, A], hence over the algebraic closure of its fraction field (an injective ring map). Over an algebraically closed field factor F₀ = c₀∏_i ℓ_i and F₁ = c₁∏_j m_j with c₀,c₁ nonzero into linear forms (DY.0/binary-form-factorisation; if a form is 0 both sides vanish by Polynomial.resultant_zero_left); then F_k∘A factor as ∏ (ℓ_i∘A) and ∏ (m_j∘A). Expand both sides by DY.0/binary-resultant-mul into d² factors Res_{1,1}(ℓ_i∘A, m_j∘A) and Res_{1,1}(ℓ_i, m_j). For linear forms, Res_{1,1}(ℓ∘A, m∘A) = det(A) · Res_{1,1}(ℓ, m): the coefficient matrix of (ℓ∘A, m∘A) is that of (ℓ, m) times A (Matrix.det_fin_two, Matrix.det_mul).

### 0.14 The resultant of a conjugated lift

For A ∈ M₂(R) and binary forms F₀, F₁ of degree d, Rumely's homogeneous conjugate F^A := adj(A) ∘ F ∘ A, (F^A)_i = Σ_j adj(A)_ij (F_j∘A), satisfies Res_{d,d}(F^A_0, F^A_1) = det(A)^{d²+d} · Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁).

R commutative; F_j homogeneous of degree d; A need not be invertible (for invertible A, F^A is a lift of the conjugate A^{-1}∘f∘A).

F_j∘A is homogeneous of degree d (MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.aeval); apply DY.0/resultant-postcomp-linear with the matrix adj(A), whose determinant is det(A)^{2−1} = det(A) (Matrix.det_adjugate), giving det(A)^d · Res(F∘A). Apply DY.0/resultant-precomp-linear: Res(F∘A) = det(A)^{d²} Res(F).

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/resultant-postcomp-linear`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-resultant-postcomp-linear); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/resultant-precomp-linear`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-resultant-precomp-linear); `mathlib:Matrix.det_adjugate`; `mathlib:MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.aeval`; `mathlib:Matrix.adjugate`.

([rumely-2013](#source-parent-rumely-2013), §1, p. 5 (arXiv v2) — Exactly the formula, with Rumely's convention (7) F^γ = Adj(γ) ∘ F ∘ γ; [levy-2011](#source-parent-levy-2011), §1, p. 1 (arXiv v2) — The consequence for SL₂ (det = 1) used to define the conjugation action on Rat_d.)

**Endpoint checks.** A = [[1, 1], [0, 1]] (translation) leaves the resultant unchanged: det = 1. A = diag(2, 1) on (X₀², X₁²): F^A = (4X₀², 2X₁²), a lift of A⁻¹ ∘ z² ∘ A = 2z², has resultant 64 = 2^{d² + d}; its normalised lift (2X₀², X₁²) has resultant 4, so 2z² has bad reduction at 2.

### 0.15 The resultant as a Nullstellensatz certificate

For a commutative ring R, d ≥ 1 and binary forms F₀, F₁ homogeneous of degree d, there are binary forms G_{k,j} (k, j ∈ {0, 1}) homogeneous of degree d − 1 with G_{k,0}F₀ + G_{k,1}F₁ = Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁) · X_k^{2d−1} for k = 0, 1. In particular, over a field, if Res ≠ 0 then F₀(x) = F₁(x) = 0 forces x = 0, and q_{k,j} = G_{k,j}/Res is the certificate consumed by Mathlib's Height.logHeight_eval_ge with M = d − 1, N = d.

d ≥ 1; R commutative (no domain hypothesis).

Apply Polynomial.exists_mul_add_mul_eq_C_resultant to f = F₀(X, 1), g = F₁(X, 1) with formal degrees d, d (natDegree ≤ d by homogeneity): f·p + g·q = C(Res) with deg p, deg q < d. Homogenise to degree 2d − 1 = d + (d − 1): F₀·homogenize p (d−1) + F₁·homogenize q (d−1) = Res·X₁^{2d−1} (Polynomial.homogenize_mul, Polynomial.homogenize_eq_of_isHomogeneous, Polynomial.homogenize_C); this is the case k = 1. For k = 0 apply the case k = 1 to F∘σ with σ the swap of variables and substitute σ back; DY.0/resultant-precomp-linear gives Res(F∘σ) = det(σ)^{d²} Res(F) = (−1)^{d} Res(F), absorbed into the G_{0,j}. If Res ≠ 0 over a field and F₀(x) = F₁(x) = 0 then Res·x_k^{2d−1} = 0 for both k, so x = 0.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-resultant-of-a-rational-map); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/resultant-precomp-linear`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-resultant-precomp-linear); `mathlib:Polynomial.exists_mul_add_mul_eq_C_resultant`; `mathlib:Polynomial.homogenize_mul`; `mathlib:Polynomial.homogenize_eq_of_isHomogeneous`; `mathlib:Polynomial.homogenize_C`; `mathlib:Polynomial.isHomogeneous_homogenize`; `mathlib:Height.logHeight_eval_ge`.

([silverman-aws-2010](#source-parent-silverman-aws-2010), §4.1, p. 10, proof sketch of Theorem 12(a) — The certificate is the precise form of this relative primality, as Mathlib's lower height bound consumes it; [milnor-1993](#source-parent-milnor-1993), Appendix A, p. 40 (arXiv v1) — The nonvanishing direction of this criterion is the last step.)

**Endpoint checks.** F = (X₀², X₁²): Res = 1 and the certificate is X₀·X₀² + 0 = X₀³, 0 + X₁·X₁² = X₁³. F = (X₀² + 2X₁², X₀X₁): Res = 2 and 2X₁³ = X₁·(X₀² + 2X₁²) − X₀·(X₀X₁).

### 0.16 Homogeneous lifts of a degree-d self-map of ℙ¹

For a field K and d ∈ ℕ, HomogeneousLift K d is the type of pairs F = (F₀, F₁) of binary forms in K[X₀, X₁], homogeneous of degree d, not both zero, with Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁) ≠ 0. Evaluation F(x) = (F₀(x), F₁(x)) satisfies F(x) ≠ 0 for x ≠ 0 and F(cx) = c^d F(x). Constructors: scaling by c ∈ K^×, the identity (X₀, X₁), polynomial maps (Mathlib's toTupleMvPolynomial), invertible matrices (degree 1) and base change along field homomorphisms.

K a field. The condition 'not both zero' only matters for d = 0 (for d ≥ 1 it follows from Res ≠ 0). By DY.0/binary-resultant-eq-zero-iff, for d ≥ 1 the condition Res ≠ 0 says that F₀, F₁ have no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. no common factor.

Define the structure with fields forms, isHomogeneous, forms_ne_zero, binaryResultant_ne_zero. eval_ne_zero: by DY.0/resultant-certificate, Res·x_k^{2d−1} = Σ_j G_{k,j}(x)F_j(x) = 0 for both k if F(x) = 0, so x = 0 (d ≥ 1); for d = 0, F(x) = (F₀, F₁) ≠ 0. eval_smul: homogeneity (MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous gives F(cx) = c^d F(x)). ofPolynomial: Mathlib's toTupleMvPolynomial p is a pair of forms of degree natDegree p with resultant lead(p)^{natDegree p} (binaryResultant_toTupleMvPolynomial), nonzero for p ≠ 0, and equal to 1 for p = 0 (natDegree 0, pair (0, 1)). ofGL γ = (γ₀₀X₀ + γ₀₁X₁, γ₁₀X₀ + γ₁₁X₁) has resultant det γ ≠ 0 (the linear case of DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map). map σ: MvPolynomial.map σ preserves homogeneity (MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.map) and Res (Polynomial.resultant_map_map, σ injective).

### 0.17 Composition of homogeneous lifts

For lifts F of degree d and G of degree e over a field K, F ∘ G := (F₀(G₀, G₁), F₁(G₀, G₁)) (MvPolynomial.aeval G.forms) is a lift of degree d·e, with (F ∘ G)(x) = F(G(x)); composition is associative up to equality of forms, (X₀, X₁) is a two-sided unit, and scaling F scales F ∘ G.

K a field; F, G lifts of degrees d, e (any d, e ∈ ℕ).

Homogeneity: F_i(G₀, G₁) is homogeneous of degree e·d (MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.aeval); rewrite e·d = d·e. Nonvanishing: if some x ≠ 0 in K̄² were a common zero of F ∘ G, then y = G(x) ≠ 0 (DY.0/binary-resultant-eq-zero-iff for G over K̄) and F(y) = 0 (the same for F): a contradiction; so Res(F ∘ G) ≠ 0 by DY.0/binary-resultant-eq-zero-iff for d·e ≥ 1 (for d·e = 0 one of the lifts is constant and the composite is a nonzero constant pair). eval_comp: evaluation of aeval is composition (MvPolynomial.eval of aeval). Associativity and units: aeval is associative under substitution (MvPolynomial.bind₁ is a monad), aeval ![X₀, X₁] = id.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/homogeneous-lift`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-homogeneous-lift); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/binary-resultant-eq-zero-iff`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-binary-resultant-eq-zero-iff); `mathlib:MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.aeval`; `mathlib:MvPolynomial.aeval`; `mathlib:MvPolynomial.bind₁`; `mathlib:AlgebraicClosure`.

### 0.18 Rational self-maps of ℙ¹ over a field

For a field K, RationalMap K is the quotient of Σ_d HomogeneousLift K d by the relation 'same degree and proportional forms'. Its degree is the degree of any lift. Composition of lifts makes RationalMap K a monoid (unit: the class of (X₀, X₁)), with deg(f g) = deg f · deg g, so f^n is the n-th iterate as a map (not merely on points). Polynomial maps p ↦ z ↦ p(z) embed K[X] (under composition) via Mathlib's toTupleMvPolynomial, and f ↦ F₀(X, 1)/F₁(X, 1) ∈ RatFunc K is injective on the maps of positive degree. The total toRatFunc sends both constant 0 and constant ∞ to 0, so it is not injective on all maps.

K a field. Maps of degree 0 are the constants, one for each point of ℙ¹(K); Rat_d(K) is {f | deg f = d}.

Define the setoid on Σ_d HomogeneousLift K d and RationalMap K as its quotient; mk F is the class of F and degree is the first component (well defined). Monoid: mul on representatives is DY.0/homogeneous-lift-comp; well defined because (cF) ∘ G = c(F ∘ G) and F ∘ (cG) = c^d (F ∘ G) (homogeneity); associativity and units from the corresponding lift identities. ofPolynomial p is mk (HomogeneousLift.ofPolynomial p) (for p = 0 the lift (0, 1) is the constant 0); ofPolynomial (p ∘ q) = ofPolynomial p * ofPolynomial q because the composite of the lifts (homogenize p m, X₁^m) and (homogenize q n, X₁^n) is (homogenize (p ∘ q) (mn), X₁^{mn}) (Polynomial.homogenize_mul). toRatFunc f := F₀(X, 1)/F₁(X, 1) in RatFunc K (well defined on the class). For deg f ≥ 1, F₁(X, 1) ≠ 0 and Res ≠ 0 makes F₀(X, 1), F₁(X, 1) coprime with max(deg F₀(X, 1), deg F₁(X, 1)) = deg f, so f is recovered from the fraction; the constant map ∞ goes to Mathlib's junk value 0 = (1 : RatFunc K)/0, which is why injectivity is stated on {f | 1 ≤ deg f}.

([silverman-aws-2010](#source-parent-silverman-aws-2010), §2, p. 4 — The rational function of a map; our degree is the common degree d of the forms, equal to max{deg F, deg G} by the no-common-factor condition; [milnor-1993](#source-parent-milnor-1993), Appendix B, p. 40 (arXiv v1) — Rat_d is the set of lifts of degree d up to scaling, i.e. the degree-d part of RationalMap K; [levy-2011](#source-parent-levy-2011), §1, p. 1 (arXiv v2) — The same data for n = 1.)

- **`RationalMap.degree`** (projection): deg f ∈ ℕ.
- **`RationalMap.degree_mk`** (simp): deg (mk F) = d for F of degree d.

### 0.19 The action of a rational map on ℙ¹(K)

RationalMap.toEnd : RationalMap K →* Function.End (ℙ¹(K)) sends f = mk F to [x] ↦ [F(x)] on Mathlib's ℙ K (Fin 2 → K). It is a monoid homomorphism, so toEnd (f^n) = (toEnd f)^[n]. It is injective when K is infinite and not injective over finite fields.

K a field; ℙ¹(K) = Mathlib's Projectivization ℙ K (Fin 2 → K), with [x : 1] = mk ![x, 1] and ∞ = [1 : 0].

Well defined on points: F(x) ≠ 0 for x ≠ 0 (DY.0/homogeneous-lift, eval_ne_zero) and F(cx) = c^d F(x), so Projectivization.lift applies; scaling F does not change [F(x)] (Projectivization.mk_eq_mk_iff). Multiplicativity from (F ∘ G)(x) = F(G(x)) (DY.0/homogeneous-lift-comp); powers are iterates since Function.End's power is iteration. Injectivity for infinite K: if f, g of degrees d, e act identically then F₀G₁ − F₁G₀ vanishes on K², hence is 0 (MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.funext), so F₀G₁ = F₁G₀; as F₀, F₁ have no common factor (Res ≠ 0) the lifts are proportional and d = e. Over 𝔽_p, z^p fixes every point of ℙ¹(𝔽_p) (Fermat), so toEnd (z^p) = toEnd 1 while z^p ≠ 1.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-good-reduction-of-a-rational-map"></a>

### 0.20 Good reduction of a rational map

Let R be a valuation ring with fraction field K and residue field k. A rational map f over K has good reduction (over R) if it has a lift (F₀, F₁) with coefficients in R, at least one unit coefficient, and whose resultant Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁) is a unit of R. Its reduction f̃ is then the class over k of the reduced lift (F̃₀, F̃₁), a rational map of the same degree d.

R a valuation ring (e.g. ℤ_(p), ℤ_p, the valuation ring of a complete nonarchimedean field), K = Frac R, k = R/𝔪.

Define HasGoodReduction R f by the existence of an integral homogeneous lift with a unit coefficient and unit resultant. The normalization condition prevents the degree-zero pair from reducing to (0, 0); for positive degree it already follows from a unit resultant. Reduce a normalized integral lift coefficientwise. Its residue pair is nonzero because a unit coefficient survives, and its resultant is nonzero because it is the residue of a unit. Normalized lifts of the same map differ by an R-unit, so their reduced classes agree; the degree remains d. For a polynomial p of positive degree n, the standard lift is normalized because its second form is X₁^n, and its resultant is lead(p)^n. Thus good reduction is equivalent to a unit leading coefficient. Constants, including nonunits and zero, have good reduction via a normalized constant pair. Degree-one maps from GL₂(R): resultant det γ ∈ R^×.

### 0.21 Units of the monoid of rational maps: PGL₂

The units of RationalMap K are exactly the maps of degree 1, and unitsEquivPGL : (RationalMap K)ˣ ≃* PGL(2, K) (Mathlib's Matrix.ProjGenLinGroup) sends the class of the linear lift of γ ∈ GL₂(K) to the class of γ; the action of a unit on ℙ¹(K) is Mathlib's action of PGL(2, K) on ℙ K (Fin 2 → K).

K a field.

deg is multiplicative with deg 1 = 1, so a unit has degree 1; a degree-1 lift (a X₀ + b X₁, c X₀ + e X₁) has resultant ae − bc ≠ 0 (DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map, linear case), i.e. is ofGL of an invertible matrix, with inverse the class of ofGL γ⁻¹. The map GL₂(K) → (RationalMap K)ˣ, γ ↦ mk (ofGL γ) is a surjective homomorphism with kernel the scalars, which is the kernel of Matrix.ProjGenLinGroup.mk; this gives the MulEquiv. Compatibility with points: toEnd (mk (ofGL γ)) [x] = [γ x] = Projectivization.PGL.mk_smul_mk.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-rational-map-base-change"></a>

### 0.22 Base change of rational maps and points

For a field homomorphism σ : K → L, RationalMap.map σ : RationalMap K →* RationalMap L applies σ to the coefficients of a lift, and projMap σ : ℙ¹(K) → ℙ¹(L) applies σ to coordinates; both are injective, deg is preserved, and toEnd (map σ f) (projMap σ P) = projMap σ (toEnd f P). Over a field F algebraic over ℚ every rational map is the base change of a map over a number field L ⊆ F.

σ a ring homomorphism of fields (injective).

map on lifts is HomogeneousLift.map (DY.0/homogeneous-lift); it respects proportionality and composition (MvPolynomial.map commutes with aeval), giving a monoid homomorphism. projMap σ [x] = [σ x] via Projectivization.lift (σ injective keeps σ x ≠ 0); compatibility with toEnd because MvPolynomial.eval (σ ∘ x) (map σ F) = σ (eval x F). Field of definition: the finitely many coefficients of a lift generate L = ℚ(coefficients) (IntermediateField.adjoin), finite-dimensional because F is algebraic over ℚ (IntermediateField.finiteDimensional_adjoin); the lift has coefficients in L.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-good-reduction-iff-normalized-resultant-unit"></a>

### 0.23 Good reduction is read off a normalised lift

Let R be a valuation ring with fraction field K and f a rational map of degree d over K. For any integral lift F of f that is normalised (some coefficient is a unit of R): f has good reduction iff Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁) ∈ R^× iff the reduced forms F̃₀, F̃₁ over k have nonzero resultant (the reduction still has degree d).

R a valuation ring, K = Frac R; F integral and normalised.

Normalised lifts exist and are unique up to R^×: scale any lift by the inverse of a coefficient of minimal valuation (valuation ring property); two normalised lifts differ by c ∈ K^× with c and c^{-1} integral. For d ≥ 1, an integral lift c·F of a normalized lift has c ∈ R and resultant c^{2d}Res(F); this is a unit exactly when both c and Res(F) are units. For d = 0 the resultant is always 1, and the normalized nonzero constant pair directly supplies good reduction. IsUnit x ↔ residue x ≠ 0 in a local ring (IsLocalRing.residue_ne_zero_iff_isUnit), and the residue of Res(F) is the resultant of the reduced forms (Polynomial.resultant_map_map). For d ≥ 1, the reduced resultant is nonzero iff the reduced forms have no common zero over k̄ (DY.0/binary-resultant-eq-zero-iff), i.e. no common factor, i.e. the reduced map has degree d.

### 0.24 Reduction commutes with evaluation

Let R be a valuation ring with fraction field K and f a rational map with good reduction. For every P ∈ ℙ¹(K): projReduction (f(P)) = f̃(projReduction P).

R a valuation ring; f with good reduction.

Take an integral lift F with unit resultant and a representative x ∈ R² of P with a unit coordinate. F(x) ∈ R² reduces to F̃(x̃), which is nonzero because x̃ ≠ 0 and F̃ is a lift over k (DY.0/homogeneous-lift, eval_ne_zero); so F(x) has a unit coordinate and projReduction [F(x)] = [F̃(x̃)] (DY.0/reduction-of-points).

### 0.25 Conjugation of rational maps by PGL₂

PGL(2, K) acts on RationalMap K by γ • f = γ ∘ f ∘ γ⁻¹ (the action of the unit group through unitsEquivPGL and Mathlib's ConjAct); two maps are conjugate iff they are IsConj in the monoid RationalMap K. Conjugation preserves degree, intertwines the actions on ℙ¹(K) (toEnd (γ • f) ∘ γ = γ ∘ toEnd f), and on lifts is γ ∘ F ∘ adj(γ), whose resultant is det(γ)^{d²+d} Res(F). Convention: Silverman's and Rumely's f^γ = γ⁻¹ ∘ f ∘ γ is γ⁻¹ • f.

K a field.

Define the action as the pullback along unitsEquivPGL.symm of Mathlib's MulDistribMulAction of ConjAct (RationalMap K)ˣ on the monoid (ConjAct.units_smul_def). IsConj f g ↔ ∃ γ, γ • f = g by definition of IsConj (a unit c with c * f = g * c). Degree: deg (γ f γ⁻¹) = 1·d·1; points: toEnd is a monoid homomorphism (DY.0/rational-map-action-on-points) and units act by PGL(2, K) (DY.0/units-of-rational-maps). Lift formula: γ⁻¹ is the class of adj(γ); the resultant of the lift γ ∘ F ∘ adj(γ) is given by DY.0/resultant-conj (applied to adj γ, whose adjugate is γ). Preperiodic points correspond under the bijection γ of ℙ¹(K) (DY.0/preperiodic-of-semiconj).

### 0.26 Rational maps as endomorphisms of the scheme ℙ¹_K

For a field K there is an injective monoid homomorphism RationalMap K → End(ℙ¹_K) into the K-endomorphisms of the projective line ℙ¹_K = Proj K[X₀, X₁], sending mk F to the morphism [F₀ : F₁]; its action on K-points is RationalMap.toEnd and every K-endomorphism of ℙ¹_K is in the image. Hence f^n corresponds to the n-th power of a scheme morphism, and by DY.0/iterate-of-endomorphism-on-points iterate equality is equality of morphisms of schemes.

K a field; ℙ¹_K and the morphism attached to forms without common zero are supplied by SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0 (request).

Take the morphism [F₀ : F₁] of the supplier for each lift; proportional lifts give the same morphism, composites of forms give composites of morphisms, (X₀, X₁) gives the identity. Injectivity: two morphisms that agree agree on K̄-points, where they are toEnd of the base changes (DY.0/rational-map-base-change), which is injective since K̄ is infinite (DY.0/rational-map-action-on-points). The K-point compatibility is the supplier's description of [F₀ : F₁] on points; iterate statements follow from DY.0/iterate-of-endomorphism-on-points with T = Spec K. Surjectivity is the requested classification of K-endomorphisms of ℙ¹_K by a pair of sections of O(d) without a common zero. Use that supplier statement and pass its nonzero pair to the corresponding HomogeneousLift; it includes constant morphisms in degree zero.

### 0.27 Reduction commutes with composition and iteration

Let R be a valuation ring with fraction field K. If f and g have good reduction then so does f g, and (f g)~ = f̃ g̃; in particular f^n has good reduction and (f^n)~ = (f̃)^n.

R a valuation ring; f, g with good reduction.

Take integral lifts F, G with unit resultants. F ∘ G has integral coefficients and reduces to F̃ ∘ G̃ (reduction is a ring homomorphism, compatible with MvPolynomial.aeval). F̃ and G̃ have nonzero resultant over k, so F̃ ∘ G̃ is a lift over k (DY.0/homogeneous-lift-comp), i.e. its resultant — the residue of Res(F ∘ G) — is nonzero; hence Res(F ∘ G) is a unit (IsLocalRing.residue_ne_zero_iff_isUnit) and f g has good reduction with reduction mk(F̃ ∘ G̃) = f̃ g̃. Powers by induction.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-moduli-space-of-rational-maps"></a>

### 0.28 The moduli space M_d(K) of degree-d maps

For a field K and d ∈ ℕ, ModuliSpace K d is the set of conjugacy classes (Mathlib's ConjClasses of the monoid RationalMap K) of maps of degree d, i.e. Rat_d(K)/PGL₂(K). For d ≥ 2 and K algebraically closed it is the set of K-points of Silverman's geometric quotient M_d = Rat_d/SL₂ (whose scheme structure is recorded as a gap); for non-closed K it separates twists. Base change K → L induces M_d(K) → M_d(L).

K a field; no algebraic closedness in the definition. The scheme structure, affineness and dimension 2d − 2 for d ≥ 2 are separate GIT targets. Degree 0 and 1 here refer only to the orbit set; the degree-one GIT quotient does not separate all conjugacy classes.

Degree is a conjugacy invariant (DY.0/conjugacy-of-rational-maps), so it descends to ConjClasses (RationalMap K) (conjDegree); ModuliSpace K d is the fibre over d. mk f = mk g iff IsConj f g (ConjClasses.mk_eq_mk_iff_isConj); every class has a representative. Base change: IsConj is preserved by the monoid homomorphism map σ (DY.0/rational-map-base-change).

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-fixed-points-of-a-rational-map"></a>

### 0.29 The fixed points of a rational map, with multiplicity

For f = mk F of degree d, the fixed-point form is X₁F₀ − X₀F₁ (degree d + 1), and fixedPoints f := binaryRoots (d + 1) (X₁F₀ − X₀F₁). For d ≥ 2 the form is nonzero, P ∈ fixedPoints f iff toEnd f P = P, the multiset has d + 1 elements over an algebraically closed field, and conjugation transports it: fixedPoints (γ • f) = γ · fixedPoints f.

K a field; d ≥ 2 for the nonvanishing of the form (for the identity map the form is 0).

Well defined on the class: scaling F scales the form (DY.0/roots-of-a-binary-form, binaryRoots_smul). Nonvanishing for d ≥ 2: if X₁F₀ = X₀F₁ then X₀ | F₀ and X₁ | F₁ with F₀ = X₀H, F₁ = X₁H, and H of degree d − 1 ≥ 1 is a common factor, contradicting Res ≠ 0 (DY.0/binary-resultant-eq-zero-iff). Membership: [x] is fixed iff F(x) is proportional to x iff x₁F₀(x) − x₀F₁(x) = 0 (DY.0/roots-of-a-binary-form, mem_binaryRoots_iff). Conjugation: the fixed-point form of γ ∘ F ∘ adj(γ) is the fixed-point form of F composed with adj(γ) (the 2 × 2 determinant det[y, γF(adj(γ)y)] with y = γx/det γ), whose roots are γ applied to those of F.

- **`RationalMap.card_fixedPoints`** (other): Over an algebraically closed field, deg f ≥ 2: d + 1 fixed points with multiplicity.
- **`RationalMap.fixedPoints_smul`** (functoriality): fixedPoints (γ • f) = (fixedPoints f).map (γ • ·).

**Checks.**

- **`TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics.RationalMap.fixedPoints_translation`** (degenerate): z ↦ z + 1 has the single fixed point ∞ with multiplicity 2.
- **`TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics.RationalMap.fixedPoints_sq_add_one`** (non-example): Over ℚ, fixedPoints (z² + 1) = {∞}: the K-points of the multiset miss the irrational fixed points.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-critical-points-of-a-rational-map"></a>

### 0.30 The critical points of a rational map, with multiplicity

For f = mk F of degree d, the Jacobian form Jac(F) = ∂₀F₀·∂₁F₁ − ∂₁F₀·∂₀F₁ is a binary form of degree 2d − 2, and criticalPoints f := binaryRoots (2d − 2) (Jac F). In characteristic 0 and d ≥ 1, at a finite point [z : 1] with F₁(z, 1) ≠ 0 membership is equivalent to f'(z) = 0. In characteristic 0 and d ≥ 1 there are 2d − 2 critical points with multiplicity over an algebraically closed field (Riemann–Hurwitz), each of multiplicity at most d − 1; conjugation transports them.

K a field; the affine derivative and ramification interpretations below require characteristic 0 and positive degree. In characteristic p the Jacobian can vanish even for separable degree-p maps (for example z^p + z), so this total definition is not the critical divisor in that generality.

Jac(cF) = c² Jac(F), so the roots depend only on f (DY.0/roots-of-a-binary-form, binaryRoots_smul); Jac(F) is homogeneous of degree 2(d − 1) (MvPolynomial.pderiv lowers degree by 1). Affine characterisation: with f_i = F_i(X, 1), Euler's identity z∂₀F_i + ∂₁F_i = d F_i at (z, 1) gives Jac(F)(z, 1) = d·(f₀'f₁ − f₀f₁')(z); in characteristic 0, for F₁(z, 1) ≠ 0 the point is critical iff the derivative of f₀/f₁ vanishes at z. Nonvanishing and count in characteristic 0: f₁ ≠ 0 (otherwise F₁ = 0 and Res = 0), and d·f₁²·(f₀/f₁)' ≠ 0 because a map of degree d ≥ 1 is not constant; so Jac(F) ≠ 0 and it has 2d − 2 roots (card_binaryRoots). Conjugation: Jac(γ ∘ F ∘ adj γ) = det(γ)^2 · (Jac F) ∘ adj(γ) by the chain rule, so criticalPoints (γ • f) = γ · criticalPoints f; chain rule for composites gives the critical points of f ∘ g.

- **`RationalMap.criticalPoints_smul`** (functoriality): criticalPoints (γ • f) = (criticalPoints f).map (γ • ·).
- **`RationalMap.count_criticalPoints_le`** (other): Characteristic 0: each critical point has multiplicity ≤ d − 1.
- **`RationalMap.mk_one_mem_criticalPoints_iff`** (characterisation): Characteristic 0, d ≥ 1: at [x : 1] with F₁(x, 1) ≠ 0, critical iff (f₀'f₁ − f₀f₁')(x) = 0 for f_i = F_i(X, 1).
- **`RationalMap.mem_criticalPoints_mul_iff`** (relation): Chain rule: P is critical for f ∘ g iff P is critical for g or g(P) is critical for f.

- **`TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics.RationalMap.criticalPoints_milnor`** (compatibility): For Milnor's normal form, [ω : 1] is critical iff μ₂ω² + 2ω + μ₁ = 0.

### 0.31 Conjugation by GL₂(R) preserves good reduction

Let R be a valuation ring with fraction field K and γ ∈ GL₂(R). Then γ • f has good reduction iff f does.

γ with entries in R and det γ ∈ R^×.

If F is an integral lift with unit resultant, γ ∘ F ∘ adj(γ) is integral and is a lift of γ • f (DY.0/conjugacy-of-rational-maps, smul_mk), with resultant det(γ)^{d²+d} Res(F) (DY.0/resultant-conj), a unit. The converse applies the same to γ⁻¹ ∈ GL₂(R).

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-fixed-point-multiplier"></a>

### 0.32 The multiplier of a rational map at a fixed point

For f with lift F and a fixed point P: if P = [z : 1] then μ_P(f) = f'(z), the derivative at z of the rational function F₀(X, 1)/F₁(X, 1) (F₁(z, 1) ≠ 0 at a finite fixed point); if P = ∞ then μ_∞(f) = μ_0(ι • f) with ι(z) = 1/z. Coordinate-free (all characteristics): if F(x) = c·x with c ≠ 0 then μ_{[x]}(f) = (∂₀F₀(x) + ∂₁F₁(x))/c − d. The value at a non-fixed point is unspecified (junk).

K a field; P fixed by f for the value to be meaningful.

Finite fixed point: with f(z) = F₀(z,1)/F₁(z,1) and F₁(z, 1) ≠ 0 (since f(z) = z is finite), μ = (F₀'F₁ − F₀F₁')(z)/F₁(z, 1)² (Polynomial.derivative). At ∞ use the unit ι = [z ↦ 1/z] of DY.0/units-of-rational-maps and the finite formula for ι • f at 0. Trace formula: Euler's identity x₀∂₀F_i + x₁∂₁F_i = d F_i for forms of degree d (MvPolynomial.pderiv) gives, at a finite fixed point [z : 1] with F(z, 1) = c(z, 1), ∂₀F₀ − z∂₀F₁ = tr DF − dc, and f'(z) = (∂₀F₀ − z∂₀F₁)/c. Polynomial maps: μ_{[z:1]} = p'(z); μ_∞ = 0 when deg p ≥ 2 (ι • p = 1/p(1/w) = w^n/(...) vanishes to order n at 0). For a fixed point of a map of degree at least 2, μ_P = 1 iff P is a multiple root of the nonzero fixed-point form: its chart derivative is c(μ_P − 1). The identity is excluded, since its fixed-point form is zero and fixedPoints returns the empty multiset.

### 0.33 Critically marked maps and their moduli M_d^cm(K)

A critically marked map of degree d is (f, c) with deg f = d and c : Fin (2d − 2) → ℙ¹(K) listing criticalPoints f with multiplicity; PGL(2, K) acts on (f, c) by γ • (f, c) = (γ • f, γ ∘ c), and CriticallyMarkedModuliSpace K d is the orbit quotient. The forgetful map to M_d(K) is surjective over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, and its fibres are the orbits of the relabelling action of Sym(2d − 2).

K a field; the finite branched cover M_d^cm → M_d of DeMarco–Mavraki–Ye carrying a universal family is scheme-level and belongs to the geometric-invariant-theory gap.

Define CriticallyMarkedMap K d as the subtype and the action through DY.0/conjugacy-of-rational-maps and DY.0/critical-points-of-a-rational-map (criticalPoints_smul keeps the marking valid). Quotient by MulAction.orbitRel; forget (f, c) = mk f is well defined. Surjectivity: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 the multiset has 2d − 2 elements (card_criticalPoints), so it can be listed. Fibres: two markings of the same f differ by a permutation; conjugacies of the map act compatibly.

### 0.34 Multipliers are conjugation invariant

For γ ∈ PGL(2, K), f a rational map and P a fixed point of f: μ_{γ•P}(γ • f) = μ_P(f).

P fixed by f (then γP is fixed by γ • f).

Use the trace formula with G = γ ∘ F ∘ adj(γ), t = det(γ) and y = γx. Homogeneity gives G(y) = t^d·c·y and DG(y) = t^{d−1}·γ·DF(x)·adj(γ). Its trace is t^d·tr DF(x), so the trace divided by the eigenvalue, and hence the multiplier, is unchanged. Degree zero has zero derivatives and multiplier zero. Alternatively in charts: the derivative of γ ∘ f ∘ γ⁻¹ at γ(z) equals f'(z) by the chain rule (Polynomial.derivative_comp) when both points are finite.

### 0.35 Milnor's normal forms for quadratic maps

Let K be algebraically closed of characteristic 0 and f of degree 2 over K. Either f has two distinct fixed points and is conjugate to z(z + μ₁)/(μ₂z + 1) with μ₁μ₂ ≠ 1, μ₁ and μ₂ the multipliers at 0 and ∞; or f has a single fixed point and is conjugate to z + 1/z. In the first case the normal form is determined by (μ₁, μ₂).

K algebraically closed of characteristic 0; deg f = 2.

Two distinct fixed points: move them to 0 and ∞ by a unit (DY.0/units-of-rational-maps, 2-transitivity of PGL₂ on ℙ¹, Mathlib's generalLinearGroup_is_two_pretransitive); then f(z) = z(az + b)/(cz + e) with a ≠ 0, e ≠ 0, ae − bc ≠ 0; scale the lift so that e = 1 and conjugate by z ↦ kz to make a = 1. Read off μ₀ = b and μ_∞ = c from DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier; the condition Res ≠ 0 is 1 − bc ≠ 0. One fixed point: move it to ∞ and its preimage other than ∞ to 0, so f = p(z)/z with f(z) − z = (p(z) − z²)/z having no finite zero, hence f = z + c/z with c ≠ 0; conjugating by z ↦ √c z (characteristic ≠ 2, K closed) gives z + 1/z.

### 0.36 Milnor: M₂^cm is the surface A³(A − 1) = BC

There is a bijection M₂^cm(K) ≅ {(A, B, C) ∈ K³ : A³(A − 1) = BC}, given on the critical point normal form (αz² + β)/(γz² + δ) with αδ − βγ = 1 (critical points marked 0, ∞) by A = αδ, B = α³β, C = γδ³; the relabelling (ω₁, ω₂) ↦ (ω₂, ω₁) corresponds to (A, B, C) ↦ (A, C, B).

## Layer 1: Canonical heights

Tate’s elementary limiting argument is the common engine. Separate the projective-line construction on native height carriers from the general-variety and divisorial-eigenclass endpoints, which require RP.0. Zero height implies preperiodicity only with the stated Northcott and field hypotheses.

Planets: Tate's limit; Canonical height on ℙ¹; Call–Silverman canonical height; Zero canonical height iff preperiodic; Northcott for preperiodic points; Canonical height of a divisorial eigenclass.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-1-tate-limit"></a>

### 1.1 Tate's limit of a height along a self-map

For a set S, a self-map φ : S → S, a function h : S → ℝ and α ∈ ℝ, tateLimit φ h α P := lim_{n→∞} h(φⁿ(P))/αⁿ, defined as Mathlib's limUnder along atTop. When α > 1 and h ∘ φ − αh is bounded the limit exists (DY.1/tate-limit-tendsto); the value then depends on h only up to bounded functions, is linear in h, and is unchanged when (φ, α) is replaced by (φ^k, α^k).

S any type; α real; the junk value of limUnder is never used by the theorems, which all assume α > 1 and the bound |h(φQ) − αh(Q)| ≤ C for all Q ∈ S (Call–Silverman (3)).

Define tateLimit as Filter.limUnder atTop (n ↦ h(φ^[n] P)/α^n). tateLimit_congr_of_bounded: if h' − h is bounded by B, then h' satisfies the hypothesis with constant C + (α + 1)B and tateLimit φ h' α satisfies (i) and (ii) of DY.1/tate-limit-unique for h, hence equals tateLimit φ h α. tateLimit_const_mul and tateLimit_iterate: the sequences for c·h and for (φ^k, α^k) are c times, respectively a subsequence of, the sequence for (φ, h, α) (Filter.Tendsto.const_mul, Filter.Tendsto.comp). tateLimit_nonneg: a limit of nonnegative terms (le_of_tendsto).

*Needs:* `mathlib:Filter.limUnder`; `mathlib:Filter.Tendsto.const_mul`; `mathlib:Filter.Tendsto.comp`; `mathlib:le_of_tendsto`.

([call-silverman-1993](#source-parent-call-silverman-1993), §1, Proposition 1.2, (4), p. 169 — The defining limit, for h = h_{V,η}; [silverman-ads-sample](#source-parent-silverman-ads-sample), §3.4, Theorem 3.20, p. 97 — The abstract setting on a set S used here.)

The reusable interface consists of the following statements.

- **`tateLimit`** (data): tateLimit φ h α : S → ℝ.
- **`tateLimit_def`** (characterisation): tateLimit φ h α P = limUnder atTop (n ↦ h(φⁿ P)/αⁿ).
- **`tateLimit_congr_of_bounded`** (relation): α > 1, h ∘ φ − αh bounded and h' − h bounded ⇒ tateLimit φ h' α = tateLimit φ h α.
- **`tateLimit_const_mul`** (relation): tateLimit φ (c · h) α = c · tateLimit φ h α.
- **`tateLimit_iterate`** (relation): tateLimit φ^[k] h (α^k) = tateLimit φ h α for k ≥ 1.

### 1.2 Tate's telescoping estimate

Let α > 1 and C ≥ 0 with |h(φQ) − αh(Q)| ≤ C for all Q ∈ S (Call–Silverman (3)). Then for every P ∈ S and m ≤ n: |h(φⁿP)/αⁿ − h(φᵐP)/αᵐ| ≤ C/((α − 1)αᵐ).

α > 1. |h(φQ) − αh(Q)| ≤ C for all Q ∈ S (Call–Silverman (3)).

Telescoping: h(φⁿP)/αⁿ − h(φᵐP)/αᵐ = Σ_{i=m+1}^{n} α^{−i}(h(φQ_i) − αh(Q_i)) with Q_i = φ^{i−1}P (Function.iterate_succ_apply'). Triangle inequality (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs) and the hypothesis bound each term by Cα^{−i}. Σ_{i=m+1}^{n} α^{−i} ≤ Σ_{i>m} α^{−i} = α^{−m}/(α − 1) (geom_sum_eq).

*Needs:* `mathlib:Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs`; `mathlib:geom_sum_eq`; `mathlib:Function.iterate_succ_apply'`.

### 1.3 The absolute logarithmic Weil height on ℙ¹

For a field F of characteristic 0, projLineAbsLogHeight : ℙ¹(F) → ℝ is h([x₀ : x₁]) = absLogHeight₁(x₀/x₁) if x₁ ≠ 0 and h([1 : 0]) = 0, where absLogHeight₁ is Mathlib's absolute logarithmic Weil height of a field element (junk value 0 at transcendental elements). It is nonnegative, invariant under x ↦ 1/x and under field embeddings, and on a number field K equals Mathlib's relative Projectivization.logHeight divided by [K : ℚ].

F of characteristic 0; the values are meaningful at points with algebraic coordinates (F algebraic over ℚ in every theorem that uses them).

Well defined on ℙ¹: scaling (x₀, x₁) by t ≠ 0 does not change x₀/x₁ or the vanishing of x₁ (Projectivization.lift). Nonnegativity: absLogHeight₁ = log absMulHeight₁ with absMulHeight₁ ≥ 1 (a power of Mathlib's mulHeight₁ ≥ 1, or the junk 1). Inversion: absLogHeight₁(1/x) = absLogHeight₁(x) (Height.logHeight₁ of an inverse is unchanged, Mathlib's logHeight₁_inv, transported by DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/abs-mul-height-eq-rpow). Embeddings: DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/abs-mul-height-eq-of-minpoly-eq (conjugate elements have equal absolute height).

### 1.5 Mathlib's height-bound constant under finite extension

Let K ⊆ L be number fields and p : ι' → MvPolynomial ι K a finite family. Then Height.mulHeightBound (map (algebraMap K L) ∘ p) = Height.mulHeightBound p ^ [L : K]. Consequently the normalised constants log max(mulHeightBound p, 1)/[K : ℚ] do not depend on the number field in which they are computed.

K ⊆ L number fields (an algebra K → L), heights relative to NumberField.instAdmissibleAbsValues.

mulHeightBound is the product over archimedean places (with multiplicity) of max_j Σ_s |coeff_s p_j|_v and over finite places of max_j max(max_s |coeff_s p_j|_v, 1); mapping the coefficients to L does not change the supports (MvPolynomial.support_map_of_injective, MvPolynomial.coeff_map). Archimedean part: for w | v, w(σc) = v(c) (NumberField.InfinitePlace.comap_apply); regroup by DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/infinite-places-over (Σ_{w|v} mult w = mult v·[L:K]); rewrite the multiset products by NumberField.prod_archAbsVal_eq. Finite part: for P | p, |σc|_P = |c|_p^{e(P|p) f(P|p)} (NumberField.FinitePlace.equivHeightOneSpectrum_symm_apply_algebraMap), maxima commute with the power, and Σ_{P|p} e f = [L : K] (Ideal.sum_ramification_inertia_eq_finrank). Multiply the two parts; take logarithms and divide by [L : ℚ] = [L : K][K : ℚ] (Module.finrank_mul_finrank). The finite-place rank is the field degree: use the finite flat ring-of-integers extension and rank comparison in DT.0/mul-height-algebra-map, rather than identifying the two ranks without justification.

### 1.17 Northcott's theorem for preperiodic points of a rational map

Let F be algebraic over ℚ and f a rational map over F of degree ≥ 2. (a) There is C with h(P) ≤ C for every preperiodic P ∈ ℙ¹(F). (b) For every number field K, a map over K has finitely many preperiodic points in ℙ¹(K). (c) For every D, the set of x ∈ F with [x : 1] preperiodic and deg minpoly_ℚ x ≤ D is finite.

F algebraic over ℚ; deg f ≥ 2.

(a) DY.1/height-bound-of-preperiodic with the constant of DY.1/absolute-height-estimate-for-rational-map. (b) Over K, preperiodic points have relative height ≤ [K : ℚ]·C (DY.1/weil-height-eq-log-height-div-finrank) and DY.1/northcott-on-the-projective-line applies. (c) Embed F into ℂ (IsAlgClosed.lift, ℂ algebraically closed); the absolute height and the degree are preserved (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/abs-mul-height-eq-of-minpoly-eq), and algebraic numbers of bounded degree and height form a finite set (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/northcott-absolute-height).

### 1.18 Tate's limit is transported along semiconjugacies

Let π : S → T with π ∘ φ = ψ ∘ π (Function.Semiconj π φ ψ), α > 1, h : S → ℝ and k : T → ℝ with h ∘ φ − αh and k ∘ ψ − αk bounded, and k ∘ π − h bounded. Then tateLimit ψ k α ∘ π = tateLimit φ h α.

α > 1; the three boundedness hypotheses.

g := tateLimit ψ k α ∘ π satisfies g ∘ φ = (tateLimit ψ k α) ∘ ψ ∘ π = αg (DY.1/tate-limit-functional-equation for ψ, k). g − h = (tateLimit ψ k α − k) ∘ π + (k ∘ π − h) is bounded (DY.1/tate-limit-error-bound). Conclude by DY.1/tate-limit-unique.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-1-canonical-height"></a>

### 1.19 Call–Silverman canonical height of a polarized morphism

Let K be a number field, V/K a smooth projective variety, φ : V → V a morphism and L an ample line bundle on V with φ*L ≅ L^{⊗d} for an integer d ≥ 2, and let h_L : V(K̄) → ℝ be a Weil height for L. Then ĥ_{V,φ,L}(P) = lim d^{−n} h_L(φⁿP) exists for every P ∈ V(K̄), |ĥ_{V,φ,L} − h_L| ≤ c/(d − 1) where c bounds |h_L ∘ φ − d h_L|, ĥ_{V,φ,L} ∘ φ = d·ĥ_{V,φ,L}, ĥ_{V,φ,L} is the unique function with ĥ − h_L bounded and ĥ ∘ φ = dĥ, and it does not depend on the choice of the Weil height h_L.

K a number field; V smooth projective over K; φ a morphism over K; L ample with φ*L ≅ L^{⊗d}, d ≥ 2. The Weil height machine for line bundles on V (functoriality, additivity, dependence on the isomorphism class) is supplied by HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions:RP.0 (request).

Height machine (RP.0): h_L ∘ φ = h_{φ*L} + O(1) = h_{L^{⊗d}} + O(1) = d·h_L + O(1); this is Call–Silverman (2), the hypothesis of Tate's lemma with α = d. Existence, bound, functional equation: DY.1/tate-limit-tendsto, DY.1/tate-limit-error-bound, DY.1/tate-limit-functional-equation applied to (V(K̄), φ, h_L, d). Uniqueness: DY.1/tate-limit-unique. Independence of h_L: two Weil heights for L differ by a bounded function (RP.0), so the limits agree (tateLimit_congr_of_bounded, a consequence of DY.1/tate-limit-unique).

### 1.20 The Tate limit of doubling on an elliptic curve and Tau Ceti's canonical height

Let F be a field with Height.AdmissibleAbsValues, W an elliptic curve over F and h the naive height of the x-coordinate (Tau Ceti's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.naiveHeight). Then tateLimit (Q ↦ 2•Q) h 4 = 2·canonicalHeight (Tau Ceti's Point.canonicalHeight), and for every integer m ≥ 2, tateLimit (Q ↦ m•Q) h m² = 2·canonicalHeight. Normalisation: Call–Silverman's ĥ_{E,[m],η} for η the class of 2(O), with h_{2(O)} = h, is twice Tau Ceti's canonical height, which is the Néron–Tate height for (O); points of Tate limit 0 are exactly the torsion points under Northcott for the field height.

F with admissible absolute values and decidable equality (Tau Ceti's group law); W elliptic.

(2 • ·)^[n] P = 2^n • P (smul_iterate); Tau Ceti's Point.tendsto_naiveHeight_two_pow_nsmul_div_four_pow says h(2^nP)/(2·4^n) → canonicalHeight P, so h(2^nP)/4^n → 2·canonicalHeight P (Filter.Tendsto.const_mul) and tateLimit returns this limit (Filter.Tendsto.limUnder_eq). Zero set: Point.canonicalHeight_eq_zero_iff_isOfFinAddOrder (Northcott transferred from the field height by Tau Ceti's instance).

### 1.21 The relative canonical height of a rational map

For a field K with Height.AdmissibleAbsValues (a global height field) and a rational map f over K, relCanonicalHeight f := tateLimit (toEnd f) Projectivization.logHeight (deg f) on ℙ¹(K). For deg f ≥ 2 it is the unique function with ĥ − h bounded and ĥ ∘ f = (deg f)·ĥ; it is nonnegative, vanishes at preperiodic points, is invariant under iteration and conjugation, and scales by [L : K] under an extension of number fields.

K with admissible absolute values; the properties need deg f ≥ 2.

Iteration: tateLimit_iterate with toEnd (f^n) = (toEnd f)^[n]; conjugation: DY.1/tate-limit-semiconj with the bounded function logHeight ∘ γ − logHeight (the degree-one case of the height estimate). Extension of number fields: Projectivization.logHeight over L of a K-point is [L : K] times that over K (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/mul-height-algebra-map), and tateLimit_const_mul.

<a id="dy-2"></a>
## Layer 2: Local heights, Julia sets and canonical measures

Build escape rates, local heights and canonical measures before identifying support. The classical and Berkovich stability definitions use different carriers and topologies. The transfer proof, the entropy upper bound and uniqueness among maximal-entropy invariant measures are separate routes. Good reduction, inseparable maps and the period-exponent constants provide independent checks.

Planets: Homogeneous escape rate; Local decomposition of the canonical height; Periods of points under good reduction; Canonical measure; Fatou and Julia sets; Canonical measure and Julia support.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-lift-norm-upper-bound"></a>

### 2.1 Upper bound ‖F(x)‖_v ≤ C_v ‖x‖_v^d for a lift

Let F = (F₀, F₁) be a pair of binary forms of degree d over a field K and v an absolute value on K. Put C_v(F) = max_i Σ_m v(coeff_m F_i) (sum over the monomials of F_i) and, when v is nonarchimedean, C_v(F) = max_{i,m} v(coeff_m F_i). Then ‖F(x)‖_v ≤ C_v(F)·‖x‖_v^d for every x ∈ K². In particular, if v is nonarchimedean and every coefficient of F lies in the valuation ring (v ≤ 1 on the coefficients), then ‖F(x)‖_v ≤ ‖x‖_v^d.

F₀, F₁ homogeneous of the same degree d v an absolute value on K (archimedean or not)

Apply Mathlib's AbsoluteValue.eval_mvPolynomial_le (archimedean form: v(p(x)) ≤ (Σ_m v(coeff_m p))·(⨆ i, v(x i))^N for p homogeneous of degree N) to F₀ and F₁ and take the maximum. For v nonarchimedean use IsNonarchimedean.eval_mvPolynomial_le instead, which gives the constant ⨆_m v(coeff_m p). If all coefficients are v-integral the nonarchimedean constant is ≤ 1.

*Needs:* `mathlib:AbsoluteValue.eval_mvPolynomial_le`; `mathlib:IsNonarchimedean.eval_mvPolynomial_le`; `mathlib:MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous`; [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-rational-map-of-the-projective-line).

### 2.2 The homogeneous escape rate G_{F,v}

Conventions (pinned for the whole layer): K is a field and v : K → ℝ an absolute value (Mathlib's AbsoluteValue K ℝ); for x = (x₀, x₁) ∈ K², ‖x‖_v = max(v(x₀), v(x₁)) (Mathlib's ⨆ i, v (x i)). A lift of a rational map f of degree d is a pair F = (F₀, F₁) of binary forms of degree d with Res(F) ≠ 0 (DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line, DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map); f([x₀ : x₁]) = [F₀(x) : F₁(x)], the affine coordinate is z ↔ [z : 1], ∞ = [1 : 0], and Fⁿ is the n-fold composite, a lift of fⁿ of degree dⁿ. The (homogeneous) escape rate of F at v is G_{F,v}(x) = lim_{n→∞} d^{−n}·log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖_v for x ∈ K² ∖ {0} (d ≥ 2); by DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto the limit exists. It is defined at every absolute value, archimedean or not, without completeness of K; for a place v of a number field K it is taken with the absolute value v itself (Mathlib's InfinitePlace, resp. normalised FinitePlace).

d ≥ 2 Res(F) ≠ 0 x ≠ 0 (the formula is extended by the junk value of limUnder at x = 0)

Define G_{F,v}(x) as the limit (limUnder along atTop) of the real sequence d^{−n}·log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖_v. Existence of the limit, the uniform rate and every transformation rule are separate nodes (DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto and following).
