([demarco-krieger-ye-2020](#source-parent-demarco-krieger-ye-2020), (2.3), §2.2, p. 7 (arXiv v2; the norm is misprinted, see ArithmeticDynamics/E301) — The escape rate of the Lattès lift F_t; the node is the same construction for an arbitrary lift F of degree d; [baker-rumely-2006](#source-parent-baker-rumely-2006), §3.1, p. 8 (arXiv v2) — Baker–Rumely's homogeneous local dynamical height is G_{F,v} (with their normalised |·|_v; see the API item escapeRate_rpow_abv).)

The reusable interface consists of the following statements.

- **`escapeRate`** (data): For v an absolute value on K, a lift F of degree d and x ∈ K², escapeRate v F x = lim_{n→∞} d^{−n}·log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖_v (defined through limUnder; DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto shows the limit exists for x ≠ 0 and d ≥ 2).
- **`escapeRate_tendsto`** (characterisation): d ≥ 2, Res F ≠ 0, x ≠ 0 ⟹ d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖_v → escapeRate v F x (node DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto).
- **`escapeRate_apply_lift`** (relation): escapeRate v F (F x) = d · escapeRate v F x (node DY.2/escape-rate-functional-equation).
- **`escapeRate_smul`** (relation): escapeRate v F (a • x) = escapeRate v F x + log (v a) for a ≠ 0 (node DY.2/escape-rate-homogeneity).
- **`escapeRate_const_smul_lift`** (relation): escapeRate v (c • F) x = escapeRate v F x + log (v c)/(d − 1) for c ≠ 0 (node DY.2/escape-rate-scale-lift).
- **`escapeRate_iterate_lift`** (relation): If G is a lift of degree dᵐ (m ≥ 1) with G.eval = (F.eval)^[m], then escapeRate v G x = escapeRate v F x (node DY.2/escape-rate-iterate-lift).
- **`escapeRate_conj`** (relation): For A ∈ GL₂(K) and a lift G with G.eval y = A⁻¹·F.eval(A·y) (a lift of the conjugate map): escapeRate v G x = escapeRate v F (A·x) (node DY.2/escape-rate-conjugation).
- **`escapeRate_abs_sub_log_norm_le`** (other): There is C with |escapeRate v F x − log ‖x‖_v| ≤ C for all x ≠ 0; explicitly log c_v(F)/(d − 1) ≤ escapeRate v F x − log ‖x‖_v ≤ log C_v(F)/(d − 1) (node DY.2/escape-rate-sub-log-norm-bounds).
- **`escapeRate_algebraMap`** (compatibility): For a field extension L/K and an absolute value w on L restricting to v, escapeRate w (F.map (algebraMap K L)) (algebraMap x) = escapeRate v F x (node DY.2/escape-rate-base-change).
- **`escapeRate_comp_ringEquiv`** (compatibility): For σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L and absolute values w, w′ on L with w′ = w ∘ σ: escapeRate w′ F y = escapeRate w F (σ ∘ y) for F defined over K: the escape rate is Galois-equivariant (used for the Galois-averaged decomposition of DeMarco–Krieger–Ye (2.3)).
- **`escapeRate_rpow_abv`** (compatibility): For 0 < s ≤ 1 (so that v^s is again an absolute value), escapeRate (v^s) F x = s · escapeRate v F x; this converts between the normalised absolute values of Mathlib's places and the standard ones |·|_p used by DeMarco–Krieger–Ye.
- **`continuous_escapeRate`** (instance): For E a normed field and v its norm (NormedField.toAbsoluteValue), escapeRate is continuous on E² ∖ {0} (node DY.2/escape-rate-continuous).
- **`escapeRate_nonpos_iff`** (characterisation): escapeRate v F x ≤ 0 ⟺ the orbit (Fⁿ(x))ₙ is bounded (node DY.2/escape-rate-nonpos-iff-bounded-orbit).
- **`escapeRate_monomial`** (example): For F = (X₀^d, X₁^d), escapeRate v F x = log ‖x‖_v at every absolute value v.

**Checks.**

- **`escapeRate_powerMap`** (computation): For F = (X₀², X₁²) over ℚ and v = |·|_∞: escapeRate v F (3, 1) = log 3 and escapeRate v F (1, 1) = 0.
- **`escapeRate_padicCantor_zero`** (computation): For p prime, F = (X₀^p − X₀X₁^{p−1}, pX₁^p) over ℚ and v = |·|_p: escapeRate v F (0, 1) = −(log p)/(p − 1); the one-step value (1/p)·log ‖F(0, 1)‖_p = −(log p)/p is different, so the limit is not the first term.
- **`escapeRate_goodReduction_degenerate`** (degenerate): For F = (X₀² − X₀X₁ − X₁², X₁²) and any prime p, escapeRate |·|_p F x = log ‖x‖_p for every x ∈ ℚ² ∖ {0}.
- **`escapeRate_monicPolynomial_compat`** (compatibility): For a polynomial map f(z) = z² + c over ℂ with lift F = (X₀² + cX₁², X₁²): escapeRate |·| F (z, 1) = lim 2^{−n} log max(|fⁿ(z)|, 1), the Green function of the filled Julia set; for c = 0 this is Real.posLog |z|.
- **`escapeRate_depends_on_lift`** (non-example): The escape rate depends on the lift, not only on f: with F = (X₀², X₁²) and 2F, escapeRate |·|_∞ (2F) x = escapeRate |·|_∞ F x + log 2 ≠ escapeRate |·|_∞ F x.
- **`escapeRate_nonmonic_polynomial_orbit`** (non-example): For p = 2, F = (X₀² − X₀X₁, 2X₁²) and z ∈ ℂ₂ with z² = 2: the polynomial orbit under (z² − z)/2 is unbounded, but G_F(z,1) = −log 2/4 < 0. The sublevel criterion concerns F-orbits in two dimensions.

**Endpoint checks.** G_{F,v} = log ‖·‖_v for F = (X₀^d, X₁^d) at every v. For the (z^p − z)/p lift at p, G(0, 1) = −(log p)/(p − 1).

### 2.3 Periodic points reduce to periodic points with dividing period

Setting: v is a nonarchimedean absolute value on K with valuation ring 𝒪 = {a : v(a) ≤ 1}, maximal ideal 𝔪 = {a : v(a) < 1} and residue field k = 𝒪/𝔪 (Mathlib's ValuationSubring and IsLocalRing.ResidueField), a ↦ ã the residue map; p = char k ≥ 0 is the residue characteristic. A lift F is normalised if its coefficients lie in 𝒪 and one of them is a unit; f has good reduction at v when v(Res F) = 1 for a normalised lift (DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map), and then f̃ = [F̃₀ : F̃₁] is a rational map over k of the same degree d. If f has good reduction at v and P ∈ ℙ¹(K) is periodic for f of exact period n, then red(P) is periodic for f̃ of exact period m dividing n. Preperiodic points reduce to preperiodic points.

v nonarchimedean f has good reduction at v P periodic of exact period n

By DY.0/reduction-commutes-with-evaluation, red semiconjugates f to f̃, so IsPeriodicPt f n P implies IsPeriodicPt f̃ n (red P) (Mathlib's Function.IsPeriodicPt.map). Hence minimalPeriod f̃ (red P) divides n (Function.IsPeriodicPt.minimalPeriod_dvd). For preperiodic P, fᵃ(P) = fᵇ(P) gives f̃ᵃ(red P) = f̃ᵇ(red P).

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-multiplier-of-a-periodic-cycle"></a>

### 2.4 The multiplier of a periodic cycle

Let f be a rational map of degree d ≥ 1 over a field K (any characteristic; DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line) and P ∈ ℙ¹(K) periodic of exact period n ≥ 1. The multiplier of the cycle of P is λ(P) = λ_{fⁿ}(P), the fixed-point multiplier of fⁿ at P (DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier). With a lift F, Φ = Fⁿ and Φ(x) = μ·x for a representative x of P, DY.0's trace formula gives λ(P) = tr(DΦ(x))/μ − dⁿ with dⁿ read in K: no division by the degree occurs, so the residue characteristic is kept (in characteristic p | d the value is still defined). In an affine chart containing the orbit, λ(P) = ∏_{i<n} f′(fⁱ(z)) (DY.2/multiplier-chain-rule); it is the same for all points of the cycle (DY.2/multiplier-constant-on-cycle), and for P fixed by fᵐ (n | m) the multiplier of P for fᵐ is λ(P)^{m/n}.

P periodic of exact period n ≥ 1 for f

Define λ(P) := λ_{fⁿ}(P) with n = minimalPeriod (toEnd f) P (Mathlib's Function.minimalPeriod; toEnd is DY.0/rational-map-action-on-points), using DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier for fⁿ, the n-th power in DY.0's monoid of rational maps. The trace formula is DY.0's characterisation of the fixed-point multiplier, applied to the lift Fⁿ of fⁿ.

- **`cycleMultiplier_toEnd`** (relation): cycleMultiplier f (toEnd f P) = cycleMultiplier f P (node DY.2/multiplier-constant-on-cycle).

### 2.5 Chain rule: the multiplier of a cycle is a product of derivatives

Write λₙ(P) = λ_{fⁿ}(P) for the multiplier of P as a fixed point of fⁿ (DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier). If P = [z : 1] has fⁿ(P) = P and the orbit z, f(z), …, f^{n−1}(z) avoids ∞ and the poles of f, then λₙ(P) = ∏_{i=0}^{n−1} f′(fⁱ(z)).

fⁿ(P) = P orbit in the affine chart where f is regular

By DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier, λ_{fⁿ}(P) is the derivative at z of the rational function of fⁿ, and (fⁿ)′(z) = ∏ f′(fⁱ(z)) by the chain rule for rational functions (Polynomial.derivative_comp on numerators and denominators).

### 2.6 Expansion of a map of good reduction on a fixed residue disc

Setting: v is a nonarchimedean absolute value on K with valuation ring 𝒪 = {a : v(a) ≤ 1}, maximal ideal 𝔪 = {a : v(a) < 1} and residue field k = 𝒪/𝔪 (Mathlib's ValuationSubring and IsLocalRing.ResidueField), a ↦ ã the residue map; p = char k ≥ 0 is the residue characteristic. A lift F is normalised if its coefficients lie in 𝒪 and one of them is a unit; f has good reduction at v when v(Res F) = 1 for a normalised lift (DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map), and then f̃ = [F̃₀ : F̃₁] is a rational map over k of the same degree d. Let g have good reduction and suppose red(0) = [0 : 1] is fixed by g̃ (v(g(0)) < 1). Then for z ∈ 𝔪: g(z) = µ + λz + z²·A(z)/(1 + z·B(z)) with µ = g(0) ∈ 𝔪, λ = g′(0) ∈ 𝒪, A, B ∈ 𝒪[z]; g maps 𝔪 into 𝔪, λ̃ is the multiplier of the fixed point 0̃ of g̃, and for every ν ∈ 𝔪 with µ ∈ ν𝒪: g(z) ≡ µ + λz mod ν²𝒪 for all z ∈ ν𝒪.

v nonarchimedean g has good reduction g̃ fixes 0̃

Write g = (a₀ + a₁z + …)/(b₀ + b₁z + …) from a normalised lift. Good reduction forbids ã₀ = b̃₀ = 0 (then [0 : 1] would be a common zero of G̃₀, G̃₁), and g̃(0̃) = 0̃ forces ã₀ = 0, so b₀ ∈ 𝒪^×. Divide numerator and denominator by b₀; the denominator is 1 + z·B(z) with B ∈ 𝒪[z], a unit for z ∈ 𝔪; long division gives the expansion with A ∈ 𝒪[z], µ = a₀/b₀ and λ = g′(0). λ̃ = g̃′(0̃) by reducing the expansion (DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier over k); the congruence follows since z² ∈ ν²𝒪 and 1 + zB(z) is a unit.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-fixed-point-multiplier); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-good-reduction-of-a-rational-map).

### 2.7 Exceptional points

For a self-map f of X, backwardOrbit(f,a)={x : ∃n≥0, f^n(x)=a} and exceptionalSet(f)={a : backwardOrbit(f,a) is finite}. The n=0 term contains a. For a surjective finite-fibre rational map of degree ≥2 this agrees with finite grand orbit; finiteness of a single fibre does not define exceptional. On the Berkovich line distinguish the classical exceptional set from the set computed on the full analytic carrier.

Use native Nat.iterate and Set.Finite; expose the union of iterated preimages. For rational maps, finite backward orbit is mapped onto itself; hence it is a finite union of cycles and includes its forward orbit. This proves equivalence with the source’s grand-orbit convention.

*Needs:* `mathlib:Nat.iterate`; [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-action-on-points`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-rational-map-action-on-points).

([Benedetto2010](#source-dy2-benedetto2010), Definition 1.10 and Theorem 1.11, pp.6–7 — Finite grand orbits define exceptional points; the rational-map setting identifies them with finite backward orbits; [FRLergodicv3](#source-dy2-frlergodicv3), Definition 2.7, p.14 — Uses finite backward orbit, with a separate pure-inseparable alternative.)

The reusable interface consists of the following statements.

- **`mem_backwardOrbit`** (characterisation): x∈backwardOrbit f a iff some n≥0 has f^n(x)=a.
- **`self_mem_backwardOrbit`** (simp): a∈backwardOrbit f a.
- **`mem_exceptionalSet`** (characterisation): a∈exceptionalSet f iff backwardOrbit f a is finite.
- **`backwardOrbit_conjugate`** (functoriality): For an equivalence h and g=h∘f∘h⁻¹, backwardOrbit g (h a)=h(backwardOrbit f a); exceptional sets transform by h.
- **`exceptional_iff_finite_grandOrbit`** (compatibility): For a surjective self-map (in particular a nonconstant rational map), finite backward orbit iff finite grand orbit {x:∃m,n≥0, f^m(x)=f^n(a)}. Surjectivity forces the finite backward set to be permuted.
- **`exceptional_iterate`** (relation): For any finite-fibre self-map and m≥1, exceptionalSet(f^m)=exceptionalSet(f). Rational maps have finite fibres; arbitrary self-maps need not satisfy this law.

**Checks.**

- **`Exceptional.identity`** (degenerate): For id on any X, E=id’s entire carrier; each backward orbit is a singleton.
- **`Exceptional.integerTranslation`** (non-example): For f(n)=n+1 on Z, E=∅ because each backward orbit contains a−k for every k≥0.
- **`Exceptional.powerSphere`** (value): For z↦z^d on P¹(C), d≥2, E={0,∞}; on affine C the same self-map has E={0}.
- **`Exceptional.frobenius`** (comparison): On P¹(K), K algebraically closed of characteristic p>0 and r≥1, z↦z^(p^r) has E=P¹(overline(F_p)), an infinite set.

**Endpoint checks.** Do not remove n=0 or confuse degree with the cardinality of a fibre.

### 2.8 Classical Fatou and Julia sets

On a uniform space X define classicalFatou f={x : ∃open U containing x, UniformEquicontinuousOn (n↦f^n) U}; classicalJulia f is its complement. For P¹(C), use the unique uniformity compatible with the compact sphere topology, equivalently its chordal metric. For P¹(K) nonarchimedean, use the chordal metric topology, not the one-point compactification topology on K. On C the local condition agrees with normality of meromorphic iterates for uniform convergence on compact subsets in the spherical target metric.

The abstract predicate uses only a self-map and a uniform space. Rational-map conclusions assume degree ≥2 and the indicated valued field.

Use the native UniformEquicontinuousOn predicate on the whole neighborhood, rather than EquicontinuousAt at its center. Shrink to relatively compact neighborhoods on the complex sphere. Native Arzelà–Ascoli compares compact-open relative compactness of continuous maps with local uniform equicontinuity. The sphere charts and meromorphic-limit comparison in the normal-family supplier identify these limits with holomorphic sphere maps, including constant infinity; a set equivalence alone supplies none of this analytic structure.

The reusable interface consists of the following statements.

- **`mem_classicalFatou`** (characterisation): Membership is the displayed open-neighborhood UniformEquicontinuousOn condition.
- **`classicalJulia_eq_compl`** (simp): classicalJulia f=(classicalFatou f)ᶜ.
- **`isOpen_classicalFatou`** (structure): classicalFatou f is open for every self-map.
- **`isClosed_classicalJulia`** (structure): classicalJulia f is closed for every self-map.
- **`classicalFatou_uniformConjugate`** (functoriality): For a uniform equivalence h, Fatou(h∘f∘h⁻¹)=h(Fatou f), and likewise Julia.
- **`classicalFatou_complex_normal`** (compatibility): On P¹(C), membership iff iterates are normal on some neighborhood in the compact-open spherical topology. This needs the complex analytic supplier, not only a set equivalence.

**Checks.**

- **`ClassicalFatou.identity`** (degenerate): On any uniform space the identity has Fatou=X and Julia=∅.
- **`ClassicalFatou.constant`** (value): Any constant self-map has Fatou=X: the n=0 identity and constant positive iterates form an equicontinuous family.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-zieve-weighted-coefficient-divisibility"></a>

### 2.10 Weighted divisibility for p-fold composition

Let p be an odd prime and H=X+∑b_iX^i be the generic polynomial over Z[b_0,…,b_D]. For 0≤β≤p−1, every monomial c∏b_i^α_i with coefficient c not divisible by p in [X^β](H^p−X) satisfies ∑_{i=0}^{p−1}α_i≥p and 2α_0+α_1≥p−1. Every composition monomial has weight ∑(i−1)α_i=β−1. For β=0 the only monomials with α_0=1 are binom(p,l+1)b_0b_1^l; in particular the term p b_0 is distinguished. Here H^p means p-fold composition, not ordinary multiplication.

Generic finite-degree polynomial; p odd prime.

Track substitution monomials by weighted degree to obtain ∑(i−1)α_i=β−1 and the β=0 binomial exceptions (Lemma 42). Reduce modulo p; high-index coefficients i≥p cannot occur in the relevant low-degree monomials with α_0<p (Lemma 39). For total low-index degree use the substitution matrix on R[X]/(X^p), with R=F_p[b_0,…,b_{p−1}]/(b_0,…,b_{p−1})^p. The operator is I+N with N^p=0, so its p-th power is I (Lemma 40). For weighted low degree embed b_0=u b_1² modulo b_1^(p−1), invert b_2, and use nilpotent quadratic preparation to find a root δ in the ideal (b_1) after a monic quadratic extension. Translate X by δ: substitution becomes triangular with diagonal 1,(1+ε),…,(1+ε)^(p−1), ε^(p−1)=0. The cyclotomic product gives characteristic polynomial t^p−1; Cayley–Hamilton gives the required identity (Lemma 41). The exact preparation step is retained as an algebra supplier gap.

*Needs:* `mathlib:Polynomial.comp`; `mathlib:Polynomial.coeff`; `mathlib:Nat.iterate`.

**Endpoint checks.** Keep p-fold composition distinct from the polynomial power. This node refines the parent valuation recursion rather than reproducing its bound.

### 2.11 Lower bound c_v ‖x‖_v^d ≤ ‖F(x)‖_v from the resultant

Let F = (F₀, F₁) be binary forms of degree d ≥ 1 over K with Res(F) ≠ 0, and v an absolute value on K. There is a constant c_v(F) > 0 with c_v(F)·‖x‖_v^d ≤ ‖F(x)‖_v for all x ∈ K². ### 2.14 The orbit congruence 1 + λ + ⋯ + λ^{N−1} ∈ 𝔪

In the setting of DY.2/residue-disc-expansion suppose 0 is periodic for g of exact period N ≥ 2 (so µ = g(0) ≠ 0). Then g^j(0) ≡ µ·(1 + λ + ⋯ + λ^{j−1}) mod µ²𝒪 for all j ≥ 1, and consequently 1 + λ + ⋯ + λ^{N−1} ∈ µ𝒪 ⊆ 𝔪. Hence: if λ̃ ≠ 1 then λ̃ ≠ 0 and λ̃^N = 1; if λ̃ = 1 then N = 0 in k.

### 2.15 Valuation recursion along p-power iterates (Hutz)

Setting: v is a nonarchimedean absolute value on K with valuation ring 𝒪 = {a : v(a) ≤ 1}, maximal ideal 𝔪 = {a : v(a) < 1} and residue field k = 𝒪/𝔪 (Mathlib's ValuationSubring and IsLocalRing.ResidueField), a ↦ ã the residue map; p = char k ≥ 0 is the residue characteristic. A lift F is normalised if its coefficients lie in 𝒪 and one of them is a unit; f has good reduction at v when v(Res F) = 1 for a normalised lift (DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map), and then f̃ = [F̃₀ : F̃₁] is a rational map over k of the same degree d. Assume moreover that char K = 0 and v is discrete, with additive valuation ord normalised by ord(π) = 1 for a uniformiser π, write ord for the valuation (so ord(p) is the absolute ramification index when char K = 0), and p = char k > 0. Let g have good reduction, with 0 a periodic point of exact period p^e (e ≥ 1), g̃(0̃) = 0̃ and g′(0) ≡ 1 mod 𝔪. For 0 ≤ k ≤ e − 1 put x_k = g^{p^k}(0), b_k = ord(x_k) and c_k = ord((g^{p^k})′(0) − 1) (∞ if the difference is 0). Then b₀, c₀ ≥ 1, and for 0 ≤ k ≤ e − 2: b_{k+1} ≥ min(2b_k, b_k + (p − 1)c_k, b_k + ord(p)) and c_{k+1} ≥ min(b_k, c_k + ord(p), p·c_k). Moreover min(b_{e−1}, c_{e−1}) ≤ ord(p), and if b_{e−1} > ord(p) then (p − 1)·c_{e−1} ≤ ord(p).

v discrete, normalised residue characteristic p > 0 0 of exact period p^e, e ≥ 1, fixed mod 𝔪 with multiplier ≡ 1 Mixed characteristic: char K = 0, so ord(p) is finite; ord is additive and ord(π) = 1, whereas v is the multiplicative absolute value.

Apply DY.2/residue-disc-expansion to h_k = g^{p^k}: h_k(z) = x_k + λ_k z + O(z²) on 𝔪, with λ_k = 1 + (unit)·π^{c_k}. x_{k+1} = h_k^p(0) ≡ (1 + λ_k + ⋯ + λ_k^{p−1})·x_k mod x_k²; expand λ_k^i = Σ_j C(i, j)(λ_k − 1)^j and use the hockey-stick identity Σ_{i=1}^{p−1} C(i, j) = C(p, j + 1) (Mathlib's Nat.sum_Icc_choose), divisible by p for 1 ≤ j ≤ p − 2 (Nat.Prime.dvd_choose_self), with the last coefficient 1: this gives the bound for b_{k+1}. (h_k^p)′(0) ≡ (h_k′(0))^p mod π^{b_k} (chain rule along the orbit, which stays within π^{b_k}𝒪 of 0), and (1 + u)^p − 1 has valuation ≥ min(c_k + ord(p), p·c_k): this gives the bound for c_{k+1}. At k = e − 1, x_e = g^{p^e}(0) = 0 ≠ x_{e−1}, so 1 + λ + ⋯ + λ^{p−1} ≡ 0 mod π^{b_{e−1}}; its valuation is min(ord(p), (p − 1)c_{e−1}) when these differ, giving the final assertions.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-exceptional-classification"></a>

### 2.16 Classical exceptional-set dichotomy

Over an algebraically closed field, a degree-d≥2 rational map has either at most two classical exceptional points, or characteristic p>0 and a PGL₂ conjugacy to z↦z^(p^r) for r≥1. In the latter case E is the conjugate of P¹(overline(F_p)) and is countably infinite. In particular E is Borel and countable for every valued field here; in characteristic zero it has at most two points. Every degree-at-least-two map of separable degree one belongs to the Frobenius alternative.

Algebraically closed field; the absolute value is irrelevant to classification.

Surjectivity permutes every finite backward orbit. If there are three exceptional points, a common iterate fixes all three and each has a singleton inverse fibre. Normalize them to 0,1,∞. Factorization of the zero and pole forms makes that iterate z↦z^D; its singleton fibre above 1 forces z^D−1=(z−1)^D, so D is a power of the characteristic. Write f as a separable rational map composed with a Frobenius power. Separable degrees multiply under composition, so the preceding iterate forces separable degree one. A degree-d map of separable degree one has d+1 distinct fixed points: its local derivative is zero, so each fixed-point equation has a simple zero. Normalize three fixed points to 0,1,∞. In these coordinates f=M∘Frobenius^r and M fixes 0,1,∞, hence M is the identity. For Frobenius, a finite backward orbit is equivalent to algebraicity over the finite prime field. Transport by conjugacy. If the three-point alternative fails there are at most two exceptional points. No characteristic-zero critical-point theorem is used.

### 2.17 Nonclassical finite grand orbits

If a point ζ of type II, III or IV has finite grand orbit under f on P¹,an_K, there is exactly one nonclassical point with this property; it is type II, fixed and totally invariant. Moving ζ to ζ_G by any PGL₂ transformation makes f have good reduction.

K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.

Pass to an iterate fixing all points in the finite orbit; the inverse fibre of each is a singleton and the local degree equals the full degree. Two such points would bound an annulus whose logarithmic modulus is multiplied by d^n under the iterate. Fixed endpoints force its positive modulus to equal d^n times itself, a contradiction. The full-degree local branch excludes type III/IV; normalize the unique type-II point to Gauss. Every residue component maps into one component, so zeros and poles cannot share a component; the resultant is a unit.

### 2.18 Classical invariance laws

For a nonconstant rational map on P¹(C) or P¹(K) with the corresponding chordal uniformity, F and J are open/closed complements, completely invariant: f⁻¹F=f(F)=F and f⁻¹J=f(J)=J. They are unchanged by replacing f with f^m, m≥1, and are transported by PGL₂ conjugacy. These rational-map assertions are not universal laws for arbitrary topological self-maps.

Either the complex sphere case, or the complete algebraically closed nontrivially nonarchimedean chordal case; f is nonconstant in that case.

Openness follows from the local definition. For backward invariance restrict to inverse neighborhoods; for forward invariance use openness of the finite holomorphic/rational map and its local normal form. For iterate invariance write each exponent as mn+i; the finitely many rational maps f^i have uniform Lipschitz bounds in chordal metrics. PGL₂ maps and inverses have finite chordal Lipschitz constants, so they transport the local uniform condition.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-nonarchimedean-disc-criterion"></a>

### 2.19 Disc criterion for classical stability

For a family G of rational functions on P¹(K), local chordal uniform equicontinuity at x is equivalent to the existence of a projective disc D containing x such that, for every g∈G, g(D) lies in one residue class. For the family of iterates, x∈F_I iff some sufficiently small disc has this property. Equivalently there is a disc whose forward saturation omits an infinite set of classical points.

K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.

Normalize a target residue class. The pole-free rational expansion and ultrametric coefficient bound give a common chordal Lipschitz constant on a smaller disc. Conversely a common small chordal image bound places each image in the residue class of its center (Lemmas 4.18–4.19). For the converse omitted-value criterion, move two omitted values to a finite point and infinity. Disc images of pole-free expansions are discs; an omitted finite value gives the common Lipschitz bound of Theorem 4.27 and Corollary 4.28. Infinite omission in particular provides two distinct values. For a stable disc D, no returned image can strictly contain D: the coefficient giving strict expansion would force some further returned image to leave its residue class (Lemma 4.30). If D never meets a positive iterate, shrink to D′⊊D and the saturation omits D∖D′. Otherwise some return image is contained in D, and all forward images lie in finitely many residue classes; a different residue class is omitted. Both complements are uncountable (Theorem 4.29).

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.2/classical-fatou-julia`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-classical-fatou-julia); `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.1`.

### 2.20 Inseparable maps have empty classical Julia set

Write f=ψ∘(z↦z^p); ψ has a finite chordal Lipschitz constant C. Chordal distance under Frobenius is its p-th power. On a disc of radius at most C^(-1/(p−1)), f contracts or preserves each distance; this property persists under iteration. The chain rule gives multiplier zero for every periodic cycle.

### 2.21 Sharp p-power jet growth

Let R be a characteristic-zero DVR of residue characteristic p, v(π)=1 and e_K=v(p)≥1. For H∈R[X] with H(0)∈m and H′(0)≡1 mod m, write c_i(j)=[X^i](H^(p^j)−X), C_i(j)=v(c_i(j)), with v(0)=∞. If p is odd and p^(j−1)≤2e_K/(p−1), then C_0(j),C_1(j)≥(p^j+1)/2 and C_i(j)≥(p^j−1)/2 for 2≤i≤p−1. At the first index ℓ with p^ℓ>2e_K/(p−1), any finite C_0(ℓ) remains finite and then increases by exactly e_K per p-fold iteration. If p=2, C_0(j),C_1(j)≥2^j while 2^(j−1)≤e_K; at the first ℓ with 2^ℓ>e_K a finite C_0(ℓ) likewise grows by exactly e_K. Therefore a point in m of exact H-period p^n, n≥1, satisfies p^(n−1)≤2e_K/(p−1), sharpened to 2^(n−1)≤e_K when p=2.

DVR in mixed characteristic; H is integral and tangent to the identity modulo m; conjugate the selected cycle point to 0.

Odd p: apply weighted coefficient divisibility to bound the next jet by the minimum of p-divisible terms and weighted non-p-divisible monomials. Induct on j as in Proposition 31. Past the first threshold, every constant-term summand except p c_0 has valuation strictly greater than e_K+C_0; Proposition 32 gives exact noncancelling linear valuation growth and persistence of the other jet bounds. For p=2 give the short direct argument omitted by the source: if H=X+c_0+c_1X+… then C_0(next)≥min(e_K+C_0,C_0+C_1,2C_0), and C_1(next)≥min(e_K+C_1,2C_1,e_K+C_0,2C_0). The term with i=2 in the derivative carries the factor 2; i≥3 contributes at least 2C_0. Those inequalities double both lower bounds up to the threshold. Once C_0,C_1>e_K, only 2c_0 can have the least constant-term valuation, so C_0(next)=e_K+C_0 and C_1 stays >e_K. A periodic 0 eventually has C_0=∞. Finite noncancelling growth past ℓ contradicts that, forcing its period to divide p^ℓ. Translate ℓ into the displayed inequalities.

### 2.22 ‖F(x)‖_v = ‖x‖_v^d for a lift with good reduction

v nonarchimedean F v-integral with v(Res F) = 1 d ≥ 1; at d = 0 a constant pair can have resultant 1 without a unit coefficient.

Upper bound ‖F(x)‖ ≤ ‖x‖^d from DY.2/lift-norm-upper-bound (integral case). Lower bound v(Res F)·‖x‖^d ≤ ‖F(x)‖ from DY.2/lift-norm-lower-bound (integral case) with v(Res F) = 1. Iterate by induction on n.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-escape-rate-tendsto"></a>

### 2.23 Existence of the escape rate, with a uniform rate

Let F be a lift of degree d ≥ 2 with Res(F) ≠ 0 and v an absolute value on K, with constants c_v = c_v(F) > 0 and C_v = C_v(F) from DY.2/lift-norm-lower-bound and DY.2/lift-norm-upper-bound, and B_v = max(log C_v, −log c_v). For every x ∈ K² ∖ {0} the limit G_{F,v}(x) = lim d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖_v exists, and |d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖_v − G_{F,v}(x)| ≤ B_v/((d − 1)·dⁿ) for all n ≥ 0; the convergence is uniform on K² ∖ {0}.

d ≥ 2 Res(F) ≠ 0 x ≠ 0 (so Fⁿ(x) ≠ 0 for all n, by the lower bound)

Put T_j(x) = d^{−(j+1)} log ‖F^{j+1}(x)‖ − d^{−j} log ‖F^j(x)‖ = d^{−(j+1)}(log ‖F(F^j x)‖ − d log ‖F^j x‖). By the two bounds applied at y = F^j(x) ≠ 0: log c_v ≤ log ‖F(y)‖ − d log ‖y‖ ≤ log C_v, so |T_j(x)| ≤ B_v/d^{j+1}. The telescoping series Σ_j T_j converges absolutely and uniformly (geometric tail, summable_geometric_of_lt_one), and its tail from n is ≤ B_v/((d − 1)dⁿ). Hence the partial sums d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖ = log ‖x‖ + Σ_{j<n} T_j(x) converge uniformly; the limit is G_{F,v}(x) (limUnder of a convergent sequence).

([baker-rumely-2006](#source-parent-baker-rumely-2006), Lemma 3.5 and proof, p. 8 (arXiv v2) — The theorem, with the telescoping proof; the rate |T_j| ≤ C/d^{j+1} is BR's estimate.)

**Endpoint checks.** For F = (X₀², X₁²) all T_j vanish and G = log ‖·‖. For the ℚ₃ example F = (X₀² + X₁², 3X₀X₁) and x = (i, 1) ∈ ℂ₃², the sequence 2^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖₃ equals −(1/2)·log 3 from n = 1 on.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-complex-repelling-periodic-density"></a>

### 2.25 Repelling periodic points are dense in Julia

For a rational map on the complex sphere of degree at least two, the closure of its repelling periodic points is exactly the classical Julia set.

f∈C(z), algebraic degree d≥2, acting holomorphically on the compact Riemann sphere with spherical topology.

At a repelling periodic point the derivatives of return iterates grow without bound, ruling out a normal neighborhood; hence repelling periodic points lie in Julia. The reverse inclusion is the density theorem used in Lyubich §3. The cited paper states this classical input without its proof. Record its full dynamical proof as the explicit gap below; do not infer density from Montel alone or use the downstream uniform blowing-up theorem to prove its own input.

### 2.26 Classical trace of Berkovich stability

If ι:P¹(K)→P¹,an_K is the type-I embedding, ι⁻¹(F_Ber)=F_I and ι⁻¹(J_Ber)=J_I. This compares subsets through the native type-I embedding, whose subspace topology agrees with the classical chordal topology. The full analytic line also contains nonclassical points and is not OnePoint K.

K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.

For x∈F_I choose a disc with infinitely many omitted classical points. Its Berkovich disc has the same images on type-I points, so remains stable. For a type-I point in F_Ber shrink its stable weak-open neighborhood to a Berkovich disc. Select two omitted points and a separating type-II point. An image disc containing that separator would contain one omitted point; hence all image discs stay in residue classes at the separator. The disc criterion gives x∈F_I.

### 2.28 Multipliers of cycles reduce to multipliers

Setting: v is a nonarchimedean absolute value on K with valuation ring 𝒪 = {a : v(a) ≤ 1}, maximal ideal 𝔪 = {a : v(a) < 1} and residue field k = 𝒪/𝔪 (Mathlib's ValuationSubring and IsLocalRing.ResidueField), a ↦ ã the residue map; p = char k ≥ 0 is the residue characteristic. A lift F is normalised if its coefficients lie in 𝒪 and one of them is a unit; f has good reduction at v when v(Res F) = 1 for a normalised lift (DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map), and then f̃ = [F̃₀ : F̃₁] is a rational map over k of the same degree d. Let f have good reduction at v and P ∈ ℙ¹(K) with fⁿ(P) = P. Then the multiplier λₙ(f, P) := λ_{fⁿ}(P) (DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier) lies in 𝒪 and its residue is the multiplier of the reduced point: (λₙ(f, P))~ = λₙ(f̃, red P) ∈ k, computed in characteristic p = char k by the same formula. In particular |λₙ(f, P)|_v ≤ 1, and λₙ(f, P) ∈ 𝔪 whenever f̃ⁿ is inseparable (in characteristic p, f̃ⁿ ∈ k(z^p) has derivative 0, so all its multipliers vanish).

v nonarchimedean f has good reduction at v fⁿ(P) = P

Let x be a primitive representative and Φ = Fⁿ, a normalised lift of fⁿ with good reduction and reduction F̃ⁿ (DY.0/reduction-commutes-with-composition). Φ(x) = μx with v(μ) = ‖Φ(x)‖ = 1 (DY.2/lift-norm-of-good-reduction), so μ ∈ 𝒪^×, and reducing gives Φ̃(x̃) = μ̃x̃ with x̃ ≠ 0: red P is fixed by f̃ⁿ. DΦ has entries in 𝒪[X] and reduction commutes with partial derivatives (MvPolynomial.pderiv_map); so the trace formula of DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier gives λ_{fⁿ}(P) = tr(DΦ(x))/μ − dⁿ ∈ 𝒪, whose residue is tr(DΦ̃(x̃))/μ̃ − dⁿ = λ_{f̃ⁿ}(red P) by the same formula over k; red P is DY.0/reduction-of-points.

### 2.29 Two-sided bound for G_{F,v} − log ‖·‖_v

Under the hypotheses of DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto, for every x ∈ K² ∖ {0}: log c_v(F)/(d − 1) ≤ G_{F,v}(x) − log ‖x‖_v ≤ log C_v(F)/(d − 1). In particular |G_{F,v}(x) − log ‖x‖_v| ≤ B_v/(d − 1). If v is nonarchimedean and F is v-integral: log ‖x‖_v + log v(Res F)/(d − 1) ≤ G_{F,v}(x) ≤ log ‖x‖_v.

d ≥ 2 Res(F) ≠ 0 x ≠ 0

G(x) − log ‖x‖ = Σ_{j≥0} T_j(x) with d^{−(j+1)} log c_v ≤ T_j(x) ≤ d^{−(j+1)} log C_v (proof of DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto). Sum the geometric series Σ_{j≥0} d^{−(j+1)} = 1/(d − 1). The integral case uses c_v = v(Res F) and C_v ≤ 1 from the integral clauses of the two bound lemmas.

### 2.31 Logarithmic homogeneity G_{F,v}(αx) = G_{F,v}(x) + log v(α)

d ≥ 2 Res(F) ≠ 0 α ≠ 0 x ≠ 0

Fⁿ is homogeneous of degree dⁿ, so Fⁿ(αx) = α^{dⁿ}Fⁿ(x) and d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ(αx)‖ = log v(α) + d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖. Pass to the limit (DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto); ‖αx‖ = v(α)‖x‖ gives the descent.

### 2.32 Changing the lift: G_{cF,v} = G_{F,v} + log v(c)/(d − 1)

d ≥ 2 Res(F) ≠ 0 c ≠ 0

### 2.34 Transformation of the escape rate under conjugation

Let A ∈ GL₂(K) and F^A = A⁻¹ ∘ F ∘ A (a lift of the conjugate φ⁻¹ ∘ f ∘ φ, φ the Möbius map of A; DY.0/conjugacy-of-rational-maps). Then G_{F^A,v}(x) = G_{F,v}(A x) for all x ≠ 0. More generally, for A, B ∈ GL₂(K) with B ∘ F = F′ ∘ B (F′ another lift of degree d), G_{F′,v}(Bx) = G_{F,v}(x). In DY.0's convention γ • f = γ ∘ f ∘ γ⁻¹ (DY.0/conjugacy-of-rational-maps), with γ the class of A, γ • f has the lift A ∘ F ∘ A⁻¹ and G_{A∘F∘A⁻¹, v}(x) = G_{F,v}(A⁻¹x).

d ≥ 2 Res(F) ≠ 0 A ∈ GL₂(K)

(F^A)ⁿ = A⁻¹ ∘ Fⁿ ∘ A by induction. For y ∈ K²: ‖A⁻¹y‖_v ≤ 2·‖A⁻¹‖·‖y‖_v and ‖y‖_v ≤ 2·‖A‖·‖A⁻¹y‖_v with ‖A‖ = max v(entries) (Mathlib's AbsoluteValue.iSup_abv_linearMap_apply_le; no factor 2 at nonarchimedean v). ### 2.35 G_{F,v} = log ‖·‖_v on an algebraically closed field implies good reduction

Let K be a field with a nonarchimedean absolute value v whose residue field is algebraically closed (for instance K algebraically closed, e.g. ℂ_v), and let F be a lift of degree d ≥ 2 with v-integral coefficients, some coefficient of absolute value 1. If G_{F,v}(x) = log ‖x‖_v for all x ∈ K² ∖ {0}, then v(Res F) = 1, i.e. f has good reduction at v. The hypothesis on the residue field cannot be dropped: see DY.2/example-bad-reduction-nonclosed-field.

v nonarchimedean residue field k of v algebraically closed F v-integral and normalised (max v(coeff) = 1) d ≥ 2

Suppose v(Res F) < 1. By DY.0/good-reduction-iff-normalized-resultant-unit the resultant of the reduced forms F̃₀, F̃₁ vanishes in k (the resultant commutes with reduction, an API item of DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map), and F̃ ≠ (0, 0) since F is normalised. By DY.0/binary-resultant-eq-zero-iff the forms F̃₀, F̃₁ have a common nontrivial zero over an algebraic closure of k, hence over k itself since k is algebraically closed; call it ỹ ≠ 0 in k². Lift ỹ to y in the valuation ring with ‖y‖ = 1; then ‖F(y)‖ < 1. By the integral upper bound ‖F(z)‖ ≤ ‖z‖^d, ‖Fⁿ(y)‖ ≤ ‖F(y)‖^{d^{n−1}}, so G(y) ≤ (1/d)·log ‖F(y)‖ < 0 = log ‖y‖, a contradiction.

### 2.36 The lift bounds at points of the Berkovich affine line

Setting: K is a complete nonarchimedean field (algebraically closed where stated, e.g. ℂ_v) with absolute value |·|; P^{1,an}_K = A^{1,an}_K ∪ {∞} is the Berkovich projective line of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0, whose points x ∈ A^{1,an}_K are multiplicative seminorms g ↦ [g]_x on K[T] extending |·|, with the weakest topology making every x ↦ [g]_x continuous; When K is algebraically closed with nontrivial absolute value, ℙ¹(K) is dense in P^{1,an}_K. The disc point ζ_{a,r} is the translated Gauss seminorm (equal to the sup-norm on D(a, r) under those hypotheses) and ζ_{0,1} is the Gauss point; a rational map f acts by its analytification f^{an} ([g]_{f^{an}(x)} = [g ∘ f]_x in an affine chart where the rational expression is defined). The Laplacian Δ on P^{1,an}_K is the one of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.1, normalised as in DeMarco–Krieger–Ye: Δ log max([T], 1) = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} − δ_∞ (the negative of Baker–Rumely's). For a lift F of degree d ≥ 2 with Res(F) ≠ 0 over K and every x ∈ A^{1,an}_K: c(F)·max([T]_x, 1)^d ≤ max([F₀(T, 1)]_x, [F₁(T, 1)]_x) ≤ C(F)·max([T]_x, 1)^d, with the nonarchimedean constants of DY.2/lift-norm-lower-bound and DY.2/lift-norm-upper-bound. Hence the functions x ↦ d^{−n}·log max([Fⁿ₀(T, 1)]_x, [Fⁿ₁(T, 1)]_x) − log max([T]_x, 1) converge uniformly on A^{1,an}_K.

K complete nonarchimedean Res(F) ≠ 0 d ≥ 2 for the asserted uniform convergence.

A multiplicative seminorm on K[T] extending a nonarchimedean absolute value is nonarchimedean ([n]_x = |n| ≤ 1 for n ∈ ℕ), so the ultrametric estimates of DY.2/lift-norm-upper-bound hold for [·]_x. Evaluate the certificate identities H₀F₀ + H₁F₁ = Res(F)·X₁^{2d−1}, G₀F₀ + G₁F₁ = Res(F)·X₀^{2d−1} at (T, 1) and apply [·]_x (multiplicative) as in DY.2/lift-norm-lower-bound. Uniform convergence: the telescoping of DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto works verbatim with ‖·‖ replaced by max([·]_x, [·]_x).

### 2.37 Complex blowing up and inverse branches

For f on P¹(C), J is nonempty, perfect and completely invariant; E has at most two points and lies in F. For every open U meeting J and every compact K⊆P¹(C)∖E, there exists N with K⊆f^n(U) for all n≥N. For each a outside E, J is contained in the closure of its backward orbit (with equality if a∈J). Any family of holomorphic inverse branches of f^m defined on a domain U is spherical normal. If U meets J, their image diameters on every V compactly contained in U tend uniformly to zero as m→∞. Write Z_ℓ=⋃_{j=1}^ℓ f^j(Crit f) and τ=#f(Crit f). On any simply connected U disjoint from Z_ℓ, the number σ_m(U) of inverse branches satisfies σ_m(U)≥d^m(1−2τd^(−ℓ)) for m,ℓ≥1.

f∈C(z), algebraic degree d≥2, acting holomorphically on the compact Riemann sphere with spherical topology.

Meromorphic Montel bounds the permanent omitted values of forward images of a Julia neighborhood by two; backward invariance of this finite omitted set puts it in E. Exceptional cycles are superattracting and lie in F. If J were empty, compactness would give a uniformly convergent subsequence of global iterates. Uniformly close sphere maps are homotopic, contradicting deg(f^n)=d^n. Backward density and E⊂F rule out isolated Julia points. For uniform blowing up choose a repelling periodic point in U by the density theorem. A small V⊆U satisfies f^p(V)⊃V for its period p. Enlarge K to compact L outside E with f(L)⊃L using invariant exceptional-neighborhood bases. Montel for f^p and equality of exceptional sets under iteration show ⋃_{j≥0}f^{pj}(V) covers L. These open sets increase, so a single one covers L. Applying f(L)⊃L gives the claimed inclusion for every sufficiently large exponent. For normality of all inverse branches, locally choose a periodic orbit of at least three points avoiding the domain neighborhood. Every inverse branch omits this orbit, since its forward image is outside the orbit. Montel applies; disjointness of branch images is not the omitted-value hypothesis. If U meets J and an inverse-branch subsequence of increasing order has a nonconstant limit, Hurwitz gives a neighborhood Y of the limiting image of a Julia point with Y contained in each branch image of a smaller domain U′. Complete invariance and closedness put that limiting image in J. Thus f^{m_j}(Y)⊆U′, contradicting uniform blowing up to a nonexceptional point outside U′. Normality then gives uniform shrinking on compact V. There are d^m branches when m≤ℓ. At each later step at most τ of the mutually disjoint branch images contain a critical value; the rest each admit d further branches. Induction gives d^m−σ_m≤τ∑_{i=1}^{m−ℓ}d^i≤2τd^{m−ℓ}.

### 2.38 Periodic points and multipliers

A classical periodic point a of f over K is in J_I iff its cycle multiplier λ satisfies |λ|>1; it is in F_I iff |λ|≤1. This includes indifferent points. Through the type-I embedding the same alternatives locate a in J_Ber or F_Ber.

K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.

Replace f by the return iterate and move a to 0. If |λ|≤1 choose a small invariant disc using the convergent local expansion. Iterates are uniformly Lipschitz there. If |λ|>1, every punctured sufficiently small disc is eventually expanded outside itself; take initial points arbitrarily close to a to contradict local uniform equicontinuity. The Berkovich statement uses the classical-trace comparison, not a multiplier definition on nonclassical points.

### 2.39 G_{F,v} = log ‖·‖_v at all but finitely many places

Let K be a number field, F a lift over K of degree d ≥ 2 with Res(F) ≠ 0 and x ∈ K² ∖ {0}. There is a finite set S of finite places of K such that for every finite place v ∉ S: F is v-integral with v(Res F) = 1, ‖x‖_v = 1, and G_{F,v}(x) = log ‖x‖_v = 0.

K a number field Res(F) ≠ 0 x ≠ 0

Each nonzero element of K has v(a) = 1 for all but finitely many finite places v (Mathlib's NumberField.FinitePlace.hasFiniteMulSupport); apply it to the nonzero coefficients of F, to Res(F) and to the nonzero coordinates of x. Outside the union S of these finite sets, F has good reduction at v and ‖x‖_v = 1; conclude with DY.2/escape-rate-of-good-reduction.

### 2.40 No repelling cycles under potential good reduction

If f has good reduction at v then every periodic point P ∈ ℙ¹(K̄_v) (over any extension of v) has |λ(P)|_v ≤ 1. If some conjugate φ⁻¹ ∘ f ∘ φ (φ ∈ PGL₂(K̄)) has good reduction, the same holds. Consequently a map with a repelling cycle (|λ| > 1) at v does not have potentially good reduction at v.

v nonarchimedean

Apply DY.2/multiplier-reduction over the extension (good reduction is preserved by extension of v). For a conjugate use DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier-conj.

### 2.41 Periods of points under good reduction (Morton–Silverman)

Setting: v is a nonarchimedean absolute value on K with valuation ring 𝒪 = {a : v(a) ≤ 1}, maximal ideal 𝔪 = {a : v(a) < 1} and residue field k = 𝒪/𝔪 (Mathlib's ValuationSubring and IsLocalRing.ResidueField), a ↦ ã the residue map; p = char k ≥ 0 is the residue characteristic. A lift F is normalised if its coefficients lie in 𝒪 and one of them is a unit; f has good reduction at v when v(Res F) = 1 for a normalised lift (DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map), and then f̃ = [F̃₀ : F̃₁] is a rational map over k of the same degree d. Let f have degree d ≥ 2 and good reduction at v, and let P ∈ ℙ¹(K) be periodic of exact period n. Let m be the exact period of red(P) under f̃, λ̃ = λ_m(f̃, red P) ∈ k the multiplier of the reduced cycle, and r the multiplicative order of λ̃ in k^× (r = ∞ when λ̃ = 0 or λ̃ is not a root of unity). Then either n = m, or n = m·r·p^e for some e ≥ 0, where p = char k; if char k = 0 then e = 0. (Over ℚ_p the exponent satisfies e ≤ 1 for p odd and e ≤ 3 for p = 2 by DY.2/period-exponent-bound.)

v nonarchimedean f of degree ≥ 2 with good reduction at v P ∈ ℙ¹(K) periodic of exact period n

m | n by DY.2/reduction-of-periodic-points. Replace f by g = f^m (good reduction and g̃ = f̃^m by DY.0/reduction-commutes-with-composition); P has exact period N = n/m under g (Function.minimalPeriod_iterate_eq_div_gcd) and red P is fixed by g̃ with multiplier λ̃. If N = 1 then n = m. Otherwise choose A ∈ GL₂(𝒪) whose second column is a primitive representative of P (so A·[0 : 1] = P and det A is a unit) and conjugate: the conjugate has good reduction (DY.0/good-reduction-conj-integral), P moves to 0, and periods and multipliers are unchanged (DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier-conj). If λ̃ ≠ 1: by DY.2/orbit-congruence-geometric-sum λ̃ ≠ 0 and λ̃^N = 1, so r is finite and r | N. Replace g by g^r and N by N/r; the new multiplier λ̃^r = 1. If N/r = 1 then n = m·r. If λ̃ = 1 and N ≥ 2: DY.2/orbit-congruence-geometric-sum gives N = 0 in k, so p = char k > 0 and p | N; replace g by g^p (multiplier still ≡ 1) and N by N/p, and repeat. The process stops since N decreases; it ends with N = 1, giving n = m·r·p^e (r = 1 when the reduced multiplier was already 1). In characteristic 0 the second case would give N = 0 in k with N ≥ 2, impossible; so e = 0.

### 2.42 G_{F,v}(x) ≤ 0 exactly on the filled Julia set of F

For a lift F of degree d ≥ 2 with Res(F) ≠ 0, v an absolute value and x ∈ K²: the orbit (Fⁿ(x))ₙ is bounded for ‖·‖_v if and only if x = 0 or G_{F,v}(x) ≤ 0. If G_{F,v}(x) > 0 then ‖Fⁿ(x)‖_v → ∞.

d ≥ 2 Res(F) ≠ 0

If ‖Fⁿ x‖ ≤ M for all n then d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ x‖ ≤ d^{−n} log M → 0. Conversely put R = c_v^{−1/(d−1)} (so c_v = R^{−(d−1)}), giving ‖F(z)‖ ≥ R·(‖z‖/R)^d for all z (DY.2/lift-norm-lower-bound). If ‖y‖ > R, put α = ‖y‖/R > 1; by induction ‖Fⁿ(y)‖ ≥ R·α^{dⁿ}, hence G(y) ≥ lim d^{−n}(log R + dⁿ log α) = log α > 0 and ‖Fⁿ(y)‖ → ∞. An unbounded orbit reaches some y = F^{n₀}(x) with ‖y‖ > R, and G(x) = d^{−n₀}·G(y) > 0 by DY.2/escape-rate-functional-equation.

### 2.43 Continuity of the escape rate

Let K be a normed field (archimedean or nonarchimedean, e.g. ℂ or ℂ_p) and v = ‖·‖. For a lift F of degree d ≥ 2 with Res(F) ≠ 0, x ↦ G_{F,v}(x) is continuous on K² ∖ {0}, and so is x ↦ G_{F,v}(x) − log ‖x‖_v, which descends to a continuous bounded function on ℙ¹(K).

K a normed field, v its norm d ≥ 2 Res(F) ≠ 0

Each x ↦ d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖ is continuous on K² ∖ {0}: Fⁿ is polynomial, Fⁿ(x) ≠ 0 there (DY.2/lift-norm-lower-bound), and log and max are continuous on (0, ∞). The convergence is uniform (DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto); a uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous (TendstoUniformly.continuous). The difference with log ‖x‖ is bounded (DY.2/escape-rate-sub-log-norm-bounds) and homogeneous of degree 0 (DY.2/escape-rate-homogeneity), hence descends to ℙ¹(K) with the quotient topology.

### 2.44 The local canonical height λ̂_{F,v}

Conventions (pinned for the whole layer): K is a field and v : K → ℝ an absolute value (Mathlib's AbsoluteValue K ℝ); for x = (x₀, x₁) ∈ K², ‖x‖_v = max(v(x₀), v(x₁)) (Mathlib's ⨆ i, v (x i)). A lift of a rational map f of degree d is a pair F = (F₀, F₁) of binary forms of degree d with Res(F) ≠ 0 (DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line, DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map); f([x₀ : x₁]) = [F₀(x) : F₁(x)], the affine coordinate is z ↔ [z : 1], ∞ = [1 : 0], and Fⁿ is the n-fold composite, a lift of fⁿ of degree dⁿ. The local canonical height of F at v (relative to the divisor (∞), in the affine coordinate) is λ̂_{F,v}(z) = G_{F,v}(z, 1) for z ∈ K; homogeneously, λ̂_{F,v}([x₀ : x₁]) = G_{F,v}(x₀, x₁) − log v(x₁) for x₁ ≠ 0, which is independent of the representative by DY.2/escape-rate-homogeneity. It is the DeMarco–Krieger–Ye local height λ_{t,v} (for F = F_t) and the Baker–Rumely height ĥ_{F,v,(∞)} (in their chart), and depends on the lift F only through the additive constant log v(c)/(d − 1).

d ≥ 2 Res(F) ≠ 0

Define λ̂_{F,v}(z) := G_{F,v}(z, 1). The homogeneous formula: G_{F,v}(x₀, x₁) = G_{F,v}(x₀/x₁, 1) + log v(x₁) by DY.2/escape-rate-homogeneity.

### 2.45 The normalised dynamical Green function g_{F,v} on ℙ¹(K)

For a lift F of degree d ≥ 2 with Res(F) ≠ 0 and an absolute value v on K, the dynamical Green function is g_{F,v} : ℙ¹(K) → ℝ, g_{F,v}([x]) = G_{F,v}(x) − log ‖x‖_v. It is bounded, and λ̂_{F,v}(z) = g_{F,v}([z : 1]) + log⁺ v(z). It is the function that extends to the Berkovich line (DY.2/berkovich-escape-potential) and whose Laplacian gives the canonical measure.

d ≥ 2 Res(F) ≠ 0

Define g on nonzero vectors by G_{F,v}(x) − log ‖x‖_v; it is invariant under x ↦ αx (DY.2/escape-rate-homogeneity), hence descends to ℙ¹(K) (Mathlib's Projectivization). Boundedness is DY.2/escape-rate-sub-log-norm-bounds; the relation with λ̂ uses ‖(z, 1)‖_v = max(v(z), 1) and log max(v(z), 1) = log⁺ v(z).

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-complex-transfer-limit"></a>

### 2.46 Lyubich transfer limit

For f on P¹(C) define the native continuous-function operator Aψ(z)=d⁻¹∑_{f(w)=z}deg_w(f)ψ(w). There is a Radon probability ν_f such that A^nψ converges to the constant ∫ψ dν_f uniformly on every compact subset of P¹(C)\E. It is atom-free and balanced and supp ν_f=J. In particular d⁻n(f^n)*δ_a converges weakly to ν_f for a outside E. No new transfer-operator carrier is required; use continuous linear maps on native continuous functions.

f∈C(z), algebraic degree d≥2, acting holomorphically on the compact Riemann sphere with spherical topology.

Finite local-degree branches make Aψ continuous even across critical values and give ||A||≤1, positivity and A1=1. First use a compact L⊆P¹(C)∖E with f⁻¹L⊆L. Inverse-branch counting and normality prove equicontinuity of A_L^nψ. At critical preimages use continuous roots; at a nonexceptional period-r point the return multiplicity t<d^r makes the unresolved branch weight (t/d^r)^k tend to zero. Arzelà–Ascoli gives relatively compact orbits in C(L). Use the almost-periodic Banach contraction splitting of Lyubich §2. Peripheral eigenfunctions must be constant and eigenvalue 1: a modulus maximizer and backward-density force equality on J. The transient part tends to zero. The exceptional cycles have forward-invariant neighborhood bases. Every compact K outside E lies in such a compact backward-invariant L. Julia is contained in each L by backward density. The measures constructed on different L agree by evaluating the same transfer limit at a fixed Julia point, so uniform convergence descends to K. The positive normalized limit functional on C(L) is represented by a Radon probability using native Riesz–Markov. Duality gives balance and normalized preimage convergence. Construct the same limit on L=J, which is compact, backward invariant and disjoint from E. Independence of L gives ν=ν_J, hence supp ν⊆J. Conversely, for nonnegative ψ on J positive at a chosen Julia point, uniform blowing up makes A^Nψ strictly positive everywhere on J; compactness gives a positive minimum. The limit functional is therefore positive on ψ, proving J⊆supp ν. A maximal positive atom of a balanced invariant probability must have full local degree along its forward orbit; the finite critical set then forces a finite grand orbit, so the atom would belong to E, disjoint from J. Thus ν is atom-free.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.2/complex-julia-blowing-up`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-complex-julia-blowing-up); `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/FuchsianOrbifolds#layer-5-compact-surface-degree-theory-and-fuchsian-applications`; `mathlib:ArzelaAscoli.isCompact_of_equicontinuous`; `mathlib:MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure`; `mathlib:RealRMK.rieszMeasure`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/BelyiMaps#layer-8-riemann-surfaces-and-analytic-riemann-existence`; `mathlib:RealRMK.integral_rieszMeasure`.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-complex-bowen-net-bound"></a>

### 2.47 Polynomial-size Bowen nets for rational sphere maps

For every δ>0 there is a constant C_δ>0 such that, for every integer m≥1, the compact complex sphere has a finite net in the spherical Bowen metric max_{0≤j<m}Δ(f^j x,f^j y), of radius δ and cardinality at most C_δ m⁵d^m. The constant may depend on f and δ, but not on m.

f∈C(z), algebraic degree d≥2, acting holomorphically on the compact Riemann sphere with spherical topology.

Fix a finite spherical net X containing the critical points and at least three distinct values. Inverse branches on discs avoiding X_m=⋃_{j=1}^m f^j(X) omit X. Normalize each source disc to the unit disc. The requested spherical Montel theorem gives equicontinuity on a smaller disc, hence a uniform shrink factor k for this fixed omitted net; this replaces the Koebe-based proof of Lyubich Proposition 8 without planning a new distortion theory. Use the planar annulus-cover estimate of §6 and a finite smooth sphere atlas: outside an ε-neighborhood of a finite set Z there is a variable-radius net of size ≤C|Z|²(log(δ/ε)+A)+R, with radii bounded by k times distance to Z (Proposition 7). For Z=X_m, |X_m|=O(m), and ε_m=δ/(2L^m) for a spherical Lipschitz bound L>1, this gives O(m³) centers. For each orbit, record the last time outside the critical-net neighborhood, a center at that time, a branch of the preceding iterate, and the next nearby point of X_m. Inverse-branch equicontinuity controls the earlier orbit and the Lipschitz bound controls the later orbit. There are at most C(δ)m⁵d^m such records, hence a spherical Bowen net of that size (Theorem 7).

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.2/complex-julia-blowing-up`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-complex-julia-blowing-up); `ConformalMappingPartII:V0`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/BelyiMaps#layer-8-riemann-surfaces-and-analytic-riemann-existence`.

The fixed omitted-net branch estimate is derived here from the separately requested spherical Montel theorem.)

**Endpoint checks.** Use full-sphere nets, including critical and exceptional orbits; estimates only off the postcritical set do not bound global entropy. The variable-radius covering argument is part of this key dynamical estimate; no missing Koebe theorem is assumed.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-berkovich-fatou-julia-properties"></a>

### 2.48 Berkovich invariance laws

On P¹,an_K the Fatou/Julia sets are open/closed complements and are completely invariant under f. PGL₂ conjugacy transports them. Every classical exceptional point is in F_Ber. The iterate law is proved separately by the canonical-measure comparison below.

K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.

Let U be stable and A the infinite complement of its forward saturation S(U). The analytic map is open, so f(U) is open and still omits A. The set A is backward invariant. Finite fibres and surjectivity make f⁻¹(A) infinite; it misses both f⁻¹(U) and S(U), hence the whole saturation of f⁻¹(U). This proves forward and backward stability without an iterate argument. PGL₂ acts by homeomorphisms on the analytic carrier, so it transports open neighborhoods, saturations and infinite complements. If E is finite, its cycles have singleton inverse fibres and full local degree, hence zero return multiplier. The nonarchimedean periodic dichotomy and classical-trace comparison put them in F_Ber. In the Frobenius alternative every classical point is stable by the inseparable-map theorem, and the same trace comparison applies.

### 2.49 The global height limit is the sum of the escape rates

Let K be a number field with Mathlib's places: InfinitePlace K (with multiplicity mult(v)) and FinitePlace K (normalised absolute values), so that Height.logHeight x = Σ_{v | ∞} mult(v)·log ‖x‖_v + Σ_{v ∤ ∞} log ‖x‖_v for x ∈ K² ∖ {0}. For a lift F over K of degree d ≥ 2 with Res(F) ≠ 0 and x ∈ K² ∖ {0}, the limit lim_{n→∞} d^{−n}·Height.logHeight(Fⁿ(x)) exists and equals Σ_{v | ∞} mult(v)·G_{F,v}(x) + Σ_{v ∤ ∞} G_{F,v}(x), a sum with only finitely many nonzero terms. The right-hand side does not change when x is replaced by αx (α ∈ K^×) or F by cF (c ∈ K^×).

K a number field d ≥ 2 Res(F) ≠ 0 x ≠ 0

Let S be the finite set of DY.2/escape-rate-trivial-at-almost-all-places for F and x. For v ∉ S finite, ‖Fⁿ(x)‖_v = 1 for all n (DY.2/lift-norm-of-good-reduction), so those places contribute 0 to every term. Hence d^{−n}·logHeight(Fⁿ x) = Σ_{v | ∞} mult(v)·d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ x‖_v + Σ_{v ∈ S} d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ x‖_v (NumberField.mulHeight_eq, sum over a finite set), a finite sum of convergent sequences (DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto). Independence of x ↦ αx: the sum changes by Σ_v n_v log v(α) = 0 (product formula NumberField.prod_abs_eq_one) using DY.2/escape-rate-homogeneity; independence of F ↦ cF: it changes by (1/(d − 1))·Σ_v n_v log v(c) = 0 using DY.2/escape-rate-scale-lift.

### 2.50 Bound on the p-power in the period (Hutz)

Setting: v is a nonarchimedean absolute value on K with valuation ring 𝒪 = {a : v(a) ≤ 1}, maximal ideal 𝔪 = {a : v(a) < 1} and residue field k = 𝒪/𝔪 (Mathlib's ValuationSubring and IsLocalRing.ResidueField), a ↦ ã the residue map; p = char k ≥ 0 is the residue characteristic. A lift F is normalised if its coefficients lie in 𝒪 and one of them is a unit; f has good reduction at v when v(Res F) = 1 for a normalised lift (DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map), and then f̃ = [F̃₀ : F̃₁] is a rational map over k of the same degree d. Let char K = 0 and v be discrete, with additive ord(π) = 1 and p = char k > 0, and let f have good reduction. In DY.2/periods-under-good-reduction the exponent satisfies 2^{e−1} ≤ ord(p) if p is odd, and F_{e−1} ≤ ord(2) if p = 2, where F_j is the j-th Fibonacci number (Mathlib's Nat.fib). In particular over ℚ_p (ord(p) = 1): e ≤ 1 for p odd and e ≤ 3 for p = 2.

v discrete normalised p = char k > 0 f good reduction Mixed characteristic: char K = 0, so ord(p) is finite; ord is additive and ord(π) = 1, whereas v is the multiplicative absolute value.

Reduce as in DY.2/periods-under-good-reduction to g = f^{m r} with 0 of exact period p^e, fixed mod 𝔪 with multiplier ≡ 1. Let k₀ ≤ e − 1 be the first index with b_{k₀} > ord(p) (k₀ = e if none). For k < k₀, DY.2/p-power-iterate-valuation-recursion gives inductively b_k ≥ 2^k and c_k ≥ 2^{k−1} (p odd), respectively b_k ≥ F_{k+1} and c_k ≥ F_k (p = 2), starting from b₀, c₀ ≥ 1 and b₁ ≥ 2. If b_{e−1} ≤ ord(p) then 2^{e−1} ≤ b_{e−1} ≤ ord(p) (resp. F_e ≤ ord(2)). If b_{e−1} > ord(p) then (p − 1)·c_{e−1} ≤ ord(p) by DY.2/p-power-iterate-valuation-recursion. The b_k increase strictly (each term of the b-recursion exceeds b_k), so b_k ≥ ord(p) + 1 for all k ≥ k₀, and the c-recursion gives c_{k+1} ≥ min(ord(p) + 1, p·c_k) for k₀ ≤ k ≤ e − 2. If for some such k the minimum were ord(p) + 1, then (inductively) c_{e−1} ≥ ord(p) + 1 > ord(p)/(p − 1), a contradiction; so c_{k+1} ≥ p·c_k along the chain and c_{e−1} ≥ p^{e−1−k₀}·c_{k₀} ≥ 2^{e−2} for p odd (using c_{k₀} ≥ 2^{k₀−1}, or c₀ ≥ 1 if k₀ = 0), respectively ≥ F_{e−1} for p = 2 (F_{i+1} ≤ 2F_i). Hence 2^{e−1} ≤ (p − 1)·2^{e−2} ≤ ord(p) for p odd, and F_{e−1} ≤ c_{e−1} ≤ ord(2) for p = 2 (Mathlib's Nat.fib); in the first case likewise F_{e−1} ≤ F_e ≤ ord(2).

### 2.51 Polynomial realization of a rational cycle

For a mixed-characteristic DVR R and P,Q∈R[X], let h=P/Q∈Frac(R)(z). Suppose a finite cycle σ lies in R and Q(a) is a unit for every a∈σ. There exists θ∈R[X] with θ(a)=h(a) on σ and with the same reduced return multiplier when the cycle has more than one point in a residue class. For a good-reduction projective rational map, apply this to its residue-return cycle after a PGL₂(R) coordinate change or reciprocal chart. Combining the parent residue-period and multiplier-order factorization with sharp jet growth proves the existing parent Zieve endpoint; it is not a new copy of that endpoint.

Finite K/Q_p for the parent consequence; more generally a DVR and good reduction at every point in the selected projective cycle suffice.

For the finite set S={Q(a):a∈σ} of units, construct a polynomial Ψ with 1−tΨ(t)=∏_{s∈S}(1−t/s). Then θ=P·Ψ(Q) agrees with h on σ. For two distinct points in one residue class with matching images, the first-order difference quotient shows the derivatives of the corresponding return polynomials agree modulo m. Apply it to θ’s return map and the polynomial realization of h’s return; the derivative of Ψ at a denominator value gives the rational chain-rule derivative modulo m (Lemma 46). Use the parent reduction of periodic points to pass to the residue-return orbit, all in one residue disc, and normalize it to m. Unit denominators follow from pointwise good reduction; reciprocal coordinates handle a disc at infinity. The parent period theorem supplies the order r of the reduced multiplier. Replace the return map by its r-th iterate and use the polynomial realization to reach the tangent-to-identity hypotheses of sharp jet growth. Insert p^(n−1)≤2e_K/(p−1) (and p=2 sharpening) in the parent zieve-period-exponent-bound. No assertion that global polynomial interpolation preserves exact characteristic-zero multipliers is needed.

### 2.52 λ̂_{F,v} − log⁺ v is bounded

For all z ∈ K: |λ̂_{F,v}(z) − log⁺ v(z)| ≤ B_v/(d − 1), with the one-sided bounds log c_v/(d − 1) ≤ λ̂_{F,v}(z) − log⁺ v(z) ≤ log C_v/(d − 1). Thus λ̂_{F,v} is a Weil local height for the divisor (∞), and at every nonarchimedean v of good reduction λ̂_{F,v} = log⁺ v.

d ≥ 2 Res(F) ≠ 0

λ̂(z) − log⁺ v(z) = G(z, 1) − log ‖(z, 1)‖ since ‖(z, 1)‖ = max(v(z), 1); apply DY.2/escape-rate-sub-log-norm-bounds. The good reduction case is DY.2/escape-rate-of-good-reduction.

d ≥ 2 Res(F) ≠ 0 F₁(z, 1) ≠ 0

F(z, 1) = F₁(z, 1)·(f(z), 1), so by DY.2/escape-rate-homogeneity G(F(z, 1)) = G(f(z), 1) + log v(F₁(z, 1)). By DY.2/escape-rate-functional-equation G(F(z, 1)) = d·G(z, 1); rearrange.

### 2.55 The escape potential on the Berkovich line

Setting: K is a complete nonarchimedean field (algebraically closed where stated, e.g. ℂ_v) with absolute value |·|; P^{1,an}_K = A^{1,an}_K ∪ {∞} is the Berkovich projective line of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0, whose points x ∈ A^{1,an}_K are multiplicative seminorms g ↦ [g]_x on K[T] extending |·|, with the weakest topology making every x ↦ [g]_x continuous; When K is algebraically closed with nontrivial absolute value, ℙ¹(K) is dense in P^{1,an}_K. The disc point ζ_{a,r} is the translated Gauss seminorm (equal to the sup-norm on D(a, r) under those hypotheses) and ζ_{0,1} is the Gauss point; a rational map f acts by its analytification f^{an} ([g]_{f^{an}(x)} = [g ∘ f]_x in an affine chart where the rational expression is defined). The Laplacian Δ on P^{1,an}_K is the one of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.1, normalised as in DeMarco–Krieger–Ye: Δ log max([T], 1) = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} − δ_∞ (the negative of Baker–Rumely's). For a lift F of degree d ≥ 2 with Res(F) ≠ 0, the Berkovich escape potential ĝ_F : P^{1,an}_K → ℝ is ĝ_F(x) = lim_n (d^{−n} log max([Fⁿ₀(T, 1)]_x, [Fⁿ₁(T, 1)]_x) − log max([T]_x, 1)) for x ∈ A^{1,an}_K and ĝ_F(∞) = g_{F,v}([1 : 0]). It is continuous and bounded, and when K is algebraically closed with nontrivial norm, it is the unique continuous extension of the Green function g_{F,v} of DY.2/dynamical-green-function. The extended local canonical height is λ̂^{an}_F = ĝ_F + log max([T], 1) on A^{1,an}_K.

K complete nonarchimedean d ≥ 2 Res(F) ≠ 0 The uniqueness from classical values needs K algebraically closed and its absolute value nontrivial; the seminorm construction itself works over any complete nonarchimedean K.

On A^{1,an}_K the defining sequence converges uniformly (DY.2/berkovich-lift-bounds), and each term is continuous in the Gelfand topology (TB.0), so ĝ_F is continuous on A^{1,an}_K. Near ∞ use the chart u = 1/T: in the coordinates (X₁, X₀) the same construction applies to the swapped lift, and the two formulas agree on A^{1,an}_K ∖ {0} (homogeneity, DY.2/escape-rate-homogeneity, applied seminorm-wise); this gives continuity at ∞. On type I points the limit is g_{F,v} (the evaluation seminorm at a is g ↦ |g(a)|); for algebraically closed K with nontrivial norm, uniqueness of the extension follows from density of ℙ¹(K) in P^{1,an}_K (TB.0).

### 2.56 The canonical measure at an archimedean place

Let f be a rational map of degree d ≥ 2 over ℂ with lift F, and g_F = dynamical-green-function at the usual absolute value, a continuous function on the Riemann sphere ℙ¹(ℂ) = OnePoint ℂ (= P^{1,an}_ℂ). With Δ the measure-valued Laplacian on ℙ¹(ℂ) normalised as dd^c (Δ log|z| = δ₀ on ℂ, so Δ log⁺|z| = ω − δ_∞ with ω the normalised arc length on the unit circle), the archimedean canonical measure is µ_{f,∞} = Δg_F + ω. Equivalently Δλ̂_{F,∞} = µ_{f,∞} − δ_∞, and on ℂ µ_{f,∞} = (1/2π)·Δ_eucl(G_F(z, 1)) in the sense of distributions. For v an archimedean place of a number field K one uses the embedding K → ℂ of v.

d ≥ 2 The measure-valued sphere Laplacian is supplied on differences of subharmonic potentials with Radon Riesz measures; the escape potential belongs to this domain. Continuity alone does not give a measure-valued Laplacian.

On each affine chart the escape potential is a locally uniform limit of subharmonic functions, by DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto, so it has a positive Radon Riesz measure. Subtracting the chart reference potential gives the global continuous g_F in the differences-of-subharmonic domain. Use the exact sphere Riesz/Laplacian contract retained in the DY.2 continuation’s gap; no measure Laplacian is asserted for an arbitrary continuous function. Define µ_{f,∞} = Δg_F + ω; it does not depend on the lift, since g_{cF} − g_F is constant.

### 2.58 Gauss Julia set at good reduction

For a degree-d≥2 good-reduction map over K, J_Ber={ζ_G}. Every point outside ζ_G lies in F_Ber. If f has potentially good reduction, the Julia set is the transported type-II point.

K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted. Good reduction, with the potential-good-reduction conclusion obtained by conjugacy.

A residue component either has a periodic forward itinerary, omitting all other components, or has a wandering itinerary, omitting a predecessor component. Thus every point outside Gauss has a stable neighborhood. Prove Gauss is Julia directly: a weak-open neighborhood contains all but finitely many residue components. Any components omitted by all its forward images form a finite backward-invariant residue set. After an iterate each omitted residue direction is fixed with full local degree; forward images of the neighborhood’s thin annulus fill that component except at most one classical point. The omitted complement is therefore finite, even for pure Frobenius. Transport under PGL₂. This direct proof does not depend on Julia nonemptiness from Fatou-component classification.

### 2.63 The canonical measure µ_{f,v} on the Berkovich line

Setting: K is a complete nonarchimedean field (algebraically closed where stated, e.g. ℂ_v) with absolute value |·|; P^{1,an}_K = A^{1,an}_K ∪ {∞} is the Berkovich projective line of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0, whose points x ∈ A^{1,an}_K are multiplicative seminorms g ↦ [g]_x on K[T] extending |·|, with the weakest topology making every x ↦ [g]_x continuous; When K is algebraically closed with nontrivial absolute value, ℙ¹(K) is dense in P^{1,an}_K. The disc point ζ_{a,r} is the translated Gauss seminorm (equal to the sup-norm on D(a, r) under those hypotheses) and ζ_{0,1} is the Gauss point; a rational map f acts by its analytification f^{an} ([g]_{f^{an}(x)} = [g ∘ f]_x in an affine chart where the rational expression is defined). The Laplacian Δ on P^{1,an}_K is the one of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.1, normalised as in DeMarco–Krieger–Ye: Δ log max([T], 1) = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} − δ_∞ (the negative of Baker–Rumely's). For a rational map f of degree d ≥ 2 over K with lift F, the canonical measure is µ_{f,v} = Δĝ_F + δ_{ζ_{0,1}}, a Borel measure on P^{1,an}_K; equivalently Δλ̂^{an}_F = µ_{f,v} − δ_∞ (DeMarco–Krieger–Ye's normalisation). It does not depend on the lift (ĝ_{cF} − ĝ_F is constant, and Δ kills constants). For K not algebraically closed one works over the completion of an algebraic closure (ℂ_v); the measure is invariant under the continuous automorphisms of that field over K.

K complete nonarchimedean d ≥ 2

For the n-step potential g_n, Poincaré–Lelong and pullback compatibility (TB.1) give δ_ζ + Δg_n = d^{−n}(fⁿ)^*δ_ζ, a positive probability measure. Hence the total variation of Δg_n is at most 2. Uniform convergence g_n → ĝ_F (DY.2/berkovich-escape-potential), together with TB.1 weak continuity of the Laplacian under this uniform variation bound, produces a finite signed Δĝ_F and its positive probability measure δ_ζ + Δĝ_F. Uniform convergence alone would not imply bounded differential variation. Define µ_{f,v} = Δĝ_F + δ_{ζ_{0,1}}; independence of the lift follows from berkovichEscapePotential_const_smul_lift.

### 2.64 The archimedean canonical measure: mass, invariance, no atoms

For f of degree d ≥ 2 over ℂ: µ_{f,∞} is a Borel probability measure on ℙ¹(ℂ) without atoms, Δλ̂_{F,∞} = µ_{f,∞} − δ_∞, and f^*µ_{f,∞} = d·µ_{f,∞}, f_*µ_{f,∞} = µ_{f,∞}.

d ≥ 2 The measure-valued sphere Laplacian is supplied on differences of subharmonic potentials with Radon Riesz measures; the escape potential belongs to this domain. Continuity alone does not give a measure-valued Laplacian.

Total mass 1: the distributional Laplacian pairs to zero with the constant test function on the compact sphere. Since g_F is in the stated Riesz domain, its Laplacian is a signed measure of total mass zero. Positivity: on ℂ, λ̂_{F,∞} = G_F(·, 1) is a uniform limit of subharmonic functions, hence subharmonic; near ∞ use the chart 1/z (DY.2/escape-rate-conjugation). No atoms: a measure with a continuous potential has no atoms (Riesz decomposition). Invariance: apply Δ to the functional equation of DY.2/local-canonical-height-functional-equation, with Δ(h ∘ f) = f^*Δh and Δ log|F₁(z, 1)| = Σ δ_{zeros} − deg·δ_∞, exactly as in DY.2/canonical-measure-invariance; then f_* f^* = d.

### 2.65 Behaviour of λ̂_{F,v} at ∞

Let K be a normed field and v its norm. Then λ̂_{F,v}(z) − log v(z) → c_v(F) := G_{F,v}(1, 0) as v(z) → ∞. G is continuous at (1, 0) (DY.2/escape-rate-continuous, on the completion if K is not complete, DY.2/escape-rate-base-change), and (1, 1/z) → (1, 0). ### 2.70 Complex canonical measure comparison and support

The parent archimedean measure μ_{f,∞}=Δg_F+ω equals ν_f from the complex transfer limit. Hence its native support is the classical Julia set, and it is the unique atom-free balanced Radon probability. More generally it is the unique balanced Radon probability with zero mass on E, and every nonexceptional point has normalized preimages converging to μ_{f,∞}.

f∈C(z), algebraic degree d≥2, acting holomorphically on the compact Riemann sphere with spherical topology. The sphere measure-valued Laplacian supplier must first construct the parent measure and establish its positivity, mass one, atomlessness and balance.

The parent measure is atom-free, hence μ(E)=0 because E is finite. For each continuous ψ, balance says ∫A^nψ dμ=∫ψ dμ. Transfer convergence holds at every point outside E and |A^nψ|≤||ψ||; dominated convergence identifies ∫ψdμ with ∫ψdν. Equality of Radon measures on continuous tests proves μ=ν. The same reasoning proves uniqueness for every exceptional-null balanced probability. Support equality and preimage convergence now transport through the equality.

### 2.72 Worked example: z² − z − 1, a polynomial with good reduction everywhere

Let f(z) = z² − z − 1 over ℚ with lift F = (X₀² − X₀X₁ − X₁², X₁²). Then: (a) Res(F) = 1, so f has good reduction at every prime p; G_{F,p} = log ‖·‖_p, λ̂_{F,p} = log⁺|·|_p and µ_{f,p} = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} for every p. (b) The points ±1 form a 2-cycle with multiplier λ₂ = f′(1)f′(−1) = −3, and G_{F,∞}(±1, 1) = 0, so every local canonical height of ±1 vanishes and ĥ_f(±1) = 0. (c) Modulo 2 the cycle reduces to the fixed point 1 of f̃ = z² + z + 1 over 𝔽₂, with reduced multiplier 1 = (−3)~: m = 1, r = 1 and n = 2 = m·r·p, the p-power case of DY.2/periods-under-good-reduction (e = 1, within Hutz's bound e ≤ 3 and Zieve's e ≤ 1 over ℚ₂). (d) Modulo 3 the cycle reduces to the 2-cycle {1, 2} of z² + 2z + 2 over 𝔽₃ (m = n = 2), and its multiplier reduces to (−3)~ = 0: the reduced cycle is superattracting although the cycle upstairs is repelling at ∞. (e) The fixed points 1 ± √2 have multipliers 1 ± 2√2; in ℚ₇ (√2 ≡ 3 mod 7) they reduce to the fixed points 4, 5 of f̃ over 𝔽₇, whose multipliers 0, 2 are the residues of 1 ± 2√2. (f) Holomorphic fixed-point formula: 1/(1 − 0) + 1/(1 − (1 + 2√2)) + 1/(1 − (1 − 2√2)) = 1 (∞ has multiplier 0).

f(z) = z² − z − 1 over ℚ

Res(F) = F₀(1, 0)² = 1 because F₁ = X₁² has the double root [1 : 0] (DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map); apply DY.2/escape-rate-of-good-reduction, DY.2/local-canonical-height-weil-bound and DY.2/canonical-measure-of-good-reduction. f(1) = −1, f(−1) = 1; multipliers by DY.2/multiplier-chain-rule. At ∞: ‖Fⁿ(z, 1)‖_∞ ≥ |Fⁿ₁(z, 1)| = 1 gives G_{F,∞}(z, 1) ≥ 0, and the bounded orbit gives G_{F,∞}(±1, 1) ≤ 0 (DY.2/escape-rate-nonpos-iff-bounded-orbit); sum with DY.2/local-decomposition-of-canonical-height. Reduction mod 2: f̃ = z² + z + 1, f̃(1) = 1, f̃′(1) = 2·1 + 1 = 1 in 𝔽₂ (DY.2/multiplier-reduction; λ̃₂ = f̃′(1)² = 1 ≡ −3). Reduction mod 3: f̃(1) = 2, f̃(2) = 1; f̃′(1)·f̃′(2) = 1·3 ≡ 0. Mod 7: 3² ≡ 2, fixed points 1 + 3 = 4 and 1 − 3 ≡ 5, f̃′ = 2z − 1 gives 7 ≡ 0 and 9 ≡ 2. Formula (f): direct computation with the multipliers of (a)–(e) (Benedetto's Theorem 1.6).

### 2.73 µ_{f,v} is a probability measure

Setting: K is a complete nonarchimedean field (algebraically closed where stated, e.g. ℂ_v) with absolute value |·|; P^{1,an}_K = A^{1,an}_K ∪ {∞} is the Berkovich projective line of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0, whose points x ∈ A^{1,an}_K are multiplicative seminorms g ↦ [g]_x on K[T] extending |·|, with the weakest topology making every x ↦ [g]_x continuous; When K is algebraically closed with nontrivial absolute value, ℙ¹(K) is dense in P^{1,an}_K. The disc point ζ_{a,r} is the translated Gauss seminorm (equal to the sup-norm on D(a, r) under those hypotheses) and ζ_{0,1} is the Gauss point; a rational map f acts by its analytification f^{an} ([g]_{f^{an}(x)} = [g ∘ f]_x in an affine chart where the rational expression is defined). The Laplacian Δ on P^{1,an}_K is the one of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.1, normalised as in DeMarco–Krieger–Ye: Δ log max([T], 1) = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} − δ_∞ (the negative of Baker–Rumely's). µ_{f,v} is a positive Borel measure of total mass 1 on P^{1,an}_K, and it gives no mass to type I points.

K complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean d ≥ 2

Total mass: Δĝ_F has total mass 0 because ĝ_F is continuous on the compact space P^{1,an}_K (TB.1); so µ(P^{1,an}_K) = 1. Positivity on A^{1,an}_K: λ̂^{an}_F is the uniform limit (DY.2/berkovich-lift-bounds) of u_n = d^{−n} log max([Fⁿ₀(T, 1)], [Fⁿ₁(T, 1)]), and each u_n is subharmonic on A^{1,an}_K (log [P] is subharmonic for P ∈ K[T] and a maximum of subharmonic functions is subharmonic, TB.1); uniform limits of subharmonic functions are subharmonic (TB.1), so µ|_{A^{1,an}} = Δλ̂^{an}_F|_{A^{1,an}} ≥ 0 (DY.2/laplacian-of-local-canonical-height). Positivity at ∞: apply the previous step to the conjugate of f by z ↦ 1/z, whose canonical measure is the pull-back of µ_{f,v} (DY.2/canonical-measure-conjugation). No mass on type I points: ĝ_F is a continuous potential (TB.1).

### 2.74 Potential good reduction ⟺ µ_{f,v} is a point mass at a type II point

Setting: K is a complete nonarchimedean field (algebraically closed where stated, e.g. ℂ_v) with absolute value |·|; P^{1,an}_K = A^{1,an}_K ∪ {∞} is the Berkovich projective line of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0, whose points x ∈ A^{1,an}_K are multiplicative seminorms g ↦ [g]_x on K[T] extending |·|, with the weakest topology making every x ↦ [g]_x continuous; When K is algebraically closed with nontrivial absolute value, ℙ¹(K) is dense in P^{1,an}_K. The disc point ζ_{a,r} is the translated Gauss seminorm (equal to the sup-norm on D(a, r) under those hypotheses) and ζ_{0,1} is the Gauss point; a rational map f acts by its analytification f^{an} ([g]_{f^{an}(x)} = [g ∘ f]_x in an affine chart where the rational expression is defined). The Laplacian Δ on P^{1,an}_K is the one of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.1, normalised as in DeMarco–Krieger–Ye: Δ log max([T], 1) = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} − δ_∞ (the negative of Baker–Rumely's). Let K be algebraically closed. f has potentially good reduction at v (some φ⁻¹ ∘ f ∘ φ, φ ∈ PGL₂(K), has good reduction) if and only if µ_{f,v} = δ_ξ for a type II point ξ ∈ P^{1,an}_K; in that case φ can be any Möbius map with φ^{an}(ζ_{0,1}) = ξ.

K complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean d ≥ 2

(⟹) If f^φ = φ⁻¹∘f∘φ has good reduction, µ_{f^φ} = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} (DY.2/canonical-measure-of-good-reduction), so by DY.2/canonical-measure-conjugation µ_f = δ_{φ^{an}(ζ_{0,1})}, and φ^{an} maps type II points to type II points (TB.1). (⟸) PGL₂(K) acts transitively on type II points (TB.1); choose φ with φ^{an}(ζ_{0,1}) = ξ. Then µ_{f^φ} = (φ^{an})^*δ_ξ = δ_{ζ_{0,1}}, and f^φ has good reduction by DY.2/good-reduction-of-canonical-measure.

### 2.75 Entropy of the canonical measure

The invariant probability ν_f=μ_{f,∞} has Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy h_{ν_f}(f)=log d. The Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy carrier and partition API belong to the generic ergodic supplier; this packet does not define a competing entropy.

f∈C(z), algebraic degree d≥2, acting holomorphically on the compact Riemann sphere with spherical topology.

Pushforward invariance follows by duality from balance. Critical points have zero mass since ν is atom-free. Disintegrate ν over the inverse fibres; almost every fibre has d distinct noncritical points, each conditional weight 1/d. The fibre entropy is log d. Use the generic conditional-entropy formula to obtain hν(f)≥log d; combine with the measure-to-topological entropy inequality and the native topological entropy result to obtain equality.

### 2.76 Power-map acceptance across places

For f(z)=z^d, d≥2, on P¹(C), J is the unit circle and μ is normalized angular probability there; F consists of |z|<1 and |z|>1 including infinity, and E={0,∞}. On P¹(K) the same map has good reduction, J_I=∅, J_Ber={ζ_G}, and μ=δ_{ζ_G}. In characteristic p and d=p^r, the nonarchimedean classical exceptional set is P¹(overline(F_p)), even though the Berkovich Julia set remains the Gauss singleton.

Separate complex and nonarchimedean specializations of the same power map; d≥2.

The parent escape-rate formula is log max(|z|,1). Its complex normalized Laplacian is angular probability on the unit circle; its nonarchimedean Laplacian is Gauss Dirac minus infinity Dirac. Iterates converge to 0 or infinity off the complex unit circle, while radial perturbations on the circle are eventually separated. Use good reduction for the nonarchimedean conclusions and exceptional classification for the characteristic-p warning.
