### 2.77 Nonarchimedean preimage equidistribution

Let μ_f be the parent canonical Radon probability on P¹,an_K, and E the classical exceptional set. For every Radon probability ρ with ρ(E)=0, d^(-n)(f^n)*ρ converges weakly to μ_f. Conversely, convergence implies ρ(E)=0. Pullbacks count analytic local degrees, including inseparable multiplicity. In particular normalized preimages of any a outside E converge, and μ_f is the unique balanced probability assigning E mass zero.

K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.

Identify the parent Δg_F+δ_G measure with the telescoping pullback construction of FRL Proposition-Definition 3.1: their potential difference is constant by uniqueness. Represent ρ−δ_G=Δu with u≤0, possibly singular. Prove d^(-n)u∘f^n→0 on the hyperbolic line, then use Hartogs and weak Laplacian convergence. Near exceptional attracting cycles use ρ’s arbitrarily small mass in small discs. Outside those basins and for separable degree >1, pass to an iterate and use diam(fζ)≥C diam(ζ)^(d−1); the resulting (d−1)^n growth is dominated by d^n. For separable degree one normalize to a Frobenius power. The residue orbit is periodic or wanders through disjoint classes; in the latter case their ρ-masses tend to zero. This handles the infinite exceptional set without an at-most-two assertion. Any positive ρ-mass on the countable classical E gives positive mass to a finite exceptional cycle. Its periodic atomic pullback part cannot converge to the parent measure, which has no type-I atoms. For balanced exceptional-null ρ, convergence of its constant normalized-pullback sequence proves uniqueness.

### 2.78 Worked example: (z^p − z)/p, bad reduction with Haar canonical measure

Let p be prime and f(z) = (z^p − z)/p over ℚ_p, with normalised lift F = (X₀^p − X₀X₁^{p−1}, pX₁^p). Then: (a) Res(F) = p^p (e.g. 4 for p = 2, 27 for p = 3), so f has bad reduction at p; the fixed point 0 has multiplier −1/p and the fixed points with z^{p−1} = 1 + p have multiplier p + 1 − 1/p, all of absolute value p > 1, so f has no potentially good reduction at p. (b) G_{F,p}(z, 1) = λ̂_{F,p}(z) = −(log p)/(p − 1) for z ∈ ℤ_p and = log|z|_p for |z|_p > 1; the filled Julia set of f in ℂ_p is ℤ_p. (c) λ̂_{F,p}(z) = ∫_{ℤ_p} log|z − y|_p dH(y) for all z ∈ ℂ_p, with H the Haar probability measure of ℤ_p, and λ̂^{an}_F(ζ_{0,1}) = 0. (d) µ_{f,p} = H, viewed on ℤ_p ⊂ ℙ¹(ℂ_p) ⊂ P^{1,an}_{ℂ_p}; in particular µ_{f,p} is not a point mass (DY.2/potential-good-reduction-iff-point-mass).

p prime K = ℚ_p, computations over ℂ_p

(a) Res(F) by the Sylvester determinant (DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map); the multipliers by DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier (f′(z) = (p z^{p−1} − 1)/p); DY.2/good-reduction-multipliers-integral excludes potential good reduction. (b) For z ∈ ℤ_p, z^p ≡ z mod p, so f(ℤ_p) ⊆ ℤ_p; Fⁿ₁(z, 1) = p^{(pⁿ−1)/(p−1)} and Fⁿ₀(z, 1) = fⁿ(z)·Fⁿ₁(z, 1), so ‖Fⁿ(z, 1)‖_p = p^{−(pⁿ−1)/(p−1)} and G = −(log p)/(p − 1). For |x₀| > |x₁| one has ‖F(x)‖ = ‖x‖^p and again |F₀(x)| > |F₁(x)|, so G(z, 1) = log|z|_p. Points of ℂ_p ∖ ℤ_p have unbounded orbits (Benedetto, Example 4.40), This is the polynomial orbit, not the homogeneous orbit: homogeneous G need not be positive outside ℤ_p, since λ̂_F equals the polynomial escape rate minus log p/(p − 1). (c) Put u(z) = ∫ log|z − y| dH(y). Then u = −(log p)/(p − 1) on ℤ_p (the H-measure of {|y − z| = p^{−k}} is p^{−k}(1 − 1/p)) and u = log|z| for |z| > 1, For arbitrary z in the unit disc of ℂ_p, a ball of radius p^{−k} around z either misses ℤ_p or has Haar mass at most p^{−k}. Integrating these ball bounds gives −log p/(p − 1) ≤ u(z) ≤ 0; outside the unit disc u(z) = log|z|. Thus u − log⁺|·| is bounded throughout ℂ_p. For w ∈ ℤ_p, f(z) − w = (1/p)·∏_{f(y) = w}(z − y) with the p preimages in ℤ_p (Hensel), and f^*H = p·H (f maps each disc y + p^kℤ_p, k ≥ 1, bijectively onto f(y) + p^{k−1}ℤ_p); hence u(f(z)) = p·u(z) + log p = p·u(z) − log|F₁(z, 1)|_p, the functional equation of λ̂ (DY.2/local-canonical-height-functional-equation). Since f is a polynomial every orbit in ℂ_p avoids ∞, and DY.2/green-function-uniqueness gives u = λ̂. At the Gauss point every Fⁿ₀(T, 1) has Gauss norm 1, so λ̂^{an}(ζ_{0,1}) = 0 = ∫ log max(1, |y|) dH(y). (d) By continuity (DY.2/berkovich-escape-potential, TB.1) λ̂^{an}_F(x) = ∫ log[T − y]_x dH(y) on A^{1,an}, whose Laplacian is H − δ_∞ (TB.1); by DY.2/laplacian-of-local-canonical-height µ_{f,p} = H.

### 2.79 Worked example: (z² + 1)/(3z), the algebraic-closure hypothesis is needed

Let f(z) = (z² + 1)/(3z) over ℚ with lift F = (X₀² + X₁², 3X₀X₁). Then: (a) Res(F) = 9, so f has good reduction at every p ≠ 3 and bad reduction at 3. (b) Over ℚ₃: ‖F(x)‖₃ = ‖x‖₃² for all x ∈ ℚ₃², so G_{F,3} = log ‖·‖₃ on ℚ₃² and g_{F,3} = 0 on ℙ¹(ℚ₃) although f has bad reduction; over ℂ₃, G_{F,3}(i, 1) = −(1/2)·log 3 < 0 = log ‖(i, 1)‖₃. So DY.2/good-reduction-of-escape-rate fails without an algebraically closed residue field. (c) The fixed points are ∞ (multiplier 3) and ±1/√2 (multiplier −1/3); |−1/3|₃ = 3 > 1, so f has no potentially good reduction at 3 and µ_{f,3} is not a point mass. (d) Reduction does not commute with f at 3: i and i + 3 have the same reduction in ℙ¹(𝔽̄₃) but f(i) = 0 and f(i + 3) = (2i + 3)/(i + 3) reduce to 0 and 2. (e) At p = 2 (good reduction, f̃(z) = z + 1/z over 𝔽₂): the three fixed points ∞, ±1/√2 all reduce to ∞ (|±1/√2|₂ = √2 > 1), the triple fixed point of f̃, and their multipliers 3, −1/3, −1/3 all reduce to 1, the multiplier of ∞ for f̃. (f) Holomorphic fixed-point formula: 1/(1 − 3) + 2/(1 + 1/3) = 1.

f(z) = (z² + 1)/(3z) over ℚ

(a) Res(F) = F₁(i, 1)·F₁(−i, 1) = (3i)(−3i) = 9 (Sylvester determinant, DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map). (b) For x ∈ ℚ₃² primitive, x₀² + x₁² ≢ 0 mod 3 because −1 is not a square mod 3, so ‖F(x)‖₃ = 1 = ‖x‖₃²; iterate (F(x) is again primitive) to get G = log ‖·‖ (DY.2/escape-rate). Over ℂ₃: F(i, 1) = (0, 3i), F(0, 3i) = (−9, 0), and (1, 0) is fixed up to squaring of the scalar, so ‖Fⁿ(i, 1)‖₃ = 3^{−2^{n−1}} for n ≥ 1 and G(i, 1) = −(1/2)·log 3. (c) Multipliers by DY.2/multiplier-of-a-periodic-cycle (at ∞: tr DF(1, 0) − 2 = 5 − 2 = 3) and DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier (f′ = (z² − 1)/(3z²) = −1/3 at z² = 1/2); conclude with DY.2/good-reduction-multipliers-integral and DY.2/potential-good-reduction-iff-point-mass. (d) (i + 3)² + 1 = 3(3 + 2i) and 3(i + 3) give f(i + 3) = (2i + 3)/(i + 3), a 3-adic unit reducing to 2ĩ/ĩ = 2. (e) Over 𝔽₂, F̃ = (X₀² + X₁², X₀X₁) has fixed-point form X₁F̃₀ − X₀F̃₁ = X₁³, and tr DF̃(1, 0) − 2 = 1 in 𝔽₂ (DY.2/multiplier-reduction; −1/3 ≡ 1 and 3 ≡ 1 in ℤ₂/2). (f) Direct computation with the multipliers of (c) (Benedetto's Theorem 1.6).

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-complex-maximal-entropy-uniqueness"></a>

### 2.80 Unique maximal-entropy measure

If η is any f-invariant Borel probability on P¹(C) with h_η(f)=log d, then η=ν_f=μ_{f,∞}. Thus the parent archimedean maximal-entropy endpoint is supplied by the identification, the entropy value and this uniqueness theorem.

f∈C(z), algebraic degree d≥2, acting holomorphically on the compact Riemann sphere with spherical topology. Invariant means pushforward invariance, not balance; competitors need not be atom-free.

For a distinct ergodic η, singularity with ν and local inverse branches produce a positive-η set whose preferred inverse-branch blocks occur with frequency above the uniform 1/N threshold. Apply the existing Birkhoff node to the indicator of this positive-η set. Count branch words with this excessive frequency using binomial estimates/Stirling: their growth rate is θ<N. The critical-disc Bowen-net construction contributes only a polynomial factor. Lyubich’s positive-measure-set entropy lemma, proved using Shannon–McMillan–Breiman, gives hη(f)<log d. For general invariant η use the generic ergodic decomposition and entropy integration theorem; almost every ergodic component of a maximizing η must maximize and thus equal ν.

### 2.82 µ_{f,∞} is Lyubich's measure of maximal entropy

For f of degree d ≥ 2 over ℂ, µ_{f,∞} equals the Lyubich / Freire–Lopes–Mañé measure: it is the unique Borel probability measure on ℙ¹(ℂ) without atoms with f^*µ = d·µ; for every non-exceptional a ∈ ℙ¹(ℂ), d^{−n}·Σ_{fⁿ(z) = a} δ_z → µ_{f,∞} weakly (with multiplicity); and µ_{f,∞} is the unique f-invariant measure of maximal entropy log d (Lyubich; Mañé). The Haar-measure description for Lattès maps is a downstream DY.6 application of this identification.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-berkovich-blowing-up-minimality"></a>

### 2.83 Berkovich blowing up and minimality

If an open U meets J_Ber, ⋃_{n≥0}f^n(U) contains P¹,an_K\E, with E the classical exceptional set. Consequently J_Ber is contained in every closed backward-invariant S with S\E nonempty; the Julia set is the smallest nonempty closed completely invariant set not contained in E. If J_Ber has at least two points, it has no isolated point.

K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.

If U meets J, its forward saturation has finite complement A by the definition. Since A is backward invariant, every point of A has finite grand orbit. Classical points in A belong to E. A nonclassical point in A forces potential good reduction by finite-grand-orbit rigidity. The singleton Julia point would then lie in U, contradicting its omission. For a∈S\E every U meeting J contains a backward iterate of a. Closedness and backward invariance imply J⊆S. If a Julia point were isolated, apply blowing up to a neighborhood meeting J only there. Complete invariance then forces its backward orbit to be finite, and the nonclassical rigidity forces a singleton Julia set.

### 2.84 Berkovich canonical measure has Julia support

For every f of degree ≥2 over K, the native measure support of the parent canonical measure is exactly J_Ber: supp μ_f=J_Ber. The support is nonempty and compact, f⁻¹(supp μ_f)=supp μ_f=f(supp μ_f), and μ_f gives the classical exceptional set mass zero.

K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.

The previous containment theorem gives supp μ⊆J and nonempty support. Local-degree measure pullback has support f⁻¹(supp μ); balance f*μ=dμ gives backward invariance of support. Closedness comes from the native support theorem; compactness follows from the native compact analytic carrier. The parent canonical-measure-is-probability theorem gives no type-I atoms; E is countable, so μ(E)=0. Conull support then has a point outside E. Apply Julia minimality to S=supp μ for the reverse containment. Pushforward invariance and surjectivity give the image equality.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-berkovich-julia-singleton-dichotomy"></a>

### 2.86 Singleton and perfect Julia sets

The following are equivalent: J_Ber is a singleton; J_Ber is at most countable; J_Ber has an isolated point; f has potentially good reduction. In that case the point is type II and μ_f is its Dirac mass. Otherwise J_Ber is nonempty, uncountable and perfect.

K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.

Potential good reduction gives the transported Gauss singleton. A countable nonempty compact Hausdorff space has an isolated point by the Baire theorem: without isolated points it would be a countable union of nowhere-dense singletons. An isolated Julia point forces a singleton by blowing up. Complete invariance then gives a nonclassical finite grand orbit, since classical exceptional points are Fatou; rigidity gives potential good reduction. Alternatively singleton support of a Radon probability is Dirac, and the parent point-mass criterion gives the same converse.

### 3.1 The order of a binary form at a point of ℙ¹

Let K be a field, F ∈ K[X, Y] a binary form and P = [a : b] ∈ ℙ¹(K), given by a nonzero vector (a, b). The order of F at P is ord_P F := the largest k ≥ 0 with (bX − aY)^k ∣ F in K[X, Y], i.e. Mathlib's multiplicity of the linear form ℓ_P = bX − aY in F (with Mathlib's junk value when F = 0). It depends only on the point: replacing (a, b) by (ca, cb), c ≠ 0, multiplies ℓ_P by the unit c. For F ≠ 0 homogeneous of degree D, ord_[a:1] F is the root multiplicity of a in the dehomogenisation F(X, 1), and ord_[1:0] F = D − deg F(X, 1). Points over an extension L of K are treated by mapping F to L[X, Y].

K is any field; F ∈ K[X, Y] = MvPolynomial (Fin 2) K with X = X 0, Y = X 1. The order is used only for F ≠ 0 and P ≠ 0; no algebraic closedness is assumed in the definition.

Define ord_P F := multiplicity(ℓ_P, F) with ℓ_P = P₁·X − P₀·Y (mathlib:multiplicity). ℓ_P has degree one, hence is irreducible and prime in the unique factorisation domain K[X, Y] (instance inference: MvPolynomial over a field is a unique factorisation monoid), so ord_P(F·G) = ord_P F + ord_P G for F, G ≠ 0. Scaling P by c ≠ 0 scales ℓ_P by c, which does not change the multiplicity. Dehomogenisation: for P = [a : 1] and F homogeneous of degree D, F = (X − aY)^k·H with H(a, 1) ≠ 0 if and only if F(X, 1) = (X − a)^k·H(X, 1) with H(a, 1) ≠ 0; hence ord_[a:1] F = rootMultiplicity a (F(X, 1)) (mathlib:MvPolynomial.aeval, mathlib:Polynomial.rootMultiplicity). At ∞ the power of Y dividing F is D − deg F(X, 1) (mathlib:MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous).

*Needs:* `mathlib:multiplicity`; `mathlib:MvPolynomial.aeval`; `mathlib:Polynomial.rootMultiplicity`; `mathlib:MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous`.

([ms95](#source-parent-ms95), §4, proof of Theorem 4.1, display (21), printed p. 100 — Multiplicities of the roots of a binary form on ℙ¹ are the orders defined here.)

The reusable interface consists of the following statements.

- **`binaryFormOrder`** (constructor): ord_P F ∈ ℕ for F ∈ K[X, Y] and P : Fin 2 → K.
- **`binaryFormOrder_eq_zero_iff`** (characterisation): For a nonzero homogeneous F and P ≠ 0: ord_P F = 0 iff F(P) ≠ 0.
- **`binaryFormOrder_mul`** (simp): For F, G ≠ 0 and P ≠ 0: ord_P(FG) = ord_P F + ord_P G.
- **`binaryFormOrder_smul_point`** (extensionality): ord_{cP} F = ord_P F for c ≠ 0: the order depends only on the point of ℙ¹.
- **`binaryFormOrder_affine`** (compatibility): For F ≠ 0 homogeneous: ord_[a:1] F = rootMultiplicity a (F(X, 1)) (Mathlib's Polynomial.rootMultiplicity).
- **`pow_dvd_iff_le_binaryFormOrder`** (characterisation): For F ≠ 0, P ≠ 0: ℓ_P^k ∣ F iff k ≤ ord_P F.

**Checks.**

- **`TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics.binaryFormOrder_test_zero`** (computation): ord_[0:1](X²Y) = 2 over ℚ.
- **`TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics.binaryFormOrder_test_infinity`** (computation): ord_[1:0](X²Y) = 1 over ℚ (the order at ∞ counts the power of Y).
- **`TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics.binaryFormOrder_test_const`** (degenerate): A nonzero constant has order 0 at every point.

### 3.2 The n-th period polynomial Φₙ(φ) = Y·Fₙ − X·Gₙ

Let R be a commutative ring and φ = (F, G) a pair of forms in R[X, Y] (a lift of a self-map of ℙ¹). The composite lift of φⁿ is (F₀, G₀) = (X, Y) and (F_{n+1}, G_{n+1}) = (F(Fₙ, Gₙ), G(Fₙ, Gₙ)). The n-th period form is Φₙ(φ) := Y·Fₙ(X, Y) − X·Gₙ(X, Y) ∈ R[X, Y]. If F, G are homogeneous of degree d then Φₙ is homogeneous of degree dⁿ + 1; Φ₀ = 0; replacing the lift by (uF, uG), u ∈ R^×, multiplies Φₙ by u^{1 + d + ⋯ + d^{n−1}}. For a polynomial map f of degree d with lift (Y^d f(X/Y), Y^d), Φₙ(X, 1) = fⁿ(X) − X.

R is any commutative ring; convention X = X 0, Y = X 1, and the sign Y·Fₙ − X·Gₙ of Morton–Silverman (21). The lift, not only the rational map, is part of the data: the forms of φⁿ are the composite ones.

The composite lift is DY.0's iterate of the rational map (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); define Φₙ := Y·Fₙ − X·Gₙ. Homogeneity: Fₙ, Gₙ are homogeneous of degree dⁿ by induction, since substituting forms of degree dⁿ into forms of degree d gives forms of degree d^{n+1} (mathlib:MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous); hence Φₙ is homogeneous of degree dⁿ + 1. Φ₀ = Y·X − X·Y = 0. Scaling: (uF, uG) has composite lift u^{1+d+⋯+d^{n−1}}(Fₙ, Gₙ) by induction. For a polynomial map: Fₙ = Y^{dⁿ} fⁿ(X/Y) and Gₙ = Y^{dⁿ} by induction, so Φₙ(X, 1) = fⁿ(X) − X (mathlib:Polynomial.iterate_comp_eval).

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-0-rational-map-of-the-projective-line); `mathlib:MvPolynomial.aeval`; `mathlib:MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous`; `mathlib:Polynomial.iterate_comp_eval`.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-3-fixed-point-germ"></a>

### 3.3 The formal germ of a map at a fixed point

For a lift φ = (F, G) over a field K with F(0, 1) = 0 ≠ G(0, 1) (the point 0 = [0 : 1] is fixed), the germ of φ at 0 is g_φ := F(z, 1)·G(z, 1)⁻¹ ∈ K[[z]], a power series with constant coefficient 0 (G(z, 1) is a unit of K[[z]]). Its linear coefficient is the multiplier λ = φ′(0) of the fixed point (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.2/multiplier-of-a-periodic-cycle). For a germ g with constant coefficient 0, gⁿ denotes the n-fold substitution iterate (g⁰ = z, g^{n+1} = g ∘ gⁿ, Mathlib's PowerSeries.subst). A general fixed point P ∈ ℙ¹(K) is moved to 0 by a conjugation (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-conjugation), which leaves the multiplier unchanged.

K is a field; F(0, 1) = 0 and G(0, 1) ≠ 0 (for a morphism lift, F(0,1) = 0 already forces G(0,1) ≠ 0). The junk value of Mathlib's power-series inverse is irrelevant because G(0, 1) ≠ 0.

Dehomogenise: F(z, 1), G(z, 1) ∈ K[z] (mathlib:MvPolynomial.aeval), viewed in K[[z]] (mathlib:Polynomial.coeToPowerSeries.ringHom); G(z, 1) has nonzero constant term so is invertible. g_φ := F(z, 1)·G(z, 1)⁻¹; its constant coefficient is F(0,1)/G(0,1) = 0. Iteration uses mathlib:PowerSeries.subst, legitimate since the substituted series has constant coefficient 0 (mathlib:PowerSeries.HasSubst.of_constantCoeff_zero'). The coefficient of z in gⁿ is λⁿ (chain rule for substitution: the linear coefficient of g ∘ h is the product of those of g and h, mathlib:PowerSeries.coeff). Conjugating by z ↦ uz (u ≠ 0) replaces g(z) by u⁻¹g(uz), leaving the linear coefficient unchanged; this is the compatibility with DY.2's conjugation-invariant multiplier.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.2/multiplier-of-a-periodic-cycle`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-multiplier-of-a-periodic-cycle); `mathlib:MvPolynomial.aeval`; `mathlib:Polynomial.coeToPowerSeries.ringHom`; `mathlib:PowerSeries.subst`; `mathlib:PowerSeries.HasSubst.of_constantCoeff_zero'`; `mathlib:PowerSeries.coeff`.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-3-moebius-transform-of-a-multiplicity-profile"></a>

### 3.4 The Möbius transform of a multiplicity profile

Let r ≥ 1, let p be a prime or 0, let B : ℕ → ℤ, and put A(k) = B(v_p(k/r)) if r ∣ k and A(k) = 1 otherwise (v₀ ≡ 0). Then for every N ≥ 1: Σ_{k ∣ N} μ(N/k)·A(k) = [N = 1] + [N = r]·(B(0) − 1) + Σ_{a ≥ 1} [N = r·pᵃ]·(B(a) − B(a − 1)).

r ≥ 1; p = 0 or p prime; v_p = Mathlib's padicValNat, which is identically 0 on positive integers when p = 0.

Write A(k) = 1 + [r ∣ k]·β(v_p(k/r)) with β = B − 1. Σ_{k∣N} μ(N/k) = [N = 1] (mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.coe_moebius_mul_coe_zeta). The second part vanishes unless r ∣ N; then with M = N/r it is Σ_{j ∣ M} μ(M/j) β(v_p(j)). Write M = pᵃM′ with p ∤ M′ (for p = 0: a = 0, M′ = M); since μ is multiplicative (mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.isMultiplicative_moebius) the sum factors as (Σ_{i ≤ a} μ(p^{a−i}) β(i))·(Σ_{j′ ∣ M′} μ(M′/j′)) = (β(a) − β(a − 1))·[M′ = 1], with β(−1) := 0. Collecting terms gives the formula; for p = 0 only N = r survives, with value B(0) − 1.

For the family z² + c this is Φₙ(z, c) ∈ ℤ[z, c] of Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer and Morton.

### 3.6 An explicit height bound for preperiodic points

Let L be a number field and φ = (F₀, F₁) a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over L with a Nullstellensatz certificate: forms q(k, j) homogeneous of degree M with Σⱼ q(k, j)·Fⱼ = X_k^{M+d} for k = 0, 1. Let f be the induced map of ℙ¹(L). Then every preperiodic point P = [v] satisfies h(v) ≤ C/(d − 1), where h is Mathlib's logarithmic height Height.logHeight (relative to L) and C = log(2^{[L:ℚ]}·max(H(q), 1)) is the explicit constant of Height.logHeight_eval_ge (H(q) = Height.mulHeightBound q). For a morphism the certificate exists with M = d − 1 by dividing a resultant identity A·F₀ + B·F₁ = Res(F₀, F₁)·X_k^{2d−1} by the resultant.

L a number field with Mathlib's admissible absolute values; φ homogeneous of degree d ≥ 2; the certificate identities hold in L[X, Y]. x is preperiodic for f when some iterate fᵐ(x) is periodic (Mathlib: ∃ m, f^[m] x ∈ Function.periodicPts f); equivalently its forward orbit is finite.

For every v ≠ 0: h(F(v)) ≥ d·h(v) − C (mathlib:Height.logHeight_eval_ge with ι' = Fin 2, N = d; the certificate evaluated at v gives its hypothesis). h is invariant under scaling (mathlib:Height.logHeight_smul_eq_logHeight), so it is a function on ℙ¹(L), and h(f(P)) = h(F(v)). If P is preperiodic its forward orbit is finite; let Q be a point of the orbit of maximal height. Then f(Q) is in the orbit, so h(Q) ≥ h(f(Q)) ≥ d·h(Q) − C, whence h(Q) ≤ C/(d − 1), and h(P) ≤ h(Q). Existence of the certificate for a morphism: the resultant of F₀, F₁ is nonzero and Res·X_k^{2d−1} ∈ (F₀, F₁) with cofactors of degree d − 1 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map).

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-3-unicritical-preperiodic-valuation-lemma"></a>

### 3.8 Denominators of preperiodic points of z^d + c

Let K be a field with a nonarchimedean valuation v (for instance a number field and a finite place), d ≥ 2, c ∈ K and α ∈ K preperiodic for f(z) = z^d + c. If v(c) < 0 then v(c) = d·v(α); if v(c) ≥ 0 then v(α) ≥ 0. Over ℚ: the denominator of every rational preperiodic point α satisfies den(α)^d = den(c); if den(c) is not a d-th power there is no finite rational preperiodic point.

d ≥ 2; v a nonarchimedean valuation (over ℚ: the p-adic valuations padicValRat); stated for preperiodic points, which is what the proof gives and what the search in Hutz 2015 uses (ArithmeticDynamics/E408). x is preperiodic for f when some iterate fᵐ(x) is periodic (Mathlib: ∃ m, f^[m] x ∈ Function.periodicPts f); equivalently its forward orbit is finite.

Case v(c) < 0 and d·v(α) < v(c): v(f(α)) = d·v(α) by the ultrametric inequality, and inductively v(fⁿ(α)) = dⁿ·v(α) → −∞, so the orbit is infinite. Case v(c) < 0 and d·v(α) > v(c): v(f(α)) = v(c), so d·v(f(α)) = d·v(c) < v(c) and f(α) falls in the previous case; α is not preperiodic. Case v(c) ≥ 0 and v(α) < 0: v(f(α)) = d·v(α) < v(α) < 0 and inductively v(fⁿ(α)) → −∞. Hence for preperiodic α: v(c) < 0 forces d·v(α) = v(c), and v(c) ≥ 0 forces v(α) ≥ 0 (mathlib:padicValRat for K = ℚ).

*Needs:* `mathlib:padicValRat`; `mathlib:Function.periodicPts`.

### 3.9 Preperiodic points of z^d + c satisfy |x| ≤ 1 + |c|

For d ≥ 2 and c ∈ ℚ (more generally c in a field with an archimedean absolute value), every preperiodic x of f(z) = z^d + c satisfies |x| ≤ 1 + |c|.

If |x| > 1 + |c|, then |x| > 1 and |f(x)| ≥ |x|^d − |c| ≥ |x|² − |c| > |x|(1 + |c|) − |c| = |x| + |c|(|x| − 1) ≥ |x|. The strict inequality remains valid when c = 0. So |f(x)| > 1 + |c| again, and the sequence |fⁿ(x)| is strictly increasing; the forward orbit consists of distinct points and is infinite, so x is not preperiodic.

### 3.10 Odd-degree z^d + c over ℚ: only fixed points

For odd d ≥ 3 and c ∈ ℚ, every rational preperiodic point of f(z) = z^d + c is fixed; there are at most three of them, so #PrePer(f, ℙ¹(ℚ)) ≤ 4 (with ∞), and f has no rational periodic point of exact period > 1.

d odd, d ≥ 3; c ∈ ℚ. x is preperiodic for f when some iterate fᵐ(x) is periodic (Mathlib: ∃ m, f^[m] x ∈ Function.periodicPts f); equivalently its forward orbit is finite.

f is strictly increasing on ℚ (odd d), hence injective; if f^{m+n}(x) = fᵐ(x) then fⁿ(x) = x, so preperiodic points are periodic. A periodic point x of a strictly increasing map is fixed: if x < f(x) then x < f(x) < f²(x) < ⋯ never returns to x (and symmetrically). Fixed points are rational roots of z^d − z + c, whose derivative d·z^{d−1} − 1 has exactly two real zeros (d − 1 even), so there are at most three real roots (Rolle).

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-3-orbit-repetition-check"></a>

### 3.11 The orbit-repetition check

For a type α with decidable equality, a self-map f, a finite set S ⊆ α, a fuel bound N and a start x, the check iterates x, f(x), f²(x), … for at most N steps, keeping the list of values seen: it returns true as soon as a value repeats, false as soon as a value lies outside S, and false when the fuel runs out. It is sound (true implies x preperiodic) and, when S contains every preperiodic point of f and N ≥ |S| + 1, complete (x preperiodic implies true).

α has decidable equality (for number fields this is the exact carrier of ComputationalNumberTheory:CN.0; for ℚ Mathlib's DecidableEq ℚ). x is preperiodic for f when ∃ m, f^[m] x ∈ Function.periodicPts f.

Define by recursion on the fuel: check 0 _ _ = false; check (N + 1) seen x = true if x ∈ seen, else if x ∈ S then check N (x :: seen) (f x) else false. Soundness: if the check returns true at a value y = fʲ(x) already seen as fⁱ(x), i < j, then fⁱ(x) is periodic (mathlib:Function.periodicPts), so x is preperiodic. Completeness: see ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/preperiodic-filter-correct.

### 3.12 The candidate box for rational preperiodic points of z^d + c

For d ≥ 1 and c ∈ ℚ, the candidate box is the finite set of rationals a/b with b ≥ 1, b^d = den(c) and |a| ≤ ⌈b·(1 + |c|)⌉ (empty when den(c) is not a d-th power). It is computable from (d, c).

d ≥ 1 (the containment theorem needs d ≥ 2); c ∈ ℚ with Mathlib's normalised denominator Rat.den.

Enumerate b ∈ {0, …, den c} with b^d = den c and, for each, the integers a in [−⌈b(1 + |c|)⌉, ⌈b(1 + |c|)⌉], and form a/b (Finset.biUnion and Finset.image; computable with Mathlib's DecidableEq ℚ). The number of candidates is at most 2⌈den(c)(1 + |c|)⌉ + 1.

*Needs:* `mathlib:padicValRat`.

### 3.13 The points of ℙ¹(ℚ) of height at most H

For H ∈ ℕ, the finite set of points [a : b] ∈ ℙ¹(ℚ) with a, b ∈ ℤ, |a|, |b| ≤ H, (a, b) ≠ (0, 0). A point [v] lies in it if and only if its multiplicative height H(v) = Height.mulHeight v (Mathlib, relative to ℚ) is at most H.

H ∈ ℕ; heights are Mathlib's (scaling invariant), so the condition is on points of ℙ¹(ℚ).

Take the image of the pairs in [−H, H]² ∖ {0} under Projectivization.mk (mathlib:Projectivization.mk; classical decidable equality on ℙ¹(ℚ) for the image; the concrete carrier of ComputationalNumberTheory:CN.0 represents a point by a primitive integer pair). Compatibility: a primitive integer vector (a, b) has H = max(|a|, |b|) (mathlib:Height.mulHeight at the archimedean place, all nonarchimedean factors 1), and every point has a primitive representative; H is scaling invariant (mathlib:Height.mulHeight₁_div_eq_mulHeight).

### 3.14 Poonen's conjecture: no rational cycles of length ≥ 4

Poonen's conjecture is the proposition: for all c, x ∈ ℚ and N ≥ 4, x does not have exact period N for z² + c. It is recorded as a statement, used only as an explicit hypothesis. It is proved for N = 4 (Morton) and N = 5 (Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer), and for N = 6 under the hypothesis of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/stoll-conditional-no-rational-six-cycles.

An open conjecture: no theorem consumes it except as an explicit hypothesis (roadmap acceptance).

Define PoonenConjecture : Prop := ∀ c x : ℚ, ∀ N ≥ 4, minimalPeriod (z ↦ z² + c) x ≠ N (mathlib:Function.minimalPeriod). Projections: the N = 4 and N = 5 instances are ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/morton-no-rational-four-cycles and ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/flynn-poonen-schaefer-no-rational-five-cycles (unconditional).

*Needs:* `mathlib:Function.minimalPeriod`.

### 3.15 Primitive binary necklaces at infinity

For n≥1, a binary word is w:Fin n→Fin 2. It is primitive when no nonidentity rotation fixes it. Let Bₙ be primitive words modulo cyclic rotation. Complement w↦1−w induces an involution on Bₙ; let Iₙ be its orbit set. The separate ramification theorem identifies these finite quotients with the geometric places over c=∞ in X₀,2(n). Write ν(n)=ν₂(n)/2 and eₙ=|Iₙ|. Then |Bₙ|=2ν(n)/n and eₙ=ν(n)/n for odd n; for even n, eₙ=ν(n)/n+(1/(2n))Σ_{r|n,2|r,n/r odd} μ(n/r)2^{r/2}. All divisions in these formulas are rational equalities, followed by integrality theorems.

n≥1; binary words have labelled positions before quotienting. Primitivity excludes all proper cyclic periods, not only constant words.

Use finite cyclic group rotation on Fin n and its action on functions; define primitive words by stabilizer triviality. Complement commutes with rotation. Möbius inversion counts primitive words. Burnside on rotations and complement counts Iₙ; rotations paired with complement contribute only in the even case with the displayed parity restriction. Morton Lemma 12 identifies these complement-orbits with places at infinity after adjoining u with c=u²; the sign change u↦−u exchanges binary symbols.

*Needs:* `mathlib:MulAction.orbitRel`; `mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.moebius`; `mathlib:Nat.totient`.

([morton96](#source-dy3-morton96), §3, Lemma 12, pp.340–341; Theorem 13 proof, p.342 — Primitive necklace count and its infinity-place interpretation; [fps](#source-dy3-fps), §2, p.5 — Quadratic specialization of the even-period correction.)

- **`necklaceComplement`** (structure): Complement involution on necklaces, commuting with rotation and squaring to identity.
- **`infinityNecklace`** (constructor): Orbit under complement of a primitive necklace.
- **`infinityNecklace_eq_iff`** (characterisation): Equality iff words differ by a rotation, or by a rotation followed by complement.
- **`infinityNecklace_card`** (characterisation): The finite cardinality is the displayed Burnside count; its geometric interpretation belongs to quadratic-parameter-ramification.

### 3.16 Rational quadratic differentials on the complex plane

A rational quadratic differential is q(z)dz² with q∈RatFunc ℂ. Its pole orders are those of q on the affine plane; at ∞ use w=1/z, giving coefficient q(1/w)/w⁴. For a bounded measurable U⊂ℂ and q with at most simple affine poles, define its local mass ∫_U |q(z)| dA, using Lebesgue area on ℂ≃ℝ² and ignoring finitely many poles. It is finite on bounded sets. The double-pole differentials used for multiplier variation are the same rational carrier but are not assigned a finite mass on sets containing their poles.

q rational; local mass assertions require at most simple affine poles. Affine local integrability does not imply integrability on the sphere.

Use RatFunc ℂ; polynomial numerator/denominator and multiplicity give pole orders. The dz² notation is a coordinate label, with the stated inversion rule. Represent evaluation away from poles by numerator/denominator; the arbitrary values at the finite poles do not change the integral. Near a simple pole use |q(z)|≤C/|z−a| and polar integration; cover the bounded closure by finitely many pole discs and regular compact pieces.

*Needs:* `mathlib:RatFunc`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves#layer-1-the-rational-function-field`.

([gao-ou](#source-dy3-gao-ou), §2.1, pp.2–3; §2.3, pp.9–10 — Local mass for simple poles and separate double-pole coefficients.)

- **`rationalQuadraticDifferential`** (data): Reuse RatFunc ℂ for the coefficient; record dz² and pole-coordinate convention.
- **`quadraticDifferential_ext`** (extensionality): Equality is equality of rational coefficients, equivalently agreement on any nonempty open set avoiding poles.
- **`quadraticDifferentialPoleOrder`** (projection): At a finite point use denominator minus numerator order; at ∞ use q(1/w)/w⁴.
- **`quadraticDifferentialMass`** (data): Local Lebesgue integral of |q| over a bounded measurable set.
- **`quadraticDifferentialMass_zero`** (simp): The zero differential has mass 0 on every set.
- **`quadraticDifferentialMass_smul`** (structure): Mass(aq,U)=|a|Mass(q,U); mass is subadditive.
- **`quadraticDifferentialMass_mono`** (relation): U⊂V implies mass(U)≤mass(V); strictly so for q≠0 if V∖U contains a nonempty open set away from poles.
- **`quadraticDifferential_pole_change`** (compatibility): Under z=h(w), coefficient becomes q(h(w))h′(w)²; at inversion this is q(1/w)/w⁴.

**Checks.**

### 3.17 Kneading sequences with a boundary symbol

Fix d≥2. On T=ℝ/ℤ use τ(θ)=dθ. For θ represented in [0,1), let b_j=(θ+j)/d for 0≤j<d. For k≥1, ν_θ(k) is ⋆ if τ^{k−1}(θ)=b_j for some j; it is j+1 if it lies strictly between b_j and b_{j+1} for 0≤j<d−1; it is 0 on the remaining open circular arc from b_{d−1} to b₀. The value ⋆ belongs to Option(Fin d), distinct from every digit. For θ of exact τ-period n, the first ⋆ is at k=n and the kneading sequence is periodic of length n. A word of length n ending in ⋆ is cyclic if it is w^{s−1}w⋆ for a word w of length t<n with n=ts; w⋆ replaces only the final digit by ⋆. Its cyclic expression uses the unique primitive such w.

d≥2; normalized representative of θ in [0,1); indices k begin at 1. Circular wrap interval has label 0, not d; endpoints have label ⋆.

Use AddCircle 1 for ℝ/ℤ and its normalized representative; make endpoint tests before open-arc tests. The nth iterate criterion gives the first boundary visit and period of the sequence. Primitive word means trivial cyclic-rotation stabilizer; the word-combinatorics node proves uniqueness of the primitive cyclic expression.

### 3.18 Böttcher coordinates and unicritical external rays

For d≥2 let K_c={z: the forward orbit under f_c=z^d+c is bounded}, using the inherited escape-rate/bounded-orbit comparison and M_d={c:0∈K_c}. Construct the normalized Böttcher coordinate near ∞, φ_c(f_c(z))=φ_c(z)^d and φ_c(z)/z→1. For c∈M_d extend it to ℂ∖K_c≅ℂ∖closedDisc(0,1). Define dynamical rays as inverse radial half-lines, with landing a radial limit as radius decreases to 1; for c∉M_d extend the rays maximally, stopping at a critical preimage if continuation breaks. Construct the parameter coordinate Φ_d(c)=φ_c(c), a biholomorphism ℂ∖M_d→ℂ∖closedDisc(0,1); parameter rays are its inverse radial half-lines. These are actual curves, not names for arbitrary choices of landing functions.

d≥2; normalization at ∞ fixes the d−1 root-of-unity ambiguity. For disconnected K_c do not assert a global Böttcher isomorphism ℂ∖K_c; use maximal rays and their critical obstructions.

Construct the near ∞ Böttcher coordinate from iterated d-th roots and uniform convergence, normalized by its asymptotic expansion. Extend on the escaping basin when K_c is connected; prove parameter uniformization and connectivity of M_d using the critical-value coordinate. Analytic continuation along rays defines the maximal external ray; continuation ends at a precritical point or lands on K_c. The foundational source-to-baseline proof of these dynamical inputs is gap G1; the general conformal/monodromy theory is imported, not replanned.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-3-binary-form-divisibility-criterion"></a>

### 3.19 Divisibility of binary forms is decided by their orders on ℙ¹

(a) Let K be algebraically closed and F, G ∈ K[X, Y] nonzero binary forms. Then F ∣ G in K[X, Y] if and only if ord_P F ≤ ord_P G for every P ∈ ℙ¹(K); in particular F = c·∏_P ℓ_P^{ord_P F} with c ∈ K^× and Σ_P ord_P F = deg F. (b) For any field extension L/K and F, G ∈ K[X, Y], if F ∣ G in L[X, Y] then F ∣ G in K[X, Y].

(a) needs K algebraically closed; (b) holds for every field extension. F, G are homogeneous and nonzero in (a).

Write f = F(X, 1), g = G(X, 1). For F homogeneous of degree a, F = Y^{a − deg f}·Y^{deg f} f(X/Y), so F ∣ G iff a − deg f ≤ b − deg g and f ∣ g in K[X]. By mathlib:IsAlgClosed.dvd_iff_roots_le_roots, f ∣ g iff roots f ≤ roots g, i.e. rootMultiplicity x f ≤ rootMultiplicity x g for all x (mathlib:Polynomial.count_roots); by the affine API of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/binary-form-order-at-a-point these are ord_[x:1] F ≤ ord_[x:1] G, and a − deg f = ord_∞ F. The factorisation and Σ_P ord_P F = deg F follow from the splitting of f (mathlib:IsAlgClosed.card_roots_eq_natDegree) together with the power of Y. (b): K[X, Y] → L[X, Y] (mathlib:MvPolynomial.map) is injective and L[X, Y] = L ⊗_K K[X, Y] is free over K[X, Y] on a K-basis of L containing 1. If G = F·H with H ∈ L[X, Y], expanding H in that basis and comparing the coefficient of 1 gives G = F·H₁ with H₁ ∈ K[X, Y].

### 3.20 The zeros of Φₙ are the points of period n

Let φ be a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d ≥ 1 over a field K, inducing f : ℙ¹(K) → ℙ¹(K). For n ≥ 0 and P = [v] ∈ ℙ¹(K): Φₙ(φ)(v) = 0 if and only if fⁿ(P) = P.

K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.

The composite lift of a morphism has no common zero: (Fₙ(v), Gₙ(v)) ≠ 0 for v ≠ 0 (induction, DY.0's iterate of a morphism), and fⁿ([v]) = [Fₙ(v) : Gₙ(v)]. Φₙ(v) = v₁Fₙ(v) − v₀Gₙ(v) is minus the determinant of the vectors v and (Fₙ(v), Gₙ(v)); it vanishes iff they are proportional, i.e. iff [Fₙ(v) : Gₙ(v)] = [v₀ : v₁] (mathlib:Projectivization.mk).

### 3.21 Φₖ(φᵐ) = Φ_{mk}(φ)

For every lift φ over a commutative ring and all m, k ≥ 0, the composite lift of (φᵐ)ᵏ equals the composite lift of φ^{mk}; hence Φₖ(φᵐ) = Φ_{mk}(φ) and a_P(φᵐ, k) = a_P(φ, mk).

No hypothesis beyond R commutative; exact equality of forms, not only up to scalars.

Substitution of forms is associative: (F ∘ G) ∘ H = F ∘ (G ∘ H) for pairs of forms (mathlib:MvPolynomial.aeval, evaluation of a composite). Induction on k: the lift of (φᵐ)^{k+1} is φᵐ ∘ (φᵐ)ᵏ = φᵐ ∘ φ^{mk} = φ^{m(k+1)}. Apply the definition of Φ and of a_P.

### 3.22 The period form under conjugation by GL₂

Let φ be a lift over a field K and A ∈ GL₂(K). Let lin = A·(X, Y)ᵀ and let ψ = A⁻¹ ∘ φ ∘ A be the conjugate lift, ψᵢ = Σⱼ (A⁻¹)ᵢⱼ φⱼ(lin). Then for every n, Φₙ(ψ) = det(A)⁻¹·Φₙ(φ)(lin); consequently ord_P Φₙ(ψ) = ord_{AP} Φₙ(φ), i.e. a_P(ψ, n) = a_{AP}(φ, n) and a*_P(ψ, n) = a*_{AP}(φ, n).

A is invertible; ψ is the lift of the conjugate map α⁻¹ ∘ f ∘ α of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/conjugacy-of-rational-maps.

The composite lift of ψ is A⁻¹ ∘ (lift of φⁿ) ∘ A: the inner A⁻¹ and A cancel between consecutive factors. For a vector v: Φ(ψ)(v) = −det(v, A⁻¹w) with w = φⁿ(Av), and det(v, A⁻¹w) = det(A)⁻¹det(Av, w), so Φₙ(ψ)(v) = det(A)⁻¹Φₙ(φ)(Av). The substitution v ↦ Av is a graded automorphism of K[X, Y] with ℓ_{AP}(Av) = det(A)·ℓ_P(v), so multiplicities of ℓ_{AP} in Φₙ(φ) and of ℓ_P in Φₙ(φ)(lin) agree (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/binary-form-order-at-a-point). The statement for a* follows by summing with Möbius weights.

### 3.23 The period form commutes with change of coefficients

No hypothesis on g; the geometric meaning over the residue field requires good reduction (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map).

mathlib:MvPolynomial.map is a ring homomorphism commuting with substitution (map ∘ aeval = aeval ∘ map on mapped arguments), so induction on n. Apply g to Y·Fₙ − X·Gₙ.

### 3.24 The dynatomic polynomial Φ*ₙ(φ)

Let φ be a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d ≥ 2 over a field K and n ≥ 1. The n-th dynatomic polynomial Φ*ₙ(φ) ∈ K[X, Y] is the unique binary form whose image in the fraction field of K[X, Y] is ∏_{m ∣ n} Φₘ(φ)^{μ(n/m)}. It exists by ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-is-polynomial and is unique because K[X, Y] → Frac K[X, Y] is injective; equivalently it is determined recursively by ∏_{m ∣ n} Φ*ₘ(φ) = Φₙ(φ). It is homogeneous of degree Σ_{m∣n} μ(n/m)(dᵐ + 1), its order at every point P is a*_P(n), and its zeros are the points of formal period n. (The Lean prototype is total, with junk value 0 when the Möbius product is not a polynomial.)

K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio. The definition depends on the chosen lift through the Φₘ; scaling the lift by u ∈ K^× scales Φ*ₙ by a power of u.

Form the element ∏_{(i, j) ∈ divisorsAntidiagonal n} ι(Φⱼ(φ))^{μ(i)} of FractionRing K[X, Y] (mathlib:FractionRing, mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.moebius; ι = algebraMap, zpow in the fraction field). If it is ι(Q) for some Q, set Φ*ₙ := Q; Q is unique by mathlib:IsFractionRing.injective. Otherwise the junk value 0 (never used for morphisms of degree ≥ 2). Existence and all listed properties are proved in ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-is-polynomial and ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-degree.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-3-period-form); `mathlib:FractionRing`; `mathlib:IsFractionRing.injective`; `mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.moebius`; `mathlib:Nat.divisorsAntidiagonal`.

([ms95](#source-parent-ms95), §1, printed p. 86 — Z*ₙ(φ) = Σ_{d∣n} μ(n/d) Z_d(φ); Φ*ₙ is the binary form of this cycle; [hutz10](#source-parent-hutz10), §1, p. 1 — The dynatomic cycle; as a form it is our Φ*ₙ; [fps95](#source-parent-fps95), §2, display (2), p. 3 — The affine dynatomic polynomial for z² + c (FPS's display (2) prints the exponent as μ(m); see ArithmeticDynamics/E401).)

### 3.25 The germ of φⁿ is the n-th iterate of the germ

Let φ = (F, G) be a lift over a field K with F(0, 1) = 0 ≠ G(0, 1). Then for every n the composite lift of φⁿ fixes [0 : 1] with Gₙ(0, 1) ≠ 0, and its germ is the n-fold substitution iterate of the germ of φ: g_{φⁿ} = (g_φ)ⁿ.

K a field; F(0, 1) = 0 and G(0, 1) ≠ 0.

Induction on n. By homogeneity Fₙ₊₁(z, 1) = F(Fₙ(z, 1), Gₙ(z, 1)) = Gₙ(z, 1)^d·F(gₙ, 1) where gₙ = Fₙ(z, 1)/Gₙ(z, 1), and likewise for G; hence Gₙ₊₁(0, 1) = Gₙ(0,1)^d G(0, 1) ≠ 0 and g_{φⁿ⁺¹} = F(gₙ, 1)/G(gₙ, 1). Substitution of gₙ (constant coefficient 0, mathlib:PowerSeries.HasSubst.of_constantCoeff_zero') is a K-algebra homomorphism K[[z]] → K[[z]] (mathlib:PowerSeries.substAlgHom), so it commutes with polynomial evaluation and with inverses of units: F(gₙ, 1)/G(gₙ, 1) = (F(z,1)/G(z,1)) ∘ gₙ = g_φ ∘ gₙ = g_φ^{n+1}. The dehomogenised forms and germs are those of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/fixed-point-germ and the lift iterates those of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form.

Hence ord(gⁿ − z) ≥ 1, with equality iff λⁿ − 1 ≠ 0 (mathlib:PowerSeries.order, mathlib:PowerSeries.coeff).

### 3.27 ord(gⁿ − z) ≥ ord(g − z)

Let g ∈ K[[z]] have constant coefficient 0. For every n ≥ 1, ord(gⁿ − z) ≥ ord(g − z). Consequently a_P(φ, kn) ≥ a_P(φ, k) for all k, n ≥ 1 at a point P of period k.

K is a field and g ∈ K[[z]] has constant coefficient 0; gⁿ is the n-fold substitution iterate (germIterate).

Let e = ord(g − z), so g = z + O(z^e). If h = z + O(z^e) then g ∘ h = h + (g − z) ∘ h = h + O(h^e) = z + O(z^e), since h has order ≥ 1 (mathlib:PowerSeries.subst). By induction gⁿ = z + O(z^e), i.e. ord(gⁿ − z) ≥ e. For the corollary apply this to the germ of φᵏ at P (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-equals-germ-order, ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/germ-of-an-iterate).

### 3.29 Finitely many L-rational preperiodic points (Northcott)

Let L be a number field and φ a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d ≥ 2 over L with induced map f. Then the set of preperiodic points of f in ℙ¹(L) is finite.

L is a number field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(L̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio. x is preperiodic for f when some iterate fᵐ(x) is periodic (Mathlib: ∃ m, f^[m] x ∈ Function.periodicPts f); equivalently its forward orbit is finite.

A certificate exists (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map), so preperiodic points have h ≤ C/(d − 1) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/height-bound-for-preperiodic-points). Points of ℙ¹(L) of bounded height are finite: ∞ together with the [x : 1] with h(x, 1) = log H₁(x) bounded (mathlib:Height.mulHeight₁_div_eq_mulHeight), a finite set by Northcott (mathlib:NumberField.finite_setOfPred_mulHeight₁_le).

### 3.30 Points of type (m, 1) are negatives of periodic points

Let c ∈ ℚ and m ≥ 1. A rational x is of type (m, 1) for z² + c iff −x is a nonzero rational point of exact period m. The number of rational points of type (m, 1) equals the number of rational points of period m, except for (c, m) = (−1, 2) and (0, 1), where there is one fewer.

f_c(z) = z² + c with c ∈ ℚ; exact period is Mathlib's Function.minimalPeriod of f_c on ℚ (0 for non-periodic points). A point of type (m, n) (n ≥ 1) enters an m-cycle after exactly n steps: minimalPeriod(fⁿ(x)) = m and f^{n−1}(x) is not periodic (Poonen 1995, §3).

If x is of type (m, 1) then f(fᵐ(x)) = f(x) but fᵐ(x) ≠ x, so fᵐ(x) = −x; −x is periodic of period m and nonzero. Conversely if −x ≠ 0 has period m then f(x) = f(−x) is periodic of period m and fᵐ(x) = −x ≠ x. If 0 is preperiodic, c is integral by DY.3/unicritical-preperiodic-valuation-lemma. If |c| > 2, the next value satisfies |c² + c| ≥ |c|² − |c| > |c|, and the same estimate makes all subsequent absolute values grow without bound, a contradiction. Check c ∈ {−2,−1,0,1,2} directly: only −2,−1,0 give finite orbits of 0; only −1 (period 2) and 0 (period 1) make 0 periodic.

### 3.34 Pushforward of rational quadratic differentials

For a nonconstant polynomial f over ℂ, define f_*q at regular values z by Σ_{f(w)=z}q(w)/f′(w)², summing distinct preimages; extend this rational function across the finite exceptional set. This gives a ℂ-linear operator RatFunc ℂ→RatFunc ℂ, functorial as (f∘g)_*=f_*∘g_*, with identity pushforward the identity. Simple affine poles stay at most simple; double poles can stay double. For f(z)=z^d+c, d≥2: f_*(1/z)=0; for a≠0, f_*(1/(z−a))=(1/f′(a))(1/(z−f(a))−1/(z−c)) and f_*(1/(z−a)²)=1/(z−f(a))²−((d−1)/(a·f′(a)))(1/(z−f(a))−1/(z−c)).

f nonconstant; formulas on regular values first, rational extension second. The second and third displayed formulas require a≠0 for the unicritical map.

Form the finite separable extension ℂ(f(z))⊂ℂ(z), of degree deg f by RatFunc.finrank_eq_max_natDegree, and apply Mathlib's Algebra.trace to q/f′²; identify the target rational coefficient with variable z. On regular fibres the trace equals the displayed finite sum (trace_eq_sum_embeddings). Extension, linearity and composition follow from rational-function equality and trace transitivity (Algebra.trace_trace). At poles use local expansions to bound the pushed pole order. For z^d+c sum over d-th roots to obtain Levin’s three formulas (Gao–Ou Lemma 2.4).

Every nonempty finite word has a unique primitive root under concatenation. If a nonprimitive word is changed at exactly its last digit, the resulting word is primitive. A cyclic starred kneading block has a unique primitive cyclic expression. For a τ-periodic angle maximal in its orbit, its kneading block is its periodic base-d expansion with the last digit replaced by ⋆.

### 3.36 Periodic ray landing and unicritical parabolic structure

For d≥2, every periodic parameter ray of exact angle period n lands at a parabolic parameter c₀. Its dynamic ray lands at an exact m-period point with m|n and multiplier a primitive (n/m)-th root of unity. Each period-n hyperbolic component has one root at which two period-n parameter rays land and d−2 co-roots at which one such ray lands; the root is primitive exactly when the two landing angles have distinct τ-orbits. An exact m-cycle with primitive r-th-root multiplier has the local splitting into one m-cycle and one mr-cycle described in Gao–Ou Lemma 3.9; at primitive multiplier 1 a single parabolic cycle splits into two m-cycles. Unicriticality gives the one critical attracting basin and the exact petal count used in transversality. Let c_m→c₀ along the parameter ray of angle θ, and put R(c)=R_c(θ)∪{c,∞} (the compactified dynamic ray through the critical value) and S(c)=f_c⁻¹(R(c)) (the d precritical dynamic rays together with 0 and ∞). After passing to a subsequence, R(c_m)→R and S(c_m)→S in the Hausdorff topology on compact subsets of the Riemann sphere, with S=f_{c₀}⁻¹(R); R meets ℂ∖K_{c₀} exactly in the dynamic ray R_{c₀}(θ), meets ∂K_{c₀} only at the parabolic point γ_{c₀}(θ), and meets the interior of K_{c₀} only inside that point’s immediate basin, so S meets ∂K_{c₀} only in preimages of that point. These are the primitive and distinguished-satellite configurations used by the two monodromy propositions.

### 3.37 The multiplicity a_P(n) of a point of period n

For a lift φ of a morphism of ℙ¹ over a field K, n ≥ 1 and P ∈ ℙ¹(K), the multiplicity of P as a point of period n is a_P(n) = a_P(φ, n) := ord_P Φₙ(φ). It is positive exactly when φⁿ(P) = P; Σ_{P ∈ ℙ¹(K̄)} a_P(n) = dⁿ + 1 for d ≥ 2; a_P(φ, mk) = a_P(φᵐ, k); it is invariant under conjugation (a_P(ψ, n) = a_{AP}(φ, n)). On ℙ¹ it equals Morton–Silverman's intersection multiplicity (Δ·Γ(φⁿ))_{(P,P)}, whose cycle they identify with the root cycle of (21).

K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio. Points over an extension L are handled by base change of φ to L (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-base-change).

Define a_P(n) := ord_P Φₙ(φ) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/binary-form-order-at-a-point). Positivity: ord_P Φₙ > 0 iff Φₙ(P) = 0 iff φⁿ(P) = P (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-zero-locus). Total count over K̄: Φₙ is a nonzero form of degree dⁿ + 1 (API of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form), so Σ_P ord_P Φₙ = dⁿ + 1 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/binary-form-divisibility-criterion). ### 3.38 Rotation germs: r ∣ ord(gʳ − z) − 1

Let g ∈ K[[z]] have constant coefficient 0 and linear coefficient λ a primitive r-th root of unity with r ≥ 2, and suppose gʳ ≠ z. Then s := ord(gʳ − z) satisfies r ∣ s − 1; in particular s ≥ r + 1 ≥ 3.

K is a field and g ∈ K[[z]] has constant coefficient 0; gⁿ is the n-fold substitution iterate (germIterate). λ is a primitive r-th root of unity, r ≥ 2 (so the characteristic of K does not divide r); gʳ ≠ z.

h := gʳ has linear coefficient λʳ = 1 (API coeff_one_germIterate), so h = z + c·z^s + O(z^{s+1}) with c ≠ 0 and s ≥ 2 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/germ-order-multiplier-criterion). h ∘ g = g ∘ h since both are g^{r+1} (mathlib:PowerSeries.subst is associative on series with zero constant term). g ∘ h = g(z + c z^s + O(z^{s+1})) = g(z) + g′(z)·c z^s + O(z^{2s}) = g(z) + λ c z^s + O(z^{s+1}) (Taylor expansion of the substitution; s ≥ 2). h ∘ g = g + c·g^s + O(g^{s+1}) = g(z) + c λ^s z^s + O(z^{s+1}). Comparing the coefficient of z^s: λc = λ^s c, so λ^{s−1} = 1 and r ∣ s − 1 (mathlib:IsPrimitiveRoot.pow_eq_one_iff_dvd); s ≥ 2 gives s ≥ r + 1.

### 3.39 Iterates of a germ tangent to the identity

Let g ∈ K[[z]] with g = z + z^e·u, e ≥ 2, u(0) ≠ 0 (so ord(g − z) = e). Then gⁿ = z + n·z^e·u + O(z^{2e−1}); hence ord(gⁿ − z) = e when n ≠ 0 in K, and ord(gⁿ − z) ≥ 2e − 1 when n = 0 in K (n ≥ 1).

K is a field and g ∈ K[[z]] has constant coefficient 0; gⁿ is the n-fold substitution iterate (germIterate). e ≥ 2 (g is tangent to the identity); n ≥ 1.

For every power series h with constant coefficient 0 and any i, h ∘ gⁱ = h + O(z^e) (from ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/germ-order-monotone): this is Morton–Silverman's (8). Induction: z∘g^{n} = z + z^e Σ_{i<n} u∘gⁱ + O(z^{2e−1}) (their (9)): g^{n+1} = g ∘ gⁿ = gⁿ + (gⁿ)^e·u(gⁿ) and (gⁿ)^e = z^e(1 + O(z^{e−1}))^e = z^e + O(z^{2e−1}). Substituting (8) into (9): gⁿ = z + n z^e u + O(z^{2e−1}) (their (10)). Since u(0) ≠ 0 and 2e − 1 > e, ord(gⁿ − z) = e if n·u(0) ≠ 0, i.e. n ≠ 0 in K, and ≥ 2e − 1 if n = 0 in K.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-3-uniform-boundedness-conjecture"></a>

### 3.40 The Morton–Silverman uniform boundedness conjecture

For integers N ≥ 1, d ≥ 2 and D ≥ 1, the uniform boundedness conjecture UBC(N, d, D) is the proposition: there is a constant C(N, d, D) such that for every number field K with [K : ℚ] ≤ D and every morphism φ : ℙᴺ → ℙᴺ of degree d defined over K, #PrePer(φ, ℙᴺ(K)) ≤ C(N, d, D). It is recorded as a statement (the Lean prototype states N = 1, with Set.encard), used only as an explicit hypothesis; for each fixed φ the set is finite (Northcott), and uniformity across all maps of fixed degree is the open content.

An open conjecture; no theorem of this roadmap consumes it except as an explicit hypothesis (DY.6 acceptance). d ≥ 2 is essential: in degree 1 the identity has every point preperiodic.

Define UniformBoundednessConjecture d D : Prop := ∃ C, ∀ number fields L with [L : ℚ] ≤ D, ∀ lifts φ of morphisms of ℙ¹ of degree d over L, #{preperiodic points of the induced map} ≤ C (Set.encard, so infinite sets are not bounded). Monotonicity in D, the trivial case D = 0, and the necessity of d ≥ 2 are API/tests; the per-map finiteness is ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/finiteness-of-rational-preperiodic-points.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/finiteness-of-rational-preperiodic-points`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-3-finiteness-of-rational-preperiodic-points); `mathlib:Function.periodicPts`.

([bijmst18](#source-parent-bijmst18), §4, Conjecture 4.2, p. 7 — The statement (the survey uses [K : ℚ] = D; bounding for each D ≤ D₀ is equivalent); [hutz15](#source-parent-hutz15), Introduction, p. 1 — The ≤ D form used here; [fps95](#source-parent-fps95), §1, Conjecture 1, p. 2 — Morton–Silverman's conjecture as stated by FPS; [bijmst18](#source-parent-bijmst18), Conjecture 4.2, p. 7 (arXiv v2) — The node states the case N = 1; [bijmst18](#source-parent-bijmst18), Theorem 4.1, p. 7 (arXiv v2) — For fixed f the finiteness is DY.1/northcott-for-preperiodic-points; the conjecture adds uniformity.)

- **`UniformBoundednessConjecture.mono`** (other): UBC(d, D′) implies UBC(d, D) for D ≤ D′.
- **`finite_preperiodicPts`** (compatibility): For each fixed morphism the set is finite (promoted: ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/finiteness-of-rational-preperiodic-points); the conjecture asks for uniformity.

### 3.41 Correctness of the preperiodic filter

Let f : α → α with decidable equality and S a finite set containing every preperiodic point of f. Then for every x: x ∈ preperiodicFilter f S if and only if x is preperiodic for f.

S ⊇ PrePer(f) (a certified candidate set). x is preperiodic for f when ∃ m, f^[m] x ∈ Function.periodicPts f.

⇒: soundness of the check (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/orbit-repetition-check). ⇐: x ∈ S by hypothesis. Every fᵏ(x) is preperiodic, hence in S, so the check never meets a value outside S. The values x, f(x), …, f^{|S|}(x) are |S| + 1 elements of S, so two coincide (pigeonhole, mathlib:Finset.exists_ne_map_eq_of_card_lt_of_maps_to) and the check returns true within the fuel |S| + 1 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/preperiodic-points-from-candidates).

### 3.43 Local contraction for nonzero simple-pole differentials

Let f∈ℂ[z] have degree≥2 and q≠0 have at most simple affine poles. There is R>0 such that U=f⁻¹(ball(0,R)) has closure contained in V=ball(0,R), and for every sufficiently large such R, mass(f_*q,V)≤mass(q,U)<mass(q,V). Hence f_*q≠q. The zero differential and degree-one identity are excluded.

Degree f≥2; q≠0; at most simple affine poles.

Polynomial growth of degree≥2 gives a sufficiently large disc with relatively compact preimage. Away from critical points the complex Jacobian is |f′|²; partition regular fibres and apply area change of variables and the triangle inequality. Exceptional finite sets have measure 0. The annular complement contains a nonempty open set; a nonzero rational coefficient cannot vanish there, giving strict mass loss.

### 3.44 Symbolic coding outside the Multibrot set

For c∉M_d lying on a nonzero-angle parameter ray, the d precritical dynamic rays cut the plane into sectors U₀,…,U_{d−1}, with U₀ containing ray 0 and the others numbered counterclockwise. Itinerary gives a bijection ι_c:K_c→(Fin d)^ℕ conjugating f_c to the left shift. Thus exact point period equals exact sequence period. On X=ℂ∖(M_d∪R_{M_d}(0)), the inverse x(ι,c) for a fixed sequence is continuous in c, and for a periodic sequence is holomorphic. This supplies the consistent labels for periodic roots in the monodromy calculation.

d≥2; c∈X; the cut label convention is part of the statement. Holomorphic periodic-root continuation is asserted on X, not across parabolic landing parameters.

Each sector maps conformally to the slit critical-value complement; inverse branches form nested compact sets with unique intersection. Recover the unique itinerary point; show conjugacy and exact period preservation. For periodic itineraries apply the implicit function theorem since their cycles are repelling outside M_d. Parameter uniformization slit at ray 0 makes X simply connected and fixes the labels.

### 3.45 The essential (dynatomic) multiplicity a*_P(n)

For a lift φ over a field K, n ≥ 1 and P ∈ ℙ¹(K), a*_P(n) := Σ_{d ∣ n} μ(n/d)·a_P(d) ∈ ℤ, the coefficient of P in the n-th dynatomic cycle Z*ₙ(φ) = Σ_{d∣n} μ(n/d) Z_d(φ). By Möbius inversion a_P(n) = Σ_{d∣n} a*_P(d); a*_P(1) = a_P(1); if P has exact period n then a*_P(n) = a_P(n).

K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio. μ is Mathlib's ArithmeticFunction.moebius; the sum runs over Nat.divisorsAntidiagonal n.

Define a*_P(n) := Σ_{(i, j) ∈ divisorsAntidiagonal n} μ(i)·a_P(j) (mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.moebius, mathlib:Nat.divisorsAntidiagonal). Möbius inversion a_P(n) = Σ_{d∣n} a*_P(d): mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.sum_eq_iff_sum_mul_moebius_eq. If P has exact period n, then a_P(d) = 0 for d ∣ n, d < n (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-of-a-periodic-point), so a*_P(n) = a_P(n).

### 3.46 At a fixed point a_P(n) is the order of gⁿ(z) − z

Let φ be a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d ≥ 2 over a field K fixing 0 = [0 : 1], with germ g. Then for every n ≥ 1, a_{[0:1]}(φ, n) = ord_z(gⁿ(z) − z) (Mathlib's PowerSeries.order, finite since φⁿ ≠ id).

K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio. F(0, 1) = 0 (the point [0 : 1] is fixed).

By ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/germ-of-an-iterate, Fₙ(z, 1) = Gₙ(z, 1)·gⁿ(z) in K[[z]], so Φₙ(z, 1) = Fₙ(z, 1) − z·Gₙ(z, 1) = Gₙ(z, 1)·(gⁿ(z) − z). Gₙ(z, 1) is a unit of K[[z]] (Gₙ(0, 1) ≠ 0), so ord_z Φₙ(z, 1) = ord_z(gⁿ − z) (mathlib:PowerSeries.order_mul). For a polynomial, the power-series order at 0 is the root multiplicity at 0 (mathlib:Polynomial.rootMultiplicity), and ord_[0:1] Φₙ = rootMultiplicity 0 (Φₙ(z, 1)) by the affine API of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/binary-form-order-at-a-point. The order is finite because Φₙ ≠ 0 (API periodForm_ne_zero of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form).

### 3.47 Certified enumeration of PrePer(φ, ℙ¹(ℚ))

Every preperiodic point has log-height ≤ log(2·max(H(q), 1))/(d − 1), hence multiplicative height ≤ H (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/height-bound-for-preperiodic-points). So ratPointsOfHeightLE H contains all preperiodic points (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/rational-points-of-bounded-height), and ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/preperiodic-filter-correct gives the equality.

### 3.48 Certified enumeration over a number field from a height enumeration

### 3.50 Transversality at unicritical parabolic parameters

For f_c(z)=z^d+c,d≥2, at an exact m-cycle with multiplier ρ=1 the derivative ∂_c(f_c^m(z)−z) is nonzero and the cycle has one attracting petal. At an exact m-cycle with primitive r-th-root multiplier ρ≠1 (r>1), the implicit continuation ζ(c) exists and its multiplier ρ(c) has ρ′(c₀)≠0. For P(c,z)=(f_c^{mr}(z)−z)/(f_c^m(z)−z), polynomial division gives ∂_cP(c₀,z₀)=rρ′(c₀)/(ρ(ρ−1))≠0. Locally the relevant dynatomic branch is a graph c=c(z), with ramification index 2 in the first case and r in the second.

At multiplier 1, form the rational simple-pole differential whose coefficients solve the orbit recurrence; its pushforward difference has the parameter derivative as its sole critical-value coefficient. Local-quadratic-contraction forces that coefficient nonzero. At ρ≠1, use the implicit function theorem for the m-period equation and differentiate the divided equation to obtain the displayed identity. For multiplier variation use Q=Σ_k(1/(z−z_k)²+μ_k/(z−z_k)), with μ_{k+1}=μ_k/f′(z_k)−(d−1)/(d z_k^d). Levin's double-pole formula (pushforward API unicriticalPushforward_double) and this recurrence give, as in Lemma 2.8, f_*Q−Q=−(ρ′/ρ)/(z−c₀). Lemma 2.9 excludes equality by puncturing discs about the cycle and comparing annular masses; double poles cannot use the simple-pole integral theorem. Use the local parabolic normal form and the unique critical basin to give one petal for primitive parameters and r petals for a multiplier of exact order r; this is the named ray/basin gap G1.

### 3.51 Reduction of a*_P to a fixed point

Let φ be a lift of a morphism of degree d ≥ 2 and P a point of exact period m ≥ 1. Then for every n ≥ 1, a*_P(φ, n) = a*_P(φᵐ, n/m) if m ∣ n, and a*_P(φ, n) = 0 if m ∤ n. If P is not periodic, a*_P(φ, n) = 0 for all n.

K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.

a_P(φ, k) > 0 iff φᵏ(P) = P iff m ∣ k (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-of-a-periodic-point; mathlib:Function.IsPeriodicPt.minimalPeriod_dvd). So a*_P(φ, n) = Σ_{d ∣ n, m ∣ d} μ(n/d) a_P(φ, d); if m ∤ n the sum is empty. If m ∣ n write N = n/m and d = mk: a_P(φ, mk) = a_P(φᵐ, k) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-of-an-iterate), so the sum is Σ_{k ∣ N} μ(N/k) a_P(φᵐ, k) = a*_P(φᵐ, N).

### 3.52 Formal period versus exact period

Let φ be a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ over a field K. A point P ∈ ℙ¹(K) has formal period n (n ≥ 1) if a*_P(n) > 0, i.e. P occurs in the n-th dynatomic cycle (Morton–Silverman's essential period, Hutz's formal period). Its exact period is Mathlib's Function.minimalPeriod of the induced map f at P. Every point of exact period n has formal period n; a point of formal period n satisfies fⁿ(P) = P and its exact period m divides n, with n ∈ {m, m·r, m·r·pᵉ} (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/formal-period-classification). Formal period 1 is the same as being fixed.

K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio. f : ℙ¹(K) → ℙ¹(K) is the map induced by φ (DY.0).

Define IsOfFormalPeriod φ n P :⟺ 0 < a*_P(n) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/essential-multiplicity). fⁿ(P) = P: a*_P(n) > 0 forces a_P(d) > 0 for some d ∣ n, hence f^d(P) = P and fⁿ(P) = P (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-zero-locus). Exact period divides n: mathlib:Function.IsPeriodicPt.minimalPeriod_dvd. Formal period 1 ⟺ a_P(1) > 0 ⟺ fixed.

### 3.53 The multiplicity profile k ↦ a_P(k) at a fixed point

Let φ be a lift of a morphism of degree d ≥ 2 over a field K of characteristic p ≥ 0 with a fixed point P, multiplier λ, and r the multiplicative order of λ (r = 0 if λ is 0 or not a root of unity). Then for k ≥ 1: a_P(k) = 1 if r = 0 or r ∤ k, and a_P(k) = B(v_p(k/r)) if r ≥ 1 and r ∣ k, where B(a) := a_P(r·pᵃ) for p > 0, and B(a) := a_P(r) for all a when p = 0. Moreover B(0) ≥ 2, B is nondecreasing, and if p > 0 then B(a + 1) ≥ 2B(a) − 1.

K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio. P is fixed by φ; after a conjugation (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-conjugation) P = [0 : 1] with germ g.

By ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-equals-germ-order, a_P(k) = ord(gᵏ − z). If r = 0 or r ∤ k then λᵏ ≠ 1, so a_P(k) = 1 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/germ-order-multiplier-criterion). If r ∣ k, write k = r·j and h = gʳ; h has linear coefficient 1, so e₀ = ord(h − z) = B(0) ≥ 2 (same lemma). Write j = pᵃj′ with p ∤ j′ (a = 0 if p = 0). For p = 0 use a = 0 and the constant profile B. For p > 0, h^{pᵃ} is tangent to the identity with order B(a) ≥ e₀ ≥ 2 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/germ-order-monotone), and since j′ ≠ 0 in K, ord((h^{pᵃ})^{j′} − z) = B(a) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/germ-order-parabolic-iterate). Monotonicity from ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/germ-order-monotone; for p > 0, B(a + 1) = ord((h^{pᵃ})ᵖ − z) ≥ 2B(a) − 1 since p = 0 in K (germ-order-parabolic-iterate).

### 3.54 Relative height bounds for certified dynamical candidates

Let K be a number field of degree s=[K:ℚ]>0 and f a rational map of degree at least 2 over K. Mathlib's Height.logHeight of a representative of a point of ℙ¹(K) is relative to K (no division by s); the absolute height of DY.1/weil-height-eq-log-height-div-finrank is h_abs(P)=Height.logHeight(P.rep)/s. Take rationals D≥1 and 0<τ≤1 with D≥exp(B_nat); when the available bound is instead an absolute one, h_abs(P)≤B, take D≥exp(sB). Then the projective union T of both ED.0 output lists plus ∞ contains every preperiodic point, and filtering T by the inherited orbit-repetition check with fuel |T|+1 yields exactly PrePer(f,ℙ¹(K)); equality tests at the height boundary are unnecessary. This adapter supplies a sufficient finite superset, and does not advertise T as an exact height-cutoff list.

An explicit valid bound is supplied together with its normalization: native B_nat with D≥exp(B_nat), or absolute B with D≥exp(sB); an integral power basis and complete embedding certificates are supplied as ED.0 requires. Exact field/projective evaluation and equality are supplied by the runtime adapter.

For an absolute bound first multiply by the positive degree s (DY.1/weil-height-eq-log-height-div-finrank), then exponentiate. ED.0 completeness applies to both lists together, including every boundary point; add ∞ of height 0 as in its projective contract. Forward iterates of a preperiodic point remain preperiodic and hence stay in T. The inherited filter correctness theorem supplies both soundness and completeness with finite fuel. No uniform-in-map bound is used.

### 3.55 Local monodromy on labelled periodic points

Let θ have exact angle period n≥2 and kneading block ε₁…εₙ₋₁⋆. For θ=1−1/(d^n−1), the landing is satellite with fixed parabolic point and the loop permutes cyclically all n points in the cycle labelled (d−1)…(d−1)(d−2). A satellite landing of a maximal angle has cyclic kneading w^{s−1}w⋆ and final digit w_t−1; its parabolic period is |w|.

d≥2,n≥2; analytic continuation based on the consistent labels from X; loops avoid all other branch parameters.

At a primitive point the local projection is c=c₀+δ²; a turn exchanges its two branches. Ray-limit control identifies the two symbolic labels and their rotations. At the distinguished satellite point the local projection is c=c₀+δ^n, so the branches cycle. Identify its fixed parabolic point with the maximal-angle orbit using Lemma 3.14 and the ray-limit exclusion in Proposition 3.15. Lemma 3.11 gives the satellite cyclic-expression constraint; Lemma 3.12 constructs primitive landing angles when its digit constraint fails.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-3-dynatomic-cycle-effective"></a>

### 3.57 Effectivity of the dynatomic cycle

Let φ be a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d ≥ 2 over a field K (any characteristic). Then a*_P(n) ≥ 0 for every n ≥ 1 and every P ∈ ℙ¹(K̄); that is, the n-th dynatomic cycle Z*ₙ(φ) = Σ_{d∣n} μ(n/d) Z_d(φ) is effective.

K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio. The statement for points over K̄ is the statement over K̄ for the base-changed lift (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-base-change).

If P is not periodic, a*_P(n) = 0; otherwise let m be its exact period; a*_P(φ, n) = 0 if m ∤ n and = a*_P(φᵐ, n/m) otherwise (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/essential-multiplicity-of-an-iterate). Replace φ by ψ = φᵐ, so P is fixed, and move P to [0 : 1] by a conjugation over K̄ (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/conjugacy-of-rational-maps, ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-conjugation). If r = 0 then a_P(ψ, k) = 1 for all k and a*_P(ψ, N) = [N = 1] ≥ 0 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-profile-at-a-fixed-point). If r ≥ 1, the profile of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-profile-at-a-fixed-point and ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/moebius-transform-of-a-multiplicity-profile give a*_P(ψ, N) = [N = 1] + [N = r](B(0) − 1) + Σ_{a≥1}[N = r pᵃ](B(a) − B(a − 1)), a sum of nonnegative terms since B(0) ≥ 2 and B is nondecreasing.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-3-morton-no-rational-four-cycles"></a>

### 3.58 No rational 4-cycles for z² + c (Morton)

There are no c, x ∈ ℚ such that x has exact period 4 for z² + c; equivalently Φ*₄(x, c) = 0 has no rational points.

f_c(z) = z² + c with c ∈ ℚ; exact period is Mathlib's Function.minimalPeriod of f_c on ℚ (0 for non-periodic points).

A rational point of exact period 4 is a rational point of Φ*₄(x, c) = 0 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/exact-period-is-formal-period; Φ*₄ = Morton's degree-12 Φ₄, ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/unicritical-dynatomic-polynomial). Put w = x + f²(x) = x⁴ + 2cx² + x + c + c² ∈ ℚ; the function field of Φ₄ = 0 is ℚ(w, Δ) with Δ² = (w⁴ − 1)(w² + 2w − 1) and x = w/2 ± Δ/(2(w³ − w)) (Morton 1998, Proposition 2); with u = −(w + 1)/(w − 1) and v = (u + 1)³Δ/4 one gets the curve v² = u(u² + 1)(1 + 2u − u²) (Proposition 3), a model of X₁(16). Request to EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3: the rational points of v² = u(u² + 1)(1 + 2u − u²) are exactly (0, 0), (±1, ±2) and the point at infinity (Morton cites Washington; J₁(16)(ℚ) is finite). The affine curve Φ₄(x, c) = 0 is nonsingular: the ideal (Φ₄, ∂Φ₄/∂x, ∂Φ₄/∂c) is the unit ideal of ℚ[x, c] (a Gröbner-basis certificate, verified by computer algebra). Hence every rational point (x, c) is a degree-one place of the function field ℚ(x, c) = ℚ(w, Δ), and Morton's divisor computation (proof of Theorem 4) shows that the six degree-one places are poles of x or c, so no finite (x, c) is rational.

### 3.59 No rational 5-cycles for z² + c (Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer)

There are no c, x ∈ ℚ such that x has exact period 5 for z² + c.

f_c(z) = z² + c with c ∈ ℚ; exact period is Mathlib's Function.minimalPeriod of f_c on ℚ (0 for non-periodic points).

A rational 5-cycle gives a rational point (t, c) of the trace curve τ₅(t, c) = 0 with t = x + f(x) + ⋯ + f⁴(x) (FPS §3; τ₅ displayed there). The affine curve τ₅ = 0 has a single singular point (−1, −4/3), a node. FPS's substitutions (z = r − 1, c = s − 4/3; s = rt; r = q − t; completing the square in t; p = 192y, q = −1 − 4x/3) map every rational point with r ≠ 0 and 216 + 144q − 72q² ≠ 0 to a rational point of C : y² = x⁶ + 8x⁵ + 22x⁴ + 22x³ + 5x² + 6x + 1. From the displayed models, the excluded rational points have r = 0 (c ∈ {−4/3, −2}) or q ∈ {3, −1}, where the equation is linear in t with solutions (q, t) = (3, −4/3) and (−1, 1/3), i.e. c = −64/9 and c = −16/9. Requests: EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3 (J(C)(ℚ) ≅ ℤ by a 2-descent, FPS Theorem 3) and EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4 (Chabauty–Coleman at p = 3 shows C(ℚ) = {(0, ±1), (−3, ±1), ∞±}, FPS Theorem 6). The six points have c ∈ {∞, −16/9, −64/9, −2} (FPS Table 2). So c ∈ {−2, −16/9, −64/9, −4/3}; for these, ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/unicritical-rational-preperiodic-enumeration-correct returns {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2} (c = −2) and ∅ (the others), with no point of exact period 5.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-3-formal-period-classification"></a>

### 3.60 Which formal periods occur: n ∈ {m, m·r, m·r·pᵉ}

Let φ be a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d ≥ 2 over a field K of characteristic p ≥ 0, P ∈ ℙ¹(K̄) periodic of exact period m, and r the multiplicative order in K̄^× of the multiplier (φᵐ)′(P) (r = ∞ if it is 0 or not a root of unity). For n ≥ 1, a*_P(n) ≥ 1 if and only if (i) n = m; or (ii) n = m·r (if r = 1 then a*_P(m) ≥ 2); or (iii) p > 0 and n = m·r·pᵉ for some e ≥ 1, in which case a*_P(n) ≥ 2^{e−1}(a_P(m·r) − 1). If P is not periodic, a*_P(n) = 0.

K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio. r = ∞ excludes (ii) and (iii); p = 0 excludes (iii).

Reduce to a fixed point of ψ = φᵐ at [0 : 1] as in ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-cycle-effective (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/essential-multiplicity-of-an-iterate, ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-conjugation). With N = n/m: a*_P(ψ, N) = [N = 1] + [N = r](B(0) − 1) + Σ_{a≥1}[N = r pᵃ](B(a) − B(a − 1)) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/moebius-transform-of-a-multiplicity-profile, ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-profile-at-a-fixed-point); for r = ∞ it is [N = 1]. Each displayed term is ≥ 1 exactly on its support: B(0) − 1 ≥ 1, and for p > 0, B(a) − B(a − 1) ≥ B(a − 1) − 1 ≥ 2^{a−1}(B(0) − 1) ≥ 1 by the growth B(a + 1) ≥ 2B(a) − 1 (same profile lemma), with B(0) = a_P(mr). For r = 1 the terms at N = 1 add: a*_P(m) = 1 + (B(0) − 1) = a_P(m) ≥ 2.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-3-dynatomic-polynomial-is-polynomial"></a>

### 3.61 The Möbius product ∏ Φₘ^{μ(n/m)} is a polynomial

Let φ be a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d ≥ 2 over a field K and n ≥ 1. Then ∏_{m ∣ n} Φₘ(φ)^{μ(n/m)} ∈ Frac K[X, Y] lies in K[X, Y]; i.e. ι(Φ*ₙ(φ)) = ∏_{m∣n} ι(Φₘ(φ))^{μ(n/m)}, ∏_{m∣n} Φ*ₘ(φ) = Φₙ(φ), and ord_P Φ*ₙ(φ) = a*_P(n) for all P.

K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.

Strong induction on n: suppose forms Q_m with ord_P Q_m = a*_P(m) (all P over K̄) are built for the proper divisors m of n with ∏_{k∣m} Q_k = Φ_m. The product D = ∏_{m ∣ n, m < n} Q_m has ord_P D = Σ_{m∣n, m<n} a*_P(m) = a_P(n) − a*_P(n) ≤ a_P(n) (Möbius inversion, mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.sum_eq_iff_sum_mul_moebius_eq; effectivity ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-cycle-effective). Hence D ∣ Φₙ over K̄ (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/binary-form-divisibility-criterion (a); Φₙ ≠ 0 by the API of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form) and so over K (part (b)); put Qₙ := Φₙ/D, with ord_P Qₙ = a*_P(n). Möbius inversion in the multiplicative group of Frac K[X, Y] (mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.prod_eq_iff_prod_pow_moebius_eq_of_nonzero; all Φₘ ≠ 0) turns ∏_{k∣m} Q_k = Φ_m into Qₙ = ∏_{m∣n} Φₘ^{μ(n/m)}; so Qₙ = Φ*ₙ(φ) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial).

### 3.62 Characteristic zero: formal period n and exact period m < n force n = m·r

Let K have characteristic 0, φ a lift of a morphism of degree d ≥ 2 over K and P of exact period m. If P has formal period n > m, then n = m·r and the multiplier (φᵐ)′(P) is a primitive (n/m)-th root of unity; in particular P has at most two formal periods, m and m·r.

K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio. char K = 0.

Apply ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/formal-period-classification with p = 0: case (iii) is excluded, and n ≠ m leaves n = m·r with r finite. r is the order of the multiplier, so the multiplier is a primitive r-th root of unity (mathlib:orderOf, mathlib:IsPrimitiveRoot) with r = n/m.

### 3.63 A formal periodic point of multiplicity one has exact period n

Let φ be a lift of a morphism of degree d ≥ 2 over K and n ≥ 1 with n ≠ 0 in K. If a*_P(n) = 1 then P has exact period n. Equivalently, if P has exact period m < n and a*_P(n) ≠ 0 then a*_P(n) ≥ 2.

K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio. n ≠ 0 in K (Hutz's Example 3.2 shows this is necessary in dimension 2).

By ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/formal-period-classification, n ∈ {m, mr, mrpᵉ}; since p ∤ n (n ≠ 0 in K), n ∈ {m, mr}. Suppose n = mr with r ≥ 2. The Möbius formula gives a*_P(n) = B(0) − 1 with B(0) = ord((g_{φᵐ})ʳ − z) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/moebius-transform-of-a-multiplicity-profile, ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-profile-at-a-fixed-point). ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/germ-order-rotation-congruence gives r ∣ B(0) − 1 with B(0) − 1 ≥ r ≥ 2, contradicting a*_P(n) = 1. So n = m (r = 1 also gives n = m).

### 3.64 Dynatomic cycles with non-divisible indices are disjoint

Let φ be a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d ≥ 2 over a field K, and n₁, n₂ ≥ 1 with n₁ ∤ n₂ and n₂ ∤ n₁. Then Z*_{n₁}(φ) and Z*_{n₂}(φ) have disjoint supports: no point has both formal periods.

K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.

If P lies in both supports, each of n₁, n₂ is m, mr or mrpᵉ (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/formal-period-classification). These numbers form a chain under divisibility, so the smaller of n₁, n₂ divides the larger, a contradiction.
