### 3.65 The degree of Φ*ₙ

For a lift of a morphism of degree d ≥ 2 and n ≥ 1, Φ*ₙ(φ) is homogeneous of degree Σ_{m∣n} μ(n/m)(dᵐ + 1) = νd(n) + [n = 1], where νd(n) = Σ_{m∣n} μ(n/m) dᵐ; for a polynomial map the affine Φ*ₙ(f) has degree νd(n). For d = 2: ν₂(n) = 2, 2, 6, 12, 30, 54, 126 for n = 1, …, 7.

K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.

Φₘ is homogeneous of degree dᵐ + 1 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form), degrees add in products of homogeneous forms, and ∏_{m∣n} Φ*ₘ = Φₙ (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-is-polynomial). Möbius inversion of n ↦ dⁿ + 1 (mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.sum_eq_iff_sum_mul_moebius_eq) and Σ_{m∣n} μ(n/m) = [n = 1].

### 3.66 Reduction of the dynatomic polynomial at a prime of good reduction

Let R be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field K and residue field k, and φ a lift with coefficients in R such that both φ_K and its reduction φ̃ are lifts of morphisms of degree d ≥ 2 (good reduction). Then for n ≥ 1 there is a form Q ∈ R[X, Y] with Q = u·Φ*ₙ(φ_K) for some u ∈ K^× and Q̃ = Φ*ₙ(φ̃). In the language of cycles: the reduction of Z*ₙ(φ) is Z*ₙ(φ̃) (and likewise for Zₙ).

R is a discrete valuation ring; φ has good reduction (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map): after scaling the lift so that its coefficients lie in R with one of them a unit, φ̃ has no common zero over k̄ (equivalently the resultant is a unit).

Composite lifts and period forms commute with reduction (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-base-change), and Φₙ(φ̃) ≠ 0 since φ̃ is a morphism of degree ≥ 2 (API of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form); so Φₙ(φ) ∈ R[X, Y] has unit content. Clear denominators of each Φ*ₘ(φ_K) and divide by the lowest coefficient valuation to obtain primitive Qₘ over R. The residue polynomial of a primitive form is nonzero; since k[X,Y] is a domain, a product of primitive forms is primitive. Thus lowest coefficient valuations add under multiplication. The product identity for Φ* and the unit content of Φₙ imply ∏_{m∣n} Qₘ = v Φₙ with v a unit of R. This supplies the content argument directly, without an uncited general Gauss-content theorem. Reducing, ∏_{m∣n} Q̃ₘ = ṽ·Φₙ(φ̃) for all n with Q̃ₘ ≠ 0; Möbius inversion over k (as in ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-is-polynomial, applied to φ̃, and mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.prod_eq_iff_prod_pow_moebius_eq_of_nonzero) gives Q̃ₙ = w·Φ*ₙ(φ̃) with w ∈ k^×; lift w to R^× and rescale Qₙ (mathlib:IsLocalRing.residue).

### 3.67 The affine and homogeneous dynatomic polynomials agree

Let K be a field and f ∈ K[z] monic of degree d ≥ 2, with lift φ_f = (Y^d f(X/Y), Y^d). For n ≥ 1, Φ*ₙ(φ_f)(X, 1) = Φ*ₙ(f)(X). In particular ∞ has essential multiplicity [n = 1] (it is a superattracting fixed point).

K a field; f monic of degree d ≥ 2.

Strong induction on n. Put Dₘ := Φ*ₘ(φ_f)(X, 1). Dehomogenising ∏_{m∣n} Φ*ₘ(φ_f) = Φₙ(φ_f) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-is-polynomial) gives ∏_{m∣n} Dₘ = fⁿ(X) − X (API aeval_periodForm_polynomialLift of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form). Each Dₘ is monic: Dₘ = ∏_{k∣m}(f^k − X)^{μ(m/k)} in K(X) and each f^k − X is monic, so the leading coefficients multiply to 1. By induction Dₘ = Φ*ₘ(f) for the proper divisors; the product D of these is monic, so Dₙ = (fⁿ − X) /ₘ D = Φ*ₙ(f) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-of-a-polynomial-map, mathlib:Polynomial.divByMonic). At ∞: the germ of φ_f at ∞ has multiplier 0, so a_∞(n) = 1 for all n (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-profile-at-a-fixed-point, case r = 0) and a*_∞(n) = [n = 1].

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-3-transitive-marked-monodromy"></a>

### 3.68 Transitivity of unicritical marked-point monodromy

For d≥2,n≥1, remove from the parameter plane the finite branch parameters of the period-n dynatomic curve. Analytic continuation acts transitively on its generic formal period-n roots (all exact period n there). Consequently the smooth affine dynatomic curve has one connected component and its defining polynomial is irreducible over ℂ[c,x].

Generic parameter away from every branch value; n=1 handled by the explicit graph c=z−z^d.

For n>1 rotate a primitive periodic word to its maximal lexicographic marking. If its maximal angle fails the satellite condition, primitive monodromy raises the last digit. If it satisfies the satellite condition, use the primitive angles of Lemma 3.12 successively to reach a word whose total digit sum increases. The sum is bounded by n(d−1)−1, so the process reaches the distinguished orbit with word (d−1)…(d−1)(d−2). Use the distinguished satellite loop to connect every marking in that orbit; concatenate and reverse loops to connect any two initial roots. For a smooth affine plane curve, transitivity gives connectedness and hence irreducibility; use analytic/algebraic comparison gap G2 for this final bridge.

### 3.69 Periods of rational periodic points at a prime of good reduction

Let K be the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring R with residue field k of characteristic p ≥ 0, and φ a lift of a morphism of degree d ≥ 2 with good reduction. Let P ∈ ℙ¹(K) have exact period n, let m be the exact period of its reduction P̃ under φ̃, and r the multiplicative order in k̄^× of the multiplier (φ̃ᵐ)′(P̃) (r = ∞ if it is 0). Then n = m, or n = m·r, or n = m·r·pᵉ for some e ≥ 1.

R a discrete valuation ring; good reduction as in ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-reduction; P is K-rational (or, after a finite extension of K and a prime above p, rational over that extension).

P has formal period n (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/exact-period-is-formal-period), so a*_P(φ, n) ≥ 1. Let Q be the integral model of Φ*ₙ(φ) from ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-reduction. Over a finite extension where Φ*ₙ splits, Q = c·∏ ℓ_{P′}^{a*_{P′}(n)} with integrally normalised linear forms (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/binary-form-divisibility-criterion); all exponents are ≥ 0 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-cycle-effective). Reducing, the multiplicity of P̃ in Q̃ = Φ*ₙ(φ̃) is Σ_{P′ ↦ P̃} a*_{P′}(n) ≥ a*_P(n) ≥ 1, so P̃ has formal period n for φ̃. Apply ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/formal-period-classification to φ̃ over k: n ∈ {m, m·r, m·r·pᵉ}.

### 3.70 ∏_{m∣n} Φ*ₘ(f) = fⁿ(z) − z for monic f over any ring

Let R be a commutative ring and f ∈ R[z] monic of degree d ≥ 2. For every n ≥ 1, ∏_{m ∣ n} Φ*ₘ(f) = fⁿ(z) − z; each Φ*ₘ(f) is monic of degree νd(m).

R is a commutative ring and f ∈ R[z] is monic of degree d ≥ 2 (for z^d + c: R = ℤ[c] or any ring containing c).

Field case: by ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-dehomogenisation, Φ*ₘ(f) is the dehomogenisation of Φ*ₘ of the lift, and dehomogenising ∏_{m∣n} Φ*ₘ = Φₙ (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-is-polynomial) gives fⁿ(z) − z (API aeval_periodForm_polynomialLift of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form). Induct on n: proper-divisor factors are monic, so comparison of leading coefficients in the product identity makes the remaining factor monic. Domain case: map to the fraction field, which is injective, and use mathlib:Polynomial.map_divByMonic. General case: let A = ℤ[a₀, …, a_{d−1}] and F = z^d + Σ aᵢzⁱ ∈ A[z], a monic polynomial over a domain; the ring homomorphism A → R with aᵢ ↦ coeff i f maps F to f, and both sides of the identity commute with this map (mathlib:Polynomial.map_divByMonic; map commutes with comp), so the identity for F implies it for f. The field-case induction gives monicity; monic division and the universal coefficient ring then preserve it over arbitrary R. The product has degree dⁿ; subtract the degrees of proper-divisor factors and use Möbius inversion (ArithmeticFunction.sum_eq_iff_sum_mul_moebius_eq) to obtain νd(n).

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-3-dynatomic-curve"></a>

### 3.71 The dynatomic curve Y₁(n) of the family x^d + c

For d ≥ 2 and n ≥ 1, the dynatomic curve Y₁(n) is the affine plane curve over ℤ defined by Φ*ₙ(x, c) = 0, i.e. Spec of the coordinate ring ℤ[c][x]/(Φ*ₙ(x, c)). Its points in a ring L are the pairs (x, c) ∈ L² with Φ*ₙ(x, c) = 0; over a field these are the pairs with x of formal period n for x^d + c (exact period n apart from the points described by ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/formal-period-classification, e.g. (−1/2, −3/4) on Y₁(2)). The substitution σ : x ↦ x^d + c induces an automorphism of Y₁(n) whose n-th power is the identity. This node owns only the affine coordinate ring and rotation. The downstream projective-dynatomic-model and dynatomic-cycle-quotient targets construct X₁(n) and X₀(n) over characteristic-zero fields; quadratic-dynatomic-genera computes their genera. These downstream constructions are not prerequisites of the affine curve.

d ≥ 2, n ≥ 1; the coordinate ring is Mathlib's AdjoinRoot of Φ*ₙ(x, c) over ℤ[c].

Define the coordinate ring as AdjoinRoot (Φ*ₙ(x, c)) (mathlib:AdjoinRoot) over ℤ[c] (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/unicritical-dynatomic-polynomial). Points: ring homomorphisms ℤ[c][x]/(Φ*ₙ) → L correspond to pairs (x₀, c₀) with Φ*ₙ(x₀, c₀) = 0 (mathlib:AdjoinRoot.lift); over a field, Φ*ₙ(x₀, c₀) = 0 iff x₀ has formal period n for x^d + c₀ (API eval_dynatomicForm_eq_zero_iff with ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-dehomogenisation). σ: Φ*ₙ(x, c) divides Φ*ₙ(x^d + c, c) in ℤ[c][x]. Over an algebraic closure of ℚ(c) the roots of Φ*ₙ are permuted by f = x^d + c with multiplicities preserved, because f is a local isomorphism at each root (the critical point 0 is not periodic for transcendental c) and conjugating germs preserves a*; divide Φ*ₙ(f(x),c) by the monic Φ*ₙ in ℤ[c][x]. Division commutes with the injection ℤ[c] → ℚ(c) (Polynomial.map_divByMonic); its remainder is zero over ℚ(c), hence zero over ℤ[c]. σⁿ = id modulo Φ*ₙ because Φ*ₙ ∣ fⁿ(x) − x (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-of-a-polynomial-map-product).

### 3.72 From analytic branches to the algebraic dynatomic curve

For d≥2,n≥1, the complex zero scheme of the inherited Φ*ₙ,d is reduced, smooth and geometrically integral; its complex points are the closure in ℂ² of exact n-period pairs with multiplier≠1. At a pair of exact period m dividing n with multiplier of order r>1, it belongs to that closure exactly when n=mr; multiplier 1 points of exact n-period also belong. The complex smoothness/irreducibility descends to any characteristic-zero field by the integral-coefficient model and faithful field extension. This refines the inherited smooth-irreducible endpoint with the missing closure-to-equation and descent contracts.

d≥2,n≥1; do not identify every root of f_c^n(z)−z with a dynatomic point. Formal/exact-period classification is the inherited one; boundary means closure minus the open exact-period, multiplier≠1 locus, not the topological boundary of a curve in ℂ².

Use the inherited formal-period classification to list possible lower-period roots. Local transversality and parabolic splitting identify exactly which branches occur in the closure. Local defining equations have a nonzero partial derivative; compare the monic product factorization f_c^n−z=∏_{e|n}Φ*ₑ to identify the reduced local equations, not only their zero sets. Transitive marked monodromy gives irreducibility of the reduced curve. Transfer the analytic Jacobian and component assertions to smooth/geometrically integral affine schemes and descend by faithful field extension; gap G2 states the exact comparison input.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-3-stoll-conditional-no-rational-six-cycles"></a>

### 3.74 No rational 6-cycles for z² + c, conditionally (Stoll)

Let J be the Jacobian of the genus-4 curve X₀^dyn(6) = X₁^dyn(6)/⟨σ⟩ for z² + c. If the Mordell–Weil rank of J(ℚ) is 3, then X₀^dyn(6) has exactly ten rational points and there are no c, x ∈ ℚ with x of exact period 6 for z² + c. (Stoll deduces rank J(ℚ) ≤ 3, hence = 3, from the weak Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture for J together with analytic continuation and the functional equation of L(J, s); that hypothesis is not consumed here.)

f_c(z) = z² + c with c ∈ ℚ; exact period is Mathlib's Function.minimalPeriod of f_c on ℚ (0 for non-periodic points). Explicit hypothesis: rank J(ℚ) = 3. The Jacobian, its Mordell–Weil group and its rank are supplied through EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3; the statement is not formalisable in Mathlib at the pinned commit, so no Lean form is suggested.

Ten known rational points of X₀^dyn(6) generate a torsion-free subgroup G of rank 3 of J(ℚ) (Stoll §3); if rank J(ℚ) = 3 then G has finite index and J(ℚ) is the saturation of G (request EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3: saturation at the required primes). A Chabauty argument at p = 5 with a differential annihilating G shows that no further rational point maps into the saturation of G (request EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4, Stoll's lemma before Theorem 6). None of the non-cuspidal points among the ten lifts to a rational point of X₁^dyn(6), and a rational 6-cycle gives a non-cuspidal rational point of X₁^dyn(6) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-curve, ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/exact-period-is-formal-period).

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-3-unicritical-dynatomic-curve-smooth-irreducible"></a>

### 3.75 Y₁(n) over ℂ is smooth and irreducible

For d ≥ 2 and n ≥ 1, the polynomial Φ*ₙ(x, c) is irreducible in ℂ[x, c] and the affine curve Φ*ₙ(x, c) = 0 in ℂ² is nonsingular: there is no (x, c) with Φ*ₙ = ∂Φ*ₙ/∂x = ∂Φ*ₙ/∂c = 0 (Bousch for d = 2; Buff–Tan; Gao–Ou for all d).

d ≥ 2, n ≥ 1, over ℂ. The closure of the exact-period, multiplier-not-one locus is identified with the reduced zero set of Φ*ₙ by ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/analytic-dynatomic-identification, including its parabolic boundary and its unresolved analytic/comparison inputs. Formal-period classification alone does not supply that identification. Generic simple roots make Φ*ₙ squarefree.

analytic-dynatomic-identification identifies the reduced analytic marked-periodic curve with V(Φ*ₙ), including its parabolic boundary. Its two explicit analytic and comparison gaps remain prerequisites of this endpoint. Use the quadratic-differential pushforward and contraction, transversality, kneading and labelled monodromy targets to obtain smoothness and transitivity. Gao–Ou Theorems 1.1–1.2 supply the endpoint; the detailed contracts are the follow-up nodes, rather than an undecomposed appeal to holomorphic dynamics. Generic simple roots make Φ*ₙ squarefree; smoothness of the reduced zero set and transitive marked monodromy then give the stated polynomial irreducibility and nonvanishing gradient.

### 3.76 Smooth projective models of marked dynatomic curves

For d≥2,n≥1 and a characteristic-zero field k, put A=k[c,x]/(Φ*ₙ,d), using the inherited monic dynatomic polynomial. Once geometric integrality of A is established, F=Frac(A) is a one-variable function field with exact constants k. Define X₁,d(n) as the regular projective model of F supplied by AlgebraicCurves, with the open immersion Y₁,d(n)→X₁,d(n) from the smooth affine model. The element c∈F induces a finite morphism π₁:X₁,d(n)→ℙ¹_k of degree ν_d(n)=Σ_{e|n} μ(n/e)d^e. This is the normalization of the projective closure; the possibly singular plane closure is not the model used for genus or rational points.

k a field of characteristic zero; d≥2,n≥1. Geometric integrality and affine smoothness are discharged by the analytic identification target, not assumed to follow from monicity.

Use the inherited coordinate ring and its geometric-integrality endpoint, refined by analytic-dynatomic-identification below. Monicity makes A finite over k[c]. Use AlgebraicCurves Layers 0,2,12 to form the function field and its unique regular projective model; characteristic zero makes the regular model smooth. Extend c and x as rational functions on the model; the field inclusion k(c)⊂F gives π₁, of degree deg_x Φ*. Uniqueness of the model gives the normalization and base-change comparisons.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-3-quadratic-rational-cycles-of-length-at-most-three"></a>

### 3.77 Rational points of period 1, 2, 3 for z² + c

Let c ∈ ℚ and f = z² + c. (1) f has a rational fixed point iff c = 1/4 − ρ² for some ρ ∈ ℚ; the fixed points are 1/2 ± ρ. (2) f has a rational point of exact period 2 iff c = −3/4 − σ² for some σ ∈ ℚ, σ ≠ 0; they are −1/2 ± σ and form a 2-cycle. (3) f has a rational point of exact period 3 iff c = −(τ⁶ + 2τ⁵ + 4τ⁴ + 8τ³ + 9τ² + 4τ + 1)/(4τ²(τ + 1)²) for some τ ∈ ℚ ∖ {0, −1}; the cycle is x₁ = (τ³ + 2τ² + τ + 1)/(2τ(τ + 1)) ↦ x₂ = (τ³ − τ − 1)/(2τ(τ + 1)) ↦ x₃ = −(τ³ + 2τ² + 3τ + 1)/(2τ(τ + 1)) ↦ x₁, and τ = x₁ + x₂. The at-most-one rational 3-cycle conclusion is owned separately by morton-rational-three-cycle-reduction.

f_c(z) = z² + c with c ∈ ℚ; exact period is Mathlib's Function.minimalPeriod of f_c on ℚ (0 for non-periodic points).

(1) f(x) = x iff c = x − x² = 1/4 − (x − 1/2)²: put ρ = x − 1/2. (2) A point of exact period 2 is a root of Φ*₂ = x² + x + c + 1 that is not fixed (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/exact-period-is-formal-period, API of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-of-a-polynomial-map); x = −1/2 ± σ with σ² = −3/4 − c, and σ = 0 is exactly the fixed point −1/2 of formal period 2 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/lower-period-root-of-a-dynatomic-polynomial). (3) Parametrisation: substituting shows x₁ ↦ x₂ ↦ x₃ ↦ x₁ under z² + c(τ) (checked by computer algebra). Converse: for a rational point x of exact period 3, Φ*₃(x, c) = 0; put τ := x + f(x) ∈ ℚ. Modulo Φ*₃(x, c), 2τ(τ + 1)·x = τ³ + 2τ² + τ + 1 and 4τ²(τ + 1)²·c = −(τ⁶ + ⋯ + 1) (identities verified by reduction modulo the monic Φ*₃ in ℚ[c][x]); the first identity forces τ ∉ {0, −1}, so c = c(τ) and x = x₁(τ).

### 3.78 Projective quotient by cycle rotation

Extend the inherited rotation σ(x)=x^d+c, σ(c)=c to F and its smooth projective model. Its order is exactly n (including order 1 at n=1), since a generic marked point has exact period n. Set F₀=F^{⟨σ⟩}; X₀,d(n) is the regular projective model of F₀. The inclusion F₀⊂F gives q:X₁→X₀ of degree n, and π₁ factors uniquely through π₀:X₀→ℙ¹ of degree ν_d(n)/n. On the open subset of exact-period points away from ramification, geometric fibres of q are the n cyclic markings of one cycle. A k-point of X₀ there represents a Galois-stable cycle, which need not have any k-rational marked point.

Characteristic zero field k; d≥2,n≥1. Use the open exact-period locus for the cycle interpretation; boundary and lower-period points remain in the projective quotient.

The ring automorphism extends to the fraction field; its n-th power is identity. Generic exact period gives order exactly n. Import AlgebraicCurves Layer 11 fixed-field degree theorem and Layer 12 dictionary to define the quotient model and finite maps. Over an algebraic closure, q identifies precisely the rotation orbits; descent of that orbit is Galois stability. A rational lift requires trivial Galois action on the marked points, an additional condition.

The reusable interface consists of the following statements.

- **`dynatomicCycleModel`** (constructor): Regular projective model of F^{⟨σ⟩}.
- **`dynatomicRotation`** (structure): Automorphism σ of X₁, order exactly n, with σ(x)=x^d+c and σ(c)=c on function fields.
- **`dynatomicCycleProjection`** (projection): q:X₁→X₀, q∘σ=q, finite of degree n.
- **`cycleProjection_factor`** (universal-property): Any invariant morphism from X₁ to a regular projective curve factors uniquely through q.
- **`cycleProjection_fibre`** (characterisation): On the unramified exact-period locus, q(P)=q(Q) iff Q=σ^j(P) for some 0≤j<n.
- **`cycleModel_baseChange`** (functoriality): Characteristic-zero field extensions commute with the fixed-field quotient and its maps.
- **`rationalCyclePoint_iff`** (compatibility): A rational quotient point on the free locus is a Galois-stable geometric cycle; rational marked lift iff every point in that cycle is rational.

### 3.83 The symmetric curve for two marked 3-cycles

Define H(t,u)=(t²−1)u³+(t³−2t²−9t+2)u²−9(t²−1)u−(t³−2t²−9t+2) over ℚ, and let the affine Morton curve be H=0. It is symmetric in t,u. With ζ=t+u,υ=tu, its equation is υ²(ζ−2)−υ(6ζ+4)−(ζ³−2ζ²−9ζ+2)=0. Define t(c,x)=1+2c+2x+2x² on a marked period 3 point. For t²≠1, its inverse is x=(t³+t²−t+7)/(4(t²−1)), c=−(t⁶−2t⁵+11t⁴+20t³+23t²−18t+29)/(16(t²−1)²). The rotation sends t to (t+3)/(1−t), and η(t)=(t³−9t)/(t²−1) is constant on the cycle, with c=−(η²−2η+29)/16.

All explicit coordinates over ℚ; inverses and rotation formulas have their displayed nonzero denominators. Two different cycles at the same c have η values adding to 2; repeating the same cycle does not supply the required symmetric-curve point.

Use the explicit Φ₃ polynomial of Morton §1 and eliminate c after introducing t; polynomial division gives the inverse formulas. Substitute f_c(x) into t to find the fractional-linear rotation; sum its three orbit values to obtain η and its quadratic parameter relation. For two distinct cycles the two roots η and 2−η of that quadratic give H(t,u)=0. Expand in symmetric functions to obtain the displayed equation.

### 3.84 Ramification of the quadratic parameter maps

Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, put ν(n)=½Σ_{e|n}μ(n/e)2^e. For X₁(n)→ℙ¹_c the degree is 2ν(n); above ∞ there are ν(n) places each of index 2. The finite branch parameters partition into primitive period-n parabolic parameters (bₙ of them) and satellite parameters of exact cycle period e<n with multiplier of order n/e (b_{n,e} of them). Here b_{n,e}=ν(e)φ(n/e) and bₙ=ν(n)−Σ_{e|n,e<n}b_{n,e}. Each primitive parameter has n ramified places of index 2; each satellite parameter has e places of index n/e; all other places above those parameters are unramified. Consequently deg Diff(F/k(c))=nν(n)−Σ_{e|n,e<n}eν(e)φ(n/e)+ν(n). For F₀/k(c), finite different degree is bₙ and infinity different degree is 2ν(n)/n−eₙ.

k algebraically closed, char 0; n≥1. Ramification of the normalized curve is used; the discriminant of a possibly nonnormal multiplier plane equation is not its field different.

Use parabolic-parameter-transversality and the local branch descriptions to count primitive and satellite branch parameters via multiplier/cyclotomic factors. Morton Proposition 9 proves the affine coordinate ring is the integral closure and computes finite different exponents, including the satellite contribution n−e. At infinity use c=u² and the distinct Laurent expansions of periodic roots (Morton Proposition 10); for F₀ use primitive binary necklaces and their complement stabilizers. Characteristic zero is tame, so import different exponent e−1 from AlgebraicCurves Layer 7; sum contributions with residue degree 1. The quotient is unramified at satellite parameters, not at primitive ones.

<a id="dy-4"></a>
## Layer 4: Adelic equidistribution and dynamical pairings

Start with local energies and adelic measures on P¹, then construct heights and pairings and prove small-point equidistribution. This P¹ route does not close the global Arakelov and moduli gaps beneath the general-variety endpoints. Distinct periodic-point averages and multiplicity-counted averages have different proof inputs.

Planets: Adelic measure; Equidistribution of small points on P¹; Arakelov–Zhang pairing; Yuan's equidistribution theorem; Dynamical equidistribution; Vanishing of the dynamical pairing.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-analytic-line-at-a-place"></a>

### 4.1 The analytic projective line at a place of a number field, with its kernel, circle measures and weight

Let K be a number field and v a place of K. Fix a complete algebraically closed field C_v containing the completion K_v, with the absolute value |·|_v extending the standard absolute value of ℚ (|p|_v = 1/p when v lies over the prime p; the usual absolute value when v is infinite, where C_v = ℂ), and fix an embedding ι_v : K̄ → C_v extending K → K_v; put |x|_v := |ι_v(x)|_v, an absolute value on K̄ extending v. The analytic line at v is the compact Hausdorff space P¹_v^an equal to the Riemann sphere P¹(ℂ) when v is infinite and to the Berkovich projective line over C_v when v is finite, together with: (i) the inclusion P¹(K̄) → P¹_v^an of type I points, x ↦ ι_v(x), ∞ ↦ ∞; (ii) the kernel δ_v on A¹_v^an × A¹_v^an, equal to |x − y| on ℂ at an infinite place and to the Hsia kernel relative to ∞ at a finite place (δ_v(x, y) = diam(x ∨ y), the diameter of the smallest disc point above x and y; Favre–Rivera-Letelier's sup{x, y}), so that δ_v(ι_v x, ι_v y) = |x − y|_v for x, y ∈ K̄; (iii) for a ∈ K̄ and r > 0 the circle measure m_{a,r,v}, the normalised arc-length probability measure on {z : |z − ι_v a| = r} at an infinite place and the Dirac mass at the point ζ_{ι_v a, r} (the sup-norm on the disc D(ι_v a, r)) at a finite place; (iv) the weight r_v = [K_v : ℚ_v]/[K : ℚ].

K is a number field; v ranges over its places (Mathlib's NumberField.InfinitePlace K ⊔ NumberField.FinitePlace K). At a finite place the Berkovich projective line over C_v and its points ζ_{a,r} are imported from TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.1.

Choose C_v: ℂ at an infinite place; at a finite place over p the completion of an algebraic closure of K_v (isometric to Mathlib's PadicComplex p). Extend K → K_v ⊂ C_v to ι_v : K̄ → C_v, which exists because C_v is algebraically closed (IsAlgClosed.lift). At a finite place take the Berkovich projective line over C_v, with its type I–IV points, the points ζ_{a,r}, compactness and the Hsia kernel relative to ∞, from TB.1 (request). At an infinite place take OnePoint ℂ with its compact Hausdorff topology. Define δ_v, the circle measures m_{a,r,v} and the weight r_v as in the statement. At an infinite place w the weight is mult(w)/[K : ℚ] (NumberField.InfinitePlace.mult); at a finite place it is [K_v : ℚ_p]/[K : ℚ]. With these weights r_v log|a|_v = [K : ℚ]^{-1} log ‖a‖_v, where ‖·‖_v is Mathlib's normalised place value (w(a)^{mult w} at infinite w, the FinitePlace value at finite v), so the product formula of Mathlib (NumberField.prod_abs_eq_one) reads Σ_v r_v log|a|_v = 0 for a ∈ K^×. Another embedding ι'_v differs from ι_v by an element of Gal(K̄/K), so every construction below made from Galois-stable data is independent of the choice (see DY.4/galois-orbit-measure).

*Needs:* `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.1`; `mathlib:NumberField.InfinitePlace`; `mathlib:NumberField.FinitePlace`; `mathlib:NumberField.InfinitePlace.mult`; `mathlib:AlgebraicClosure`; `mathlib:IsAlgClosed.lift`; `mathlib:PadicComplex`; `mathlib:OnePoint`; `mathlib:NumberField.prod_abs_eq_one`; `mathlib:circleAverage_log_norm_sub_const_eq_log_radius_add_posLog`.

- **`NumberFieldPlace.sum_weight_infinite`** (relation): Σ_{v infinite} r_v = 1.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-generic-sequence"></a>

### 4.2 Generic sequences of algebraic points

Let X be an integral scheme of finite type over K. A sequence (x_n) of points of X with values in K̄ (viewed as points of the underlying space of X) is generic if for every Zariski-closed Z ⊊ X only finitely many n satisfy x_n ∈ Z; equivalently, no infinite subsequence is contained in a proper closed subvariety of X. On a curve (in particular on P¹) a sequence is generic iff every point occurs for only finitely many n. A sequence (x_n) is small for a height h with target c if h(x_n) → c; for an adelic metrized line bundle the target is h_L̄(X).

X integral of finite type over K; points with values in K̄.

The proper closed subsets of an integral curve are the finite sets of closed points, which gives the curve criterion. If f : X → Y is a dominant morphism and x_n ∈ X generic, then f(x_n) is generic: f(x_n) ∈ Z ⊊ Y infinitely often would put x_n in the proper closed subset f^{-1}(Z). A subsequence of a generic sequence is generic.

*Needs:* `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral`; `mathlib:IsClosed`; `mathlib:Set.Finite`.

([yuan2008](#source-parent-yuan2008), §1.1, p. 3 — The definition; [yuan2008](#source-parent-yuan2008), §3.1, p. 34 — Small sequences.)

The reusable interface consists of the following statements.

- **`IsGenericSequence`** (data): The predicate: for every proper closed Z ⊊ X, {n : x_n ∈ Z} is finite.
- **`isGenericSequence_iff_finite_fibres`** (characterisation): For X of dimension 1: (x_n) is generic iff {n : x_n = x} is finite for every x.
- **`IsGenericSequence.comp_strictMono`** (functoriality): A subsequence of a generic sequence is generic.
- **`IsGenericSequence.map_dominant`** (functoriality): The image of a generic sequence under a dominant morphism is generic.
- **`not_isGenericSequence_of_forall_mem`** (other): If all x_n lie in a proper closed Z, the sequence is not generic.

**Checks.**

- **`test_not_isGenericSequence_const`** (non-example): A constant sequence in a positive-dimensional integral X is not generic.
- **`test_isGenericSequence_injective_curve`** (characterisation): An injective sequence of closed points of an integral curve is generic.
- **`test_not_isGenericSequence_line`** (non-example): A sequence of distinct points on a line in the affine plane is not generic in the plane.
- **`test_isGenericSequence_point`** (degenerate): If X = Spec K is a point, its only proper closed subset is ∅, so every sequence in X is generic.

**Endpoint checks.** On P¹ the sequence of primitive n-th roots of unity is generic; the constant sequence 0 is not. For f(z) = z^d the exceptional set {0, ∞} is a proper subvariety; the sequence x_n = 0 is small (ĥ_f(0) = 0) but not generic, and [x_n]_v = δ_0 does not converge to λ_v.

### 4.3 The standard measure λ_v at a place

The standard measure at a place v of K is λ_v := m_{0,1,v}: the normalised Haar (arc-length) probability measure on the unit circle {|z| = 1} ⊂ ℂ when v is infinite, and the Dirac mass at the Gauss point ζ_{0,1} when v is finite. Its logarithmic potential is ∫ log δ_v(z, w) dλ_v(w) = log⁺|z|_v for z ∈ P¹(C_v) ∖ {∞}, extended continuously to A¹_v^an.

v is a place of the number field K; P¹_v^an is DY.4/analytic-line-at-a-place.

Define λ_v as the circle measure m_{0,1,v} of DY.4/analytic-line-at-a-place. Its potential is log max(|z|_v, 1) = log⁺|z|_v by the circle-measure potential formula (Jensen's formula at infinite places, Mathlib circleAverage_log_norm_sub_const_eq_log_radius_add_posLog; the Gauss norm at finite places). (λ_v, λ_v)_v = −∫ log⁺|z|_v dλ_v = 0 and ([x]_v, λ_v)_v = −log⁺|x|_v follow from the Fubini formula for the mutual energy supplied by TB.6.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/analytic-line-at-a-place`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-analytic-line-at-a-place); `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.6`; `mathlib:circleAverage_log_norm_sub_const_eq_log_radius_add_posLog`.

- **`AnalyticLine.potential_standard`** (simp): ∫ log δ_v(ι_v z, w) dλ_v(w) = log⁺|z|_v for z ∈ K̄.
- **`AnalyticLine.energy_standard_self`** (simp): (λ_v, λ_v)_v = 0.
- **`AnalyticLine.energy_dirac_standard`** (simp): ([x]_v, λ_v)_v = −log⁺|x|_v for x ∈ K̄.
- **`AnalyticLine.standard_hasContinuousPotential`** (other): λ_v has continuous potential (its potential relative to itself is 0).
- **`AnalyticLine.standard_invariant_unit`** (relation): λ_v is invariant under z ↦ uz for |u|_v = 1 and, at a finite place, under PGL₂(O_{C_v}).

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-galois-orbit-measure"></a>

### 4.4 Galois-stable finite sets and their probability measures [F]_v

A finite set F ⊂ P¹(K̄) is Galois-stable if σ(F) = F for every σ ∈ Gal(K̄/K); the Galois orbit Gal(K̄/K)·x of x ∈ P¹(K̄) is the smallest Galois-stable set containing x, of cardinality [K(x) : K] (1 for x = ∞). For a nonempty finite F ⊂ P¹(K̄) and a place v, [F]_v := |F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} δ_{ι_v x} is the equidistributed probability measure on the image of F in P¹_v^an. If F is Galois-stable, [F]_v does not depend on the embedding ι_v.

F finite; for independence of ι_v, F Galois-stable.

The orbit of x ∈ K̄ is the set of roots of its minimal polynomial over K, finite of size [K(x) : K] (minpoly). The elements of C_v algebraic over K form an algebraic closure of K. Both embeddings ι_v and ι'_v map K̄ isomorphically onto that same field, so ι'_v = ι_v ∘ σ for a K-automorphism σ of K̄. Thus the images of a Galois-stable finite set, and their uniform measures, agree. Under a finite extension L/K and a place w of L above v, a Galois-stable set over K is Galois-stable over L and [F]_w = [F]_v on P¹_w^an = P¹_v^an.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/analytic-line-at-a-place`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-analytic-line-at-a-place); `mathlib:minpoly`; `mathlib:AlgebraicClosure`; `mathlib:MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac`.

([favre-rivera-letelier-2006](#source-parent-favre-rivera-letelier-2006), §1.1, p. 4 — The measure [F]; [pst2012](#source-parent-pst2012), §4.4, (20), p. 12 — Independence of the embedding.)

- **`galoisOrbitFinset`** (constructor): The Galois orbit of x ∈ P¹(K̄), as a finite set.
- **`isGaloisStableFinset_galoisOrbitFinset`** (characterisation): The orbit of x is Galois-stable, contains x, and is contained in every Galois-stable set containing x.
- **`card_galoisOrbitFinset`** (simp): |Gal·x| = [K(x) : K] for x ∈ K̄, and |Gal·∞| = 1.
- **`AnalyticLine.orbitMeasure`** (constructor): [F]_v = |F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} δ_{ι_v x}.
- **`AnalyticLine.orbitMeasure_univ`** (simp): [F]_v(P¹_v^an) = 1 for F nonempty.
- **`AnalyticLine.integral_orbitMeasure`** (simp): ∫ f d[F]_v = |F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} f(ι_v x).

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-regularisation-modulus-tends-to-zero"></a>

### 4.5 Continuous functions are uniformly approximated by their circle averages

For every place v and every continuous g : P¹_v^an → ℝ, the regularisation modulus ω_g(r) := sup_{x∈K̄} |∫ g dm_{x,r,v} − g(ι_v x)| tends to 0 as r → 0⁺. If g is κ-Hölder for the chordal metric (0 < κ ≤ 1), then ω_g(r) ≤ C r^κ.

g continuous on the compact space P¹_v^an.

Infinite place: P¹(ℂ) is a compact metric space for the chordal metric, g is uniformly continuous, and every point of the circle |z − x| = r is within chordal distance ≤ r of x; so ω_g(r) ≤ sup_{d(z,z')≤r} |g(z) − g(z')| → 0. At a finite place, argue by compactness with convergent subnets, rather than assuming sequential compactness. Along a bounded subnet, factor every polynomial over C_v and compare Π max(|x−a_i|,r) with Π|x−a_i| as r→0: the evaluation seminorms and ζ_{x,r} have the same limit. If the limit is ∞, use the reciprocal chart; r→0 and |x|→∞ put both points in every sufficiently small neighbourhood of ∞. The weak topology of TB.1 then forces the same limit, contradicting a fixed positive difference of g-values. The Hölder bound: the chordal distance between ι x and ζ_{x,r} (FRL §4.7) is at most r.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/analytic-line-at-a-place`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-analytic-line-at-a-place); `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.1`; `mathlib:CompactSpace.uniformContinuous_of_continuous`.

**Endpoint checks.** For g(z) = min(log⁺|z|_v, 1): ω_g(r) ≤ r at an infinite place (g is 1-Lipschitz in |z|) and ω_g(r) = 0 for r < 1 at a finite place (log⁺|ζ_{x,r}|_v = log⁺|x|_v). For g constant, ω_g ≡ 0.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-equidistribution-for-semipositive-adelic-line-bundles"></a>

### 4.6 Equidistribution of small points for semipositive adelic line bundles (Yuan)

Let X be a projective variety of dimension n ≥ 1 over a number field K and L̄ = (L, (‖·‖_v)_v) an ample line bundle with a semipositive adelic metric (at every place a uniform limit of semipositive model metrics, and the model metric of one integral model at almost all places; TB.6). Put h_L̄(X) := ĉ₁(L̄)^{n+1}/((n + 1) deg_L X) and h_L̄(x) := ĉ₁(L̄|_x̄)/deg x. If (x_m) is a generic sequence in X(K̄) with h_L̄(x_m) → h_L̄(X), then for every place v the Galois-orbit probability measures µ_{v,x_m} converge weakly on X_v^an to c₁(L̄_v)^n / deg_L(X), a probability measure because c₁(L̄_v)^n has total mass deg_L X.

X projective, dim X = n ≥ 1; L ample with semipositive adelic metric; (x_m) generic and small.

Reduce to the geometric case over X_{C_v}^an and to test functions f that are smooth (infinite v) or model functions (finite v; Gubler's density theorem, TB.6), by Stone–Weierstrass (Yuan §3.1–3.3). Variational principle: for ε > 0 twist the metric at v by e^{−εf}, L̄(εf); then h_{L̄(εf)}(x_m) = h_L̄(x_m) + r_v ε ∫ f dµ_{v,x_m}. Write O(f) as a difference of two ample metrized line bundles and apply Yuan's arithmetic Siu inequality (Theorem 2.2; Lemma 3.3) to obtain small sections of N·L̄(εf), hence liminf_m h_{L̄(εf)}(x_m) ≥ ĉ₁(L̄(εf))^{n+1}/((n+1)deg_L X) + O(ε²) for the generic sequence (Zhang's successive-minima inequality). Expand ĉ₁(L̄(εf))^{n+1} = ĉ₁(L̄)^{n+1} + (n+1)r_v ε ∫ f c₁(L̄_v)^n + O(ε²); divide by ε and let ε → 0⁺, then replace f by −f. The global inputs (adelic intersection numbers, heights of subvarieties, arithmetic Siu, successive minima) are gaps G1–G2 of this packet; the local measures and model approximation come from TB.6, the analytification X_v^an from TB.0 and deg_L X from SF.5.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/generic-sequence`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-generic-sequence); `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.6`; `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5`.

([yuan2008](#source-parent-yuan2008), Theorem 3.1, pp. 34–35 — The conclusion (Yuan's dim X = n − 1); [yuan2008](#source-parent-yuan2008), §3.1, p. 33 — The height of X; [yuan2008](#source-parent-yuan2008), §1.3, p. 7 — The proof strategy.)

**Endpoint checks.** For (X, L̄) = (P¹, Ō(1)) with φ semipositive the theorem is DY.4/equidistribution-for-semipositive-adelic-metrics-on-p1 (h_L̄(P¹) = ½ Ō·Ō). For an abelian variety with the Néron–Tate metric of a symmetric ample bundle it is the Szpiro–Ullmo–Zhang theorem consumed by HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions RP.5. Genericity cannot be dropped: torsion points of an abelian subvariety B ⊊ A equidistribute to the Haar measure of B(ℂ), not of A(ℂ).

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-adelic-measure"></a>

### 4.7 Adelic measures on the projective line

An adelic measure ρ over the number field K is a family (ρ_v)_{v∈M_K} of probability measures ρ_v on P¹_v^an such that (i) ρ_v = λ_v for all but finitely many places v, and (ii) each ρ_v has a continuous potential: there is a continuous g_{ρ,v} : P¹_v^an → ℝ with g_{ρ,v}(z) = ∫ log δ_v(z, w) dρ_v(w) − log⁺|z|_v for z ∈ A¹_v^an (equivalently ρ_v − λ_v = Δ g_{ρ,v} for the Laplacian of TB.6, normalised by Δ log⁺|z|_v = λ_v − δ_∞); the continuous extension satisfies g_{ρ,v}(∞) = 0. N(ρ) denotes the finite set of places with ρ_v ≠ λ_v. For a finite extension L/K an adelic measure over K defines one over L by ρ_w := ρ_v for w | v.

K a number field; P¹_v^an, δ_v and λ_v as in DY.4/analytic-line-at-a-place and DY.4/standard-measure-at-a-place. The Laplacian, potentials and the class of measures with continuous potential are those of TB.6 (request).

The data are the measures ρ_v; condition (ii) is stated through the logarithmic potential, which needs only the kernel δ_v. A measure with continuous potential charges no type I point (the potential of a point mass at a type I point is −∞ there), in particular not ∞; hence g_{ρ,v}(z) → 0 as z → ∞ (FRL, proof of Proposition 2.6), which is the normalisation g_{ρ,v}(∞) = 0. Base change: for L/K and w | v, P¹_w^an = P¹_v^an (the same C_v) and λ_w = λ_v, so (ρ_v)_{w|v} is an adelic measure over L.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/standard-measure-at-a-place`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-standard-measure-at-a-place); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/analytic-line-at-a-place`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-analytic-line-at-a-place); `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.6`; `mathlib:MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure`.

- **`AdelicMeasure.standard`** (constructor): The standard adelic measure λ = (λ_v).
- **`AdelicMeasure.exceptionalPlaces`** (data): The finite set N(ρ) = {v : ρ_v ≠ λ_v}.
- **`AdelicMeasure.potential`** (data): The continuous potential g_{ρ,v} : P¹_v^an → ℝ with g_{ρ,v}(z) = ∫ log δ_v(z, w) dρ_v(w) − log⁺|z|_v and g_{ρ,v}(∞) = 0.
- **`AdelicMeasure.potential_eq_zero`** (simp): g_{ρ,v} = 0 for v ∉ N(ρ), and g_{λ,v} = 0 for all v.
- **`AdelicMeasure.ext`** (extensionality): ρ = σ iff ρ_v = σ_v for every place v.
- **`AdelicMeasure.baseChange`** (functoriality): For L/K finite, the adelic measure (ρ_v)_{w|v} over L; heights and pairings are unchanged (see DY.4/adelic-height-of-a-galois-stable-set).
- **`AdelicMeasure.not_atom`** (other): ρ_v gives measure 0 to every type I point, in particular to ∞.

**Checks.**

- **`AdelicMeasure.test_standard_exceptionalPlaces`** (degenerate): N(λ) = ∅.
- **`AdelicMeasure.test_gauss_radius`** (computation): Over ℚ, the family with ρ_p = δ_{ζ_{0,p}} and ρ_v = λ_v for v ≠ p is an adelic measure with N(ρ) = {p} and g_{ρ,p}(z) = log max(|z|_p, p) − log⁺|z|_p.
- **`AdelicMeasure.test_not_dirac_type_one`** (non-example): A family with ρ_v = δ_{ι_v 0} at some place is not an adelic measure.
- **`AdelicMeasure.test_not_infinitely_many`** (non-example): The family with ρ_p = δ_{ζ_{0,p}} at every prime p is not an adelic measure (ρ_p ≠ λ_p for infinitely many p).

**Endpoint checks.** The standard family λ = (λ_v) is an adelic measure with N(λ) = ∅. Over ℚ, ρ_p := δ_{ζ_{0,p}} at one prime p and ρ_v := λ_v elsewhere is an adelic measure: g_{ρ,p}(z) = log max(|z|_p, p) − log⁺|z|_p is continuous. ρ_v := δ_{ι_v 0} at one place is not an adelic measure: its potential log|z|_v − log⁺|z|_v tends to −∞ at 0.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-adelic-metrized-line-bundle-on-p1"></a>

### 4.8 Adelic metrics on O_{P¹}(1)

An adelic metric on O_{P¹}(1) over K is a family φ = (φ_v)_{v∈M_K} of continuous functions φ_v : P¹_v^an → ℝ with φ_v = 0 for all but finitely many v. It defines at each place the continuous metric ‖·‖_v := ‖·‖_{st,v} e^{−φ_v} on O(1) over P¹_v^an, where the standard metric is ‖s(x)‖_{st,v} = |s(x₀, x₁)|_v / max(|x₀|_v, |x₁|_v) for a linear form s, extended continuously to P¹_v^an. With affine coordinate z = x₀/x₁ and ∞ = (1 : 0): −log‖x₁‖_v(z) = log⁺|z|_v + φ_v(z) (the section x₁ has divisor ∞) and −log‖x₀‖_v(z) = log⁺|z^{-1}|_v + φ_v(z) (divisor 0). The pair Ō = (O(1), (‖·‖_v)_v) is an adelically metrized line bundle on P¹ in the sense of Zhang, and φ ↦ Ō is a bijection onto continuous adelic metrics on O(1).

K a number field; the metrics on O(1)^an over P¹_v^an are those of TB.6 (request), described on P¹ by the function φ_v.

The standard metric is continuous on P¹_v^an: at a finite place −log‖x₁‖_st(S) = log⁺|S| is continuous on the Berkovich line (TB.1). Two continuous metrics on the same line bundle differ by e^{−φ} with φ continuous (the ratio of norms of a nowhere-vanishing local section), so every continuous metric has the stated form; this is the P¹ case of the correspondence of TB.6. The finiteness condition is Zhang's adelic condition: at all but finitely many places the metric is the model metric of the standard model P¹_{O_K}.

- **`AdelicMetric.twist`** (constructor): For constants c = (c_v), finitely many nonzero: φ + c, i.e. ‖·‖_v e^{−c_v}.
- **`AdelicMetric.average`** (constructor): The metric (‖·‖₁‖·‖₂)^{1/2}, i.e. (φ₁ + φ₂)/2.
- **`AdelicMetric.ext`** (extensionality): φ = ψ iff φ_v = ψ_v for all v.
- **`AdelicMetric.negLogNormX1`** (data): The function −log‖x₁‖_v = log⁺|z|_v + φ_v on P¹_v^an ∖ {∞}.
- **`AdelicMetric.support_finite`** (other): {v : φ_v ≠ 0} is finite.
- **`AdelicMetric.toContinuousMetric`** (compatibility): The continuous metric ‖·‖_{st,v}e^{−φ_v} on O(1)^an of TB.6, bijectively.

**Checks.**

- **`AdelicMetric.test_standard_negLogNorm`** (degenerate): For the standard metric, −log‖x₁‖_v(z) = log⁺|z|_v for z ∈ K̄.
- **`AdelicMetric.test_gauss_radius_metric`** (computation): For R ≥ 1, φ_v(z) = log max(|z|_v, R) − log⁺|z|_v at one place (0 elsewhere) is an adelic metric with φ_v(∞) = 0 and φ_v(0) = log R.
- **`AdelicMetric.test_average_standard`** (compatibility): The average of the standard metric with itself is the standard metric.
- **`AdelicMetric.test_not_adelic_all_primes`** (non-example): φ_p = 1 for every prime p (over ℚ) is not an adelic metric.

**Endpoint checks.** The standard metric φ = 0 gives −log‖x₁‖_v(z) = log⁺|z|_v. At a place v and R ≥ 1, φ_v(z) = log max(|z|_v, R) − log⁺|z|_v extends continuously to P¹_v^an with φ_v(∞) = 0; with φ_w = 0 elsewhere it is an adelic metric.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-regularised-measure-of-a-finite-set"></a>

### 4.9 Regularisation of a finite set by circles of radius r

For a place v, a nonempty finite set F ⊂ K̄ and r > 0, the regularised measure is [F]_{v,r} := |F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} m_{x,r,v}: the average of the normalised arc-length measures on the circles |z − x| = r (v infinite) or of the Dirac masses at the points ζ_{x,r} (v finite). Its potential is ∫ log δ_v(z, w) d[F]_{v,r}(w) = |F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} log max(|z − x|_v, r) for z ∈ K̄, it has a continuous potential in the sense of TB.6, and for x, y ∈ K̄ the mutual energy satisfies (m_{x,r,v}, m_{y,r,v})_v ≤ −log max(|x − y|_v, r). Equality holds at finite places; at infinite places it holds when x = y or |x − y| ≥ 2r.

F ⊂ K̄ finite nonempty (∞ ∉ F); r > 0.

The potential formula for one circle measure is AnalyticLine.potential_circle; average over F. At an infinite place the potential z ↦ |F|^{-1}Σ log max(|z − x|, r) is continuous on ℂ and log|z| + o(1) at ∞, so [F]_{v,r} − λ_v has a continuous potential on P¹(ℂ); at a finite place [F]_{v,r} is a finite combination of Dirac masses at type II/III points, which has continuous potential (FRL §4.3; TB.6). Integrate the potential of m_{x,r} against m_{y,r}. At a finite place the ultrametric disc formula gives exactly −log max(|x−y|,r). At an infinite place write log max(|z−x|,r) as the average of log|z−w| over w on the x-circle; Fubini and the circle-potential formula give its average over the y-circle at least log max(|x−y|,r). If |x−y| ≥ 2r, both circles are separated and the mean-value formula gives equality; for x = y the value is −log r. Overlapping distinct circles generally give a strict inequality. As r → 0, m_{x,r,v} → δ_{ι_v x} weakly, hence [F]_{v,r} → [F]_v.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-nonnegative-local-energy-at-standard-places"></a>

### 4.10 Nonnegativity of the local energy against the standard measure at finite places

Let v be a finite place and F ⊂ K̄ a nonempty finite set. Then (λ_v − [F]_v, λ_v − [F]_v)_v = (2/|F|) Σ_{x∈F} log⁺|x|_v − |F|^{-2} Σ_{x≠y∈F} log|x − y|_v ≥ (2/|F|²) Σ_{x∈F} log⁺|x|_v ≥ 0.

v finite (the ultrametric inequality is used).

Expand: (λ, λ) = 0, ([F], λ) = −|F|^{-1} Σ log⁺|x|_v (DY.4/standard-measure-at-a-place), ([F], [F]) = −|F|^{-2} Σ_{x≠y} log|x − y|_v. Ultrametric inequality: log|x − y|_v ≤ log⁺|x|_v + log⁺|y|_v; summing over ordered pairs x ≠ y gives Σ_{x≠y} log|x − y| ≤ 2(|F| − 1) Σ_x log⁺|x|_v. Hence the energy is ≥ (2/|F| − 2(|F| − 1)/|F|²) Σ log⁺|x|_v = (2/|F|²) Σ log⁺|x|_v ≥ 0.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/standard-measure-at-a-place`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-standard-measure-at-a-place); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/galois-orbit-measure`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-galois-orbit-measure); `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.6`.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-product-formula-for-the-energy-of-a-finite-set"></a>

### 4.11 Product formula for the energy of a Galois-stable finite set

For every finite Galois-stable F ⊂ P¹(K̄), Σ_{v∈M_K} r_v ([F]_v, [F]_v)_v = 0, where ([F]_v, [F]_v)_v = −|F|^{-2} Σ_{x≠y∈F∖{∞}} log|x − y|_v.

F Galois-stable and finite.

Let F′ = F ∖ {∞}; then ([F], [F])_v = −|F|^{-2} log|Δ_{F′}|_v with Δ_{F′} = Π_{x≠y∈F′} (x − y), a nonzero element of K̄. Every σ ∈ Gal(K̄/K) permutes the ordered pairs of F′, so σ(Δ_{F′}) = Δ_{F′}; hence Δ_{F′} ∈ K^× (the fixed field of Gal(K̄/K) in characteristic 0 is K). The product formula Σ_v r_v log|a|_v = 0 for a ∈ K^× (NumberFieldPlace.sum_weight_mul_log_eq_zero, from NumberField.prod_abs_eq_one) gives the claim.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-holder-continuity-of-canonical-potentials"></a>

### 4.12 Hölder continuity of the potential of a canonical measure

Let f be a rational map of degree d ≥ 2 over C_v (any place v) with lift F, and g_{f,v} the continuous potential of µ_{f,v} − λ_v (g_{f,v}(z) = G_{F,v}(z, 1) − log⁺|z|_v up to an additive constant). Then g_{f,v} is κ-Hölder for the chordal metric of P¹_v^an with κ = log d / log M, where M > d is a Lipschitz constant of f for that metric; consequently ω_{g_{f,v}}(r) ≤ C r^κ.

d ≥ 2; M > d a Lipschitz constant of f for the chordal metric (TB.1 at finite places).

g₁ := the potential of d^{−1} f^*λ_v − λ_v, i.e. g₁(x) = d^{−1} log‖F(x)‖_v − log‖x‖_v on lifts, is Lipschitz for the chordal metric (on the Riemann sphere the logarithm of the max norm is Lipschitz in both projective charts, although it can have corners; at finite places by the explicit form of ‖F(x)‖ on the Berkovich line, TB.1). g_{f,v} = Σ_{k≥0} d^{−k} g₁∘f^k up to a constant (telescoping the escape rate, DY.2/escape-rate), the series converging uniformly. For N ≥ 0: |g(z) − g(w)| ≤ Σ_{k<N} d^{−k} Lip(g₁) M^k d(z, w) + 2 sup|g₁| Σ_{k≥N} d^{−k} ≤ C₁ (M/d)^N d(z, w) + C₂ d^{−N}; choose N with (M/d)^N d(z, w) ≈ d^{−N} to get C d(z, w)^κ. The chordal distance between ι x and a point of the circle measure m_{x,r} is at most r, so ω_g(r) ≤ C r^κ.

**Endpoint checks.** f = z^d: g = 0. For f = z² + c at a finite place with |c|_v > 1 the potential is locally constant off the Julia set and the bound holds with κ = log 2/log M.

### 4.13 The height h_ρ attached to an adelic measure

For an adelic measure ρ over K and a finite Galois-stable set F ⊂ P¹(K̄), h_ρ(F) := ½ Σ_{v∈M_K} r_v ([F]_v − ρ_v, [F]_v − ρ_v)_v, where (·,·)_v is the mutual energy of TB.6 (the diagonal of type I points omitted, so ([F]_v, [F]_v)_v = −|F|^{-2} Σ_{x≠y∈F∖{∞}} log|x − y|_v); for x ∈ P¹(K̄), h_ρ(x) := h_ρ(Gal(K̄/K)·x). Only finitely many terms are nonzero, and h_ρ does not depend on K, on the embeddings ι_v, or on replacing K by a finite extension.

ρ adelic over K; F Galois-stable finite. All finite sets to which the height-average identities are applied are nonempty.

Finiteness: for v ∉ N(ρ) finite such that every x ∈ F ∖ {∞} is a v-adic unit or v-integral with all pairwise differences v-adic units, ([F] − λ_v, [F] − λ_v)_v = 0; all but finitely many places are of this kind (FRL §5.2). Independence of ι_v: DY.4/galois-orbit-measure. Independence of K: base change of ρ, the formula Σ_{w|v} r_w = r_v and the equality of the local terms at all w | v. Galois invariance: Gal·(σx) = Gal·x.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-canonical-adelic-measure-of-a-rational-map"></a>

### 4.14 The canonical adelic measure of a rational map

Let f : P¹ → P¹ be a rational map of degree d ≥ 2 over K. Its canonical adelic measure is ρ_f := (µ_{f,v})_{v∈M_K}, where µ_{f,v} is the canonical measure of f on P¹_v^an (DY.2/canonical-measure). It is an adelic measure: µ_{f,v} has a continuous potential, and µ_{f,v} = λ_v at every finite place where f has good reduction, hence at all but finitely many places.

f of degree d ≥ 2 over K.

Continuous potential: µ_{f,v} = λ_v + Δ(λ_{f,v} − log⁺|z|_v) with λ_{f,v} the local canonical height and λ_{f,v} − log⁺|z|_v continuous on P¹_v^an (DY.2/canonical-measure, DY.2/local-canonical-height; FRL §6.1). Good reduction: if a homogeneous lift F of f has v-integral coefficients and unit resultant, then max(|F₀|, |F₁|) = max(|x₀|, |x₁|)^d, the escape rate is log max(|x₀|, |x₁|), and µ_{f,v} = λ_v (PST Proposition 6; FRL §6.2). f has good reduction at all but finitely many places (DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map).

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-multibrot-adelic-measure"></a>

### 4.15 The adelic Multibrot measure

Fix D ≥ 2 and put P_c(z) = z^D + c. For a place v of ℚ (or of K ⊇ ℚ) let G_{M,v}(c) := lim_{n→∞} D^{−(n−1)} log⁺|P_cⁿ(0)|_v. At a finite place G_{M,v}(c) = log⁺|c|_v; at the infinite place G_M is continuous on ℂ, harmonic off the Multibrot set M_D = {c : (P_cⁿ(0))_n bounded}, zero on M_D, and G_M(c) = log|c| + o(1) as c → ∞ (M_D has logarithmic capacity 1). The family µ_{M_D} := (λ_v + Δ(G_{M,v} − log⁺|c|_v))_v — the harmonic (equilibrium) measure of M_D at the infinite place and λ_v at finite places — is an adelic measure with Hölder potentials, and ∫ log|c − w| dµ_{M_D,∞}(w) = G_M(c).

D ≥ 2; the normalisation D^{−(n−1)} corrects FRL Lemma 6.3 (sourceIssues E503).

Finite place: if |c|_v ≤ 1 all P_cⁿ(0) are v-integral; if |c|_v > 1, |P_cⁿ(0)|_v = |c|_v^{D^{n−1}} by induction, so G_{M,v}(c) = log⁺|c|_v and µ_{M,v} = λ_v. Infinite place: G_M(c) = G_{P_c}(c) = D·G_{P_c}(0) for the escape rate of P_c (DY.2/escape-rate); the telescoping estimate |D^{-n} log⁺|P_c^{n+1}(0)| − D^{−(n−1)} log⁺|P_cⁿ(0)|| ≤ D^{-n} log(1 + |c|) gives locally uniform convergence and continuity. G_M = 0 on M_D, G_M > 0 and harmonic off M_D (a locally uniform limit of harmonic functions where P_cⁿ(0) → ∞), and G_M(c) − log|c| → 0 at ∞ (|P_cⁿ(0)| = |c|^{D^{n−1}}(1 + o(1))). Hence ΔG_M = µ_{M,∞} − δ_∞ with µ_{M,∞} a probability measure on ∂M_D (TB.6, archimedean Laplacian); the potential u(c) = ∫ log|c − w| dµ_{M,∞}(w) has the same Laplacian, so u − G_M is constant, and the constant is 0 because both are log|c| + o(1) at ∞: µ_{M,∞} is the equilibrium measure of M_D and M_D has capacity 1. Hölder continuity of G_M: G_M(c) = D·G_{P_c}(0) and the escape rate is jointly Hölder in (c, z) on compact sets by the argument of FRL Proposition 6.5 (Lipschitz one-step estimate for (c, z) ↦ z^D + c, then optimisation of the truncation).

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-curvature-measures-of-an-adelic-metric"></a>

### 4.16 Curvature measures and semipositivity of an adelic metric on O(1)

For an adelic metric φ on O(1) over K, the curvature at v is initially the distribution µ_{φ,v} := λ_v + Δφ_v, with total mass 1 = deg O(1) (Laplacian of TB.6, Δ log⁺|z|_v = λ_v − δ_∞), characterised by Δ(−log‖s‖_v) = µ_{φ,v} − δ_{div s} for every linear form s; φ is semipositive if every curvature distribution is positive; in this case it is represented by a positive Radon measure. For semipositive φ, µ_φ = (µ_{φ,v})_v is an adelic measure: µ_{φ,v} = λ_v when φ_v = 0, and ∫ log δ_v(z, w) dµ_{φ,v}(w) − log⁺|z|_v = φ_v(z) − φ_v(∞), so the potential of µ_{φ,v} is g_{µ_φ,v} = φ_v − φ_v(∞). This is the P¹ case of the Chambert-Loir measure c₁(Ō_v) of TB.6.

φ an adelic metric on O(1) over K. An arbitrary continuous metric need not have a measure-valued Laplacian; only the semipositive case asserts curvature is a measure. The archimedean distribution and its positive-measure representation are part of the recorded analytic supplier gap.

Δ(−log‖x₁‖_v) = Δ log⁺|z|_v + Δφ_v = λ_v + Δφ_v − δ_∞ (TB.6 normalisation), so µ_{φ,v} := λ_v + Δφ_v; total mass: Δφ_v has mass 0. For another linear form s = a x₀ + b x₁, −log‖s‖_v − (−log‖x₁‖_v) = −log|a z + b|_v + (log of the constant part), whose Laplacian is δ_∞ − δ_{div s}; this gives the characterisation for every s. For semipositive φ, the positive curvature distribution is represented by a Radon measure of mass 1; its potential g(z) = ∫ log δ_v(z, w) dµ(w) − log⁺|z|_v satisfies Δg = µ − λ = Δφ_v, so g − φ_v is constant (Laplacian kernel = constants, TB.6), and g(∞) = 0 fixes the constant. At the places with φ_v = 0, µ_{φ,v} = λ_v; these are all but finitely many.

The metric −φ_v with R > 1 has curvature 2λ_v − m_{0,R,v}, which is not positive: not semipositive.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-regularised-self-energy-bound"></a>

### 4.17 The self-energy bound for regularised finite sets

For every place v, every nonempty finite F ⊂ K̄ and every r > 0: ([F]_{v,r}, [F]_{v,r})_v ≤ ([F]_v, [F]_v)_v + (−log r)/|F|, where ([F], [F])_v = −|F|^{-2} Σ_{x≠y∈F} log|x − y|_v (the diagonal omitted).

F ⊂ K̄ finite nonempty, r > 0.

Expand bilinearly: ([F]_r, [F]_r)_v = |F|^{-2} Σ_{x,y∈F} (m_{x,r}, m_{y,r})_v. For x ≠ y use (m_{x,r},m_{y,r})_v ≤ −log max(|x−y|_v,r) ≤ −log|x−y|_v; the first inequality may be strict at an infinite place. For x = y, (m_{x,r}, m_{x,r})_v = −log r; there are |F| diagonal terms, contributing |F|^{-2}·|F|·(−log r) = (−log r)/|F|.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/regularised-measure-of-a-finite-set`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-regularised-measure-of-a-finite-set); `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.6`.

([favre-rivera-letelier-2006](#source-parent-favre-rivera-letelier-2006), Lemma 4.11, p. 30 — The finite-place case; [fili2017](#source-parent-fili2017), Lemma 12, p. 13 — The infinite-place case with circle measures; [demarco-krieger-ye-2020](#source-parent-demarco-krieger-ye-2020), §7.2, p. 40 — The uniform statement used by DKY.)

**Endpoint checks.** Equality holds at finite places when |x−y|_v≥r for all distinct x,y; at infinite places it holds when |x−y|≥2r for all distinct x,y. For F = {0, 1} at an infinite place and r = 1/4: ([F]_r, [F]_r) = (log 4)/2 = ([F], [F]) + (log 4)/2.

Suggested library home: `TauCeti/ArithmeticDynamics/Equidistribution/Regularisation`, namespace `TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics`.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-regularised-pairing-estimate"></a>

### 4.18 Regularising a finite set changes its energy against a measure with continuous potential by little

Let v be a place, ρ a probability measure on P¹_v^an with continuous potential, and g the continuous function with g(z) = ∫ log δ_v(z, w) dρ(w) − log⁺|z|_v off ∞ (a potential of ρ − λ_v). For every nonempty finite F ⊂ K̄ and 0 < r < 1: |([F]_v, ρ)_v − ([F]_{v,r}, ρ)_v| ≤ ω_g(r) + ε_v(r), with ε_v(r) = r if v is infinite and ε_v(r) = 0 if v is finite.

ρ a probability measure with continuous potential (TB.6); 0 < r < 1.

By the Fubini formula for the energy (TB.6; FRL Lemmas 2.5 and 4.4), (µ, ρ)_v = −∫ g_ρ dµ for µ = [F]_v and µ = [F]_{v,r}, where g_ρ(z) = ∫ log δ_v(z, w) dρ(w) = log⁺|z|_v + g(z). So ([F], ρ) − ([F]_r, ρ) = |F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} (∫ g_ρ dm_{x,r} − g_ρ(ι x)). The g-part is bounded by ω_g(r) (DY.4/regularisation-modulus-tends-to-zero). The log⁺-part: at an infinite place |log⁺|x + re^{it}| − log⁺|x|| ≤ r since log⁺ is 1-Lipschitz; at a finite place log⁺|ζ_{x,r}| = log⁺ max(|x|_v, r) = log⁺|x|_v because r < 1.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/regularised-measure-of-a-finite-set`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-regularised-measure-of-a-finite-set); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/regularisation-modulus-tends-to-zero`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-regularisation-modulus-tends-to-zero); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/standard-measure-at-a-place`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-standard-measure-at-a-place); `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.6`.

([favre-rivera-letelier-2006](#source-parent-favre-rivera-letelier-2006), Lemma 2.9, p. 16 — The infinite-place case; [favre-rivera-letelier-2006](#source-parent-favre-rivera-letelier-2006), Lemma 4.10, p. 29 — The finite-place case.)

**Endpoint checks.** For ρ = λ_v at a finite place and r < 1 the difference is 0. For ρ = λ_v at an infinite place and F = {0}: ([0], λ) = 0 and ([0]_r, λ) = 0 for r < 1, so the difference is 0 ≤ r.

Suggested library home: `TauCeti/ArithmeticDynamics/Equidistribution/Regularisation`, namespace `TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics`.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-adelic-height-decomposition"></a>

### 4.19 Decomposition of the adelic height into local potentials

For an adelic measure ρ over K: h_ρ(∞) = ½ Σ_v r_v (ρ_v, ρ_v)_v, and for every nonempty finite Galois-stable F ⊂ K̄ (∞ ∉ F), h_ρ(F) = h_ρ(∞) − Σ_v r_v (ρ_v, [F]_v)_v = h_ρ(∞) + Σ_v r_v |F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} ∫ log δ_v(ι_v x, w) dρ_v(w). These two identities determine h_ρ; consequently h_ρ(F) = |F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} h_ρ(x) for every nonempty Galois-stable finite F ⊂ P¹(K̄).

ρ adelic; F Galois-stable finite. All finite sets to which the height-average identities are applied are nonempty.

[∞]_v pairs to 0 with every measure (pairs involving ∞ are excluded from the energy), so ([∞] − ρ, [∞] − ρ)_v = (ρ_v, ρ_v)_v. Expand ([F] − ρ, [F] − ρ)_v = (ρ, ρ)_v − 2(ρ, [F])_v + ([F], [F])_v (bilinearity, TB.6) and sum with weights; the last terms sum to 0 by DY.4/product-formula-for-the-energy-of-a-finite-set. (ρ_v, [F]_v)_v = −|F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} ∫ log δ_v(ι_v x, w) dρ_v(w) by the Fubini formula for the energy (TB.6). The right-hand side is affine in [F]_v, so for F a disjoint union of Galois orbits O_i, h_ρ(F) = Σ_i (|O_i|/|F|) h_ρ(O_i); for ∞ ∈ F use the first identity for the orbit {∞}.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/adelic-height-of-a-galois-stable-set`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-adelic-height-of-a-galois-stable-set); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/product-formula-for-the-energy-of-a-finite-set`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-product-formula-for-the-energy-of-a-finite-set); `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.6`.

([favre-rivera-letelier-2006](#source-parent-favre-rivera-letelier-2006), Lemme 5.3, p. 33 — The statement; [demarco-krieger-ye-2020](#source-parent-demarco-krieger-ye-2020), proof of Proposition 7.3, p. 40 — The averaged form used by DKY.)

**Endpoint checks.** For ρ = λ: h_λ(∞) = 0 and h_λ(F) = Σ_v r_v |F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} log⁺|x|_v. For the Gauss-radius measure over ℚ at p: h_ρ(0) = −½ log p − (−log p) = ½ log p.

Suggested library home: `TauCeti/ArithmeticDynamics/Equidistribution/AdelicHeight`, namespace `TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics`.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-local-dynamical-energy"></a>

### 4.20 The local dynamical energy of two rational maps

For rational maps f, g of degree ≥ 2 over K and a place v, E_v(f, g) := ½(µ_{f,v} − µ_{g,v}, µ_{f,v} − µ_{g,v})_v. Equivalently E_v(f, g) = ½(∫ (λ_{f,v} − λ_{g,v}) dµ_{g,v} + ∫ (λ_{g,v} − λ_{f,v}) dµ_{f,v}) for local canonical heights λ_{f,v}, λ_{g,v} (any normalisation). E_v(f, g) ≥ 0 with equality iff µ_{f,v} = µ_{g,v}, E_v = 0 for all but finitely many v, and ⟨f, g⟩ = Σ_v r_v E_v(f, g).

f, g of degree ≥ 2 over K; v a place.

λ_{f,v} − λ_{g,v} is a continuous potential of µ_{f,v} − µ_{g,v} up to an additive constant (DY.2/canonical-measure), so (µ_f − µ_g, µ_f − µ_g)_v = −∫ (λ_f − λ_g) d(µ_f − µ_g) (Fubini, TB.6), which is the displayed formula; constants integrate to 0 against a mass-zero measure. Positivity and nondegeneracy: TB.6 (FRL Propositions 2.6, 4.5). Where both maps have good reduction, µ_f = µ_g = λ_v.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.2/canonical-measure`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-canonical-measure); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.2/archimedean-canonical-measure`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-archimedean-canonical-measure); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.2/local-canonical-height`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-2-local-canonical-height); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/canonical-adelic-measure-of-a-rational-map`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-canonical-adelic-measure-of-a-rational-map); `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.6`.

([demarco-krieger-ye-2020](#source-parent-demarco-krieger-ye-2020), Proposition 2.2, p. 11 — The definition and positivity (Lattès case; the proof is general); [pst2012](#source-parent-pst2012), proof of Proposition 18, p. 16 — The computation behind the example.)

The reusable interface consists of the following statements.

- **`RationalMap.localEnergy`** (constructor): E_v(f, g) = ½(µ_{f,v} − µ_{g,v}, µ_{f,v} − µ_{g,v})_v.
- **`RationalMap.localEnergy_eq_localHeights`** (characterisation): E_v(f, g) = ½(∫(λ_f − λ_g)dµ_g + ∫(λ_g − λ_f)dµ_f).
- **`RationalMap.localEnergy_nonneg`** (other): E_v(f, g) ≥ 0, with equality iff µ_{f,v} = µ_{g,v}.
- **`RationalMap.localEnergy_comm`** (relation): E_v(f, g) = E_v(g, f).
- **`RationalMap.localEnergy_conj`** (functoriality): E_v(γ^{-1}fγ, γ^{-1}gγ) = E_v(f, g) for γ ∈ PGL₂(C_v) (energy of mass-zero measures is PGL₂-invariant, TB.6).
- **`RationalMap.azPairing_eq_sum_localEnergy`** (relation): ⟨f, g⟩ = Σ_v r_v E_v(f, g).

**Checks.**

- **`RationalMap.test_localEnergy_pow`** (degenerate): E_v(z², z³) = 0.
- **`RationalMap.test_localEnergy_translate_finite`** (computation): At a finite place with |α|_v > 1, E_v(z², α − (α − z)²) = log|α|_v.
- **`RationalMap.test_localEnergy_translate_infinite`** (computation): At an infinite place with |α| ≥ 2, E_v(z², α − (α − z)²) = log|α|.
- **`RationalMap.test_localEnergy_self`** (characterisation): E_v(f, f) = 0 for every f.

**Endpoint checks.** E_v(z², z³) = 0 at every place. For σ_α(z) = α − (α − z)²: E_v(z², σ_α) = log⁺|α|_v at a finite place (the hyperbolic distance from ζ_{0,1} to ζ_{α,1} is 2 log⁺|α|_v) and log⁺|α|_v + I(|α|_v) at an infinite place, I as in PST Lemma 17.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-adelic-metric-of-an-adelic-measure"></a>

### 4.21 The normalised adelic metric of an adelic measure

For an adelic measure ρ over K, the normalised adelic metric Ō^ρ is φ^ρ_v := g_{ρ,v} + ½(ρ_v, ρ_v)_v, where g_{ρ,v} is the potential of ρ_v (normalised by g_{ρ,v}(∞) = 0). It is semipositive with curvature ρ, φ^ρ_v = 0 for v ∉ N(ρ) (since (λ_v, λ_v)_v = 0), and φ^ρ_v(∞) = ½(ρ_v, ρ_v)_v. Every semipositive adelic metric with curvature ρ is φ^ρ + c for a unique family of constants c = (c_v).

ρ an adelic measure over K.

φ^ρ_v is continuous (g_{ρ,v} is) and vanishes where ρ_v = λ_v. Its curvature is λ_v + Δg_{ρ,v} = ρ_v (DY.4/curvature-measures-of-an-adelic-metric). Two semipositive metrics with the same curvature differ at each place by a function with zero Laplacian, hence a constant (TB.6).

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/adelic-measure`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-adelic-measure); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/curvature-measures-of-an-adelic-metric`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-curvature-measures-of-an-adelic-metric); `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.6`.

The reusable interface consists of the following statements.

- **`AdelicMeasure.metric`** (constructor): The normalised metric φ^ρ.
- **`AdelicMeasure.metric_isSemipositive`** (other): φ^ρ is semipositive.
- **`AdelicMeasure.curvature_metric`** (simp): The curvature of φ^ρ is ρ.
- **`AdelicMeasure.metric_infty`** (simp): φ^ρ_v(∞) = ½(ρ_v, ρ_v)_v.
- **`AdelicMeasure.metric_standard`** (simp): φ^λ is the standard metric.
- **`AdelicMetric.eq_metric_curvature_add_const`** (characterisation): A semipositive φ equals φ^{µ_φ} + c with c_v = φ_v(∞) − ½(µ_{φ,v}, µ_{φ,v})_v.

**Checks.**

- **`AdelicMeasure.test_metric_standard`** (degenerate): φ^λ = 0.
- **`AdelicMeasure.test_metric_gauss_radius`** (computation): For the Gauss-radius measure at p, φ^ρ_p(∞) = −½ log p.
- **`AdelicMeasure.test_curvature_metric`** (characterisation): The curvature of φ^ρ is ρ, for every adelic measure ρ.
- **`AdelicMeasure.test_metric_not_potential`** (non-example): For the Gauss-radius measure, the metric g_{ρ,·} without the constant ½(ρ, ρ) is not φ^ρ: their heights differ by ½ log p.

**Endpoint checks.** φ^λ = 0, the standard metric. For the Gauss-radius measure at p over ℚ: φ^ρ_p(z) = log max(|z|_p, p) − log⁺|z|_p − ½ log p.

### 4.22 Lower bound for the local energy of [F] − ρ

Let v, ρ and g be as in DY.4/regularised-pairing-estimate. For every nonempty finite F ⊂ K̄ and 0 < r < 1: ([F]_v − ρ, [F]_v − ρ)_v ≥ ([F]_{v,r} − ρ, [F]_{v,r} − ρ)_v − 2(ω_g(r) + ε_v(r)) − (−log r)/|F| ≥ −2(ω_g(r) + ε_v(r)) − (−log r)/|F|.

ρ a probability measure with continuous potential; 0 < r < 1.

Expand both energies bilinearly (TB.6): (µ − ρ, µ − ρ) = (µ, µ) − 2(µ, ρ) + (ρ, ρ) for µ = [F]_v and µ = [F]_{v,r}. Compare the (µ, µ) terms by DY.4/regularised-self-energy-bound and the (µ, ρ) terms by DY.4/regularised-pairing-estimate. The second inequality: [F]_{v,r} − ρ has total mass 0 and continuous potential, so its energy is ≥ 0 by the positivity of TB.6 (FRL Propositions 2.6 and 4.5).

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/regularised-self-energy-bound`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-regularised-self-energy-bound); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/regularised-pairing-estimate`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-regularised-pairing-estimate); `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.6`.

**Endpoint checks.** The unregularised energy can be negative: for P(T) = T² + C with |C|_v > 1 at a finite v ∤ 2 and F_n the fixed points of Pⁿ, ([F_n] − µ_{P,v}, [F_n] − µ_{P,v})_v = −n2^{−n} log √|C|_v (FRL §6.7, corrected in sourceIssues E504), consistent with the bound as r → 0 only through the −log r/|F| term.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-standard-adelic-height-is-the-weil-height"></a>

### 4.23 The standard adelic measure gives Mathlib's absolute logarithmic Weil height

For every x ∈ K̄, h_λ(x) = NumberField.absLogHeight₁ x, and h_λ(∞) = 0; that is, h_λ is the absolute logarithmic Weil height on P¹(K̄) with the convention h(∞) = 0.

λ the standard adelic measure over K.

By DY.4/adelic-height-decomposition and DY.4/standard-measure-at-a-place, h_λ(∞) = ½ Σ r_v (λ_v, λ_v) = 0 and h_λ(x) = Σ_v r_v |O|^{-1} Σ_{y∈O} log⁺|y|_v with O = Gal·x. Let L = K(x). The embeddings of L into C_v over K correspond to the places w | v of L, each counted [L_w : K_v] times; hence Σ_v r_v |O|^{-1} Σ_{y∈O} log⁺|y|_v = Σ_{w∈M_L} r_w log⁺|x|_w (r_w = [L_w : ℚ_w]/[L : ℚ]). By AnalyticLine.weight_mul_log_eq over L this is [L : ℚ]^{-1} logHeight₁ x computed in L (NumberField.logHeight₁_eq), which equals absLogHeight₁ x (DT.0/abs-mul-height-eq-rpow: the absolute height may be computed in any number field containing x).

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/adelic-height-decomposition`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-adelic-height-decomposition); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/standard-measure-at-a-place`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-standard-measure-at-a-place); `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/abs-mul-height-eq-rpow`; `mathlib:NumberField.absLogHeight₁`; `mathlib:NumberField.logHeight₁_eq`.

([favre-rivera-letelier-2006](#source-parent-favre-rivera-letelier-2006), §5.2, p. 32 — The comparison; [fili2017](#source-parent-fili2017), §2.2, p. 5 — The same comparison; [favre-rivera-letelier-2006](#source-parent-favre-rivera-letelier-2006), (1), p. 3 — The naive height as a Galois average.)

**Endpoint checks.** h_λ(2) = log 2, h_λ(1/2) = log 2, h_λ(√2) = ½ log 2 over ℚ. h_λ(ζ) = 0 for every root of unity ζ, and h_λ(0) = 0.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-mahler-formula-for-adelic-heights"></a>

### 4.24 Mahler formula for adelic heights

Let ρ be an adelic measure over K and α ∈ K̄ with monic minimal polynomial P ∈ K[T]. Then h_ρ(α) = h_ρ(∞) + deg(α)^{-1} Σ_v r_v ∫ log|P|_v dρ_v, where |P|_v(S) := S(P) on A¹_v^an (the value of the multiplicative seminorm S at P at a finite place; |P(z)| at an infinite place). At a finite place with ρ_v = λ_v the integral is log of the Gauss norm max_i |a_i|_v of P = Σ a_i T^i, so the sum is finite; for ρ = λ it is the classical Mahler-measure formula for the Weil height.

ρ adelic; α ∈ K̄, P = minpoly_K(α).

DY.4/adelic-height-decomposition with F = Gal·α, the set of roots of P: h_ρ(α) = h_ρ(∞) + Σ_v r_v deg(α)^{-1} Σ_{β: P(β)=0} ∫ log δ_v(ι_v β, S) dρ_v(S). For S ∈ A¹_v^an, Σ_β log δ_v(ι_v β, S) = log S(P): at an infinite place |P(z)| = Π|z − β|; at a finite place δ_v(β, S) = S(T − β) (the Hsia kernel relative to ∞ against a type I point, TB.1) and the seminorm S is multiplicative. At a finite place with ρ_v = λ_v = δ_{ζ_{0,1}}, ζ_{0,1}(P) is the Gauss norm.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/adelic-height-decomposition`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-adelic-height-decomposition); `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.1`; `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.6`; `mathlib:minpoly`.

([favre-rivera-letelier-2006](#source-parent-favre-rivera-letelier-2006), Proposition 1.3, p. 5 — The statement; [favre-rivera-letelier-2006](#source-parent-favre-rivera-letelier-2006), §5.3, (30), p. 34 — The local identity, proved here by multiplicativity of the seminorm instead of the Laplacian.)

**Endpoint checks.** ρ = λ, K = ℚ, α = 1/2: P = T − 1/2; the place 2 contributes log|1/2|_2 = log 2 and the infinite place contributes ∫ log|z − 1/2| dλ = log⁺(1/2) = 0, so h(1/2) = log 2. ρ = λ, α = √2 over ℚ: P = T² − 2, the infinite integral is ∫ log|z² − 2| dλ = log 2, finite places give 0, so h(√2) = ½ log 2.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-arakelov-zhang-pairing-of-adelic-measures"></a>

### 4.25 The Arakelov–Zhang pairing of adelic measures (mutual-energy distance)

For adelic measures ρ, σ over K: ⟨ρ, σ⟩ := ½ Σ_v r_v (ρ_v − σ_v, ρ_v − σ_v)_v, a finite sum; the local term ⟨ρ, σ⟩_v := ½(ρ_v − σ_v, ρ_v − σ_v)_v is the local energy. Equivalently ⟨ρ, σ⟩ = h_ρ(∞) + h_σ(∞) − Σ_v r_v (ρ_v, σ_v)_v, and ⟨ρ, σ⟩ = Ō^ρ·Ō^σ.

ρ, σ adelic over K.

ρ_v − σ_v = 0 outside N(ρ) ∪ N(σ), so the sum is finite; the energy is defined because both measures have continuous potentials (TB.6). Expanding and using DY.4/adelic-height-decomposition for h_ρ(∞) and h_σ(∞) gives the second formula (Fili Proposition 7). The identification with Ō^ρ·Ō^σ is DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-of-normalised-metrics. The value is unchanged by base change to L/K (Σ_{w|v} r_w = r_v).

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/adelic-measure`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-adelic-measure); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/adelic-height-decomposition`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-adelic-height-decomposition); `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.6`.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-local-equidistribution-criterion"></a>

### 4.26 Local energy criterion for weak convergence of [F_n]

Let v be a place and ρ a probability measure on P¹_v^an with continuous potential. Let F_n ⊂ P¹(K̄) be nonempty finite sets with |F_n| → ∞ and limsup_n ([F_n ∖ {∞}]_v − ρ, [F_n ∖ {∞}]_v − ρ)_v ≤ 0. Then [F_n]_v → ρ weakly: ∫ f d[F_n]_v → ∫ f dρ for every continuous f : P¹_v^an → ℝ.

ρ probability with continuous potential; |F_n| → ∞.

Removing ∞ from F_n changes [F_n]_v by a measure of total variation ≤ 2/|F_n| → 0, so assume ∞ ∉ F_n. Let ν_{n,r} := [F_n]_{v,r} − ρ, of mass 0 with continuous potential. By DY.4/energy-lower-bound-after-regularisation, (ν_{n,r}, ν_{n,r})_v ≤ ([F_n] − ρ, [F_n] − ρ)_v + 2(ω_g(r) + ε_v(r)) + (−log r)/|F_n|, so limsup_n (ν_{n,r}, ν_{n,r})_v ≤ 2(ω_g(r) + ε_v(r)), which tends to 0 as r → 0. For a test function φ in the dense class D_v of TB.6 (smooth at infinite places; locally constant off a finite subtree and C¹ on its edges at finite places) the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality |∫ φ dν|² ≤ ⟨φ, φ⟩_v (ν, ν)_v (TB.6; FRL (32)–(33) with the squares restored, sourceIssues E501) gives limsup_n |∫ φ dν_{n,r}| ≤ (⟨φ, φ⟩_v · 2(ω_g(r) + ε_v(r)))^{1/2}. |∫ φ d([F_n]_{v,r} − [F_n]_v)| ≤ ω_φ(r) uniformly in n (DY.4/regularisation-modulus-tends-to-zero); letting n → ∞ then r → 0 gives ∫ φ d[F_n]_v → ∫ φ dρ for φ ∈ D_v. D_v is dense in C(P¹_v^an) for the sup norm and all measures involved are probability measures, so the convergence holds for every continuous f (MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_iff_forall_integral_tendsto).

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/energy-lower-bound-after-regularisation`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-energy-lower-bound-after-regularisation); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/regularisation-modulus-tends-to-zero`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-regularisation-modulus-tends-to-zero); `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.6`; `mathlib:MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_iff_forall_integral_tendsto`.

([favre-rivera-letelier-2006](#source-parent-favre-rivera-letelier-2006), Proposition 2.11, p. 18 — The infinite-place statement; [favre-rivera-letelier-2006](#source-parent-favre-rivera-letelier-2006), Proposition 4.12, p. 30 — The finite-place statement; [favre-rivera-letelier-2006](#source-parent-favre-rivera-letelier-2006), (32)–(33), p. 36 — The Cauchy–Schwarz route used here for both places (with squares restored).)

The hypothesis |F_n| → ∞ is needed: F_n = {0} for all n has ([F_n] − λ, [F_n] − λ) = 0 at a finite place but [F_n] = δ_0 ≠ λ_v.

### 4.27 Quantitative equidistribution for adelic measures with Hölder potentials

Let ρ be an adelic measure over K whose potentials are Hölder in the sense that ω_{g_{ρ,v}}(r) ≤ C₀ r^κ for 0 < r < 1 and all v ∈ N(ρ), for some C₀ > 0 and 0 < κ ≤ 1. There is C > 0 depending only on ρ such that for every place v, every test function φ ∈ D_v (TB.6) with Dirichlet norm ⟨φ, φ⟩_v and regularisation constant Lip_v(φ) (|∫ φ dm_{x,r,v} − φ(ι_v x)| ≤ Lip_v(φ) r), and every Galois-stable finite F ⊂ K̄ with |F| ≥ 2: |∫ φ d[F]_v − ∫ φ dρ_v| ≤ Lip_v(φ) |F|^{−1/κ} + (⟨φ, φ⟩_v r_v^{−1} (2h_ρ(F) + C log|F| / |F|))^{1/2}.

ρ adelic with Hölder potentials at the places of N(ρ). The square root and the factor 2/r_v correct FRL Theorem 7 (sourceIssues E501, E502).

Let N be N(ρ) together with all infinite places. The standard potentials at the added places have modulus zero, so the Hölder bound still holds. Put r := |F|^{−1/κ} ≤ |F|^{−1}. Summing DY.4/energy-lower-bound-after-regularisation over N ∪ {v} and using DY.4/nonnegative-local-energy-at-standard-places at the other places: Σ_{w∈N∪{v}} r_w ([F]_r − ρ_w, [F]_r − ρ_w)_w ≤ 2h_ρ(F) + (|N| + 1) max_w r_w (2C₀|F|^{−1} + 2r + log|F|/(κ|F|)). The place weights satisfy 0 < r_w ≤ 1, uniformly over all w; thus the constant is independent of the place v. Each regularised term is ≥ 0 (TB.6 positivity), so r_v ([F]_r − ρ_v, [F]_r − ρ_v)_v ≤ 2h_ρ(F) + C log|F|/|F|. Cauchy–Schwarz for the Dirichlet form (TB.6): |∫ φ d([F]_r − ρ_v)| ≤ ⟨φ, φ⟩_v^{1/2} ([F]_r − ρ_v, [F]_r − ρ_v)_v^{1/2}. |∫ φ d([F]_r − [F])| ≤ Lip_v(φ) r = Lip_v(φ)|F|^{−1/κ}.

### 4.28 Adelic heights differ from the Weil height by a bounded function

For an adelic measure ρ over K and every x ∈ K̄: |h_ρ(x) − h_ρ(∞) − absLogHeight₁(x)| ≤ Σ_{v∈N(ρ)} r_v sup|g_{ρ,v}|; hence h_ρ − h is bounded on P¹(K̄) (with h(∞) = 0).

ρ adelic over K.

By DY.4/adelic-height-decomposition for ρ and for λ, h_ρ(x) − h_ρ(∞) − h_λ(x) = −Σ_v r_v (ρ_v − λ_v, [O]_v)_v with O = Gal·x. For v ∉ N(ρ) the term vanishes; for v ∈ N(ρ), −(ρ_v − λ_v, [O]_v)_v = |O|^{-1} Σ_{y∈O} g_{ρ,v}(ι_v y) (Fubini, TB.6), bounded by sup|g_{ρ,v}| (continuous on a compact space). Conclude with DY.4/standard-adelic-height-is-the-weil-height.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-height-of-an-adelic-metrized-line-bundle"></a>

### 4.29 The height of an adelic metric on O(1)

For an adelic metric φ on O(1) over K and x ∈ P¹(K̄) with Galois orbit O, h_φ(x) := Σ_v r_v |O|^{-1} Σ_{y∈O} (−log‖s(y)‖_v) for any linear form s over K with s(y) ≠ 0 on O. Equivalently h_φ(x) = absLogHeight₁(x) + Σ_v r_v |O|^{-1} Σ_{y∈O} φ_v(ι_v y) for x ∈ K̄, and h_φ(∞) = Σ_v r_v φ_v(∞).

φ an adelic metric; s a linear form over K not vanishing on O.

Independence of s: two sections differ by a rational function in K(z) whose values on O multiply to an element of K^× (a norm), killed by the product formula (PST Proposition 8, proof). With s = x₁ (for x ≠ ∞): −log‖x₁‖_v = log⁺|z|_v + φ_v, and Σ_v r_v |O|^{-1} Σ_y log⁺|y|_v = absLogHeight₁(x) (DY.4/standard-adelic-height-is-the-weil-height); with s = x₀ at ∞: −log‖x₀‖_v(∞) = φ_v(∞). Independence of K and Galois invariance as for h_ρ.
