### 4.30 The Multibrot height is the canonical height of the critical value

For c ∈ K̄: h_{µ_{M_D}}(c) = ĥ_{P_c}(c) = D·ĥ_{P_c}(0) = (D/(D − 1))·Σ_{P_c′(w)=0} ĥ_{P_c}(w) (critical points in ℂ counted with multiplicity). In particular h_{µ_{M_D}}(c) = 0 iff 0 is preperiodic for P_c (c is postcritically finite).

c ∈ K̄; D ≥ 2.

By DY.4/adelic-height-decomposition, h_µ(c) = h_µ(∞) + Σ_v r_v |O|^{-1} Σ_{c′∈O} ∫ log δ_v(c′, w) dµ_v(w) = Σ_v r_v |O|^{-1} Σ_{c′} G_{M,v}(c′) (DY.4/multibrot-adelic-measure: potential G_M and h_µ(∞) = 0). Only finitely many places contribute (G_{M,v}(c′) = log⁺|c′|_v at finite v), so the limit and the sum commute: h_µ(c) = lim D^{−(n−1)} Σ_v r_v |O|^{-1}Σ_{c′} log⁺|P_{c′}ⁿ(0)|_v = lim D^{−(n−1)} h(P_cⁿ(0)) (DY.4/standard-adelic-height-is-the-weil-height). P_cⁿ(0) = P_c^{n−1}(c), so the limit is ĥ_{P_c}(c) = D ĥ_{P_c}(0) (DY.1); the only finite critical point of P_c is 0, of multiplicity D − 1. ĥ_{P_c}(0) = 0 iff 0 is preperiodic (DY.1/zero-canonical-height-iff-preperiodic).

### 4.32 Galois-stable sets of bounded height and bounded size are finite in number

Let ρ be an adelic measure over K and (F_n) a sequence of finite Galois-stable subsets of P¹(K̄) in which every finite set occurs for only finitely many n, with sup_n h_ρ(F_n) < ∞. Then |F_n| → ∞.

Each finite set occurs finitely often in (F_n); h_ρ(F_n) bounded above. F_n is nonempty for every n.

Suppose |F_n| ≤ M along a subsequence. By DY.4/adelic-height-decomposition h_ρ(F_n) = |F_n|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F_n} h_ρ(x), and by DY.4/adelic-height-is-a-weil-height h_ρ(x) ≥ h(x) + h_ρ(∞) − C ≥ h_ρ(∞) − C for every x; so every x ∈ F_n has h(x) ≤ M(H + C + |h_ρ(∞)|) + C =: B, where H bounds h_ρ(F_n). Every x ∈ F_n ∖ {∞} has degree [ℚ(x) : ℚ] ≤ M[K : ℚ]; by Northcott over ℚ̄ (DT.0/northcott-absolute-height) there are finitely many such x, so finitely many possible sets F_n — contradicting that each set occurs finitely often.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-arakelov-zhang-pairing"></a>

### 4.34 The Arakelov–Zhang pairing of adelic metrics on O(1)

For semipositive adelic metrics φ₁, φ₂ on O(1) over K with curvatures µ₁, µ₂, the Arakelov–Zhang pairing is Ō₁·Ō₂ := Σ_v r_v [φ_{2,v}(∞) + ∫ (log⁺|z|_v + φ_{1,v}(z)) dµ_{2,v}(z)], the value of Zhang's arithmetic intersection number h₁((u)) + h₂((s)) + Σ_v r_v ∫ log‖s‖_{1,v}^{-1} Δ(log‖u‖_{2,v}^{-1}) at the sections s = x₁ (divisor ∞) and u = x₀ (divisor 0). The sum is finite. For rational maps f, g of degree ≥ 2 over K, the pairing of their canonical adelic metrics is the dynamical Arakelov–Zhang pairing ⟨f, g⟩ (DY.4/dynamical-arakelov-zhang-pairing).

φ₁, φ₂ semipositive adelic metrics on O(1) over K.

The integral is finite: log⁺|z|_v + φ_{1,v} is µ_{2,v}-integrable because µ_{2,v} has continuous potential (TB.6; FRL Lemmas 2.4 and 4.3). At the places where φ₁ = φ₂ = 0 the term is ∫ log⁺ dλ_v = 0. The value at s = x₁, u = x₀: h₁(0) + h₂(∞) + Σ_v r_v [∫(log⁺|z| + φ₁) dµ₂ − φ_{1,v}(0)], and h₁(0) = Σ_v r_v φ_{1,v}(0) (DY.4/height-of-an-adelic-metrized-line-bundle), giving the formula.

- **`AdelicMetric.pairing_twist`** (simp): (φ₁ + c)·φ₂ = φ₁·φ₂ + Σ_v r_v c_v.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-canonical-adelic-metric-of-a-rational-map"></a>

### 4.35 The canonical adelic metric of a rational map

Let f be a rational map of degree d ≥ 2 over K with a homogeneous lift F = (F₀, F₁) over K (DY.0). Its canonical adelic metric is φ^{f,F}_v(z) := G_{F,v}(z, 1) − log⁺|z|_v, extended continuously to P¹_v^an with φ^{f,F}_v(∞) = G_{F,v}(1, 0), where G_{F,v} is the homogeneous escape rate (DY.2/escape-rate); equivalently −log‖x₁‖_{f,v}(z) = λ_{F,v}(z) = G_{F,v}(z, 1) (DY.2/local-canonical-height). It is an adelic metric (φ^{f,F}_v = 0 where F has good reduction), semipositive with curvature ρ_f, and its height is ĥ_f. Replacing F by aF (a ∈ K^×) replaces φ_v by φ_v + log|a|_v/(d − 1), a twist with Σ_v r_v log|a|_v/(d − 1) = 0.

f of degree d ≥ 2 over K; F a homogeneous lift over K.

G_{F,v}(z, w) − log max(|z|_v, |w|_v) is bounded and continuous (DY.2/escape-rate), so φ^{f,F}_v is continuous on P¹(C_v) and extends to P¹_v^an (DY.2). At a place of good reduction of F, G_{F,v} = log max(|z|, |w|), so φ_v = 0. Curvature: Δ(−log‖x₁‖_{f,v}) = Δλ_{F,v} = µ_{f,v} − δ_∞ (DY.2/canonical-measure), so the curvature is ρ_f (DY.4/curvature-measures-of-an-adelic-metric). Height: ĥ_f(x) = Σ_v r_v |O|^{-1} Σ_{y∈O} G_{F,v}(ỹ) for lifts ỹ (DY.2/local-canonical-height; PST Proposition 8), which is h_{φ^{f,F}}(x) (DY.4/height-of-an-adelic-metrized-line-bundle). Scaling: G_{aF,v} = G_{F,v} + log|a|_v/(d − 1).

### 4.36 Quantitative equidistribution of PCF parameters in the unicritical family

Fix D ≥ 2. There is C > 0 such that for every finite Galois-stable set F ⊂ ℚ̄ of postcritically finite parameters of z^D + c with |F| ≥ 2 and every C¹ function φ on P¹(ℂ): ||F|^{-1} Σ_{c∈F} φ(c) − ∫ φ dµ_{M_D}| ≤ C Lip(φ) (log|F| / |F|)^{1/2}.

D ≥ 2; Lip for the chordal metric.

µ_{M_D} has Hölder potentials (DY.4/multibrot-adelic-measure) and h_{µ_{M_D}}(F) = 0 (DY.4/multibrot-height-is-a-critical-height). Apply DY.4/quantitative-equidistribution at the infinite place, with ⟨φ, φ⟩ ≤ C₁ Lip(φ)² and |F|^{−1/κ} ≤ (log|F|/|F|)^{1/2} for |F| large.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-equidistribution-of-small-points-on-p1"></a>

### 4.37 Equidistribution of small points for adelic measures on P¹

Let ρ be an adelic measure over K and (F_n) a sequence of finite Galois-stable subsets of P¹(K̄) in which every finite set occurs for only finitely many n, with limsup_n h_ρ(F_n) ≤ 0. Then h_ρ(F_n) → 0 and, for every place v, [F_n]_v → ρ_v weakly on P¹_v^an. In particular, for every sequence of pairwise distinct x_n ∈ P¹(K̄) with h_ρ(x_n) → 0, the Galois-orbit measures [Gal·x_n]_v converge weakly to ρ_v at every place.

ρ adelic over K. F_n Galois-stable, each finite set occurring finitely often (in particular pairwise distinct sets, or Galois orbits of pairwise distinct points). The finite sets F_n are nonempty.

|F_n| → ∞ by DY.4/small-galois-stable-sets-grow. First remove ∞ globally. For F'_n = F_n∖{∞}, the height-average identity gives hρ(F'_n) = (|F_n|hρ(F_n)−hρ(∞))/(|F_n|−1) whenever ∞∈F_n. The heights hρ(F_n) are bounded above and below, so limsup hρ(F'_n)≤0. Repetitions remain finite and |F'_n|→∞. Prove the remaining steps for F'_n; the total variation difference of the orbit probability measures is ≤2/|F_n| and the same height identity transfers the limiting height back. No comparison of potentially unbounded unregularised local self-energies is required. Let N be N(ρ) together with the infinite places. For v ∉ N, ρ_v = λ_v at a finite place and ([F_n] − λ_v, [F_n] − λ_v)_v ≥ 0 (DY.4/nonnegative-local-energy-at-standard-places, applied to F_n ∖ {∞}). For v ∈ N and every 0 < r < 1, ([F_n] − ρ_v, [F_n] − ρ_v)_v ≥ −2(ω_{g,v}(r) + ε_v(r)) − (−log r)/|F_n| (DY.4/energy-lower-bound-after-regularisation); letting n → ∞ then r → 0 (DY.4/regularisation-modulus-tends-to-zero) gives liminf_n ([F_n] − ρ_v, [F_n] − ρ_v)_v ≥ 0. Hence liminf h_ρ(F_n) ≥ 0, and with limsup ≤ 0, h_ρ(F_n) → 0. Fix v₀. r_{v₀} ([F_n] − ρ_{v₀}, [F_n] − ρ_{v₀})_{v₀} ≤ 2h_ρ(F_n) − Σ_{v∈N∖{v₀}} r_v ([F_n] − ρ_v, [F_n] − ρ_v)_v − (nonnegative terms), so limsup_n ([F_n] − ρ_{v₀}, [F_n] − ρ_{v₀})_{v₀} ≤ 0; conclude with DY.4/local-equidistribution-criterion. For points: the Galois orbits of pairwise distinct x_n form a sequence in which each finite set occurs at most |set| times.

### 4.38 The Arakelov–Zhang pairing through mutual energies; symmetry

For semipositive adelic metrics φ₁, φ₂ on O(1) over K with curvatures µ₁, µ₂: Ō₁·Ō₂ = Σ_v r_v [φ_{1,v}(∞) + φ_{2,v}(∞) − (µ_{1,v}, µ_{2,v})_v]. In particular Ō₁·Ō₂ = Ō₂·Ō₁ and Ō·Ō = Σ_v r_v [2φ_v(∞) − (µ_v, µ_v)_v].

φ₁, φ₂ semipositive.

∫ log⁺|z|_v dµ_{2,v} = −(λ_v, µ_{2,v})_v (Fubini for the energy, TB.6, with the potential log⁺ of λ_v). φ_{1,v} − φ_{1,v}(∞) is the potential of µ_{1,v} − λ_v normalised at ∞ (DY.4/curvature-measures-of-an-adelic-metric), so ∫ (φ_{1,v} − φ_{1,v}(∞)) dµ_{2,v} = −(µ_{1,v} − λ_v, µ_{2,v})_v. Add: the integrand integrates to φ_{1,v}(∞) − (µ_{1,v}, µ_{2,v})_v; the result is symmetric because (·,·)_v is symmetric.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-essential-minimum-of-an-adelic-height"></a>

### 4.39 The essential minimum of an adelic height is nonnegative

For every adelic measure ρ over K and every ε > 0, the set {x ∈ P¹(K̄) : h_ρ(x) < −ε} is finite; equivalently, liminf_n h_ρ(x_n) ≥ 0 along every sequence of pairwise distinct points of P¹(K̄).

ρ adelic over K.

If the set were infinite, choose pairwise distinct x_n in it; their Galois orbits F_n satisfy limsup h_ρ(F_n) ≤ −ε ≤ 0 and each finite set occurs finitely often, so h_ρ(F_n) → 0 by DY.4/equidistribution-of-small-points-on-p1, a contradiction. The two formulations are equivalent by extracting subsequences.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/equidistribution-of-small-points-on-p1`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-equidistribution-of-small-points-on-p1).

([favre-rivera-letelier-2006](#source-parent-favre-rivera-letelier-2006), Théorème 1, p. 5 — The statement.)

**Endpoint checks.** For ρ = λ the height is ≥ 0 everywhere, and the essential minimum 0 is attained on the roots of unity. For the Gauss-radius measure at p, h_ρ(∞) = −½ log p < 0 at the single point ∞, consistent with finiteness of {h_ρ < −ε}.

### 4.40 Equidistribution of algebraic numbers of small Weil height (Bilu), in its adelic form

Let (α_n) be pairwise distinct elements of P¹(K̄) with absLogHeight₁(α_n) → 0 (h(∞) = 0). Then the Galois orbits of α_n equidistribute to λ_v at every place: at an infinite place [Gal·α_n]_v converges weakly to the Haar probability measure on the unit circle, and at a finite place to the Dirac mass at the Gauss point.

The α_n pairwise distinct.

By DY.4/standard-adelic-height-is-the-weil-height, h_λ(α_n) = absLogHeight₁(α_n) → 0. Apply DY.4/equidistribution-of-small-points-on-p1 to the standard adelic measure λ.

### 4.41 Equidistribution of postcritically finite parameters in the unicritical family

Fix D ≥ 2. For every sequence (F_n) of finite Galois-stable (over ℚ) sets of postcritically finite parameters c ∈ ℚ̄ (0 preperiodic for z^D + c), each set occurring for only finitely many n — for instance the Galois orbits of pairwise distinct PCF parameters — the measures [F_n]_∞ converge weakly to the harmonic measure µ_{M_D} of the Multibrot set, and [F_n]_p → λ_p at every prime p.

D ≥ 2; parameters postcritically finite.

h_{µ_{M_D}}(F_n) = 0 (DY.4/multibrot-height-is-a-critical-height and AdelicMeasure.height_eq_average). Apply DY.4/equidistribution-of-small-points-on-p1 to the adelic measure µ_{M_D} (DY.4/multibrot-adelic-measure).

### 4.42 Independence of the Arakelov–Zhang pairing from the auxiliary sections

For semipositive adelic metrics φ₁, φ₂ on O(1) over K and linear forms s, u over K with div s ≠ div u: Ō₁·Ō₂ = h_{φ₁}(div u) + h_{φ₂}(div s) + Σ_v r_v [∫ (−log‖s‖_{1,v}) dµ_{2,v} + log‖s(div u)‖_{1,v}].

div s ≠ div u; s, u defined over K.

Changing u to u′ changes the local term by log(‖s(div u′)‖_{1,v}/‖s(div u)‖_{1,v}) (PST (11)), and h_{φ₁}(div u′) − h_{φ₁}(div u) by the opposite sum over places, by DY.4/height-of-an-adelic-metrized-line-bundle and the product formula. Changing s to s′ is symmetric by DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-energy-formula (PST (12)). For s = x₁, u = x₀ the expression is the definition.

### 4.43 A semipositive metric is the normalised metric of its curvature up to constants

For every semipositive adelic metric φ on O(1) over K with curvature µ: (i) φ = φ^µ + c with c_v = φ_v(∞) − ½(µ_v, µ_v)_v and Σ_v r_v c_v = ½ Ō·Ō; (ii) h_φ = h_µ + ½ Ō·Ō on P¹(K̄); (iii) Ō^ρ·Ō^ρ = 0 for every adelic measure ρ.

### 4.44 Critical height as an adelic height and equidistribution of PCF maps in moduli (Gauthier; Yuan–Zhang)

Let d ≥ 2, M_d^cm the critically marked moduli space with its family f of degree-d maps and marked critical points c₁, …, c_{2d−2} (DY.0/moduli-space-of-rational-maps), and ĥ_crit([f]) := Σ_{i=1}^{2d−2} ĥ_f(c_i(f)) for [f] ∈ M_d^cm(ℚ̄) (DY.1 canonical heights; the critical height of DY.6). (a) ĥ_crit is the height of a nondegenerate nef adelic line bundle on the quasi-projective variety M_d^cm over ℚ̄ in the sense of Yuan–Zhang, the restriction to the ramification divisor of the f-invariant extension of O(1) on M_d^cm × P¹, with archimedean curvature the bifurcation current T_bif. (b) For every generic sequence of postcritically finite parameters in M_d^cm(ℚ̄), the Galois-orbit measures at the infinite place converge to the normalised bifurcation measure T_bif^{∧(2d−2)}/mass.

d ≥ 2; generic sequences in the sense of DY.4/generic-sequence on M_d^cm.

(a) Construct the invariant extension of O(1) on M_d^cm × P¹ and restrict to the graphs of the critical points (Yuan–Zhang §6.3): gap G3. Its archimedean curvature is T_bif = Σ_i π_*(T̂_f ∧ [Γ_{c_i}]) and T_bif^{∧(2d−2)} ≠ 0 (Bassanelli–Berteloot), which gives nondegeneracy: gap G4. (b) Apply the Yuan–Zhang equidistribution theorem for nondegenerate nef adelic line bundles on quasi-projective varieties [YZ, Theorem 5.4.3] (gap G3) to PCF parameters, which have ĥ_crit = 0 (DY.1/zero-canonical-height-iff-preperiodic). The polynomial one-parameter slice z^D + c is DY.4/equidistribution-of-pcf-parameters, proved without these inputs.

### 4.45 The canonical adelic metric of a rational map has self-intersection zero

For a rational map f of degree d ≥ 2 over K and any lift F, Ō_{f,F}·Ō_{f,F} = 0.

f of degree ≥ 2 over K.

Choose a linear form s over K and factor F*s := s(F₀, F₁) = Π_{j=1}^d s_j into linear forms (after a finite extension of K; the pairing is unchanged). The metric identity ‖s(f(x))‖_{f,v} = Π_j ‖s_j(x)‖_{f,v} holds (RationalMap.canonicalMetric_functional_equation). Invariance ∫ g∘f dµ_{f,v} = ∫ g dµ_{f,v} (DY.2/canonical-measure) applied to g = log‖s‖_{f,v} gives, with a second section t, ⟨f, f⟩_{s,t,v} − log‖s(div t)‖_{f,v} = Σ_j (⟨f, f⟩_{s_j,t,v} − log‖s_j(div t)‖_{f,v}) (PST Proposition 10). Summing over places with DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-independent-of-sections: Ō·Ō − ĥ_f(div s) = d·Ō·Ō − Σ_j ĥ_f(div s_j); since f(div s_j) = div s, ĥ_f(div s) = d ĥ_f(div s_j) (DY.1), so Ō·Ō = d·Ō·Ō, i.e. Ō·Ō = 0.

### 4.47 Zhang's essential-minimum inequality on P¹

Let φ be a semipositive adelic metric on O(1) over K. For every sequence of pairwise distinct x_n ∈ P¹(K̄), liminf_n h_φ(x_n) ≥ ½ Ō·Ō; equivalently {x ∈ P¹(K̄) : h_φ(x) ≤ b} is finite for every b < ½ Ō·Ō. In particular, for normalised semipositive Ō₁, Ō₂ and b < ½ Ō₁·Ō₂, the set {x : h_{φ₁}(x) + h_{φ₂}(x) ≤ b} is finite.

φ semipositive (deg O(1) = 1, so Zhang's bound L̄·L̄/(2 deg L) is ½ Ō·Ō).

h_φ = h_µ + ½ Ō·Ō (DY.4/height-of-a-semipositive-metric-versus-its-curvature) and liminf h_µ(x_n) ≥ 0 (DY.4/essential-minimum-of-an-adelic-height). For the last claim apply this to the average metric (φ₁ + φ₂)/2: its height is ½(h_{φ₁} + h_{φ₂}) (AdelicMetric.height_average) and its self-pairing is ¼·0 + ½ Ō₁·Ō₂ + ¼·0 = ½ Ō₁·Ō₂ (AdelicMetric.pairing_average); so liminf (h_{φ₁} + h_{φ₂})(x_n) ≥ ½ Ō₁·Ō₂ > b.

### 4.49 The adelic measure m_{F,η} and height h_{F,η} of a regularised finite set

Let F ⊂ K̄ be a nonempty Galois-stable finite set and η = (η_v) positive reals with η_v = 1 for all but finitely many v. Then m_{F,η} := ([F]_{v,η_v})_v is an adelic measure, and its normalised height h_{F,η} := h_{m_{F,η}} is the height of the adelic metric with −log‖x₁‖_v(z) = α_v + |F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} log max(|z − x|_v, η_v), α_v = ½(m_{F,η,v}, m_{F,η,v})_v; it satisfies h_{F,η}·h_{F,η} = 0 and (m_{F,η,v}, m_{F,η,v})_v ≤ ([F]_v, [F]_v)_v + (−log η_v)/|F|.

F Galois-stable, finite, nonempty, ∞ ∉ F; η_v > 0, η_v = 1 for almost all v.

At a finite place with η_v = 1 where every x ∈ F is v-integral, ζ_{x,1} = ζ_{0,1}, so m_{F,η,v} = λ_v; this holds at all but finitely many places. Each [F]_{v,η_v} has continuous potential (DY.4/regularised-measure-of-a-finite-set), so m_{F,η} is adelic. The local height: φ^m_v + log⁺|z|_v = ∫ log δ_v(z, w) dm_v(w) + ½(m_v, m_v)_v = |F|^{-1}Σ_x log max(|z − x|_v, η_v) + α_v (DY.4/adelic-metric-of-an-adelic-measure). h·h = 0 by DY.4/height-of-a-semipositive-metric-versus-its-curvature (iii); the energy bound is DY.4/regularised-self-energy-bound.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-canonical-height-is-an-adelic-height"></a>

### 4.50 The canonical height of a rational map is the adelic height of its canonical measures

For a rational map f of degree d ≥ 2 over K, ĥ_f = h_{ρ_f} on P¹(K̄); equivalently ĥ_f is the height of the normalised adelic metric Ō^{ρ_f}, and Ō_{f,F} = Ō^{ρ_f} + c with Σ_v r_v c_v = 0 for every lift F.

f of degree ≥ 2 over K.

The canonical metric Ō_{f,F} is semipositive with curvature ρ_f and height ĥ_f (DY.4/canonical-adelic-metric-of-a-rational-map), and Ō_{f,F}·Ō_{f,F} = 0 (DY.4/canonical-metric-self-intersection-zero). By DY.4/height-of-a-semipositive-metric-versus-its-curvature, ĥ_f = h_{Ō_{f,F}} = h_{ρ_f} + ½ Ō_{f,F}·Ō_{f,F} = h_{ρ_f}, and φ^{f,F} = φ^{ρ_f} + c with Σ_v r_v c_v = ½·0 = 0.

### 4.51 Nonnegativity and nondegeneracy of the Arakelov–Zhang pairing

For adelic measures ρ, σ over K, ⟨ρ, σ⟩ ≥ 0, with equality if and only if ρ = σ. Consequently, for semipositive adelic metrics φ₁, φ₂ on O(1) with Ō₁·Ō₁ = Ō₂·Ō₂ = 0: Ō₁·Ō₂ ≥ 0, with equality iff µ_{1,v} = µ_{2,v} for every v, in which case h_{φ₁} = h_{φ₂}.

ρ, σ adelic.

At each place ρ_v − σ_v has total mass 0 and a continuous potential, so (ρ_v − σ_v, ρ_v − σ_v)_v ≥ 0 with equality iff ρ_v = σ_v (TB.6; FRL Propositions 2.6 and 4.5); the weights r_v are positive. For metrics use DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-of-normalised-metrics; equal curvatures and vanishing self-pairings give φ₁ − φ₂ = c with Σ_v r_v c_v = 0 (DY.4/height-of-a-semipositive-metric-versus-its-curvature), hence equal heights (AdelicMetric.height_twist).

### 4.52 Heights along small sequences converge to the Arakelov–Zhang pairing

Let ρ, σ be adelic measures over K and (F_n) finite Galois-stable subsets of P¹(K̄), each finite set occurring for only finitely many n, with h_ρ(F_n) → 0. Then h_σ(F_n) → ⟨ρ, σ⟩. In particular, for pairwise distinct x_n ∈ P¹(K̄) with h_ρ(x_n) → 0, h_σ(x_n) → ⟨ρ, σ⟩; and for normalised semipositive adelic metrics Ō₁, Ō₂ on O(1), h_{Ō₁}(x_n) → 0 implies h_{Ō₂}(x_n) → Ō₁·Ō₂.

ρ, σ adelic; F_n as in DY.4/equidistribution-of-small-points-on-p1.

Expand h_σ(F_n) = ½Σ_v r_v [(σ, σ) − 2(σ − ρ, [F_n]) − 2(ρ, [F_n]) + ([F_n], [F_n])]_v. Σ_v r_v ([F_n], [F_n])_v = 0 (DY.4/product-formula-for-the-energy-of-a-finite-set), and from h_ρ(F_n) → 0, Σ_v 2r_v(ρ, [F_n])_v → Σ_v r_v (ρ, ρ)_v. σ_v − ρ_v vanishes outside the finite set N(ρ) ∪ N(σ) and has a continuous potential G_v; (σ − ρ, [F_n])_v = −∫ G_v d[F_n]_v → −∫ G_v dρ_v = (σ − ρ, ρ)_v by DY.4/equidistribution-of-small-points-on-p1 and the Fubini formula (TB.6). Combine: h_σ(F_n) → ½Σ_v r_v [(σ,σ) − 2(σ − ρ, ρ) − (ρ, ρ)] = ½Σ_v r_v (σ − ρ, σ − ρ) = ⟨ρ, σ⟩. The metric version follows from DY.4/height-of-the-metric-of-an-adelic-measure and DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-of-normalised-metrics.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-dynamical-arakelov-zhang-pairing"></a>

### 4.53 The Arakelov–Zhang pairing of two rational maps

For rational maps f, g of degrees ≥ 2 over K, ⟨f, g⟩ := ⟨ρ_f, ρ_g⟩ = ½ Σ_v r_v (µ_{f,v} − µ_{g,v}, µ_{f,v} − µ_{g,v})_v, which equals the Arakelov–Zhang pairing Ō_{f,F}·Ō_{g,G} of the canonical adelic metrics for any lifts F, G (Petsche–Szpiro–Tucker). The local terms E_v(f, g) := ½(µ_{f,v} − µ_{g,v}, µ_{f,v} − µ_{g,v})_v are the local dynamical energies of DY.4/local-dynamical-energy.

f, g of degree ≥ 2 over K.

The canonical metrics have self-intersection 0 and curvatures ρ_f, ρ_g (DY.4/canonical-metric-self-intersection-zero, DY.4/canonical-adelic-metric-of-a-rational-map), so Ō_f·Ō_g = ⟨ρ_f, ρ_g⟩ by DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-of-normalised-metrics. The value does not depend on K or on the lifts (twists with Σ r_v c_v = 0).

### 4.56 Quantitative equidistribution of iterated preimages at an infinite place

Let f be a rational map of degree d ≥ 2 over K and v an infinite place. There is C > 0 such that for every z ∈ P¹(K) outside the forward orbits of the critical points of f (so that f^{-n}(z) consists of dⁿ distinct points), every n ≥ 1 and every C¹ function φ on P¹(ℂ): |d^{-n} Σ_{α∈f^{-n}(z)} φ(α) − ∫ φ dµ_{f,v}| ≤ C Lip(φ) ((ĥ_f(z) + n)/dⁿ)^{1/2}.

z not a critical value of any iterate fⁿ; v infinite; Lip for the chordal metric.

The potentials of µ_{f,w} − λ_w are Hölder at every place (DY.4/holder-continuity-of-canonical-potentials), so ω(r) ≤ C₀ r^κ at the places of N(ρ_f). F := f^{-n}(z) is Galois-stable with |F| = dⁿ and h_{ρ_f}(F) = d^{-n} ĥ_f(z) (DY.4/canonical-height-is-an-adelic-height). Apply DY.4/quantitative-equidistribution at v with ⟨φ, φ⟩_v ≤ C₁ Lip(φ)² and log|F|/|F| = n log d / dⁿ.

### 4.57 The square root of the Arakelov–Zhang pairing is a metric (Fili)

d(ρ, σ) := ⟨ρ, σ⟩^{1/2} is a metric on the set of adelic measures (over K, compatibly with base change): d(ρ, σ) = 0 iff ρ = σ, d is symmetric, and d(ρ, τ) ≤ d(ρ, σ) + d(σ, τ). For normalised semipositive adelic metrics this reads (Ō₁·Ō₃)^{1/2} ≤ (Ō₁·Ō₂)^{1/2} + (Ō₂·Ō₃)^{1/2}.

Adelic measures over K.

At each place, (·,·)_v is a symmetric bilinear form on the real vector space X_v of signed measures of mass 0 with continuous potential, positive definite (TB.6); ‖ν‖_v := (ν, ν)_v^{1/2} is a norm on X_v. On the finitely supported families ν = (ν_v) ∈ ⊕_v X_v, ‖ν‖ := (½ Σ_v r_v ‖ν_v‖_v²)^{1/2} is a norm (ℓ² sum of norms with positive weights), and d(ρ, σ) = ‖ρ − σ‖. The triangle inequality for ‖·‖ gives the claim; nondegeneracy is DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-nonnegative-and-nondegenerate; the metric version is DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-of-normalised-metrics.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-adelic-measures-with-common-small-points"></a>

### 4.58 Adelic measures sharing infinitely many small points coincide (Fili)

Let ρ, σ be adelic measures over K, Z(ρ) := {x ∈ P¹(K̄) : h_ρ(x) ≤ 0}, and assume Z(ρ) ∪ Z(σ) is infinite. The following are equivalent: (1) ⟨ρ, σ⟩ = 0; (2) ρ = σ; (3) h_ρ = h_σ; (4) Z(ρ) = Z(σ); (5) Z(ρ) ∩ Z(σ) is infinite; (6) there are pairwise distinct x_n ∈ P¹(K̄) with h_ρ(x_n) + h_σ(x_n) → 0.

Z(ρ) ∪ Z(σ) infinite.

(1) ⇔ (2): DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-nonnegative-and-nondegenerate. (2) ⇒ (3) ⇒ (4): immediate. (4) ⇒ (5): Z(ρ) = Z(σ) = Z(ρ) ∪ Z(σ) is infinite. (5) ⇒ (6): take distinct x_n ∈ Z(ρ) ∩ Z(σ); then h_ρ(x_n), h_σ(x_n) ≤ 0 and liminf of each is ≥ 0 (DY.4/essential-minimum-of-an-adelic-height), so both tend to 0. (6) ⇒ (1): liminf h_ρ(x_n) ≥ 0 and liminf h_σ(x_n) ≥ 0 force h_ρ(x_n) → 0 and h_σ(x_n) → 0; then h_σ(x_n) → ⟨ρ, σ⟩ (DY.4/limit-of-heights-along-small-sequences), so ⟨ρ, σ⟩ = 0.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-nonnegative-and-nondegenerate`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-arakelov-zhang-pairing-nonnegative-and-nondegenerate); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/essential-minimum-of-an-adelic-height`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-essential-minimum-of-an-adelic-height); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.4/limit-of-heights-along-small-sequences`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-limit-of-heights-along-small-sequences).

**Endpoint checks.** The infinitude hypothesis is necessary: over ℚ take equilibrium measures on [−4,4] and [−8,8] at ∞ and standard measures at finite places. Their capacities are 2 and 4. For a finite algebraic point the archimedean potential is at least log(capacity), the finite-place height contributions are nonnegative, and hρ(x) ≥ ½ log(capacity) > 0. Meanwhile hρ(∞)=−½ log(capacity)<0. Hence both zero sets are {∞}, although the measures differ. This corrects the intervals used in Fili Remark 1 (sourceIssues E510). For canonical measures of rational maps the hypothesis always holds (infinitely many preperiodic points).

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-4-height-difference-bound-via-the-pairing"></a>

### 4.60 Upper bound for ĥ_ψ − h through the pairing with the squaring map

For a rational map ψ of degree ≥ 2 over K and every x ∈ P¹(K̄): ĥ_ψ(x) − h(x) ≤ ⟨z², ψ⟩ + log 2. In particular ĥ_ψ(x) − h(x) ≤ ⟨z², ψ⟩ + ĥ_ψ(∞) + log 2 (Petsche–Szpiro–Tucker Theorem 15, whose bound is weaker by ĥ_ψ(∞) ≥ 0).

ψ of degree ≥ 2 over K; h the Weil height with h(∞) = 0.

For x ∈ K̄ with orbit O: ĥ_ψ(x) − h(x) = h_{ρ_ψ}(∞) + Σ_v r_v |O|^{-1} Σ_{y∈O} [∫ log δ_v(y, w) dµ_{ψ,v}(w) − log⁺|y|_v] (DY.4/canonical-height-is-an-adelic-height, DY.4/adelic-height-decomposition, DY.4/standard-adelic-height-is-the-weil-height). log δ_v(y, w) ≤ log⁺|y|_v + log⁺|w|_v + θ_v with θ_v = log 2 at infinite places and 0 at finite places (triangle, resp. ultrametric, inequality for the kernel). Hence ĥ_ψ(x) − h(x) ≤ h_{ρ_ψ}(∞) + Σ_v r_v ∫ log⁺|w|_v dµ_{ψ,v} + log 2 = ⟨λ, ρ_ψ⟩ + log 2 (DY.4/pairing-with-the-standard-measure; Σ_{v|∞} r_v = 1), and ⟨λ, ρ_ψ⟩ = ⟨z², ψ⟩. At x = ∞: ĥ_ψ(∞) = h_{ρ_ψ}(∞) ≤ ⟨λ, ρ_ψ⟩ since the log⁺ integrals are ≥ 0.

### 4.61 Equidistribution of iterated preimages

Let f be a rational map of degree d ≥ 2 over K and z₀ ∈ P¹(K̄) with infinite backward orbit ⋃_n f^{-n}(Gal·z₀) (z₀ not exceptional). Then the sets F_n := f^{-n}(Gal·z₀) are Galois-stable and pairwise distinct, and [F_n]_v → µ_{f,v} weakly at every place v.

z₀ non-exceptional; F_n taken as sets (without multiplicity).

F_n is Galois-stable because f is defined over K; every y ∈ F_n has ĥ_f(y) = d^{-n} ĥ_f(z₀) (DY.1), so ĥ_f-averages tend to 0. If F_n = F_m for some n < m, then F_n = f^{-(m−n)}(F_n) is a finite totally invariant set for f^{m−n}, so the backward orbit of z₀ would be finite; hence the F_n are pairwise distinct. Apply DY.4/dynamical-equidistribution.

### 4.62 Equidistribution of periodic points

Let f be a rational map of degree d ≥ 2 over K and Fix(f^n) ⊂ P¹(K̄) the set of solutions of f^n(z) = z. For every strictly increasing sequence (n_k) along which the sets Fix(f^{n_k}) are pairwise distinct, [Fix(f^{n_k})]_v → µ_{f,v} weakly at every place v. Such sequences exist (for instance a subsequence of n_k = k! along which Fix(f^{k!}) strictly increases), because f has infinitely many periodic points.

f of degree ≥ 2; (n_k) with pairwise distinct sets.

Fix(f^n) is Galois-stable and its points are preperiodic, so ĥ_f = 0 on it (DY.1/zero-canonical-height-iff-preperiodic). Apply DY.4/dynamical-equidistribution. Existence: Fix(f^{k!}) ⊆ Fix(f^{(k+1)!}) and the union is the infinite set of periodic points (DY.3: infinitely many periodic points), so the chain increases strictly infinitely often.

### 4.63 Vanishing criterion for the dynamical Arakelov–Zhang pairing

For rational maps f, g of degree ≥ 2 over K, ⟨f, g⟩ ≥ 0, and the following are equivalent: (a) ⟨f, g⟩ = 0; (b) ĥ_f = ĥ_g on P¹(K̄); (c) Preper(f) = Preper(g); (d) Preper(f) ∩ Preper(g) is infinite; (e) there are pairwise distinct x_n ∈ P¹(K̄) with ĥ_f(x_n) + ĥ_g(x_n) → 0; (f) µ_{f,v} = µ_{g,v} for every place v.

f, g of degree ≥ 2 over K.

Nonnegativity and (a) ⇔ (f): DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-nonnegative-and-nondegenerate for ρ_f, ρ_g. (f) ⇒ (b): ĥ_f = h_{ρ_f} = h_{ρ_g} = ĥ_g (DY.4/canonical-height-is-an-adelic-height). (b) ⇒ (c): preperiodic points are exactly the zeros of the canonical height (DY.1/zero-canonical-height-iff-preperiodic). (c) ⇒ (d): Preper(f) is infinite (DY.3: infinitely many periodic points). (d) ⇒ (e): take distinct common preperiodic points. (e) ⇒ (a): ĥ_f, ĥ_g ≥ 0, so both tend to 0, and ĥ_f(x_n) → ⟨f, g⟩ (DY.4/heights-of-small-points-of-another-map).

### 4.66 Periodic-point averages counted with multiplicity (Petsche–Szpiro–Tucker Theorem 2)

For rational maps f, g of degree ≥ 2 over K with d = deg g, Σ(f, g) := lim_{n→∞} (dⁿ + 1)^{-1} Σ_{g^n(x)=x} ĥ_f(x), the sum over the dⁿ + 1 solutions counted with multiplicity, exists and equals ⟨f, g⟩.

Solutions of g^n(x) = x counted with multiplicity.

Let e_n := dⁿ + 1 − |Fix(gⁿ)| be the multiplicity excess. A solution has multiplicity > 1 only if it lies on a periodic cycle whose multiplier λ satisfies λ^{n/k} = 1 (k the exact period; DY.2/multiplier-of-a-periodic-cycle), and its multiplicity as a fixed point of gⁿ is bounded independently of n. Gap G5: g has only finitely many parabolic cycles (Fatou), so e_n is bounded and the excess points carry boundedly many values of ĥ_f; hence the multiset average differs from the set average by O(d^{-n}), and |Fix(gⁿ)| → ∞ so every set occurs finitely often. The set averages along all n converge to ⟨f, g⟩ by DY.4/limit-of-heights-along-small-sequences (as in DY.4/periodic-point-average-of-canonical-heights).

<a id="dy-5"></a>
## Layer 5: Arboreal Galois representations

Build finite preimage levels with noncollision and separability hypotheses, compatible Galois actions, the rooted-tree inverse limit and continuity. Selected maximality and index theorems follow from their exact irreducibility/ramification criteria. The all-level x²+1 example is the selected endpoint; broader density and wild-characteristic theorems remain outside its scope.

Planets: Automorphism group of a rooted tree; Preimage tree; Arboreal Galois representation; Stoll's maximality criterion; Jones's ramification criterion; Odoni's theorem.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-5-level-tower"></a>

### 5.1 Level towers and rooted trees

A level tower T is a sequence of sets (V_n)_{n≥0} (the vertices at level n) with parent maps π_n : V_{n+1} → V_n. The ancestor map at level k of a vertex at level k + j is π_k ∘ ⋯ ∘ π_{k+j−1} (the identity for j = 0); the children of v ∈ V_n are the elements of π_n^{-1}(v). T is a rooted tree when V_0 is a single point; its vertices are ⊔_n V_n and its edges join x ∈ V_{n+1} to π_n(x). T is d-regular (d ∈ ℕ) when V_0 has exactly one element, every V_n is finite, and every vertex has exactly d children. A morphism T → T' is a family of maps V_n → V'_n commuting with the parent maps; an isomorphism is a family of bijections commuting with the parent maps.

No hypotheses: any family of types and maps is a level tower. Regularity is a separate predicate. Pinned convention: levels are indexed from the root, V_0 being the root level; the parent map goes down one level.

Structure with two fields (V, parent); ancestor by recursion on j; children as a fibre; IsRegular as the conjunction of the three conditions; Hom and Iso as structures of levelwise maps with the commutation field. card_level_of_isRegular: induction on n, V_{n+1} is the disjoint union over v ∈ V_n of the children of v (the fibres of π_n), each of cardinality d, so Nat.card V_{n+1} = d · Nat.card V_n. parent_surjective_of_isRegular: a fibre of cardinality d ≥ 1 is nonempty.

*Needs:* `mathlib:Nat.card`.

([jones-arboreal-survey](#source-parent-jones-arboreal-survey), §1.1, p. 3 — The survey's tree: vertices graded by n, edges given by φ; the level tower is this grading with edges as parent maps; [jones-density-2008](#source-parent-jones-density-2008), §2, p. 6 — Rooted forests graded by level; d-regularity. (The printed 'connected to precisely d others' counts children, not neighbours: each non-root vertex also has a parent.).)

The reusable interface consists of the following statements.

- **`LevelTower.ancestor`** (data): For k, j ∈ ℕ, the ancestor map V_{k+j} → V_k, π_k ∘ ⋯ ∘ π_{k+j−1}.
- **`LevelTower.ancestor_zero`** (simp): The ancestor map with j = 0 is the identity.
- **`LevelTower.ancestor_succ`** (simp): ancestor k (j + 1) x = ancestor k j (π_{k+j} x).
- **`LevelTower.children`** (data): The children of v ∈ V_n: the subset π_n^{-1}(v) of V_{n+1}.
- **`LevelTower.IsRegular`** (other): T is d-regular: Nat.card V_0 = 1, every V_n is finite, and every vertex has exactly d children.
- **`LevelTower.card_level_of_isRegular`** (characterisation): If T is d-regular then Nat.card V_n = dⁿ for every n.
- **`LevelTower.parent_surjective_of_isRegular`** (other): If T is d-regular with d ≥ 1, every parent map π_n is surjective.
- **`LevelTower.Hom`** (functoriality): Morphisms of level towers: levelwise maps commuting with the parent maps.
- **`LevelTower.Iso`** (functoriality): Isomorphisms of level towers: levelwise bijections commuting with the parent maps.
- **`LevelTower.Iso.refl`** (functoriality): The identity isomorphism of T.
- **`LevelTower.Iso.symm`** (functoriality): The inverse of an isomorphism (levelwise inverse bijections).
- **`LevelTower.Iso.trans`** (functoriality): The composite of two isomorphisms.

**Checks.**

- **`TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics.LevelTower.test_card_binary`** (computation): If T is 2-regular then Nat.card V_3 = 8.
- **`TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics.LevelTower.test_degree_one`** (degenerate): If T is 1-regular then every level has exactly one element.
- **`TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics.LevelTower.test_not_regular`** (non-example): The tower with V_n = Fin (n + 1) and every parent map constant equal to the last vertex is not d-regular for any d (vertex 0 of level 1 has no children, the last vertex of level 1 has three).
- **`TauCeti.ArithmeticDynamics.LevelTower.test_ancestor_one`** (characterisation): The ancestor one level down is the parent: ancestor k 1 x = π_k x.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-5-capelli-lemma"></a>

### 5.3 Capelli's lemma

Let K be a field, g, h ∈ K[x] with g ≠ 0 and deg h ≥ 1, and let β be a root of g in some field extension L of K. Then g(h(x)) is irreducible over K if and only if g is irreducible over K and h(x) − β is irreducible over K(β).

deg h ≥ 1 (if h is constant, g ∘ h is constant and the statement degenerates). β is any root of g in any extension; when g is irreducible all roots are conjugate, so the condition does not depend on the choice.

For the reverse implication, choose a root γ of h − β over K(β). Irreducibility gives [K(β):K] = deg g and [K(γ):K(β)] = deg h, while β = h(γ) implies K(β,γ) = K(γ). The tower law gives [K(γ):K] = deg g · deg h = deg(g ∘ h). Since g ∘ h annihilates γ, it is a nonzero scalar multiple of its minimal polynomial and is irreducible. This works for arbitrary leading coefficients; Polynomial.irreducible_comp supplies the already formalized monic special case. ⇒, g irreducible: a factorization g = g₁g₂ into non-units gives g ∘ h = (g₁ ∘ h)(g₂ ∘ h) into non-units since deg h ≥ 1. ⇒, h − β irreducible: let γ be a root of h(x) − β in an extension; then γ is a root of g ∘ h, so [K(γ) : K] = deg g · deg h (g ∘ h irreducible), while K(β) ⊆ K(γ) because β = h(γ), [K(β) : K] = deg g (g irreducible) and [K(γ) : K(β)] ≤ deg h (IntermediateField.adjoin.finrank, Module.finrank_mul_finrank). Equality forces [K(γ) : K(β)] = deg h, so h − β, of degree deg h with root γ, is the minimal polynomial of γ over K(β) up to a unit, hence irreducible.

*Needs:* `mathlib:Polynomial.irreducible_comp`; `mathlib:IntermediateField.adjoin.finrank`; `mathlib:Module.finrank_mul_finrank`; `mathlib:IntermediateField.AdjoinSimple.gen`.

([jones-density-2008](#source-parent-jones-density-2008), §4, Lemma 4.2, p. 13 — The statement with f and g renamed h and g; the hypothesis deg h ≥ 1 is implicit in the source.)

**Endpoint checks.** g = x² + 1, h = x² over ℚ: g ∘ h = x⁴ + 1 is irreducible, and x² − i is irreducible over ℚ(i). g = x² − 2, h = x² over ℚ: x⁴ − 2 irreducible, and x² − √2 irreducible over ℚ(√2).

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-5-tower-automorphism-group"></a>

### 5.10 The automorphism group Aut(T) of a level tower and its profinite topology

For a level tower T, Aut(T) is the group of families (σ_n)_{n≥0} with σ_n a permutation of V_n and π_n ∘ σ_{n+1} = σ_n ∘ π_n for all n, under levelwise composition; it is a subgroup of ∏_n Perm(V_n). It acts on each level through levelHom n : Aut(T) → Perm(V_n). Its topology is the subspace topology from the product ∏_n Perm(V_n) with each factor discrete (for finite levels this equals pointwise convergence on vertices). When every V_n is finite, Aut(T) is a compact, Hausdorff, totally disconnected topological group, i.e. a profinite group, and finite intersections of kernels of levelHom form a basis of open neighbourhoods of 1; if every parent map is surjective, the individual level kernels form such a basis.

Profiniteness (compactness) needs every level finite; the topological group structure, Hausdorffness and total disconnectedness hold for every T.

autSubgroup: the compatibility condition is closed under composition, identity and inverses (for inverses apply σ_n^{-1} to both sides). Topological group: induced from the product of discrete groups, a topological group (Pi.topologicalSpace with the discrete topology on each Perm(V_n)). Hausdorff and totally disconnected: the product of discrete spaces is, and so is any subspace. Compactness for finite levels: the compatibility conditions are closed (each is an equality of values in a discrete space depending on finitely many coordinates), and ∏_n Perm(V_n) is compact by Tychonoff (finite discrete factors). Aut.ext_iff': equality of families is levelwise equality. Iso.autCongr: conjugation by the levelwise bijections of an isomorphism. A basic neighbourhood in the product fixes finitely many level permutations. When all parents are surjective, fixing the highest of those levels fixes its ancestors; without that condition use the finite intersection, or the kernel of truncation, rather than a single level kernel.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.5/level-tower`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-5-level-tower); `mathlib:Equiv.Perm`; `mathlib:Pi.topologicalSpace`; `mathlib:ProfiniteGrp.of`.

([jones-arboreal-survey](#source-parent-jones-arboreal-survey), §1.1, p. 3 — Aut(T_∞) is the group of permutations of the vertex set preserving the edge relation; for a graded tree these are levelwise permutations commuting with the parent maps; [jones-arboreal-survey](#source-parent-jones-arboreal-survey), §3.1, p. 14 — Aut(T_n) and its iterated-wreath description, planned in tree-automorphism-wreath-recursion.)

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-5-separable-iterates-criterion"></a>

### 5.12 Non-collision: fⁿ − α is separable iff no critical point reaches α

Let K be a field, f ∈ K[x] with deg f ≥ 1, α ∈ K and n ≥ 1. Then fⁿ(x) − α is separable if and only if for every c ∈ K̄ with f'(c) = 0 and every 1 ≤ k ≤ n, f^k(c) ≠ α. Hence fⁿ − α is separable for all n ≥ 1 iff α does not lie in the forward orbit {f^k(c) : k ≥ 1, f'(c) = 0} of the critical points (the non-collision condition). If f' = 0 (f inseparable) every c ∈ K̄ is critical and both sides fail.

deg f ≥ 1. Critical points are the roots of f' in an algebraic closure, with the convention that every point is a root of the zero polynomial.

fⁿ − α splits over K̄ with roots z (f^n(z) = α); it is separable iff its roots are simple (Polynomial.nodup_roots_iff_of_splits), iff no root z has (fⁿ)'(z) = 0. By derivative-of-iterate, (fⁿ)'(z) = ∏_{i<n} f'(fⁱ(z)); it vanishes iff c := fⁱ(z) is critical for some i < n, and then f^{n−i}(c) = α with 1 ≤ n − i ≤ n. Conversely if f'(c) = 0 and f^k(c) = α with 1 ≤ k ≤ n, choose z ∈ K̄ with f^{n−k}(z) = c (K̄ algebraically closed, deg f ≥ 1); z is a multiple root.

### 5.13 The discriminant recursion for iterates

Let K be a field, f ∈ K[x] of degree d with leading coefficient a and (d : K) ≠ 0, α ∈ K, and let R be the multiset of roots of f' in an algebraically closed L ⊇ K (the critical points with multiplicity). With Mathlib's discriminant Polynomial.discr and A = (−1)^{d(d−1)/2} d^d a^{d−1}: Disc(f^{n+1} − α) = A^{dⁿ} · a^{(dⁿ − 1)(dⁿ⁺¹ + 1)} · Disc(fⁿ − α)^d · ∏_{r ∈ R} (f^{n+1}(r) − α). For monic f (a = 1) this is Aitken–Hajir–Maire's Proposition 3.2 (specialized at t = α); for a ≠ 1 the factor a^{(dⁿ−1)(dⁿ⁺¹+1)} corrects it (ArithmeticDynamics/E601).

(d : K) ≠ 0, so that f' = d·a·∏_{r∈R}(x − r) has degree d − 1. Mathlib's Polynomial.discr, equal to lc^{2m−2} ∏_{i<j} (ζ_i − ζ_j)² for degree m.

Handle d = 1 separately: every iterate minus α is linear with discriminant 1, the critical-root multiset is empty, and all factors on the asserted right side are 1. For d ≥ 2 use the following computation. For a polynomial P of degree m, leading coefficient ℓ and roots ζ_i in L: Disc(P) = (−1)^{m(m−1)/2} ℓ^{m−2} ∏_i P'(ζ_i) (Polynomial.resultant_deriv and Polynomial.resultant_eq_prod_eval; for monic P, Polynomial.Monic.prod_roots_eval_derivative). With h_n = fⁿ − α (degree dⁿ, leading coefficient ℓ_n = a^{(dⁿ−1)/(d−1)}, ℓ_{n+1} = a ℓ_n^d): h_{n+1}' = f' · (h_n' ∘ f) (derivative-of-iterate), and as ζ runs over the roots of h_{n+1}, f(ζ) runs over the roots of h_n, each d times; so ∏_ζ h_{n+1}'(ζ) = ∏_ζ f'(ζ) · (∏_β h_n'(β))^d. ∏_ζ f'(ζ) = (da)^{dⁿ⁺¹} (−1)^{dⁿ⁺¹(d−1)} ℓ_{n+1}^{−(d−1)} ∏_{r∈R} h_{n+1}(r). Collect signs and leading coefficients; the power of a is (d−1)dⁿ (from A^{dⁿ}) plus (dⁿ−1)(dⁿ⁺¹+1).

### 5.14 Stoll's Lemma 2.1: a congruence criterion for non-square Möbius quotients

Let g ∈ ℤ[x] be even (g(−x) = g(x)), and let (γ_n)_{n≥1} be integers with γ_1 = ±g(0), γ_{n+1} = g(γ_n) and all γ_n ≠ 0; put β_n = ∏_{d∣n} γ_d^{μ(n/d)}. Suppose that for every n ≥ 1 there is m ∈ ℕ with m ∣ γ_n + γ_{2n}, m coprime to γ_n, and −1 not a square in ℤ/mℤ. Then β_n is not a square in ℚ for every n ≥ 2.

g even; the recursion; γ_n ≠ 0; the existence of the moduli m.

Write n = n'k with n' = rad(n) > 1; take m for the index k and put A = γ_{2k}. Then γ_k ≡ −A (mod m); since the k-fold iterate g_k of g is even, γ_{3k} = g_k(γ_{2k}) ≡ g_k(−γ_k) = g_k(γ_k) = γ_{2k} = A (mod m), and by induction γ_{tk} ≡ A (mod m) for t ≥ 2. β_n = ∏_{t ∣ n'} γ_{kt}^{μ(n'/t)} (only squarefree quotients n/d contribute). Modulo m the factor with t = 1 is γ_k^{μ(n')} ≡ (−A)^{μ(n')} and every other factor is A^{μ(n'/t)}; since μ(n') = ±1 and Σ_{t∣n'} μ(n'/t) = 0, splitting the divisors of n' by the sign of μ(n'/t) (two sets of equal size) writes β_n = P/Q with P ≡ −Q (mod m) and Q a unit mod m. If P/Q = (u/v)² in ℚ, clearing denominators and reducing modulo m (Q invertible, P ≡ −Q) makes −1 a square in ℤ/mℤ, a contradiction.

### 5.15 The automorphism group Aut(T_n) of the tree truncated at level n

For a level tower T and n ∈ ℕ, Aut(T_n) is the subgroup of ∏_{k=0}^{n} Perm(V_k) of families (σ_0, …, σ_n) with π_k ∘ σ_{k+1} = σ_k ∘ π_k for k < n. It comes with: restriction Aut(T_{n+1}) → Aut(T_n) (forget σ_{n+1}); truncation Aut(T) → Aut(T_n); the action toLevelPerm on the top level V_n, which is injective when every parent map is surjective; and, for finite levels, the level signs χ_k = sign ∘ (k-th component) : Aut(T_n) → {±1}, k = 0, …, n.

Injectivity of toLevelPerm needs surjective parent maps (true for d-regular towers with d ≥ 1). Surjectivity of restriction and of truncation needs regularity (every automorphism of the truncated tree extends).

truncAut: subgroup, as for autSubgroup, with the finitely many conditions k < n. restrict: σ ↦ (σ_0, …, σ_n); the conditions for k < n are among those for k < n + 1. toLevelPerm_injective: if σ_n = τ_n then σ_k = τ_k for k < n, because π_k ∘ ⋯ is surjective onto V_k and σ_k ∘ ancestor = ancestor ∘ σ_n. Aut.truncate: σ ↦ (σ_0, …, σ_n). restrict_surjective and truncate_surjective for a d-regular tower: extend σ_n to σ_{n+1} by choosing, for each v ∈ V_n, a bijection children(v) → children(σ_n v) (both have d elements); iterate for truncate. levelSign: Equiv.Perm.sign composed with evaluation at k.

### 5.17 The adjusted critical orbit of a quadratic polynomial

### 5.18 The first level over k(t) is the full symmetric group

Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic 0 and f ∈ k[x] of degree d ≥ 2 with f' separable (simple critical points) and distinct critical values (f(a) = f(b) for critical a, b implies a = b). Then the Galois group of f(x) − t over k(t) is the full symmetric group S_d, i.e. G_1(f, t) = Aut(T_1).

By discriminant-of-iterate (n = 0, α = t): Disc(f(x) − t) = A ∏_r (f(r) − t), squarefree in k[t] (distinct critical values); f(x) − t is irreducible (linear in t) and A[θ] = k[θ] is integrally closed (Aitken–Hajir–Maire Lemma 2.1). inertia-is-transposition: every inertia group at a finite prime acts as a transposition. The subgroup I generated by the finite inertia groups is normal and its fixed field is unramified at all finite places, hence equal to k(t) (no-tame-cover-of-the-affine-line); so G = I is transitive and generated by transpositions, hence S_d (closure_of_isSwap_of_isPretransitive).

### 5.19 Stoll's Lemma 2.2: congruence conditions giving the moduli

γ_n + γ_{n+1} divides γ_n + γ_{2n} (the argument of Lemma 2.1 applied n − 1 times) and is coprime to γ_n (γ_{n+1} = g(γ_n) ≡ g(0) = ±1 mod γ_n); positivity makes m := γ_n + γ_{n+1} a positive integer. (a): γ_n ≡ 1 or 2 (mod 4) according as n is odd or even, so m ≡ 3 (mod 4). (b): γ_1 + γ_2 ≡ 0 (mod 4), and for n ≥ 2 all γ_n ≡ 3 (mod 4) and equal mod 8, so m ≡ 6 (mod 8). −1 is not a square modulo an integer ≡ 3 (mod 4), ≡ 6 (mod 8), or divisible by 4; apply even-sequence-nonsquare-criterion.

### 5.20 Every d-regular level tower is isomorphic to T^d

If T is a d-regular level tower then there is an isomorphism of level towers T ≅ T^d. Consequently Aut(T) ≃* Aut(T^d) and Aut(T_n) ≃* Aut(T^d_n) for every n, compatibly with restriction and truncation; the isomorphisms are unique up to conjugation by Aut(T^d).

T is d-regular (one root, finite levels, d children per vertex).

Construct e_n : V_n ≃ Fin n → Fin d by induction: e_0 is the unique bijection of singletons; given e_n, choose for each v ∈ V_n a bijection b_v : children(v) ≃ Fin d (both have d elements) and set e_{n+1}(x) = Fin.cons (b_{π x}(x)) (e_n(π x)). Commutation: Fin.tail (e_{n+1} x) = e_n (π x) by construction; bijectivity from the fibrewise bijections. Transport of automorphisms: LevelTower.Iso.autCongr and LevelTower.Iso.truncAutCongr. Uniqueness up to conjugacy: two isomorphisms differ by an automorphism of T^d.

### 5.21 Restriction Aut(T_{n+1}) → Aut(T_n): surjectivity and kernel

Let T be d-regular. Restriction Aut(T_{n+1}) → Aut(T_n) is surjective, and its kernel is isomorphic to ∏_{v ∈ V_n} Perm(children(v)) ≅ (S_d)^{dⁿ}, of order (d!)^{dⁿ}. In particular |Aut(T_{n+1})| = |Aut(T_n)| · (d!)^{dⁿ}.

T is d-regular.

Surjectivity: LevelTower.truncAut.restrict_surjective (choice of fibrewise bijections). Kernel: σ with σ_k = id for k ≤ n preserves each fibre children(v), v ∈ V_n; the map σ ↦ (σ_{n+1}|children(v))_v is a group isomorphism onto ∏_v Perm(children(v)) (any family of fibrewise permutations defines σ_{n+1} commuting with π_n). Order: Nat.card V_n = dⁿ (LevelTower.card_level_of_isRegular) and Nat.card Perm(children v) = d!; Lagrange.

### 5.22 Affine conjugation does not change the preimage tree or its Galois action

Let K ⊆ L be fields, f ∈ K[x], α ∈ K and h(x) = ux + v with u, v ∈ K, u ≠ 0. Put ψ = h^{-1} ∘ f ∘ h = u^{-1}(f(ux + v) − v) and α' = h^{-1}(α) = u^{-1}(α − v). In particular every quadratic f = ax² + bx + c over a field of characteristic ≠ 2 is conjugate over K to a monic quadratic (x − γ)² + δ (take u = a^{-1}), and α can be moved to 0 (take v = α).

ψⁿ = h^{-1} ∘ fⁿ ∘ h by induction, so fⁿ(y) = α iff ψⁿ(h^{-1}(y)) = α'; apply preimageTree.iso with the bijection h^{-1} of L. Galois equivariance: σ(h^{-1}(y)) = h^{-1}(σ y) because u, v ∈ K. Fields: h^{-1}(y) ∈ K(y) and y ∈ K(h^{-1}(y)).

### 5.23 Preimage trees of rational maps of P¹ and their Galois action

Let φ : P¹ → P¹ be a rational map of degree d ≥ 2 defined over a field K (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line) and α ∈ P¹(K). The preimage tree T(φ, α) := preimageTree applied to the action of φ on P¹(K^sep) and the point α carries an action of Gal(K^sep/K) by tree automorphisms, and it is d-regular with dⁿ vertices at level n exactly when φⁿ(x) = α has dⁿ distinct solutions in P¹(K̄) for every n ≥ 1 (and these then lie in P¹(K^sep)). For a polynomial φ = f and α ∈ K (α ≠ ∞) it is T(f, α; K^sep) of DY.5/preimage-tree, since ∞ is totally invariant.

φ commutes with σ ∈ Gal(K^sep/K) acting on P¹(K^sep) coordinatewise, because the coefficients of the two defining forms of φ lie in K; so galois equivariance gives a homomorphism to Aut(T(φ, α)) exactly as in galois-action-on-preimage-tree. If φⁿ(x) = α has dⁿ distinct solutions in P¹(K̄), each is separable over K (a simple root of the numerator of φⁿ − α) and so lies in P¹(K^sep); every vertex at level n has d children because level n + 1 has dⁿ⁺¹ elements and each fibre has at most d. For polynomials the point ∞ is fixed with φ^{-1}(∞) = {∞}, so α ≠ ∞ has no preimage at ∞ and T(φ, α) = T(f, α; K^sep).

### 5.24 The product of the shifted roots is the adjusted critical value

Let K be a field, f = (x − γ)² + δ ∈ K[x], α ∈ K and n ≥ 1, and let L ⊇ K be a field over which f^{n−1} − α splits. Then the product over the roots β of f^{n−1}(x) − α in L, with multiplicity, of β − δ equals c_n. If moreover f^{n−1} − α is irreducible and β is one of its roots, N_{K(β)/K}(β − δ) = c_n.

f^{n−1} − α is monic of degree 2^{n−1} and splits, so (f^{n−1} − α)(y) = ∏_β (y − β) (Polynomial.Splits.eval_eq_prod_roots_of_monic). n = 1: the only root is α and α − δ = c_1. n ≥ 2: ∏_β (β − δ) = (−1)^{2^{n−1}} ∏_β (δ − β) = f^{n−1}(δ) − α = f^{n−1}(f(γ)) − α = fⁿ(γ) − α = c_n, since 2^{n−1} is even and f(γ) = δ. Norm version: β − δ generates K(β), its minimal polynomial is (f^{n−1} − α)(x + δ), and the norm is the product of the roots of the minimal polynomial (IntermediateField.AdjoinSimple.norm_gen_eq_prod_roots).

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-5-tree-automorphism-inverse-limit"></a>

### 5.30 Aut(T) is the inverse limit of the finite groups Aut(T_n)

Let T be d-regular. For every family (s_n)_{n≥0} with s_n ∈ Aut(T_n) and restrict(s_{n+1}) = s_n there is a unique σ ∈ Aut(T) with truncate_n(σ) = s_n for all n. Together with the profinite topology of Aut(T), this identifies Aut(T) with lim_n Aut(T_n) as a topological group (each Aut(T_n) finite discrete). In particular a closed subgroup H ≤ Aut(T) whose truncations are all of Aut(T_n) is Aut(T).

T is d-regular (finite levels).

Existence: σ_n := (s_n)_n (the top component); compatibility π_n ∘ σ_{n+1} = σ_n ∘ π_n holds in s_{n+1}. Uniqueness: an element of Aut(T) is determined by its levelwise components (Aut.ext_iff'). Topology: the map Aut(T) → ∏_n Aut(T_n) is a continuous injective group homomorphism from a compact space (Aut.compactSpace) to a Hausdorff space, with image the compatible families, hence a homeomorphism onto the inverse limit. Closed subgroups: if H is closed and truncate_n(H) = Aut(T_n) for all n, every σ is a limit of elements of H (agree with σ on levels ≤ n), so σ ∈ H.

### 5.31 The shift g(x) = f(x + t) − t

For a commutative ring R, f ∈ R[x] and t ∈ R, the polynomial g(x) = f(x + t) − t satisfies gⁿ(x) = fⁿ(x + t) − t for all n. Consequently, for a field k, f ∈ k[x] and t transcendental over k, the preimage tree of 0 under g over k(t) is isomorphic (by y ↦ y + t) to the preimage tree of t under f over k(t), equivariantly for Gal(k(t)^sep/k(t)); in particular G_n(g, 0) = G_n(f, t) for all n, and g is a specialization of the generic monic polynomial of degree d when f is monic of degree d.

None for the identity; the tree statement for f monic of degree d over a field.

Induction: g^{n+1}(x) = g(gⁿ(x)) = f(fⁿ(x + t) − t + t) − t = f^{n+1}(x + t) − t. The translation y ↦ y + t is a bijection of k(t)^sep commuting with the dynamics (g(y) + t = f(y + t)) and with the Galois action (t is in the base field): affine-conjugation-invariance with u = 1, v = t. The coefficients of g lie in k[t]; the substitution s_i ↦ coeff_i(g) is a ring map k[s_0, …, s_{d−1}] → k[t].

### 5.32 Polynomials without critical orbit relations exist in every degree (characteristic 0)

Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic 0, d ≥ 2 and N ≥ 1. There is f ∈ k[x] of degree d with f' separable (simple critical points), distinct critical values, and fⁿ(a) ≠ fᵐ(b) for all critical points a, b and 1 ≤ m, n ≤ N unless (m, a) = (n, b).

k algebraically closed of characteristic 0; d ≥ 2.

f_0 = x^d + a_1x + a_0 with a_0a_1 ≠ 0 generic has simple critical points (roots of dx^{d−1} + a_1) and distinct critical values f_0(w_i) = a_0 + a_1 w_i (d−1)/d. Write v_i = f_0(w_i), which are distinct. Choose λ with f_0′(λ) ≠ 0 and c = f_0(λ) different from every v_i; only finitely many λ are excluded. For f_µ(x) = f_0(µx + λ), the critical point (w_i − λ)/µ has first image v_i. Compare these orbit values as polynomials in µ. At equal time n, the difference of the i and j orbits has leading term µ^{n−1}(f_0′(λ))^{n−1}(v_i−v_j). At unequal times n < m it has leading term µ^{n−1}(f_0′(λ))^{n−1}(v_i−c). Taylor expansion and induction give these terms, including n = 1. Thus every prohibited relation is a nonzero polynomial in µ. Avoid µ = 0 and the finitely many roots of these finitely many polynomials, using Polynomial.card_roots′. This supplies the properness argument in Juul Lemma 3.6, p. 11. If needed for the monic generic family, conjugate by x ↦ u x with u^{d−1} = lc(f_µ)⁻¹, which exists because k is algebraically closed. The conjugate u⁻¹ f_µ(ux) is monic and preserves the critical orbit relations and multiplicities.

### 5.33 Jones's stability step for quadratic iterates

Let K be a field of characteristic ≠ 2, f = (x − γ)² + δ ∈ K[x], α ∈ K and n ≥ 0. If fⁿ − α is irreducible over K and c_{n+1} is not a square in K, then f^{n+1} − α is irreducible over K. (For n = 0 this says: f − α is irreducible if α − δ is not a square; the converse also holds there.)

char K ≠ 2; f monic quadratic. Only monic f is covered: for a non-monic quadratic the correct condition involves the leading coefficient (see ArithmeticDynamics/E603); reduce to the monic case by affine-conjugation-invariance.

By Capelli's lemma with g = fⁿ − α and h = f: f^{n+1} − α = g ∘ f is irreducible if g is irreducible and f(x) − β = (x − γ)² − (β − δ) is irreducible over K(β) for a root β of g. x² − a is irreducible over a field iff a is not a square (X_pow_sub_C_irreducible_iff_of_prime with p = 2), and the substitution x ↦ x − γ preserves irreducibility. If β − δ = s² in K(β) then c_{n+1} = N_{K(β)/K}(β − δ) = N(s)² is a square in K (shifted-root-product); contradiction.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-5-critical-orbit-mobius-factors"></a>

### 5.34 Stoll's Lemma 1.1: the Möbius quotients of the critical orbit are pairwise coprime integers

Let a ∈ ℤ with −a not a square and c the critical orbit of x² + a. There are integers b_n (n ≥ 1) equal to the Möbius quotients mobiusQuotient c n, with c_n = ∏_{d ∣ n} b_d, and b_m, b_n coprime for m ≠ n. More precisely, for each prime p dividing some c_n, with m = min{n : p ∣ c_n} and e = v_p(c_m): v_p(c_n) = e if m ∣ n and 0 otherwise, so p divides b_m and no other b_n.

−a not a square (so all c_n ≠ 0, n ≥ 1).

Use x_j = f^j(0), whose absolute values agree with c_j. For a prime p appearing in the orbit, let m be its first positive zero index modulo p and e = v_p(x_m). The orbit modulo p returns to 0 first at m, hence p ∣ x_j iff m ∣ j. Since x_m² is divisible by p^{e+1}, x_{m+1} = x_m² + a is congruent to x_1 = a modulo p^{e+1}. Iteration therefore gives x_{m+j} ≡ x_j modulo p^{e+1} for j ≥ 1. Reducing each positive j to its representative in 1,…,m shows v_p(c_j) = e when m ∣ j and 0 otherwise. Compute the valuation of the rational Möbius product: v_p(b_n) = Σ_{d∣n} μ(n/d)v_p(c_d) = e when n = m and 0 otherwise. Every valuation is nonnegative, so b_n is an integer, and each prime divides exactly one factor. Möbius inversion proves c_n = ∏_{d∣n} b_d.

### 5.38 Level images shrink under base extension

Let E/K be a field extension, f ∈ K[x] and α ∈ K with fⁿ − α separable for all n. Then there is an isomorphism of level towers T(f, α; E^sep) ≅ T(f, α; K^sep) under which the level image G_N(f, α) over E is carried into G_N(f, α) over K, for every N; equivalently Gal(fᴺ − α / E) is a subgroup of Gal(fᴺ − α / K) compatibly with the root actions.

fⁿ − α separable over K for all n (hence over E).

Choose a K-embedding ι : K^sep → E^sep (K^sep/K is separable algebraic and E^sep is separably closed over K). ι maps the roots of fⁿ − α in K^sep bijectively to those in E^sep (both have dⁿ elements, preimage-tree-regular) and commutes with f: a tree isomorphism (preimageTree.iso). Every τ ∈ Gal(E^sep/E) stabilizes ι(K^sep) (normality of K^sep/K) and restricts to an element of Gal(K^sep/K) acting compatibly on the levels.

### 5.39 Galois groups of iterates do not grow under specialization

Let A be an integrally closed domain with fraction field F, 𝔭 a prime of A with residue fraction field κ = Frac(A/𝔭), f ∈ A[x] monic and α ∈ A, and assume that the reductions f̄ⁿ − ᾱ are separable over κ for all n. Then there is an isomorphism of level towers T(f̄, ᾱ; κ^sep) ≅ T(f, α; F^sep) carrying the level image G_N(f̄, ᾱ) over κ into G_N(f, α) over F, for every N.

A integrally closed; f monic; all f̄ⁿ − ᾱ separable over κ (so also fⁿ − α separable over F).

Let B be the integral closure of A in F^sep ∩ (splitting fields of the fⁿ − α) and choose a prime 𝔓 of B over 𝔭 with an embedding B/𝔓 ↪ κ^sep (lying over, going up). Reduction mod 𝔓 maps the roots of fⁿ − α (integral over A, as f is monic) to roots of f̄ⁿ − ᾱ, commuting with f; since both sets have (deg f)ⁿ elements and f̄ⁿ − ᾱ is separable, it is a bijection, hence a tree isomorphism. The decomposition group D_𝔓 ≤ Gal surjects onto the automorphism group of the residue extension (Ideal.Quotient.stabilizerHom_surjective), and reduction is D_𝔓-equivariant; so every element of the residue Galois group is the reduction of an element of D_𝔓 ≤ Gal(F^sep/F) acting in the same way on the tree.

### 5.40 The characters of Aut(T_n) for binary trees are products of level signs

Let T be 2-regular and n ∈ ℕ. For every homomorphism χ : Aut(T_n) → {±1} there is a unique subset S ⊆ {1, …, n} with χ = ∏_{k∈S} χ_k, where χ_k is the sign of the permutation induced on level k. Equivalently Hom(Aut(T_n), {±1}) has exactly 2ⁿ elements and the level signs χ_1, …, χ_n form an F_2-basis of it; the largest elementary abelian 2-quotient of Aut(T_n) ≅ [C_2]^n is C_2^n.

T is binary (2-regular). The levels are finite, so the signs are defined.

Transport to T² along regular-tower-isomorphism (signs are invariant under relabelling). Count: for a regular wreath product D ≀ Q and abelian A, a homomorphism D ≀ Q → A is determined by a pair of homomorphisms D → A, Q → A (on the base D^Q it takes equal values on conjugate coordinates); by the wreath recursion Aut(T²_{n+1}) ≅ Aut(T²_n) ≀ C_2, #Hom(Aut(T²_{n+1}), ±1) = 2 · #Hom(Aut(T²_n), ±1), so the count is 2ⁿ. Independence: for each 1 ≤ k ≤ n let σ_k swap the two subtrees below one vertex at level k − 1 (fixing everything else); it acts trivially on the levels j < k, by one transposition on level k and by 2^{j−k} disjoint transpositions on each level j > k, so χ_k(σ_k) = −1 and χ_j(σ_k) = 1 for j ≠ k. An independent family of n elements in an F_2-space of cardinality 2ⁿ is a basis; uniqueness of S follows.

### 5.43 K_{n+1} is a 2-Kummer extension of K_n

Let K be a field of characteristic ≠ 2, f = (x − γ)² + δ ∈ K[x], α ∈ K, and assume f^{n+1} − α separable. Hence K_{n+1}/K_n is generated by the square roots of the 2ⁿ elements β − δ ∈ K_n, [K_{n+1} : K_n] ≤ 2^{2ⁿ}, and Gal(K_{n+1}/K_n) is an elementary abelian 2-group, equal to the kernel of G_{n+1} → G_n.

Multiquadratic degree bound: adjoining r square roots has degree ≤ 2^r (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_adjoin_range_eq_two_pow_finrank_span_squareClass, with r = 2ⁿ). Each element of Gal(K_{n+1}/K_n) sends y_β − γ to ±(y_β − γ), hence has order ≤ 2; commutativity follows.

### 5.45 Juul's disjoint ramification lemma

Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic 0, f ∈ k[x] of degree d ≥ 2 with a critical point a of multiplicity one such that fᵐ(a) ≠ f^{m'}(b) for all critical points b and 1 ≤ m' ≤ m ≤ N unless (m', b) = (m, a). For n < N let α_1, …, α_{dⁿ} be the roots of fⁿ(x) − t, M_i the splitting field of f(x) − α_i over k(α_i), and M̂_i the compositum of K_n and the M_j, j ≠ i. Then the prime (f(a) − α_i) of k[α_i] does not ramify in M̂_i.

As stated; char 0 makes all ramification tame.

(f(a) − α_i) lies over (f^{n+1}(a) − t); the primes of k(t) ramified in K_n divide Disc(fⁿ(x) − t) = ∏_b ∏_{m ≤ n} (fᵐ(b) − t)^{…} (discriminant-of-iterate), and f^{n+1}(a) ≠ fᵐ(b) for m ≤ n, so (f(a) − α_i) is unramified in K_n. A prime 𝔭 of K_n over (f(a) − α_i) ramifying in M_jK_n (j ≠ i) divides Disc(f(x) − α_j) = ∏_b (f(b) − α_j)^{e−1}, so f^{n+1}(a) = f^{n+1}(b), forcing b = a and 𝔭 | (f(a) − α_i), (f(a) − α_j); then 𝔭² divides f^{n+1}(a) − t = ∏_i (f(a) − α_i), so 𝔭 ramifies over (f^{n+1}(a) − t) in K_n: contradiction. Unramified in each M_jK_n implies unramified in the compositum (requested from AlgebraicCurves layer 8, composita).

### 5.47 Finite levels as finite étale K-schemes

Let K be a field, f ∈ K[x] of degree ≥ 1 and α ∈ K with fⁿ − α separable. The ring map K[x]/(fⁿ − α) → K[x]/(f^{n+1} − α), x ↦ f(x), is well defined since f^{n+1} − α = (fⁿ − α) ∘ f; on K^sep-points it is β ↦ f(β), the parent map. ### 5.48 Level transitivity is irreducibility of the iterate

Let deg f ≥ 1, n ≥ 1 and fⁿ − α separable. Then Gal(K^sep/K) acts transitively on level n of T(f, α; K^sep) if and only if fⁿ(x) − α is irreducible over K. Consequently, for fⁿ − α separable for all n, (f, α) is stable iff G_∞(f, α) acts transitively on every level.

### 5.49 The index recursion for level images

Assume deg f = d ≥ 1 and fⁿ − α separable for all n. Then for every n: [Aut(T_{n+1}) : G_{n+1}] · [K_{n+1} : K_n] = [Aut(T_n) : G_n] · (d!)^{dⁿ}. In particular the indices [Aut(T_n) : G_n] are non-decreasing in n, and [Aut(T_{n+1}) : G_{n+1}] = [Aut(T_n) : G_n] exactly when [K_{n+1} : K_n] = (d!)^{dⁿ}.

deg f ≥ 1; all fⁿ − α separable (so the tree is d-regular).

|Aut(T_{n+1})| = |Aut(T_n)| (d!)^{dⁿ} (truncated-restriction-kernel), |G_{n+1}| = |G_n| [K_{n+1} : K_n] (arboreal-image-finite-level, |G_n| = [K_n : K]). Divide; [K_{n+1} : K_n] ≤ (d!)^{dⁿ} (relfinrank_preimageField_succ_le) gives monotonicity.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-5-square-root-of-adjusted-critical-value"></a>

### 5.50 A square root of c_n in K_n, transformed by the level-n sign

Let K be a field of characteristic ≠ 2, f = (x − γ)² + δ ∈ K[x], α ∈ K, n ≥ 1, with fⁿ − α separable. Choose for each β ∈ V_{n−1} a child y_β ∈ V_n and put s_n := ∏_{β ∈ V_{n−1}} (y_β − γ) ∈ K_n. Then s_n² = c_n, and for every σ ∈ Gal(K^sep/K), σ(s_n) = sign(σ|V_n) · s_n, where sign(σ|V_n) is the sign of the permutation of level n induced by ρ(σ). In particular c_n is a square in K_n, and K(√c_n) ⊆ K_n is the fixed field of the kernel of χ_n ∘ ρ.

char K ≠ 2; f monic quadratic; n ≥ 1; fⁿ − α separable.

s_n² = ∏_β (y_β − γ)² = ∏_β (β − δ) = c_n (shifted-root-product). The two children of β are γ ± (y_β − γ). σ sends y_β to a child of σβ, so σ(y_β − γ) = ε_β (y_{σβ} − γ) with ε_β = ±1, and σ(s_n) = (∏_β ε_β) s_n. The permutation of V_n induced by σ is the composite of the 'label-preserving' permutation y_β ↦ y_{σβ}, 2γ − y_β ↦ 2γ − y_{σβ} (two copies of the permutation of V_{n−1}, hence even) with the transpositions {y_β, 2γ − y_β} for ε_β = −1; its sign is ∏ ε_β.

([stoll-1992-quadratic-iterates](#source-parent-stoll-1992-quadratic-iterates), Lemma 1.5, proof — c_n is a square in K_n; the sign computation identifies which character of G_n it gives; [jones-arboreal-survey](#source-parent-jones-arboreal-survey), §2.2, p. 10, (9) — Equivalent discriminant-based route: √Disc(fⁿ − α) transforms by the sign on level n (Tau Ceti's discriminant test) and Disc(fⁿ − α) ≡ c_n mod squares (quadratic-discriminant-of-iterate).)

**Endpoint checks.** n = 1: s_1 = y − γ with (y − γ)² = α − δ = c_1, and σ(s_1) = −s_1 iff σ swaps the two level-1 vertices. f = x² + 1, α = 0, n = 2: s_2² = 2, and s_2 ∈ K_2.

### 5.51 Stable pairs: all iterates fⁿ − α irreducible

Let K be a field, f ∈ K[x] and α ∈ K. The pair (f, α) is stable over K (IsStableAt f α) if fⁿ(x) − α is irreducible over K for every n ≥ 1. For α = 0 this is Jones's 'f is stable'; in Jones's terminology (f, α) is stable iff x − α is f-stable. By Capelli's lemma irreducibility of f^N − α implies irreducibility of fⁿ − α for all 1 ≤ n ≤ N, so stability is the irreducibility of a cofinal set of iterates.

No hypotheses.

Definition: ∀ n ≥ 1, Irreducible (fⁿ − C α). irreducible_iterate_of_le: f^N − α = (fⁿ − α) ∘ f^{N−n} and deg f^{N−n} ≥ 1, so Capelli's lemma (⇒) gives irreducibility of fⁿ − α. isStableAt_iff_forall_transitive: level-transitivity-iff-irreducible at every level. isStableAt_conj_iff: affine-conjugation-invariance (conjugation by an affine map over K preserves irreducibility).

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.5/capelli-lemma`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-5-capelli-lemma); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.5/level-transitivity-iff-irreducible`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-5-level-transitivity-iff-irreducible); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.5/affine-conjugation-invariance`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-5-affine-conjugation-invariance).

- **`IsStableAt.irreducible_sub`** (projection): A stable pair has f − α irreducible.
- **`irreducible_iterate_of_le`** (relation): If deg f ≥ 1, 1 ≤ m ≤ n and fⁿ − α is irreducible then f^m − α is irreducible.
- **`isStableAt_iff_forall_transitive`** (characterisation): Under separability of all iterates, (f, α) is stable iff Gal(K^sep/K) acts transitively on every level n ≥ 1 of the preimage tree.
- **`isStableAt_conj_iff`** (functoriality): For u ∈ Kˣ, v ∈ K: (f, α) is stable iff (u⁻¹(f(ux + v) − v), u⁻¹(α − v)) is.

### 5.52 The Kummer step: [K_{n+1} : K_n] is maximal iff c_{n+1} is not a square in K_n

Let K be a field of characteristic ≠ 2, f = (x − γ)² + δ ∈ K[x], α ∈ K and n ≥ 0. Assume fⁿ − α is irreducible over K and c_{n+1} ≠ 0. Then [K_{n+1} : K_n] = 2^{2ⁿ} (equivalently Gal(K_{n+1}/K_n) is the whole kernel of Aut(T_{n+1}) → Aut(T_n), 'H_{n+1} maximal') if and only if c_{n+1} is not a square in K_n.

char K ≠ 2; fⁿ − α irreducible (so G_n acts transitively on V_n); c_{n+1} ≠ 0 (so f^{n+1} − α is separable).

By quadratic-level-kummer-generation and the multiquadratic degree formula, [K_{n+1} : K_n] = 2^{2ⁿ − dim R}, where R ⊆ F_2^{V_n} is the space of relations: ε with ∏_β (β − δ)^{ε_β} a square in K_n (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_adjoin_range_eq_two_pow_finrank_span_squareClass, TauCeti.linearIndependent_squareClass_iff). R is stable under G_n = Gal(K_n/K), which permutes the β − δ; fⁿ − α is separable (an irreducible polynomial of degree 2ⁿ is separable in characteristic ≠ 2), so G_n ≤ Aut(T_n) is a 2-group (tree-automorphism-order) acting transitively on V_n (level-transitivity-iff-irreducible). two-group-invariant-vector: R ≠ 0 iff (1, …, 1) ∈ R, i.e. iff ∏_β (β − δ) is a square in K_n. ∏_β (β − δ) = c_{n+1} (shifted-root-product).

### 5.53 The index of G_∞ in Aut(T_∞)

Assume deg f = d ≥ 1 and fⁿ − α separable for all n. Then G_∞(f, α) has finite index in Aut(T_∞) iff the sequence [Aut(T_n) : G_n] is bounded, iff [K_{n+1} : K_n] = (d!)^{dⁿ} for all sufficiently large n; and then [Aut(T_∞) : G_∞] = sup_n [Aut(T_n) : G_n] = lim_n [Aut(T_n) : G_n]. In particular [Aut(T_∞) : G_∞] = 1 iff G_n = Aut(T_n) for all n.

deg f ≥ 1; all fⁿ − α separable.

G_∞ is closed and is the inverse limit of the G_n (arboreal-image-inverse-limit); Aut(T_∞) = lim Aut(T_n) (tree-automorphism-inverse-limit). For a closed subgroup H of a profinite group lim Γ_n with images H_n: the maps Γ/H → Γ_n/H_n are surjective and [Γ : H] = sup_n [Γ_n : H_n] (a finite set of cosets of H is separated at some finite level; conversely distinct cosets at level n stay distinct). Boundedness of a non-decreasing integer sequence is eventual constancy; level-index-recursion translates constancy into maximal relative degrees.

### 5.54 Juul's Theorem 3.1: full wreath image over k(t) from one clean critical orbit

Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic 0 and f ∈ k[x] of degree d ≥ 2 such that Gal(f(x) − t/k(t)) ≅ S_d (G_1(f, t) = Aut(T_1)), with a critical point a of multiplicity one satisfying fᵐ(a) ≠ f^{m'}(b) for all critical points b and 1 ≤ m' ≤ m ≤ N unless (m', b) = (m, a). Then G_N(f, t) = Aut(T^d_N) over k(t): the Galois group of f^N(x) − t over k(t) is the full iterated wreath product [S_d]^N.

k algebraically closed, characteristic 0; G_1 = S_d; the critical orbit condition up to N.

Induction on n ≤ N; n = 1 is the hypothesis. Given G_n = Aut(T_n), for each root α_i of fⁿ(x) − t, Gal(M_i/k(α_i)) ≅ S_d (α_i is transcendental; same situation as f(x) − t). Γ_i := Gal(M_i / M_i ∩ M̂_i) is normal in S_d, so Γ_i = S_d or Γ_i ≤ A_d. The prime 𝔭 = (f(a) − α_i) exactly divides Disc(f(x) − α_i), so inertia above it in M_i is a transposition (inertia-is-transposition); 𝔭 is unramified in M̂_i (juul-nonramification-lemma), so the ramification index stays 2 over M_i ∩ M̂_i and Γ_i contains a transposition; Γ_i = S_d. Hence Gal(K_{n+1}/M̂_i) ≅ S_d for each i, [K_{n+1} : K_n] = (d!)^{dⁿ}, and |G_{n+1}| = |Aut(T_{n+1})| (tree-automorphism-order, level-index-recursion); G_{n+1} ≤ Aut(T_{n+1}) gives equality.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.5/juul-nonramification-lemma`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-5-juul-nonramification-lemma); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.5/inertia-is-transposition`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-5-inertia-is-transposition); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.5/tree-automorphism-order`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-5-tree-automorphism-order); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.5/level-index-recursion`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-5-level-index-recursion); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.5/arboreal-image-finite-level`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-5-arboreal-image-finite-level); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.5/truncated-restriction-kernel`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-5-truncated-restriction-kernel).

### 5.55 Eventually stable pairs

Let K be a field, f ∈ K[x] and α ∈ K. The pair (f, α) is eventually stable over K (IsEventuallyStableAt f α) if the number of irreducible factors of fⁿ(x) − α, counted with multiplicity, is bounded independently of n. Require also fⁿ − α ≠ 0 for every n, so the zero polynomial is never assigned a factor count for this definition; positive-degree f makes this condition automatic.

No hypotheses on the input data. The definition requires all iterates minus α to be nonzero and counts UniqueFactorizationMonoid.factors with multiplicity. The extra nonzero condition excludes the library convention factors 0 = 0.

Definition: (∀ n, fⁿ − C α ≠ 0) ∧ ∃ B, ∀ n, card (factors (fⁿ − C α)) ≤ B. IsStableAt.isEventuallyStableAt: an irreducible polynomial has one factor, and f⁰ − α = x − α is irreducible; B = 1. For deg f ≥ 1 all iterates minus α have positive degree and are nonzero. Removing finitely many initial indices changes only the bound, proving isEventuallyStableAt_iff_of_le under that degree hypothesis.

### 5.57 Jones's ramification criterion for maximality

Let f = x² + bx + c with b, c ∈ ℤ, γ = −b/2, α ∈ ℤ and n ≥ 1, with fⁿ − α irreducible over ℚ. If there is an odd prime p with v_p(c_{n+1}) odd and v_p(c_k) = 0 for 1 ≤ k ≤ n, then [K_{n+1} : K_n] = 2^{2ⁿ}, i.e. H_{n+1} = Gal(K_{n+1}/K_n) is maximal (the whole kernel of Aut(T_{n+1}) → Aut(T_n)). In words: a primitive prime divisor of the adjusted critical orbit appearing to odd multiplicity forces a new maximal Kummer layer.

f monic quadratic with integer coefficients, α ∈ ℤ; fⁿ − α irreducible over ℚ (essential: the survey stresses the irreducibility hypothesis cannot be dropped). p odd, v_p(c_{n+1}) odd, v_p(c_k) = 0 for k ≤ n.

c_{n+1} ≠ 0 (odd valuation), so f^{n+1} − α is separable; fⁿ − α is separable (irreducible over ℚ). p is unramified in K_n (unramified-outside-critical-orbit); so c_{n+1} is not a square in K_n (odd-valuation-nonsquare). stoll-kummer-step gives [K_{n+1} : K_n] = 2^{2ⁿ}.

### 5.58 Infinite index for x^d + b with d ≥ 3

Let K be a field, d ≥ 3 with (d : K) ≠ 0, b, α ∈ K, f = x^d + b, and assume fⁿ − α separable for all n. Then |G_n| ≤ |G_1| · d^{d + d² + ⋯ + d^{n−1}} for all n ≥ 1, and G_∞(f, α) has infinite index in Aut(T^d_∞). Moreover the Hausdorff dimension liminf log|G_n| / log|Aut(T_n)| is at most log d / log d!.

d ≥ 3, (d : K) ≠ 0 (so x^d − 1 is separable and K_1 contains the d-th roots of unity), all fⁿ − α separable.

The roots of f(x) = β are the d-th roots of β − b; for n ≥ 1, K_n contains the ratios of the d distinct roots of f(x) − α, i.e. the d-th roots of unity (α ≠ b by separability). So K_{n+1} = K_n(y_β : β ∈ V_n), y_β^d = β − b, and [K_{n+1} : K_n] ≤ d^{dⁿ} (each adjunction has degree ≤ d; the other roots are y_β ζ). |G_n| = [K_n : K] ≤ [K_1 : K] d^{d + ⋯ + d^{n−1}} while |Aut(T_n)| = (d!)^{(dⁿ−1)/(d−1)} (tree-automorphism-order); since d! > d for d ≥ 3 the index [Aut(T_n) : G_n] → ∞; apply index-of-arboreal-image.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-5-odoni-generic-theorem"></a>

### 5.59 Odoni's theorem: the generic polynomial has full arboreal image

Let k be a field of characteristic 0, d ≥ 2, s_0, …, s_{d−1} independent indeterminates, F = k(s_0, …, s_{d−1}) and G(x) = x^d + s_{d−1}x^{d−1} + ⋯ + s_0 ∈ F[x]. Then for every n, G_n(G, 0) = Aut(T^d_n): the Galois group of Gⁿ(x) over F is the full iterated wreath product [S_d]^n; hence G_∞(G, 0) = Aut(T^d_∞).

char k = 0 (Juul extends this to all characteristics with (d, char k) ≠ (2, 2); that extension is outside the selected statement).

Separability: Gⁿ is separable over F (it specializes to separable polynomials), so the tree is d-regular. Reduce to k algebraically closed: G_n over k̄(s) is contained in G_n over k(s) (level-image-base-change), so it suffices to prove maximality over k̄(s). Pick a monic f ∈ k̄[x] (apply the scalar conjugation in the existence proof) of degree d from critical-orbit-relations-avoidable (for N = n); first-level-symmetric gives G_1(f, t) = S_d, and juul-maximality-over-function-field gives G_n(f, t) = Aut(T_n) over k̄(t). g(x) = f(x + t) − t has gⁿ(x) = fⁿ(x + t) − t (shift-to-transcendental-root), so G_n(g, 0) = G_n(f, t) = Aut(T_n); g is the specialization of G at s_i ↦ coeff_i(g) ∈ k̄[t], and galois-specialization gives Aut(T_n) = G_n(g, 0) ≤ G_n(G, 0) ≤ Aut(T_n).

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-5-stoll-maximality-criterion"></a>

### 5.60 Stoll's maximality criterion

Let K be a field of characteristic ≠ 2, f = (x − γ)² + δ ∈ K[x], α ∈ K and n ≥ 0 with fⁿ − α separable. Then G_n(f, α) = Aut(T_n) (equivalently [K_n : K] = 2^{2ⁿ−1}) if and only if c_1, …, c_n are 2-independent in K: no nonempty subproduct ∏_{i∈S} c_i, S ⊆ {1, …, n}, is a square in K (equivalently, the classes of c_1, …, c_n in Kˣ/Kˣ² are F_2-linearly independent: TauCeti.linearIndependent_squareClass_iff).

char K ≠ 2; f monic quadratic (any quadratic reduces to this by affine-conjugation-invariance); fⁿ − α separable.

Induction on n; n = 0 is trivial. Assume the equivalence at n. (Stoll Lemma 1.4) G_{n+1} = Aut(T_{n+1}) iff G_n = Aut(T_n) and [K_{n+1} : K_n] = 2^{2ⁿ}, since |Aut(T_{n+1})| = |Aut(T_n)| · 2^{2ⁿ} (tree-automorphism-order), |G_{n+1}| = |G_n| [K_{n+1} : K_n] (arboreal-image-finite-level) and [K_{n+1} : K_n] ≤ 2^{2ⁿ}. If c_1, …, c_{n+1} are independent, each c_i is a non-square, so (f, α) is stable up to n + 1 (quadratic-stability-criterion) and stoll-kummer-step applies: [K_{n+1}:K_n] = 2^{2ⁿ} iff c_{n+1} is not a square in K_n. (Stoll Lemma 1.5) If G_n = Aut(T_n) and c_1, …, c_n are independent then for c ∈ Kˣ: c is a square in K_n iff c_1, …, c_n, c are dependent. ⇐: c ≡ ∏_{i∈S} c_i mod squares and each c_i is a square in K_n (square-root-of-adjusted-critical-value). ⇒: K(√c_1, …, √c_n) ⊆ K_n has degree 2ⁿ (independence, multiquadratic degree formula), and every subfield of K_n generated by square roots of elements of K has degree ≤ #Hom(Gal(K_n/K), ±1) = 2ⁿ (binary-tree-sign-characters, as G_n = Aut(T_n)); so √c ∈ K(√c_1, …, √c_n) and square descent (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.squareClass_of_sq_mem_fintype) gives c ∏_{i∈S} c_i ∈ Kˣ². Combine: G_{n+1} maximal iff c_1..c_n independent and c_{n+1} not a square in K_n iff c_1, …, c_{n+1} independent. The equivalence of square-free subproducts with linear independence of square classes is TauCeti.linearIndependent_squareClass_iff.

### 5.61 Maximal level images for all polynomials outside a thin set

Let K be a number field, d ≥ 2 and n ≥ 1. There is a thin set E_n ⊆ K^d such that for every (a_0, …, a_{d−1}) ∈ K^d ∖ E_n the polynomial f = x^d + a_{d−1}x^{d−1} + ⋯ + a_0 has G_n(f, 0) = Aut(T^d_n). (E_n is not effectively computable from the argument, and no single f with G_∞(f) = Aut(T_∞) follows for d ≥ 3.)

By odoni-generic-theorem the Galois group of Gⁿ over K(s) is Aut(T_n) (K has characteristic 0). Hilbert's irreducibility theorem for the finite Galois extension of K(s) split by Gⁿ (requested from InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.2) gives specializations with the same Galois group outside a thin set; galois-specialization identifies the specialized trees.

char K ≠ 2; f monic quadratic; all fⁿ − α separable.

ρ surjective iff G_n = Aut(T_n) for all n (arboreal-image-inverse-limit). For each n apply stoll-maximality-criterion; finite subproducts of the whole orbit involve finitely many indices.

### 5.63 Stoll's Theorem (Section 1): maximality from non-square Möbius factors

Let a ∈ ℤ with −a not a square, f = x² + a over ℚ, α = 0 and n ≥ 1. (1) G_n(f, 0) = Aut(T_n) iff b_1, …, b_n are 2-independent in ℚ. (2) If none of |b_2|, …, |b_n| is a square in ℚ, then G_n(f, 0) = Aut(T_n).

a ∈ ℤ, −a not a square (this is also the irreducibility of every f_n with n ≥ 1).

(1): by stoll-maximality-criterion, G_n maximal iff c_1, …, c_n are 2-independent; the classes of c_1, …, c_n and of b_1, …, b_n in ℚˣ/ℚˣ² span the same F_2-subspace (c_m = ∏_{d∣m} b_d and b_m = ∏ c_d^{μ(m/d)}), so one family is independent iff the other is. (2): the b_m are pairwise coprime integers (critical-orbit-mobius-factors), and a square product of pairwise coprime integers has every factor a square up to sign; so b_1, …, b_n are 2-independent iff none of the b_m is a square and at most one of the −b_m is a square. Here b_1 = −a is not a square; if moreover no |b_m| with m ≥ 2 is a square then no b_m and no −b_m with m ≥ 2 is a square, and the family is 2-independent. Pass from (1).

### 5.64 Stoll's theorem: surjective arboreal representations for x² + a over ℚ

Let a ∈ ℤ with (a) a > 0 and a ≡ 1 (mod 4), or (b) a > 0 and a ≡ 2 (mod 4), or (c) a < 0, a ≡ 0 (mod 4) and −a not a square. Then for f = x² + a over ℚ and α = 0, G_n(f, 0) = Aut(T_n) for every n ≥ 1; equivalently the arboreal representation ρ : Gal(ℚ^sep/ℚ) → Aut(T²_∞) is surjective.

One of (a), (b), (c).

In all cases −a is not a square. Rescale: g := |a| x² + sgn(a), an even integer polynomial; with γ_1 := 1 its iteration sequence satisfies γ_n |a| = |c_n| for n ≥ 1 (induction), so γ_n > 0 (critical-orbit-positivity) and β_n = |b_n| for n ≥ 2 (the Möbius exponents sum to zero for n ≥ 2, so the factors |a| cancel). Case (a): g(0) = 1, g(1) = a + 1 ≡ 2 (mod 4); cases (b), (c): g(1) = |a| ± 1 ≡ 3 (mod 4). By even-sequence-congruence-criterion no |b_n|, n ≥ 2, is a square. stoll-mobius-criterion (2) gives G_n = Aut(T_n) for all n; the tree is regular (c_n ≠ 0, adjustedCriticalOrbit_ne_zero_iff) and surjectivity follows from arboreal-surjectivity-criterion / arboreal-image-inverse-limit.
