- **`isAffineLattes`** (characterisation): Existence of the rank-two torus affine quotient data above.
- **`affineLattes_conjugation`** (functoriality): Möbius conjugation preserves the predicate.
- **`affineLattes_degree`** (structure): The degree is |a|² for any quotient presentation.
- **`multiplication_isAffineLattes`** (compatibility): An inherited multiplication Lattès map over C satisfies this predicate.
- **`affineLattes_normalForm`** (relation): Every such map has cyclic quotient normal form n=2,3,4 or6.
- **`affineLattes_flexible_iff`** (characterisation): In the normal form the map is flexible iff n=2 and a∈Z.

**Checks.**

- **`affineLattes_degree_four`** (compatibility): Multiplication by 2 on any complex elliptic torus gives a flexible map of degree 4.
- **`affineLattes_degree_two`** (computation): Multiplication by 1+i on C/Z[i], modulo ±1, gives a rigid affine Lattès map of degree 2.
- **`affineLattes_power_nonexample`** (non-example): z^d has exceptional points 0 and infinity and is not an affine-torus Lattès map, which has none.
- **`affineLattes_translation`** (characterisation): For odd integer a, the nonzero admissible 2-torsion translation can give a flexible map with no postcritical fixed point; multiplication-only data miss it.

### 6.68 Symmetries of the Legendre escape rates (DeMarco–Krieger–Ye Proposition 2.1)

Let K be a number field, v a place of K and t ∈ K ∖ {0, 1}. With F_t the homogeneous lift of DY.6/legendre-lattes-map and G_{F,v} the escape rate of DY.2/escape-rate: G_{F_{1−t},v}(1 − z, 1) = G_{F_t,v}(z, 1) = G_{F_{1/t},v}(z, t) = G_{F_{1/t},v}(z/t, 1) + log|t|_v for all z ∈ ℂ_v.

K a number field, v any place (archimedean or not), t ≠ 0, 1.

A ∘ F_tⁿ = −F_{1−t}ⁿ ∘ A with A(z, w) = (w − z, w) (DY.6/legendre-lattes-symmetries); since ‖−u‖_v = ‖u‖_v and A is invertible linear, ‖A(u)‖_v is within a bounded factor of ‖u‖_v, so d^{−n} log ‖F_tⁿ(z, 1)‖ and d^{−n} log ‖F_{1−t}ⁿ(1 − z, 1)‖ have the same limit. B ∘ F_tⁿ = F_{1/t}ⁿ ∘ B with B(z, w) = (z, tw): the same argument gives G_{F_{1/t},v}(z, t) = G_{F_t,v}(z, 1). Logarithmic homogeneity G(cz, cw) = G(z, w) + log|c|_v (DY.2/escape-rate) with c = t gives the last equality.

### 6.69 Symmetries of the local energy (DeMarco–Krieger–Ye Proposition 2.3)

Let K be a number field, v ∈ M_K and t₁, t₂ ∈ K ∖ {0, 1}. The local energy E_v(t₁, t₂) = ½(∫(λ_{t₁,v} − λ_{t₂,v}) dμ_{t₂,v} + ∫(λ_{t₂,v} − λ_{t₁,v}) dμ_{t₁,v}) = ½(μ_{t₁,v} − μ_{t₂,v}, μ_{t₁,v} − μ_{t₂,v})_v of the Legendre heights (the local term of the Arakelov–Zhang pairing, DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing) satisfies E_v(t₂, t₁) = E_v(t₁, t₂) = E_v(1 − t₁, 1 − t₂) = E_v(1/t₁, 1/t₂).

K a number field; v any place; t₁, t₂ ≠ 0, 1.

Symmetry in (t₁, t₂) is visible from the formula. E_v(t₁, t₂) = −½ ∫ g d(μ_{t₁,v} − μ_{t₂,v}) for any continuous potential g of μ_{t₁,v} − μ_{t₂,v} (DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing); g = λ_{t₁,v} − λ_{t₂,v} + c. For t ↦ 1−t use the common conjugacy α(z)=1−z, naturality of canonical measures, and invariance of the mass-zero energy under one Möbius map. For inversion, the parameter-dependent maps γ_t(z)=z/t alone do not justify pairing invariance. The involution ι_t(z)=t/z is induced by translation by (0,0) on E_t, and f_t∘ι_t=f_t. Since f_t*μ_t=4μ_t, pulling this identity back through ι_t gives ι_t*μ_t=μ_t (equivalently use Haar invariance at the complex places). Conjugacy gives μ_{1/t}=γ_{t*}μ_t, hence μ_{1/t}=(γ_t∘ι_t)_*μ_t=β_*μ_t with the common β(z)=1/z. Apply the same mass-zero energy invariance simultaneously to both parameters. This fills the proof gap in Proposition 2.3 (E712).

(32): |ĥ_{f_{t₀}}(x) − h(x)| ≤ c₁ h(t₀) + c₂ (DY.6/uniform-canonical-height-bound-in-families). (35): |ĥ^{K(t)}_f(Q) − h_{K(t)}(Q)| ≤ c₅ (DY.1/canonical-height-over-a-global-height-field). ### 6.71 Algebraically independent integral specialization with a simple root

Let n ≥ 0, H ∈ ℤ[T₁,…,Tₙ][Y] have positive natural degree and separable image over Frac(ℤ[T₁,…,Tₙ]), and let D be a finite set of nonzero parameter polynomials. For every N ∈ ℕ there are a prime p > N, ξ ∈ ℤ_pⁿ with algebraically independent image in ℚ_p over ℚ, and η ∈ ℤ_p such that F = H(Y,ξ) satisfies F(η) = 0, F′(η) is a unit, deg F = deg H, lc(H)(ξ) is a unit, and every q(ξ), q ∈ D, is a unit.

H is supplied integral polynomial data; it need not be monic or irreducible. This is not a presentation of an arbitrary finitely generated field. The independence of ξ makes evaluation on ℚ[T] injective, but extending across an arbitrary field presentation is a separate contract.

Apply DY.6/lech-specialized-simple-prime to H, D and N. It chooses the prime p and integral residue data a,b with exactly the root, derivative, leading-coefficient and denominator exclusions required by DY.6/lech-residue-hensel-lift. Apply DY.6/lech-independent-residue-tuple to this p and a. The resulting ξ is integral, independent in ℚ_p and has the same residues; choosing merely ξ = a would destroy independence whenever n > 0. Apply DY.6/lech-residue-hensel-lift to obtain η and all asserted root, degree and unit conclusions. Retain the independence proof from the preceding step; η is algebraic over the evaluated parameter field and is not asserted independent of ξ. The finite-field-presentation adapter and extension of the induced fraction-field map to the primitive extension are not conclusions of this node. DY.6/lech-embedding-lemma consumes this parameter/root output and retains those two exact gaps.

### 6.75 Finiteness of rigid Lattès classes in fixed degree

For each d≥2, there are finitely many complex affine-torus Lattès conjugacy classes of degree d which are not flexible. The classes defined over Q̄ therefore have bounded ample moduli height.

Conjugacy classes are counted, not presentations or rational maps with chosen coordinates. The bounded-height assertion is only on algebraic classes.

If n≥3, normalize Λ to the Gaussian or Eisenstein lattice and use |a|²=d; only finitely many a and translation quotient invariants occur. For n=2, nonflexibility forces a∉Z. Its equation is a²−qa+d=0 with q²<4d, leaving finitely many a. Milnor Lemma 5.4 bounds the normalized lattice shapes for each a by writing a=r+sγ and Im γ≥√3/2. Theorem 5.1 leaves only a finite translation quotient for each fixed lattice and a. Thus only finitely many rigid classes occur, and any height is bounded on the finite algebraic subset.

### 6.76 Good reduction and canonical measures of f_t at places not above 2 (DeMarco–Krieger–Ye Proposition 3.2)

Let K be a number field, v a nonarchimedean place of K with v ∤ 2, and t ∈ K ∖ {0, 1}. Then f_t has good reduction at v (DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map) if and only if |t(t − 1)|_v = 1, in which case μ_{t,v} is the point mass at the Gauss point ζ_{0,1}. If |t(t − 1)|_v ≠ 1, then f_t does not have potential good reduction at v, and its canonical measure μ_{t,v} (DY.2/canonical-measure) is the interval measure (uniform for the hyperbolic metric) on [ζ_{0,1}, ζ_{0,|t|_v}] when |t|_v ≠ 1, and on [ζ_{0,1}, ζ_{1,|1−t|_v}] when |1 − t|_v < 1.

Good reduction: Res(F_t) = 256t⁴(t − 1)⁴ (DY.6/legendre-lattes-map) is a v-unit iff |t(t − 1)|_v = 1 when |t|_v ≤ 1 and |1 − t|_v ≤ 1; if |t|_v > 1 the normalised lift has non-unit resultant. By DY.6/legendre-escape-rate-symmetries (t ↦ 1/t, 1 − t) it suffices to treat |t|_v > 1. For |t|_v > 1 the interval I = [ζ_{0,1}, ζ_{0,|t|_v}] is totally invariant, f_t⁻¹(I) = I, and f_t acts on it by the tent map f_t(ζ_{0,|t|^r}) = ζ_{0,|t|^{2r−1}} for ½ ≤ r ≤ 1 and ζ_{0,|t|^{1−2r}} for 0 ≤ r ≤ ½ (Favre–Rivera-Letelier §5.1; the action of f_t on type II points is DY.2's dynamics on the Berkovich line). The uniform measure on I is the unique f_t-balanced probability measure supported on the totally invariant interval, hence equals μ_{t,v} (characterisation of DY.2/canonical-measure); a measure that is not a point mass at a type II point rules out potential good reduction.

### 6.77 Non-preperiodic points stay non-preperiodic in specialisations of large height

In the setting of DY.6/specialization-of-canonical-heights, if ĥ^{K(t)}_f(P) > 0 then there is H such that P_{t₀} is not preperiodic for f_{t₀} for every t₀ ∈ T⁰(f) ∩ ℚ̄ with h(t₀) > H. In particular, for every r ≥ 1 there are infinitely many t₀ ∈ ℚ̄ with [ℚ(t₀) : ℚ] ≤ r at which P_{t₀} is wandering for f_{t₀}.

K a number field; ĥ^{K(t)}_f(P) > 0 (this holds when f is not isotrivial and P is not preperiodic, by Benedetto's theorem for polynomials; that criterion is not part of DY.6, and the node takes positivity as its hypothesis).

By DY.6/specialization-of-canonical-heights, ĥ_{f_{t₀}}(P_{t₀}) ≥ ½ ĥ^{K(t)}_f(P) h(t₀) > 0 once h(t₀) is large. Preperiodic points have canonical height 0 (DY.1/zero-canonical-height-iff-preperiodic), so P_{t₀} is wandering. There are infinitely many t₀ ∈ ℚ of height > H (e.g. integers), which gives the last clause with r = 1.

### 6.82 Continuous marked escape potential across the three Legendre cusps

For c∈C(t) other than 0,1,t, choose the primitive homogeneous lift C, the cancelled F₁ and F_{n+1} of legendre-marked-degree-growth, with d=deg F₁. Its projective curvature defines a probability bifurcation measure μ_c; continuity at the cusp parameters 0,1,infinity prevents this probability from being supported only at those cusps.

A finite rational mark, including nonconstant marks, is allowed. Use the primitive cancellation and degree normalization from the preceding target. Local uniform convergence includes nonzero homogeneous parameter vectors representing the three singular fibres.

Away from the cusps, nonvanishing of the resultant gives the usual summable successive escape-rate estimate. DWY §4 separates the estimates at infinity, zero, and one; its Proposition 4.1 identifies the boundary limits through the nonzero boundary values from degree growth. These cusp-uniform estimates remain a named proof leaf, rather than being inferred from the nondegenerate estimate. Each normalized function is plurisubharmonic and logarithmically homogeneous of degree one. Local uniform convergence preserves continuity, plurisubharmonicity and the logarithmic scaling relation. ### 6.83 Ingram's theorem: the critical height is a moduli height

Let d ≥ 2 and let h_{M_d} be an ample Weil height on M_d: the Weil height (HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions:RP.0) attached to an ample line bundle on a projective compactification of the moduli space M_d (DY.0/moduli-space-of-rational-maps), restricted to M_d(ℚ̄). There are constants c₁, c₃ > 0 and c₂, c₄ ≥ 0 such that c₁ h_{M_d}([f]) − c₂ ≤ ĥ_crit([f]) ≤ c₃ h_{M_d}([f]) + c₄ for all [f] ∈ M_d(ℚ̄) outside the flexible Lattès locus L_d (DY.6/flexible-lattes-map). In particular the non-Lattès PCF classes form a set of bounded height, finite in each bounded degree.

Use a representative of minimal coefficient height and Silverman’s comparison (Ingram Lemma 13) to obtain the moduli upper bound. That comparison is an explicit recorded input. Ingram Lemma 11: move a fixed point γ of multiplier λ ≠ 0,1 to 0 and another fixed point to ∞. For γ = [α:γ₀] and the other point [β:δ], use ψ(z) = (βz+α)/(δz+γ₀), so ψ(0) is the λ-point. Normalize each column separately to bound h(ψ) by the sum of the two point heights. The homogeneous fixed-point polynomial bounds that sum, and coefficient estimates yield h_{Hom_d}(ψ⁻¹fψ) ≤ (d+2)h_{Hom_d}(f)+O_d(1). E714 records the reversed columns in the source. At an archimedean place Koebe’s quarter theorem produces a critical point in the attracting domain; at a finite place the quantitative attracting-cycle theorem of Benedetto–Ingram–Jones–Levy does this when |λ|_v is sufficiently small. Root/coefficient estimates relate the size of the attracting disc to h_{Hom_d}. The followup-quantitative-attracting-branch target identifies the archimedean and finite-place analytic inputs and keeps their proof leaves explicit. Ingram Lemma 10: use the branch divisor B′ obtained by removing critical images whose forward orbit reaches 0. The removed part has canonical height zero, while f_*^k B′ remains disjoint from 0 so its Green pairing is defined. The attracted critical orbit supplies the k log⁺|λ⁻¹|_v term; the other terms have the uniform Green lower bound. The resulting error is linear in k and in local coefficient size, with resultant term r_v(f). Ingram Lemma 12: sum with the absolute place weights. The resultant contribution cancels by the product formula; Σ_v r_v log⁺|λ⁻¹|_v = h(λ). The Green pairing sums to d^{k+1}ĥ_crit(f). Combining with the coordinate estimate gives d^{k+1}ĥ_crit(f) ≥ (k−1)h(λ) − (4d−1)(d+2)h_{Hom_d}(f) − c₀k. The cases λ = 0,1 follow directly from nonnegativity. For a sufficiently large fixed k, its positive k-dependent coefficient absorbs the remaining coefficient-height error. This proves the lower bound outside all Lattès classes, exactly as Ingram Theorem 1 states. To state the endpoint outside the flexible Lattès locus, absorb the finitely many rigid Lattès classes of fixed degree into the additive constant. ### 6.84 Explicit escape rates of f_t at places not above 2 (DeMarco–Krieger–Ye Propositions 3.3–3.4)

Let v be a nonarchimedean place of a number field K with v ∤ 2 and t ∈ K ∖ {0, 1}. ### 6.85 Canonical measures of f_t at places above 2 (DeMarco–Krieger–Ye Proposition 3.5)

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-6-tate-variation-of-canonical-height"></a>

### 6.87 Tate's theorem: the canonical height varies like a Weil height on the base

Let K be a number field, E a Weierstrass curve over K(t) with coefficients in K[t] and Δ(E) ≢ 0, and P ∈ E(K(t)). There is a constant C(E, P) such that |ĥ_{E_{t₀}}(P_{t₀}) − ĥ_{E/K(t)}(P) · h(t₀)| ≤ C(E, P) for all t₀ ∈ ℚ̄ with Δ(E)(t₀) ≠ 0 (absolute Néron–Tate heights normalised to (O), as in DY.6/elliptic-specialization-of-canonical-heights). (For a general base curve X, ĥ_{E_t}(P_t) = h_{D}(t) + O(1) for a ℚ-divisor D of degree ĥ_E(P); for X = ℙ¹ this is the displayed statement.)

K a number field; base the t-line; Δ(E)(t₀) ≠ 0.

Tate's proof decomposes ĥ_{E_{t₀}} into Néron local heights λ_{E_{t₀},v} and shows that, as functions of t₀, they differ from local Weil functions of the divisor D_P on the base by bounded amounts; this uses Néron models of E over the local rings of the base (Call–Silverman Remark after Theorem 4.1; Ingram §1). The proof is not decomposed in DY.6: Tate's article is not publicly available (see gaps); the statement is recorded as a source-bound endpoint and strengthens DY.6/elliptic-specialization-of-canonical-heights from o(h(t₀)) to O(1).

### 6.88 Embedding a finitely generated field into ℚ_p with prescribed integral elements (Lech–Cassels)

Let L/ℚ be finitely generated as a field and let s be any finite subset of L, independently of a finite field-generating set. For every N ∈ ℕ there are a prime p > N and an embedding σ : L ↪ ℚ_p with ‖σ(x)‖ ≤ 1 for every x ∈ s. Equivalently there are infinitely many such primes; one can in particular require p ≥ 5.

L is a field with a ℚ-algebra structure and Algebra.EssFiniteType ℚ L; IntermediateField.fg_top_iff identifies this with finite field generation. The marked finite set may contain zero and need not generate L. The target is ℚ_p itself, not an unspecified finite extension.

followup-integral-primitive-presentation obtains the integer parameter ring, its fraction-field embedding, generically separable primitive equation and marked expressions with parameter-only denominators from arbitrary EssFiniteType Q L. Marks may include zero and need not generate the field. Use the accepted lech-independent-hensel-specialization with bound max(N,3) to get independent integral parameters, a simple integral root, and unit denominators. followup-primitive-root-transport extends the parameter-field map through that root; evaluate the marked expressions to get integral images. followup-lech-integral-assembly joins these statements, discharging the two inherited presentation/transport gaps at planning level without assuming an embedding conclusion or using Chebotarev.

### 6.89 Infinitely many torsion specializations of a constant Legendre mark

For a∈Q̄\{0,1}, there are infinitely many distinct t∈Q̄\{0,1} for which a is preperiodic for f_t, equivalently either point of E_t over x=a is torsion.

Infinity is handled separately as a persistent mark. The choice of sign of the point does not affect torsion.

The marked degree growth implies a nonzero activity/bifurcation measure, by the convergence of normalized marked escape rates in DWY Theorem 1.5. DWY §6.5 invokes the normal-family criterion and a Montel argument: an active mark in the Legendre family has infinitely many preperiodic parameters. This analytic bridge, rather than the entire equivalence in Theorem 1.2, is the remaining gap recorded here. Each preperiodic relation is an algebraic equation over Q̄ in t. It is not identically zero by marked degree growth; its roots are algebraic. The inherited semiconjugacy identifies them with torsion parameters.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-6-polynomial-lines-dynamical-mordell-lang"></a>

### 6.92 The dynamical Mordell–Lang theorem for lines under split polynomial maps (Ghioca–Tucker–Zieve Theorem 1.4)

Let K be a field of characteristic 0, f, g ∈ K[X] and x₀, y₀ ∈ K. If {(fⁿ(x₀), gⁿ(y₀)) : n ∈ ℕ} meets a line L ⊂ 𝔸²_K in infinitely many points, then L is periodic under (f, g). Consequently {n : (fⁿ(x₀), gⁿ(y₀)) ∈ L} is a finite union of arithmetic progressions: DML(𝔸², (f, g)) holds for lines.

char K = 0; f, g arbitrary polynomials (possibly of different degrees or linear).

GTZ §5, Lemma 5.1 reduces to the diagonal. In the linear case use ArithmeticDynamics:DY.6/followup-linear-synchronized-intersection, with the S-unit/Siegel contract explicitly required there. The degree-at-least-two case uses the following height comparison and common-iterate reduction. Comparing heights of fⁿ(x₀) and gⁿ(y₀) (canonical heights, DY.1/canonical-height-on-the-projective-line) forces deg f = deg g when there are infinitely many common points (Lemma 5.7). Equal degrees: DY.6/polynomial-orbits-on-lines-equal-degree gives f^k = g^k, so the diagonal is (f, g)^k-invariant, i.e. periodic. Periodic L of period k: the return set is a union of the progressions {kj + ℓ} through the first return points, plus finitely many points (DY.6/finite-union-of-arithmetic-progressions). The first assertion counts distinct orbit points, not indices. If the orbit has only finitely many points, its time sequence is eventually periodic, which gives the return-set conclusion directly even when L is not periodic. If the orbit is infinite but has finitely many points on L, those occur at finitely many times. These cases complete the DML assertion for every orbit. Assembly supplier refinement: use DY.6/followup-bilu-tichy-equal-degree, DY.6/followup-ritt-common-iterate, DY.6/followup-linear-synchronized-intersection, DY.6/followup-global-curve-specialization. Their stated hypotheses and named proof gaps remain in force; the endpoint does not discharge those supplier gaps.

### 6.93 Cassels embedding with prescribed p-adic units

Let L/ℚ be finitely generated as a field and let s ⊂ L be a finite set of nonzero elements. For every N there are a prime p > N and a field embedding σ : L ↪ ℚ_p such that ‖σ(x)‖ = 1 for all x ∈ s. Thus these images belong to ℤ_p×, not merely to ℤ_p.

Field finite generation is Algebra.EssFiniteType ℚ L, equivalently finite generation of the top IntermediateField; it is not Algebra.FiniteType ℚ L. Every marked element is nonzero. The set s need not generate L.

Apply DY.6/lech-embedding-lemma to the finite set s together with all inverses of its elements. For each x ∈ s both σ(x) and σ(x⁻¹) have norm at most one. The embedding preserves their product x·x⁻¹ = 1, so multiplicativity forces both norms to equal one. View σ(x) in the existing PadicInt subtype; PadicInt.isUnit_iff identifies norm one with invertibility. No new unit or p-adic carrier is introduced.

### 6.94 Integral images of a localized coefficient ring

Let L/ℚ be finitely generated as a field, s ⊂ L finite, f ∈ L nonzero and N ∈ ℕ. There are p > N and an embedding σ : L ↪ ℚ_p such that ‖σ(f)‖ = 1 and every element of the ℤ-subalgebra ℤ[s,f⁻¹] has image of norm at most one.

The generated ring is the existing Algebra.adjoin ℤ of s ∪ {f⁻¹}; f is not required to lie in s. When f ∈ ℤ[s], this ring is the image inside L of the localization ℤ[s][1/f]. It is not a new localization carrier.

Apply DY.6/lech-embedding-lemma with marked set s ∪ {f,f⁻¹}. As f is nonzero, the inverse-product argument gives ‖σ(f)‖ = 1. For the p-adic-model consumer, take s to be finite ℤ-algebra generators of its coefficient ring R and f the nonzero function defining D(f). The restriction to R[1/f] lands in the existing ℤ_p subtype, so its map to Spec R lands in D(f). This node handles the coefficient-ring assertion, not the separate geometric spreading-out request.

For every ε > 0 and integer n ≥ 1 there is δ > 0 such that 1/n − ε < μ_t({|t|^{(i+1)/n} ≤ |z| ≤ |t|^{i/n}}) < 1/n + ε for all 0 < |t| < δ and i = 0, …, n − 1; consequently (taking ε = 1/n²) μ_t({|z| ≥ 1} ∪ {|z| ≤ |t|}) < 1/n for 0 < |t| < δ.

Apply DY.6/legendre-measure-degeneration (a) to the n annuli with (a, b) = ((i + 1)/n, i/n) and a constant C slightly larger than 1; the limit masses are 1/n. The complement of the n annuli in {|t| < |z| < 1} is covered by thin annuli of limit mass 0; total mass 1 gives (4.4).

### 6.98 Lower bound for the nonarchimedean local energy (DeMarco–Krieger–Ye Theorem 3.1)

Let K be a number field, v a nonarchimedean place and t₁, t₂ ∈ K ∖ {0, 1}. Then E_v(t₁, t₂) − (4/3) log|2|_v is at least log²|t₁/t₂|_v/(6 log max{|t₁|_v, |t₂|_v}) if min{|t₁|_v, |t₂|_v} > 1; at least log²|t₁/t₂|_v/(−6 log min{|t₁|_v, |t₂|_v}) if max{|t₁|_v, |t₂|_v} < 1; and at least |log|t₁/t₂|_v|/6 otherwise. Equality holds for v ∤ 2 with min{|t₁ − 1|_v, |t₂ − 1|_v} ≥ 1.

v nonarchimedean; E_v the local energy of the Legendre heights (DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing).

v ∤ 2: compute 2E_v = ∫(λ_{t₁} − λ_{t₂}) dμ_{t₂} + ∫(λ_{t₂} − λ_{t₁}) dμ_{t₁} with the explicit potentials of DY.6/legendre-escape-rate-away-from-two against the interval measures of DY.6/legendre-canonical-measure-away-from-two (integrals of quadratics in x = log|z| over [log|t|, 0] or [0, log|t|]): case |t₁| > 1 > |t₂| gives log|t₁/t₂|/3; case both > 1 gives log²|t₁/t₂|/(3 log max); the good-reduction case gives |log|t₁||/3; the remaining cases by DY.6/legendre-local-energy-symmetries. v | 2: the same computation with DY.6/legendre-escape-rate-above-two and DY.6/legendre-canonical-measure-above-two, losing at most (4/3) log|2|_v⁻¹ through the factors |4|, |16| in the intervals.

As in DY.6/etale-model-over-finitely-generated-ring.

Choose f ∈ R vanishing on Spec R ∖ U, so Spec R[1/f] ⊆ U, and write R[1/f] = ℤ[u₁, …, u_e]. Apply DY.6/lech-embedding-localized-adjoin to finite ℤ-algebra generators of R and the nonzero f with N = 3. The resulting embedding sends R[1/f] into ℤ_p and f to a unit, giving Spec ℤ_p → Spec R[1/f] → U. Base change X_U along it: smoothness, quasi-projectivity and unramifiedness are stable under base change; the special fibre is the fibre of X_U at the prime below (p), geometrically irreducible.

### 6.100 Regularising finite sets against μ_t (DeMarco–Krieger–Ye Proposition 4.4)

For every ε > 0 there is c(ε) > 0 such that |(μ_t, [F]) − (μ_t, [F]_r)| < ε max{log|t|⁻¹, log|t − 1|⁻¹, log|t|, 1} for all t ∈ ℂ ∖ {0, 1}, every nonempty finite set F ⊂ ℂ and every 0 < r ≤ c min{|t|², |t − 1|², |t|⁻²}, where [F] is the uniform probability measure on F, [F]_r spreads it uniformly on circles of radius r about the points of F, and (·, ·) is the mutual energy (DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing).

Archimedean place; t ∈ ℂ ∖ {0, 1} arbitrary; F any finite set. F is nonempty and the radius is strictly positive.

G_{F_t}(·, 1) is a potential for μ_t: ∫ log|z − w| dμ_t(z) = G_{F_t}(w, 1) + C_t, so (μ_t, [F]_r) − (μ_t, [F]) is an average over x ∈ F of the differences of G_{F_t}(·, 1) on the circle of radius r about x and at x. For t in a compact subset of ℂ ∖ {0, 1}, uniform continuity of Φ_t = G_{F_t}(·, 1) − log⁺|·| in (t, z) bounds the difference by ε. Near each cusp, DY.6/legendre-potential-continuity-near-cusp gives the bound ε log|t|⁻¹ (resp. log|t − 1|⁻¹, log|t|) for r below the stated radius; the three cusps are exchanged by DY.6/legendre-escape-rate-symmetries.

### 6.101 Archimedean energy with one parameter at a cusp (DeMarco–Krieger–Ye Theorem 5.1)

For every ε > 0 and compact C ⊂ ℂ ∖ {0, 1} there is δ > 0 such that (1/6 − ε) log|s|⁻¹ ≤ E_∞(s, t) ≤ (1/6 + ε) log|s|⁻¹ for all 0 < |s| < δ and t ∈ C, where E_∞ is the archimedean local energy of the Legendre heights (DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing).

Archimedean place.

Write E_∞(s, t) through the potentials Φ_s = G_{F_s}(·, 1) − log⁺|·| and ϕ(s, ·) = Φ_s/log|s|⁻¹. As s → 0, μ_s → μ̂_f and ϕ(s, ·) → φ̂_f in the hybrid space (DY.6/legendre-measure-degeneration), while μ_t, Φ_t stay in a compact family (t ∈ C). The leading term is −½ ∫ φ̂_f dμ̂_f · log|s|⁻¹ with ∫ φ̂_f dμ̂_f = −1/3; the remaining terms are o(log|s|⁻¹) by DY.6/legendre-potential-continuity-near-cusp.

### 6.102 Archimedean energy with both parameters at the same cusp, bounded ratio (DeMarco–Krieger–Ye Proposition 5.3)

For every ε > 0 and B > 2 there is δ > 0 such that (E₀(μ̂₁, μ̂_b) − ε) log|t|⁻¹ ≤ E_∞(s, t) ≤ (E₀(μ̂₁, μ̂_b) + ε) log|t|⁻¹ for all s, t with 0 < |t|^B ≤ |s| ≤ |t| < δ, where b = log|s|/log|t| ∈ [1, B] and E₀(μ̂₁, μ̂_b) = (b − 1)²/(6b) is the nonarchimedean energy over ℂ((T)) of the uniform measures μ̂₁, μ̂_b on [ζ_{0,e⁻¹},ζ_{0,1}] and [ζ_{0,e⁻ᵇ},ζ_{0,1}] respectively.

Archimedean place; b bounded by B.

Rescale the potentials: ϕ(t, z) = Φ_{F_t}(z, 1)/log|t|⁻¹ and b ϕ(s, z) = Φ_{F_s}(z, 1)/log|t|⁻¹. Weak convergence μ_t → μ̂₁ and μ_s → μ̂_b in the hybrid space, uniformly for b ∈ [1, B], with convergence of potentials (DY.6/legendre-measure-degeneration, DY.6/legendre-potential-continuity-near-cusp). Define μ̂_b for every real b ≥ 1 as the uniform interval measure on [ζ_{0,e⁻ᵇ},ζ_{0,1}] in the Berkovich line over ℂ((T)), normalized by |T|₀=e⁻¹; its potential is 0 outside the unit disc, −a+a²/(2b) for 0≤a≤b, and −b/2 below radius e⁻ᵇ. Integrating these quadratics gives E₀(μ̂₁,μ̂_b)=(b−1)²/(6b), the calculation underlying DY.6/nonarchimedean-legendre-energy-lower-bound. A nonintegral power T^b is not an element of ℂ((T)) and is not used.

<a id="target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-6-etale-dynamical-mordell-lang"></a>

### 6.103 The dynamical Mordell–Lang theorem for étale maps (Bell–Ghioca–Tucker)

Let X be a quasi-projective variety over ℂ, Φ : X → X an étale endomorphism (Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.Etale), V ⊆ X a closed subvariety and α ∈ X(ℂ). Then V(ℂ) ∩ O_Φ(α) is a union of finitely many orbits O_{Φ^N}(Φ^ℓ(α)) (N, ℓ ∈ ℕ); equivalently {n ∈ ℕ : Φⁿ(α) ∈ V(ℂ)} is a finite union of arithmetic progressions. That is, DML(X, Φ) holds (DY.6/dynamical-mordell-lang-conjecture).

Characteristic 0 (over ℂ); Φ étale (for smooth irreducible X, unramified suffices: Theorem 4.1).

Reduce using the finite directed graph of irreducible components under Φ: components need not be permuted globally, but each component followed by the orbit is eventually in a cycle. Pass to a suitable iterate on a cyclic component and split the time set into residue classes and a finite prefix. Induct on dimension on the singular locus; étaleness preserves regularity in both directions, and on a component’s smooth open locus apply the smooth irreducible case. Finite unions and affine preimages preserve finite unions of arithmetic progressions. Smooth irreducible case: choose a finitely generated ℤ-algebra R carrying X, Φ, V, α; spread out to a smooth quasi-projective model with unramified Φ over a dense open of Spec R (DY.6/etale-model-over-finitely-generated-ring) and embed R into ℤ_p for a prime p ≥ 5 (DY.6/p-adic-model-of-unramified-endomorphism). Replace α by an iterate whose residue class is Φ-periodic of period N; on each residue disc, Φ^N is given by power series F_j (DY.6/p-adic-power-series-coordinates) and some F_j^{M_j} ≡ id mod p (DY.6/p-adic-residue-class-returns); by DY.6/p-adic-analytic-interpolation-of-orbits there are analytic U_{j,ℓ} : ℤ_p → ℤ_p^g with U_{j,ℓ}(k) = ι_j(Φ^{N(M_j k + ℓ) + j}(α)). For each polynomial h in the ideal of V, h ∘ ι_j⁻¹ ∘ U_{j,ℓ} is analytic on ℤ_p; by DY.6/strassmann-theorem it has finitely many zeros or vanishes identically. Hence each subprogression either meets V finitely often or lies in V.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.6/finite-union-of-arithmetic-progressions`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-6-finite-union-of-arithmetic-progressions); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.6/dynamical-mordell-lang-conjecture`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-6-dynamical-mordell-lang-conjecture); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.6/etale-model-over-finitely-generated-ring`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-6-etale-model-over-finitely-generated-ring); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.6/p-adic-model-of-unramified-endomorphism`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-6-p-adic-model-of-unramified-endomorphism); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.6/p-adic-power-series-coordinates`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-6-p-adic-power-series-coordinates); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.6/p-adic-residue-class-returns`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-6-p-adic-residue-class-returns); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.6/p-adic-analytic-interpolation-of-orbits`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-6-p-adic-analytic-interpolation-of-orbits); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.6/strassmann-theorem`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-6-strassmann-theorem); `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Etale`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0`.

### 6.104 Archimedean energy with both parameters at the same cusp (DeMarco–Krieger–Ye Theorems 5.2 and 5.4)

For every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that, for all s, t with 0 < |s| ≤ |t| < δ and b = log|s|/log|t| ≥ 1: ((1/6)(1 − 1/b)² − ε) log|s|⁻¹ ≤ E_∞(s, t) ≤ ((1/6)(1 − 1/b)² + ε) log|s|⁻¹ (Theorem 5.2), equivalently ((b − 1)²/(6b) − bε) log|t|⁻¹ ≤ E_∞(s, t) ≤ ((b − 1)²/(6b) + bε) log|t|⁻¹ (Theorem 5.4).

Archimedean place; s, t near the same cusp 0.

For b ≤ B this is DY.6/archimedean-energy-same-cusp-bounded-ratio (multiply by log|t|⁻¹ = log|s|⁻¹/b). For large b choose a small r>0, then B>1/r. The cusp potential estimates bound |ϕ(t,z)| outside |z|<|t|^r and uniformly everywhere; the annular mass estimates bound the measure of the remaining small discs. Integrate the four terms in the local energy separately to obtain E∞(s,t)/log|t|⁻¹=b/6+O(bε), uniformly for b≥B (DKY (5.6)–(5.10), pp.30–32). Since |b/6−(b−1)²/(6b)|≤1/3, increasing B absorbs this difference. This argument uses the explicit uniform cusp estimates rather than applying the one-escaping-parameter theorem to a compact set that varies with t.

### 6.105 Archimedean energy with parameters at the cusps 0 and ∞ (DeMarco–Krieger–Ye Theorem 5.5)

For every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that ((1/6)(1 + 1/b) − ε) log|s|⁻¹ ≤ E_∞(s, t) ≤ ((1/6)(1 + 1/b) + ε) log|s|⁻¹ for all |t| > 1/δ and 0 < |s| ≤ 1/|t|, where b = −log|s|/log|t|.

Archimedean place.

Set u=1/t as the base parameter, keeping the original coordinate z for both measures. The first limiting potential has values −a for a≤−1, (a²+1)/2 for −1≤a≤0, and 1/2 for a≥0; its measure is uniform on the segment of radii [1,e]. The second limiting measure is uniform on [e⁻ᵇ,1]. Integrating the two potentials gives energy (b+1)/6. Repeat the bounded-b and large-b estimates of DY.6/archimedean-energy-same-cusp in this common hybrid family (DKY Theorem 5.5, p.32). Replacing only t by 1/t is not an application of the simultaneous symmetry.

### 6.108 The Arakelov–Zhang pairing of Legendre heights grows with the parameter height (DeMarco–Krieger–Ye Theorem 1.6; published Theorem 1.7)

There are α, β > 0 such that ĥ_{t₁} · ĥ_{t₂} ≥ α h(t₁, t₂) − β for all t₁ ≠ t₂ in ℚ̄ ∖ {0, 1}, where ĥ_{t₁} · ĥ_{t₂} is the Arakelov–Zhang pairing (DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing) of the Legendre canonical heights (DY.6/legendre-lattes-map) and h(t₁, t₂) the naive height on 𝔸²(ℚ̄); one may take α = 1/512.

t₁ ≠ t₂ algebraic, ≠ 0, 1.

ĥ_{t₁} · ĥ_{t₂} = Σ_v r_v E_v(t₁, t₂) with every E_v ≥ 0 (DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing), so the sum over good places is a lower bound. Apply DY.6/good-places-energy-sum-bound to (t₁,t₂) and (1−t₁,1−t₂). Since the local energies agree, add the two inequalities to get 6·pairing ≥ (3r/4)(h(t₂/t₁)+h((1−t₂)/(1−t₁))) − (3r²/2)(h(t₁,t₂)+h(1−t₁,1−t₂)) −2C. The last two heights differ by a bounded constant under this fixed projective linear change of coordinates. Divide by 6 only after this addition. h(x) + h(y) ≥ h(x, y) and DY.6/birational-height-comparison give h(t₂/t₁) + h((1 − t₂)/(1 − t₁)) ≥ ½ h(t₁, t₂) − C; the coefficient is α = r/16 − r²/2 > 0 for 0 < r ≤ 1/16, maximal 1/512 at r = 1/16.

There is δ > 0 such that ĥ_{t₁} · ĥ_{t₂} ≥ δ for all t₁ ≠ t₂ in ℚ̄ ∖ {0, 1}.

### 6.110 Finiteness of joint small points (DeMarco–Krieger–Ye Proposition 1.8; published Proposition 1.9)

Let δ be as in DY.6/legendre-pairing-uniform-positivity and 0 < b < δ/2. For every t₁ ≠ t₂ in ℚ̄ ∖ {0, 1}, the set S(b, t₁, t₂) = {x ∈ ℙ¹(ℚ̄) : ĥ_{t₁}(x) + ĥ_{t₂}(x) ≤ b} is finite.

0 < b < δ/2.

The adelic metric (‖·‖_{t₁}‖·‖_{t₂})^{1/2} on O(1) is continuous and semipositive with height h_L = ½(ĥ_{t₁} + ĥ_{t₂}) and self-pairing h_L · h_L = ¼ĥ_{t₁}·ĥ_{t₁} + ½ĥ_{t₁}·ĥ_{t₂} + ¼ĥ_{t₂}·ĥ_{t₂} = ½ ĥ_{t₁} · ĥ_{t₂} (bilinearity, ĥ_t · ĥ_t = 0: DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing). Zhang's essential-minimum inequality (liminf h_L(x_n) ≥ h_L · h_L/(2 deg L) for distinct x_n; DY.4/zhang-inequality-on-p1) gives liminf (ĥ_{t₁} + ĥ_{t₂})(x_n) ≥ ½ ĥ_{t₁}·ĥ_{t₂} ≥ δ/2 > b along any sequence of distinct points. Hence only finitely many points satisfy ĥ_{t₁} + ĥ_{t₂} ≤ b.

Fili's triangle inequality (ĥ_{t₁}·ĥ_{t₂})^{1/2} ≤ (ĥ_{t₁}·h_{F,η})^{1/2} + (ĥ_{t₂}·h_{F,η})^{1/2} (DY.4/mutual-energy-metric) with F = S(b, t₁, t₂) ∖ {∞}. Bound each ĥ_{t_i}·h_{F,η} by DY.6/legendre-pairing-upper-bound-regularized: ĥ_{t_i}(F) ≤ b; at archimedean places DY.6/legendre-regularization-estimate with η_v = c(ε′) min{|t_i|², |t_i − 1|², |t_i|⁻²}; at finite places take η_v = min{1, |t₁(t₁ − 1)|_v, |t₂(t₂ − 1)|_v}, reduced by the factor |2|_v at v | 2 so that the potentials of μ_{t_i,v} are constant on η_v-discs (DY.6/legendre-canonical-measure-away-from-two, DY.6/legendre-canonical-measure-above-two). Fix 0 < b < δ/8 (δ of DY.6/legendre-pairing-uniform-positivity) and H > 2β/α with (H − 8b/α)/(H + 1) > 3/4 (α, β of DY.6/legendre-pairing-height-lower-bound). ### 6.113 Uniform common torsion images for pairs of Legendre curves (DeMarco–Krieger–Ye Theorem 1.4; published Theorem 1.5)

There is a uniform constant B such that |π(E_{t₁}^tors) ∩ π(E_{t₂}^tors)| ≤ B for all t₁ ≠ t₂ in ℂ ∖ {0, 1}, where E_t : y² = x(x − 1)(x − t) and π(x, y) = x (with π(O) = ∞).

t₁ ≠ t₂ complex, ≠ 0, 1.

Over ℚ̄ this is DY.6/legendre-uniform-joint-small-points. Suppose a complex pair has more than B common torsion images. Choose B+1 distinct witnesses, separating the possible witness ∞ from the finite x-coordinates. For each finite witness and each of the two maps choose r<s with f_t^r(x)=f_t^s(x), using DY.6/lattes-map-preperiodic-iff-torsion. Iteration of the homogeneous Legendre forms makes this a polynomial cross-product identity in t and x, with rational coefficients. Include t₁,t₂, all finite witnesses and the inverses of t_i(t_i−1), t₁−t₂ and every difference of finite witnesses in a finitely generated ℚ-domain. Apply DY.6/algebraic-specialization-of-finitely-generated-algebras. The inverted elements stay nonzero; the specialized maps have degree four and every evaluated iterate remains a nonzero projective pair because its resultant is nonzero. The cross-product identities therefore preserve preperiodicity and hence torsion images. The possible point ∞ stays ∞, giving B+1 distinct common torsion images over ℚ̄, a contradiction. Neither a division-polynomial converse nor a claim that an algebraic witness belongs to every Legendre fibre is needed.

### 6.114 The Bogomolov–Fu–Tschinkel bound with three common branch values (DeMarco–Krieger–Ye Corollary 8.2)

There is a uniform B such that |π₁(E₁^tors) ∩ π₂(E₂^tors)| ≤ B for all elliptic curves E₁, E₂ over ℂ and standard projections π₁, π₂ (DY.6/standard-projection) with |π₁(E₁[2]) ∩ π₂(E₂[2])| = 3.

E_i elliptic over ℂ; exactly three common branch values.

Apply a Möbius map to send the three common branch values to {0, 1, ∞} (standardProjection_normalize). Replace π_i by π_i^{e_i} for suitable e_i ∈ E_i[2] so that π_i(O_i) = ∞; the torsion images are unchanged (DY.6/standard-projection). Then each π_i is the x-coordinate of a Legendre model E_{t_i} with t₁ ≠ t₂ (the fourth branch values differ), and DY.6/legendre-uniform-common-torsion-images applies.

*Needs:* [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.6/legendre-uniform-common-torsion-images`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-6-legendre-uniform-common-torsion-images); [`ArithmeticDynamics:DY.6/standard-projection`](#target-arithmeticdynamics-dy-6-standard-projection).

### PARENT: G5: finiteness of parabolic cycles and bounded multiplicities of periodic points

For a rational map g of degree d ≥ 2 over ℂ: only finitely many periodic cycles have a root of unity as multiplier (Fatou), and the multiplicity of a periodic point as a solution of gⁿ(z) = z is bounded independently of n. Hence the multiplicity excess dⁿ + 1 − |Fix(gⁿ)| is bounded. This is local complex dynamics (the natural owners are ArithmeticDynamics DY.2 or DY.3, whose interface nodes DY.2/multiplier-of-a-periodic-cycle and DY.3/formal-and-exact-period do not state it).

## Source corrections carried into the targets

These are mathematical descriptions of the discrepancies and corrections, not copied source passages. Their recorded independent verdicts are retained; acceptance of an input packet does not constitute a review of this assembly.

### ArithmeticDynamics/E101

Locator: milnor-1993, Appendix C, fixed point normal form (22), p. 42 of arXiv math/9209221v1.

Here the origin is a fixed point of multiplier µ1, and infinity is a fixed point of multiplier µ2.

For f(z) = z(z + µ1)/(µ2 z + 1) the derivative at 0 is µ1 and, in the coordinate w = 1/z, the conjugate w(w + µ2)/(1 + µ1 w) has derivative µ2 at 0; both are simple fixed points (multiplicity 1) unless µ1 = 1 or µ2 = 1. The same text in §3 (3) says 'multipliers'.

Independent verdict: confirmed (REV-ArithmeticDynamics).

### ArithmeticDynamics/E102

Locator: milnor-1993, Appendix C, proof outline of Lemma C.1, p. 44 of arXiv math/9209221v1.

'normal form (4)' should read 'normal form (3)'.

The computation that follows uses b = µ1, c = µ2 and ω± = (−1 ± √(1 − bc))/c, which are the parameters and critical points of (3) f(z) = z(z + b)/(cz + 1); normal form (4) is f(z) = z + 1/z, which has no parameters b, c.

Independent verdict: confirmed (REV-ArithmeticDynamics).

Locator: hutz-2009, Definition 21 and Lemma 22, p. 16 (arXiv v3; the same in v2, p. 13).

With x₀ = 0 the formula x_k = f^{p^k}(x₀) at k = 0 gives f(0) ≠ 0, and f^p(x_{k−1}) = f^{p + p^{k−1}}(0) ≠ f^{p^k}(0) for k ≥ 2; the proof of Lemma 22 uses x_{k+1} = F_k^p(x₀), and the base case b₁ ≥ 2 of Lemma 23 needs b₀ = v(f(0)) ≥ 1. ### ArithmeticDynamics/E306

Locator: hutz-2009, Proof of Lemma 23, p. 17 (arXiv v3; the same in v2, p. 13).

Lemma 22 gives only c_{k+1} ≥ min(b_k, c_k + v(p), p·c_k), which does not imply c_{k+1} ≥ p·c_k. Theorem 2 still holds: if b_{e−1} > v(p) then (p − 1)c_{e−1} ≤ v(p); since the b_k increase, b_k ≥ v(p) + 1 from the first index k₀ with b_{k₀} > v(p) on, so c_{k+1} ≥ min(v(p) + 1, p·c_k) there, and c_{e−1} ≤ v(p)/(p − 1) < v(p) + 1 forces c_{k+1} ≥ p·c_k along k₀ ≤ k < e − 1; with c_{k₀} ≥ 2^{k₀−1} from the regime b_k ≤ v(p) this gives c_{e−1} ≥ 2^{e−2} and 2^{e−1} ≤ v(p) (the same argument with Fibonacci numbers for p = 2).

Example of the unjustified step: v(p) = 1, k = 3, b₃ = 2 > v(p); Lemma 22 yields only c₄ ≥ min(2, c₃ + 1, p·c₃) ≥ 2, not c₄ ≥ 8. The unconditional claim c_k ≥ 2^{k−1} of Lemma 23 is therefore not established; the repaired argument in DY.2/period-exponent-bound avoids it.
